    Changelog (Developer / Technical)¶

    Full technical detail for each release. Companion to CHANGELOG.md — same section structure, same entry numbering, same bold lead per entry, but the body keeps class names, file paths, audit IDs, error fingerprints, and failed-approaches notes that get trimmed from the user-facing log.

    Lift from commit-message bodies on each release; this file is a curated rollup, not new authoring.

    Legend: 🟢 confirmed working in-app  ·  🔴 added but not yet verified in-app

    [Unreleased]¶

    Unreleased entries live in CHANGELOG_UNRELEASED_DEV.md — this file is the released archive.

    [0.8.6] - 2026-09-21¶

    Added¶

    1. 🟢 Diff State Mode colours keyed objects pink when their animation comes from a parent tier, by a parent layer, an inherited action or a borrow. Route A of doc/roadmap/active/diff-state-parent.md (companion _dev/rest-parent-state-followups.md): no third state. Keyed gains a second colour, diff_state_keyed_above_color (default 0.90/0.25/0.75, props_diff_state.py, outside the per-state loop; EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 867 → 868), drawn under Look in the Keyed fold. states.py gains OWN/ABOVE, _target_keyed_source(target, own_names) and keyed_source(obj, own_names, manual=False): per surface of iter_anim_targets_only, a bound action with keys is OWN when its name is the row's assigned action or the Rest action and ABOVE otherwise; a parent layer alone (extra_animated_channels non-empty, no own keys) is ABOVE; any OWN surface wins; pinned objects and a non-empty Object.tks_action are OWN. marked_objects computes the row's own names once (_row_own_names: the active take's tks_action, else the view layer's, plus rest_state.get_rest_action) and stores the ABOVE names in _scan['above'] (above_names()). logic.resolve_color takes above/above_color; random colour still wins; Drift ignores both. draw.py carries the flag in the plan tuple and reads the swatch into state_settings as above_color. Texts: one description constant in texts/tooltips_preferences.py, strings parked in _pending.py. Tests: +4 test_diff_state_logic.py, +7 test_diff_state_states.py, +1 test_diff_state_prefs.py (263 passed across the Diff State files, i18n guard and prefs count).

    2. 🟢 Opening a file an older add-on version saved rebuilds the cache for you, with one line saying it happened. New @persistent _rebuild_on_load on load_post in operators/ui/ops_cache_rebuild.py. It asks cache_version.stamp_mismatch() itself rather than reading the WM flags that module's own handler sets - handler order is registration order, and a rule that quietly depends on it breaks the day someone reorders register(). On a mismatch, and only with the preference on, it runs _clear_in_memory_caches() and restamp_active_scene(). It runs stage 1 ONLY: the add-on disable/enable the button also schedules is a teardown a fraction of a second after a file load, with the cascade, the preload pass and the mutation queue possibly still in flight, and is not something to do unasked. What makes that safe is dev/tests/test_rebuild_cache_reaches_everything.py, which measures every run that the clear is enough. Not guarded on having a window (Constitution rule 7): a render farm or an MCP-driven agent meets the same stale caches and is less able to notice. The note is wm.tks_cache_rebuilt_from, drawn by draw_rebuilt_strip as a line rather than a box (nothing is wrong and nothing is being asked), retired after REBUILT_NOTICE_SECONDS = 12 by a one-shot _expire_tick timer with the deferred second redraw the take-data rescue notice already needed. The handler lives in the operators layer because the clear reaches into features/ and properties/ and core may not import upward (ARCH-01). Also corrected the operator's header, which still claimed the clear alone "has historically been observed to leave the takes tree in a broken state" - true before 32c9c4bb, stale since.

    3. 🟢 New Cache preference turns that off, and then holds the add-on's panels shut until you rebuild. auto_rebuild_cache (BoolProperty, default True, props_automations.py) drawn under Preferences > Workflow > Automations > Cache, plus its expand_auto_cache section flag; EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 868 -> 870, _SAVEABLE_PREFS and the prefs_search section map both extended, two manual_map anchors added. cache_version.auto_rebuild_enabled() defaults to True when prefs cannot be read at all, which a load handler on a partly-registered add-on can hit: a rebuild the user did not want costs a cache, one that did not happen costs a session of wrong answers. The lock is wm.tks_cache_lock, raised by _check_on_load (and by register(), for an old file already open) when mismatched AND the preference is off, lowered ONLY by restamp_active_scene(). It is deliberately not tks_cache_stale: a save re-stamps the file so the banner is right to go, while the caches this session built are still the old ones - one flag for both would make Ctrl+S a way past the lock that changes nothing it guarded, and test_saving_clears_the_warning_but_not_the_lock pins it. The surfaces grey out through the same layout.enabled = False line they already use for recovery_pending, now recovery_pending(context) or cache_locked(context) in panels/context/panel.py, panels/inspector/panel.py, panels/globals_panel.py and panels/render_queue_panel.py, with a test that a surface which learned one guard learned both. The card is panels/navigation/warnings/system_cache_lock.py, drawn once in the navigation panel (four copies of one box is the mistake the store block already made and fixed) and superseding the mismatch banner rather than stacking with it. It carries both ways out - the Rebuild button and a "Rebuild automatically next time" tick - and a test asserts no file under preferences/ ever consults cache_locked, because locking the page the switch lives on would trap the user. 11 new strings parked in _pending.py. Card: doc/roadmap/active/cache-rebuild-automation.md.

    4. 🟢 A file saved by a NEWER add-on version says so and asks you to update, instead of pretending a rebuild fixed it. _is_mismatch asks whether MAJOR.MINOR differs, not which way round, so a file from a later Takes took the older file's path. That did harm twice: the caches were cleared, which repairs nothing (a newer file may hold data this version has no schema for, and dropping a cache does not conjure one), and restamp_active_scene then wrote THIS version over the file's own - erasing the only record that it came from a later one, so no later open in any version would have warned either. It also announced "Cache rebuilt for this file", which reads as handled. core/cache_version.py gains _version_tuple and _is_newer (MAJOR.MINOR compared as ints; an unreadable stamp answers False and takes the older path, because junk carries no claim about the future and the older path is always safe), the public stamp_is_from_the_future(), and wm.tks_cache_from_future set in _refresh_flags. _rebuild_on_load returns early on it, so no clear and no re-stamp. The lock goes up REGARDLESS of auto_rebuild_cache: that preference governs whether the add-on may repair unasked, and there is no repair here. system_cache_lock.py switches heading, infobox (INFOBOX_CACHE_LOCK_NEWER) and button - tks.cache_unlock ("Continue Anyway") calls unlock_without_restamping(), which exists purely so the way out is not restamp_active_scene; the auto-rebuild tick box is hidden, since automatic rebuilding is not on offer for this file. system_cache.py carries the same wording for anyone who continued anyway, and drops its Rebuild button there. Both headings are written as plain if/else rather than a conditional text=: the i18n harvester reads that argument for a literal and an expression hid both arms - no PENDING entry, no de_DE key, and test_i18n_guard cannot flag a string it never saw. 8 new strings parked. Guards: 9 new tests in test_cache_auto_rebuild.py covering direction, junk stamps, no-clear, no-restamp, locking with the preference ON, and the unlock that leaves the stamp alone. Card: doc/roadmap/active/cache-rebuild-automation.md.

    5. 🟢 While the panels are locked, hotkeys and menus refuse too, so nothing can be changed behind the lock. layout.enabled = False greys pixels and stops nothing: a keymap, a menu, F3 search and bpy.ops.tks.* from a script all reach an operator without consulting the layout that drew its button. Reported from a real session - takes deleted by hotkey out of a file the add-on had just said it could not read correctly. poll() is the one gate all those routes share, and there are 557 operators with no common base, so new core/interaction_lock.py wraps them from a bpy.utils.register_class hook installed at the top of register() and removed at the bottom. The hook is required, not tidy: Blender reads poll when register_class runs and keeps what it found, so a pass afterwards changes only the Python attribute - measured in one tick, cls.poll(context) False while bpy.ops.tks.add_viewlayer.poll() True. Two faults the suite caught: the guard read cls.__dict__["poll"], finding None for every operator that INHERITS its poll (the six cascade action popovers among them) and replacing a real refusal with an unconditional True - it resolves through the MRO now and tags itself so a subclass does not stack a second gate; and it gave a poll to tks.rest_badge, an inert chip whose job is to look bright, where anything that can refuse draws dimmed - NEVER_GUARDED skips it. unguarded_poll() lets introspection look through the guard, and test_scripted_call_safety reads poll source that way. ALWAYS_ALLOWED is the four ways out: rebuild_cache, cache_unlock, reload_addon, clear_pycache. Preferences need nothing - the auto-rebuild switch is a property. Scripted callers are blocked too: Constitution rule 7 read the right way round, since an agent meets the same unreadable file and is less able to notice. poll_message_set carries the reason into the tooltip. Guards: dev/tests/test_interaction_lock.py - the reported operator really refuses, really changes nothing when called, works again unlocked, the ways out still run, every allow-list entry names a live operator, a second wrap is a no-op, and the register_class hook is not left installed. Card: doc/roadmap/active/cache-rebuild-automation.md.

    6. 🟢 Object Take Mode. Every watched object is in one of three modes: AUTO (the take resolves and assigns the action, as before), THIS_TAKE and ALL_TAKES (the user owns it; the cascade leaves the object alone). utils/take_mode.py owns the storage and the single predicate is_hand_set. The record is JSON on a new Object.tks_take_mode StringProperty - an All Takes flag plus the scene::take keys where it is hand-set - and AUTO stores the empty string, because AUTO is nearly every object in a heavy scene and a per-object record meaning "default" is weight in every .blend for nothing. Writes go through setattr, never obj[field]: the field is a bpy.props property on the Object TYPE, and a subscript write makes an IDProperty of the same name in a store getattr never reads back. Old pins read through unchanged, including the bare view-layer entries utils/pinned.py healed for two releases, and reading one does not write. Three cascade paths asked the pin question three different ways and had drifted apart (vl_switch_fast, cascade_actions, vl_unassign); they now read one predicate. The sweep SKIPS a hand-set object entirely, sub-targets included, rather than clearing it first - the pin force-cleared, which is why pinning took an object's animation away while its own tooltip promised the opposite. Parent State rides along for free: layers are synced inside the per-target work, so an object never processed never receives them. PIN_CLR leaves the sweep's log line and HANDSET replaces it; the old number counted a destruction, the new one counts a hands-off. Guards: dev/tests/test_take_mode.py. Leaving Auto RELEASES the whole object (core/take_mode_apply.release_take_action - the action-handling half lives in core, because every one of those functions reaches into the cascade, the sweep and the target walk, and ARCH-01 rightly refused eight upward imports from a utils leaf): while it was in Auto, everything it wore came from the take, so all of it goes bar the Rest Action binding, and the object sits empty until the user assigns, animates or hands it back - returning to Auto re-runs the one sweep (reapply_take) so the take fills it again at once. The autokey mirror (features/rest_state/mirror_logic.py) now skips hand-set objects and their sub-targets before resolving anything: the release raised a depsgraph update, the mirror woke on it and bound the emptied object to the Rest Action, which the user saw as "T switches it to Rest State". Its "pinned objects live in the Rest Action" branch was unreachable after that and is removed. Guard: dev/tests/test_take_mode_mirror.py, driving the real handler with the suppress-scope fake depsgraph. And a hand-set object's binding is REMEMBERED PER TAKE (bind in the record; stored_ binding / store_binding, restored by the sweep via take_mode_apply.restore_binding in place of a bare skip): Blender gives an object one binding and every take it passes through as Auto rewrites it, so "hands off here" alone let the object come home wearing the last take's action (the trace: away HANDSET=0 assigns, back HANDSET=1 skips and keeps). Release stores "empty on purpose"; the inspector sync captures a native assignment live (capture_binding); returning to Auto forgets the entry. Nothing stored is FIRST SIGHT and is captured, never cleared - reading it as empty would wipe every adopted object on the first sweep after first open. Guard: dev/tests/test_take_mode_roundtrip.py. And the rest revert's last-key rule (features/rest_state/revert_snap.py) now skips a hand-set object's targets after updating its baseline: its key-count cache is keyed by (type, name), not by action, so rebinding a hand-set object from a keyed action to a fresh empty one read as "lost every key" and unbind_action cut the action the user had chosen a second earlier (the popover case - the second action stayed only because it was keyed before the deferred fired). Six driver tests in dev/tests/test_take_mode_fresh_action.py, one per pass in that tick window; the revert one is RED without the guard and its rig carries a Rest action and a real seed pass, because without them the revert exits before its loop and the test passed vacuously. Record: doc/troubleshooting/take_mode_fresh_action_unbound_by_rest_revert.md. A duplicated scene keeps its hand-set objects: keys are scene::take, so a linked copy - Scene.001 over the same objects - came up Auto. The add-on's own Duplicate (operators/context/ops_edit_item.py, right after scene.new) now calls take_mode.copy_scene_keys with both names in hand: a linked copy keeps the old keys beside the new, a full copy re-keys its copied objects; stored bindings travel with the keys. The same reading found scene RENAMES healed into the cascade ledgers but never into these keys (panels/context/handlers.py), so heal_scene_rename sits beside rename_scene_in_ledgers. Known gap, on the card: Blender's native scene.new from the context menus bypasses the add-on's operator and is not healed. Guard: dev/tests/test_take_mode_scene_copy.py. And the memory survives a trip through Auto: set_mode(AUTO) used to drop the stored binding ("the memory belongs to the mode"), which lost a user's whole setup on an accidental toggle off and on, because re-entry released to empty with nothing remembered (user ruling 2026-09-19). Auto keeps the entry now, and both entry routes - the row glyph and the row menu - go through one door, take_mode_apply.enter_hand_set: write the mode, release the take's actions, and if this take remembers what the user gave the object, put it back. A first entry with no memory still empties. Guards in dev/tests/test_take_mode_roundtrip.py, including the inverted pin of the old behaviour.

    7. 🟢 The watchlist column and the row menu. The pin column becomes the mode column - same place, same width, same drag. LAYER_USED for Auto, EVENT_T for This Take, EVENT_A for All Takes: three DISTINCT glyphs, never a hollow/filled pair of one shape, because choosing the wrong mode silently changes which takes own an object and at row size a hollow star and a filled star are the same picture. (SOLO_ON/SOLO_OFF were proposed and rejected for that, and because they already mean favourite in the token list.) The click still moves Auto to This Take and back and the column is still a prop, which is what gives it the drag - a menu cannot be a prop, and that is the whole reason the third choice lives elsewhere. That elsewhere is TKS_MT_watchlist_row_menu, whose new Mode block acts on every TICKED row, so twenty objects are one trip; All Takes is reached deliberately because leaving it hands the object straight back to the cascade. The sync pass resolves the mode once per object and caches the string on the row - draw_item runs per row per redraw, and parsing JSON there would be per object per frame. Three tests pin the glyphs against Blender's own icon enum: a bad icon name draws a blank box with nothing in the console.

    8. 🟢 First-contact adoption. A .blend that has never met Takes is full of hand-assigned actions, and running the cascade over it would make the add-on's first act the stripping of the file. core/take_mode_adopt.py sets every already-animated object to All Takes before the cascade is even resolved. No new marker: core/cache_version.py already stamps scene["tks_addon_version"] on save, so no scene carrying it means no version has ever written this file, and it is an IDProperty so it survives PropertyGroup churn. It runs at the top of _deferred_load_apply, where PropertyGroup writes are legal and a load_post handler's are not; a stamped file costs one keys() test per scene. It claims the whole object using the same walk the sweep does - an object whose material is animated but whose transform is not would otherwise have that material stripped. The card is a DECISION, not a notice: Keep Them, Put Them On One Take, or Drop The Assignments. Keep is the safe default and is also what closing the card does. Drop asks again with the blast radius, and reads auto_fake_user_actions rather than promising the actions survive. Its body is gated on the same condition as its nav-bar toggle, because a body that outlives its button is unclosable - the trap the split-view warnings fell into. tks_show_adopted_objects joins WARNING_TOGGLE_PROPS, and tks_show_swap_orphans and tks_show_profiler, registered and never dropped, are dropped with it; a test now walks the roster. Guards: dev/tests/test_take_mode_adopt.py.

    9. 🟢 Diff State marks objects a parent tier keys as Parent State. Pink shipped on 2026-09-17 as a second COLOUR of Take State, with the scan keeping a list of names on the side (states.above_names()) and the draw path threading an above flag through the plan. It is a state now: a row in DIFF_STATE_STATES with its own colour, marks, see-through, line width and per-kind table, like any other. keyed_source's OWN / ABOVE answer feeds classify_states straight through, so the side channel, the flag and diff_state_keyed_above_color are all retired, and resolve_color went back to one colour per state.

    10. 🟢 New Diff State state marks every object no tier keys at all. Rest State, the bottom of the cascade: keyed_source answering None is now an answer, not an absence. It ships switched OFF, and the scan always computes it while the viewport only draws it on request - in most files it is most of the scene, so it is a filter you reach for, not a wash you leave on. Cost, measured rather than reasoned: each state is 113 preferences (232 annotations at two states, 458 at four), so EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT went 870 -> 1095 with the retired swatch taken off. The window-manager switches are generated from the table (properties._switch_names) and the master summary ORs them, so a state brings its own switch. logic.STATE_ORDER is (DRIFT, KEYED, PARENT, REST): drift leads because it is the warning, the other three follow the cascade - and an object is only ever in one of them, because a value comes from one place.

    11. 🟢 The adoption card asks which take, and answers per object. TKS_OT_AdoptedToOneTake ran straight off context.view_layer with no dialog, so on the take the reader was standing on it was indistinguishable from Keep Them - the difference only shows on the OTHER takes - and it never said which take it had chosen. Reported 2026-09-19: "put them on one take does the same like keep them". It now invokes a props dialog with a take chooser defaulting to the active take, and re-applies the cascade on the take being looked at when the chosen one is different, so the card does not close on an apparently unchanged viewport. Every row on the card carries all three modes plus a take picker (user request, same day). TKS_OT_AdoptedObjectToTake serves all four: the three glyphs act on the active take in one click, and only the picker - pick_take, drawn with VIEWZOOM - opens the dialog, because a glyph that sometimes opens one and sometimes does not is two buttons wearing one face. The glyphs are read from take_mode.MODE_ICON rather than written on the card, so the card and the watchlist column cannot drift on what a mode looks like, and All Takes draws depressed because that is where adoption put every object. A description classmethod gives each button its own tooltip - one bl_description would be wrong three times out of four. Acting on a row removes just that name from the card's list, so it shrinks as the reader works through it, and the card closes on the last one. Both enums share _take_items, decorated with utils.enum_cache.retained_enum - a runtime-built enum whose items are not retained is read back after Blender frees them. The card's own text now states what the two whole-list buttons differ by rather than leaving the reader to find out. Guards in dev/tests/test_take_mode_adopt.py, including one that pins the difference the reader could not see: after One Take the object is This Take here and AUTO on every other take.

    12. 🟢 The adoption card expires on save. It is an OFFER, not a gate: a reader who never notices it loses nothing, because every object it lists is already ALL_TAKES - exactly what Keep Them does. What was missing was a rule for when it stops being RELEVANT (user question 2026-09-19). The answer falls out of the machinery adoption already uses: run_if_first_contact calls a file new when no scene carries tks_addon_version, and cache_version._stamp_on_save writes that stamp on the way out - so once the file is saved it is no longer a file Takes has never seen, and the card's own premise is false. Saving is accepting. take_mode_adopt._stand_down_on_save, a @persistent save_post handler registered beside cache_version in __init__, clears the three WM props and decides nothing for the objects. save_post and not save_pre for the same reason _check_on_save uses it: a save that fails never reaches it, and an offer withdrawn for a save that did not happen is withdrawn for nothing. Until the save the offer returns on every open, because adoption finds no stamp and runs again. Guards in dev/tests/test_take_mode_adopt.py.

    13. 🟢 The first-contact question is also asked in the viewport. The N-panel card is quiet by design and easy to miss; a reader can work for five minutes and only then meet a decision about a moment that has passed (user ruling 2026-09-19). TKS_OT_AdoptedPrompt puts the same question where they are looking, as an invoke_props_dialog carrying TWO answers, not four: keep them all, or let me decide object by object. A dialog that lands unasked in the middle of the viewport is the wrong place for a careful decision - no object list, no way to treat one object differently from the next - so it asks the one thing answerable at a glance and hands the rest to the panel, which can address a single row. Decide writes to nothing; it calls _open_the_panel, which opens the sidebar, selects the Takes tab and opens the card, because telling a reader where to look and leaving them to find it is the same miss the card already had. Cancel is a third real answer meaning "later", which leaves the card up. Raised by take_mode_adopt._raise_prompt on a 0.5s one-shot safe_register timer rather than inline: it runs from _deferred_load_apply, and an operator that opens a dialog cannot be invoked from inside the file-load work. The timer re-reads tks_adopted_count before invoking, so a question answered in the panel during that tick never raises a dialog, and it returns at once under bpy.app.background - a render or a script must not stop on a dialog nobody can answer. Guards in dev/tests/test_take_mode_adopt.py.

    14. 🟢 Animation the add-on never saw is adopted, not only on first contact. Work with Takes, switch the add-on OFF, animate, switch it on again: the file keeps its version stamp the whole time, so file_is_new_to_takes says nothing and the sweep strips the work (user ruling 2026-09-19). The file does not record that history and no attempt is made to reconstruct it. take_mode_adopt.unclaimed_objects asks what is TRUE now instead: the object is AUTO, it wears an action, and reconcile.tier_holders finds no tier of the take system holding that action - so nobody's take put it there. One check covers three shapes of the same problem: the add-on switched off and on, an object appended or linked from another file (the gap recorded on the card and now closed), and a collaborator without the add-on working in the file. Deliberately timid: the Rest action is excluded, anything a tier holds is excluded, a hand-set object is not in question, and an unreadable tier lookup counts as CLAIMED - a false "unclaimed" would offer to adopt the cascade's own action, which is worse than missing one. The adopted objects raise the same card and the same prompt. test_a_stamped_file_adopts_nothing is inverted with its reasoning: asserting that was the hole. Guards in dev/tests/test_take_mode_adopt.py.

    15. 🟢 The adoption card draws a real list. It stacked ten labels and said "and more", which a reader cannot act on - and a first-contact file can hold hundreds of objects (user ruling 2026-09-19). New panels/navigation/warnings/adopted_list.py holds TKS_AdoptedItem (a name, never a reference - the list outlives the pass that built it) and TKS_UL_AdoptedObjects, drawn through template_list over new WindowManager.tks_adopted_items / tks_adopted_index. The joined tks_adopted_names string stays as the flat record the operators read, and no longer truncates at 50 - the card scrolls. The row follows the house shape: left packs with alignment='LEFT' so the name absorbs the slack, right reserves ICON_SLOT_UNITS * 4 absolutely, because a proportional split hands the buttons a SHARE of a row already narrowed by the list's own side column and they draw as nothing. Both classes register BEFORE the WM properties, since a CollectionProperty cannot point at a PropertyGroup Blender does not know yet, and unregister after them. Guards in dev/tests/test_take_mode_adopt.py, including one that the two new props are in drop_props.

    16. 🟢 ai.switch_view_layer(scene, view_layer) — the verb the facade was missing. Measured 2026-09-19 while answering whether an assistant can build a per-take camera/animation concept: set_override returned ok, explain() agreed tier='VL' value='Cam_Shot2', and scene.camera never moved. Cause: handle_viewlayer_switch rides depsgraph_update_post (core/vl_switch.py:938) and a scripted window.view_layer = raises NO depsgraph update, so the sweep never runs — a click raises one, an agent does not. Proven by nudging an object 0.01: same scene, camera then correct. NO new mechanism: tks.switch_viewlayer already suppresses the handler and runs the whole pipeline (“ONE contract for every view-layer switch”) and was verified callable from a bpy.app.timers callback, returning {'FINISHED'}. The verb is a name-addressed door onto it — idempotent like switch_take (an agent's commonest failure is retrying a call it believes timed out), reads back which layer WENT live rather than echoing the request, and returns BAD_ARGS if the operator cancels rather than claiming a switch. takes_for_blender/ai/verbs_takes.py; re-exported and added to _MUTATING_VERBS in ai/api.py — test_every_lock_taking_verb_is_declared_mutating caught that omission. 7 tests in dev/tests/test_ai_switch_view_layer.py. AI_GUIDE.md gains the two meanings of “switching” and an explicit warning not to assign window.view_layer. Original scenario re-run: 10/10. Root cause and the four failed approaches in doc/troubleshooting/ai_view_layer_switch_never_applied_cascade.md. Cross-ref CHANGELOG_UNRELEASED.md Added 16.
    17. 🟢 compositor added to OWNED_PROPERTIES. The table an assistant reads in help() listed camera, world, action, output_rule and NOT compositor — which is a cascade kind (CascadeProperty.COMPOSITOR) whose scene.node_tree the addon rewrites on every switch. By omission the table told an assistant the compositor was Blender's to write, so that write is overwritten on the next switch with no error: exactly the trap BOUNDARY exists to close, left open for the one owned property with no verb. Listed now, with use_instead saying plainly that no verb can set it yet and that scene.node_tree must not be written. Also repaired three use_instead strings carrying mojibake (â€¦ where … was meant) in text that goes straight to an assistant. ai/api.py. Cross-ref CHANGELOG_UNRELEASED.md Added 17.
    18. 🟢 Compositor native handling, the World's shape. compositor_unassigned_mode (ADOPT / PRESERVE / CLEAR) and compositor_adopt_tier (six tiers) in props_automations.py, drawn as their own Compositor section under World (draw_workflow.py, fold flag expand_auto_compositor in props_logging.py + ACCORDION_GROUPS), indexed in prefs_search.py, tooltips in texts/tooltips_preferences.py, strings in the pending ledger. core/compositor_native_sync.py - a msgbus subscription on Scene.compositing_node_group, notify -> one-shot timer -> COMPOSITOR-filtered cascade, re-armed on load, in the Process Monitor, wired in vl_handlers. msgbus cannot be proven headless (Scene.world scores zero too). EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 1094 -> 1098.
    19. 🟢 The one first-open dialog names the compositor. User ruling: told once, in the same dialog as the animated objects. The compositor is adopted INSIDE the load-time cascade, after run_if_first_contact has announced its objects - so core/vl_lifecycle_load.py now notes candidates before the cascade (note_compositor_candidates: native node group, no tier winner), confirms after (confirm_compositor_adoptions: tracker == name AND a source tier), and finish_first_contact raises tks.adopted_prompt once for objects, compositors or both. The raise left run_if_first_contact. TKS_AdoptedItem gains kind / tier / scene_name; wm.tks_adopted_compositor_count; a compositor row with tks.adopted_compositor_clear (public resolve_compositor_adopt_target + plain setattr, then the COMPOSITOR cascade follows the tree). Title Made Without Takes; _prompt_paragraph joins the four INFOBOX_ADOPTED_PROMPT_* keys, only what was found. Known limit: the load-time cascade runs for the context scene only; another scene's compositor is adopted silently on the first switch to it, like world/camera today.
    20. 🟢 World and Camera join the one first-open dialog. Both were adopted at load through the witness rule already - silently. core/take_mode_adopt.py now drives the report-back off one table, NATIVE_KINDS (compositor / world / camera -> scene attr, tier prop, global prop, card kind): note_native_candidates() before the cascade, confirm_native_adoptions() after (tracker == name AND a source tier; Preserve confirms nothing), finish_first_contact(dict) raises tks.adopted_prompt once. A camera a timeline marker governs is never a candidate (cascade_adopt._marker_bound_camera). _prompt_paragraph(objects, comps, worlds, cameras) with four new INFOBOX_ADOPTED_PROMPT_* keys in the user's pattern; TKS_AdoptedItem.kind gains WORLD / CAMERA with their own icons; wm.tks_adopted_world_count / tks_adopted_camera_count. tks.adopted_native_clear(kind, scene_name, name) replaces tks.adopted_compositor_clear - the same _NATIVE_CLEAR table, public resolve_*_adopt_target + plain setattr, then the kind's cascade follows the tree. Every scene, not only the one the file opens into: adopt_native_elsewhere() runs the one filtered witness pass per (scene, kind) candidate outside the active scene, on its first view layer, before the confirm - the tree draws tier records, and it showed nothing for the other scenes until the first switch (user report 2026-09-20). Tests: dev/tests/test_adopted_prompt_native.py. Branch feat/adopt-whole-file.
    21. 🟢 Markers mean Multi-Cam. User ruling 2026-09-20: a timeline that cuts between cameras with markers is a multi-camera shot, and Takes' word for it is a Multi-Cam take. core/take_mode_adopt.adopt_marker_cuts(active_scene, active_view_layer) runs in _deferred_load_apply BEFORE the cascade: for every scene with camera-bound markers, ONE layer - the active view layer of the scene the file opens into, view_layers[0] elsewhere - becomes Multi-Cam holding those cuts; the other layers stay single (ruling: the Multi-Cam layer holds the list and rewrites it on return). Gated on camera_unassigned_mode == 'ADOPT'; a layer already Multi-Cam is left alone; never twice. Reached through two new providers, cameras.multicam_adopt / cameras.multicam_release (features/cameras/multicam_adopt.py), both writing inside _writing_scope so _on_multicam_changed neither re-applies from the load timer nor - on the way out - takes the cuts off the timeline. The camera pass then defers to the Multi-Cam take as it already does (cameras.multicam_api, tracker source 'Multi-Cam'). Dialog: INFOBOX_ADOPTED_PROMPT_MULTICAM_ONE/MANY in the user's pattern; card kind MULTICAM (icon MARKER_HLT, name = layer, wm.tks_adopted_multicam_count); Clear releases the layer to single-camera and leaves the markers untouched; AdoptedDrop covers it. The SCENE tier also gets a camera when it has none - rules.camera_at_frame(cuts, scene.frame_current), the cut the artist was looking at - because the single-camera layers of a marker scene otherwise started with no camera, and Isolate (Multi Camera + Hide Others) then kept nothing and hid every camera, render flag included (user report 2026-09-20, the red popover). CARD_KINDS beside NATIVE_KINDS, since a timeline is a layer flag and not a scene attribute. dev/tests/test_adopted_marker_cuts.py (13).

    Fixed¶

    1. 🟢 Diff State Mode marks an object animated only by a shape key, a material, object data, a node tree or Geometry Nodes. features/diff_state/states.py::has_keyed_slot decided the whole-object verdict from obj.animation_data alone. An Object is not one datablock: shape keys animate through obj.data.shape_keys.animation_data, and obj.data, every material, every material/light node tree and its inner groups, every Geometry Nodes group and every particle setting each carry their own animation_data with their own action and their own slot. The verdict was therefore RIGHT for anything animated by MOVING the object and silently wrong for everything else — no error, no log line, the object simply drew no mark while its shape key visibly moved. Reported by the user with a shape key that had an animation, an action and a slot.

    The addon already owned the correct walk — core/vl_targets .iter_anim_targets_only(), used by the cascade and by Value Lock — and the verdict never called it. Nothing in the tree could notice: the walk and the verdict sit in different layers so MAINT-11 cannot pair them, and no test failed because every test that animates an object animates it by moving it. This is the FIFTH hand-narrowed animation walk in this codebase.

    Fix: _target_is_keyed(target) splits out the slot-aware "bound-is-not-animated" test (unchanged — extra_animated_channels, then get_slot_fcurves(action, slot)), and has_keyed_slot runs it over iter_anim_targets_only(obj), returning on the first hit. The labelled iter_anim_targets() was rejected on cost: generate_slot_name() is ~1.5-2 ms per target and this is a draw-path reader (see doc/troubleshooting/cascade_action_clear_slow.md). Draw cost holds because the walk is a GENERATOR and its yield order is cheap-to-dear — Object, obj.data, shape keys, then the material/node-tree walks that iterate nodes — so an animated object answers on its first or second target and only a fully unanimated one pays for the whole walk; the scan is cached between draws either way (marked_objects, invalidated in features/diff_state/cache.py). extra_animated_channels is now asked per TARGET; the only registered source, features/parent_state/layers.py ::owned_strip_channels, reads only the passed ad and ignores the target, so it is safe on every surface.

    Guarded against a repeat by a new auditor rule: CORR-32 — Object-Only Animation Verdict (blender-addon-auditor a41a85d), which reports this exact shape wherever it is written. 1 finding on this tree before the fix, 0 after, 0 on the other three registered addons.

    Tests: four in dev/tests/test_diff_state_states.py — a keyed shape key, a keyed camera lens (obj.data), a keyed material, and the negative case (an object carrying a material and UNKEYED shape keys must stay dark, or the mode marks the whole scene). Write-up: doc/troubleshooting/diff_state_blind_to_non_object_animation.md. Impact-selected suite: 4341 passed, 1 failed — the failure is test_i18n_guard::test_no_untracked_new_strings on features/cameras/multicam_operators.py:487, present on main and untouched by this branch. Cross-ref CHANGELOG_UNRELEASED.md Fixed 1.

    1. 🟢 Diff State Mode counts an object animated only when a slot it owns holds at least one keyframe, not merely a channel. Follow-up to Fixed 1 the same day, from a review of the criterion rather than of the scope. The question the mode asks is exactly "does this object own a target with an Action Slot ASSIGNED whose slot holds MORE THAN ZERO keys?" — the shape the Inspector's per-row badge shows (Suzanne: object row empty, Mesh Data slot Suzanne = 2, Shape Keys slot Suzanne_Keys = 2).

    _target_is_keyed ended at bool(get_slot_fcurves(action, slot)), a count of CHANNELS. An F-Curve can exist with an empty keyframe_points — a channel created and never keyed, or one whose last key was deleted — and such a curve animates nothing. Counting channels marks an object for a channel that does nothing, and the mark never clears when the user removes the last key, because the channel survives the removal. New _slot_has_keys(action, slot) returns True only for a slot holding at least one keyframe (getattr(fc, 'keyframe_points', None) guarded — get_slot_fcurves also extends from bag.channels, which need not carry the attribute).

    The "slot assigned" half needed no new code: get_slot_fcurves() already returns [] when the action HAS slots and slot names none of them, while a legacy action with no slots at all still answers from get_all_fcurves — the only reading available for a file predating slots. Adding an explicit if slot is None: return False would have broken those files.

    Deliberately NOT reused: core/channels.get_key_count_for_target(), the counter behind the Inspector badge. It reads bpy.context, routes by target type through path filters, and counts keys AT THE CURRENT FRAME — all three right for a panel row, all three wrong for a draw-path verdict asking only "any key at all, anywhere in this slot". extra_animated_channels needs no change: its only registered source, features/parent_state/layers.py::owned_strip_channels, already filters if len(fc.keyframe_points).

    Three tests added to dev/tests/test_diff_state_states.py: a bare channel with no keyframes stays dark and lights up on the first key; deleting the last keyframe clears the mark while the channel survives; a target bound to a slotted action with no slot of its own is not keyed. 27 passed in test_diff_state_states.py, 0 failed. Write-up appended to doc/troubleshooting/diff_state_blind_to_non_object_animation.md. Cross-ref CHANGELOG_UNRELEASED.md Fixed 2.

    1. 🟢 Diff State outlines follow a shape that is being deformed, by a shape key or anything else. Two independent faults in features/diff_state/cache.py, both measured in Blender 5.2 before a line changed (probes kept at scratchpad/probe_shapekey_{1,2,3}.py).

    (a) The invalidation named an object that does not exist. _on_depsgraph read getattr(update.id, 'session_uid', None). DepsgraphUpdate.id is the EVALUATED copy, which is not in bpy.data and therefore answers session_uid == 0 — for every update, always. The store is keyed by the ORIGINAL object's uid, so every shape change in the session was recorded against uid 0 and no real object was ever rebuilt; the uid is not None guard passed 0 straight through, so _dirty filled with a number that matched nothing and looked like work. Probed on one scene: update.id.session_uid → 0, 0, 0; update.id.original.session_uid → 186, 187, 191 (Object / Mesh / Key). Never a shape-key problem — a plain vertices[0].co edit reported identically. The only reason a correct outline was ever seen is clear() firing on undo, cascade and file load. Fix: _update_uid(update) resolves through .original (an already-original ID returns itself), and invalidate() drops a FALSY uid — is not None is what let the bug live. A pure move still invalidates nothing because such an update carries is_updated_transform and not is_updated_geometry, so the local-space design is untouched; a named test pins that.

    (b) Playback never reached the handler. The store registered depsgraph_update_post + load_post. Probed: 20 × frame_set() fired frame_change_post 60 times and depsgraph_update_post 0 times, so an animated shape key deformed the mesh in silence. New @persistent _on_frame on frame_change_post marks the stored uids stale and rebuilds nothing (Constitution rule 2); registered/unregistered beside the other two and tracked as "Diff State Frame Watch" in the Process Monitor. Scoped to _geometry.keys() — a uid in the store is by definition an object the mode has drawn — never clear(), which would discard every static prop's outline on every frame.

    geometry() now REPLACES a stale entry instead of popping it first: while a rebuild is deferred the stored tuple is what keeps the outline on screen, and the dirty flag survives so the next affordable draw still rebuilds. The batch is popped only when a rebuild actually happens, or the GPU buffer and the vertex tuples would disagree.

    to_mesh() was verified to reflect the shape key before any of this (value 0.0 → max Z 1.0, 0.5 → 3.5, 1.0 → 6.0; animated, frame 10 → 3.30), so correcting the invalidation is sufficient and no extra evaluation is needed.

    TESTS. 12 in dev/tests/test_diff_state_scan_cache.py. The first three passed for the WRONG reason and had to be repaired: inside the suite addon_is_mutating reads True (read_homefile sets is_applying, nothing lowers it) and _on_depsgraph answers a raised flag with clear() + return, so the store was emptied wholesale and "not cached" was true regardless of what the handler did with the uid. Proven by reverting the fix in place — the tests still passed. _settle_mutation_flag() now lowers is_applying / is_undoing / is_redoing (addon_is_mutating is a computed property with NO setter) and asserts the lock is actually down. Re-verified after the repair: with the old invalidation restored, the shape-key and mesh-edit tests FAIL and the pure-move test passes; with the fix, all three pass. Note the suite loads the addon from the REPO path, not BLENDER_USER_EXTENSIONS — patching a copied extensions tree to test a change changes nothing. Write-up: doc/troubleshooting/diff_state_outline_keeps_the_old_shape.md. Cross-ref CHANGELOG_UNRELEASED.md Fixed 3.

    1. 🟢 New Diff State setting picks how eagerly an outline follows a deforming shape: Auto, Live or On Stop. Forced by measurement, not taste. One _extract() costs 0.1 ms at 8 verts, 13.7 ms at 1,538, 97.2 ms at 24,578 and 432.5 ms at 98,306; one frame at 60 fps is 16.7 ms. So "invalidate more" is unusable above roughly a thousand vertices and the refresh needs a policy.

    diff_state_shape_refresh (EnumProperty, default AUTO) + diff_state_shape_budget_ms (FloatProperty, default 8.0 — half a frame, leaving the other half to Blender's own drawing). LIVE always rebuilds; STOP never rebuilds while playing; AUTO decides PER OBJECT from _cost_ms[uid], the milliseconds that object's last real rebuild took, so a light prop keeps following in the same scene where a dense character holds its shape. _spent carries a running per-frame total keyed by frame number, so twenty cheap objects cannot add up to the stutter one expensive object was denied. An object with no measurement is built once — one slow frame beats never showing the true shape. Off the playback path every mode rebuilds at once: the question only exists while frames are flying past.

    _is_playing() scans EVERY window's screen.is_animation_playing, not context.screen — the draw handler's context is the area being drawn and playback can be driven from another window. A scrub is deliberately not playback. The decision lives in cache.py, not draw.py: draw.py reaches the store twice (geometry() at draw.py:606, triangle_count() at :577) and both must obey one gate. _policy() falls back to AUTO + 8.0 on any preferences failure rather than raising on a draw path.

    Wiring: DIFF_STATE_SHAPE_REFRESH_ITEMS + both properties in preferences/props/props_diff_state.py; expand_diff_state_performance in props_logging.py and in BOTH accordion groups in addon_prefs_constants.py; a Performance section in draw_interface.py (the budget row is drawn always but active = mode == 'AUTO', so it can be found and not mistaken for live); the pair indexed in prefs_search.py. UI text centralized in texts/tooltips_diff_state.py (labels + enum item descriptions) and texts/tooltips_preferences.py (the two property tooltips), parked in texts/locales/_pending.py — de_DE only once merged.

    EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 864 → 867 in preferences/__init__.py. Three new properties, and the addon REFUSES TO REGISTER until the number matches: the symptom is a register-time AssertionError reading "a mixin was likely added", surfacing as unrelated-looking test failures with no handlers installed. Cross-ref CHANGELOG_UNRELEASED.md Fixed 4.

    1. 🟢 Diff State marks and the process banner hide when the viewport's Show Overlays switch is off. Neither of the addon's two SpaceView3D.draw_handler_add callbacks ever read space.overlay.show_overlays. Grep for that attribute over takes_for_blender/ returned exactly two hits before this change, and both were WRITERS in capture paths, never a reader in a draw path: features/batch_render/batch_pipeline.py:311-312 and features/vl_preview/operators.py:240-241 each set it False around bpy.ops.render.opengl() and restore it after. So the addon switched overlays off for its own captures and then painted its own overlays over the result. View ▸ Viewport Render Image is the same switch from the user's side, and the viewport's own Rendered shading mode is where it is seen without rendering anything at all.

    The mode's panel is parented to VIEW3D_PT_overlay (features/diff_state/panel.py:52), so it already presents itself as one of Blender's overlays while ignoring that popover's master switch.

    Fix: new pure module utils/viewport.py::overlays_shown(space). It takes the space rather than reading bpy.context because the answer is PER VIEWPORT — two 3D views on one screen can disagree and a draw callback runs once per region — and it is deliberately bpy-free so it costs nothing at register time and is testable headless. It FAILS OPEN at every step (None space, no .overlay, a raising property → draw), matching diff_state.draw.visible_here() at draw.py:322-323: a mark drawn once too often beats a mode that silently draws nothing.

    Call sites. features/diff_state/draw.py::_draw asks it with the other early-outs, BEFORE gpu.state.blend_set/depth_test_set, so the finally block has nothing to restore on the hidden path; space is now read once at the top and carried down to visible_here(), replacing the second getattr(context, 'space_data', None) that used to sit mid-function. panels/process_overlay.py::_draw_callback asks it first of all, above collect_active() and build_lines(), so a hidden banner costs nothing per frame.

    Deliberately NOT gated on space.shading.type == 'RENDERED' (user ruling 2026-09-16): one switch, and Blender's own overlays stay visible in Rendered shading too. Deliberately no Takes-side preference — Blender's switch is the single source, and a second one would need a property, a prefs row, a de_DE re-key and a _SAVEABLE_PREFS entry for no user gain. No property, no registration and no EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT change.

    Not proven, and not claimed anywhere public: that these handlers ever reached a SAVED render.opengl() image. F12 never runs region draw callbacks, and the offscreen viewport draw loop is entered without a context while the Python POST_VIEW/POST_PIXEL callbacks are dispatched only when one is present. The certain symptom is in-viewport. If a saved image turns out to carry the marks, probe it with a call-recording POST_VIEW handler under a window/area/region override before asserting either way.

    Tests: dev/tests/test_overlay_visibility.py — six on the helper (on draws, off hides, and four fail-open paths) plus two source-scanning guards asserting both draw modules still reference overlays_shown, because a rewrite silently dropping the question is exactly how this got in. The two guards read the files as text: features/diff_state/draw.py imports bpy and gpu at module level and cannot be imported headless. 6. 🟢 Deleting an object's last key no longer stops it following the animation of its parent tier. Empty Action Unassign rule 1 in features/rest_state/revert_snap.py unbound the object through core/action_bind.clear_action, which also strips the owned TKS Parent N NLA tracks (by design — it is the sweep's door for a target that leaves the cascade). Nothing rebuilt them: the take is released (rule 2 → tier callback → sweep) only when it lost its keys EVERYWHERE, so with a second object still keyed in the same take the layers stayed gone and the inherited channels froze at their last value until the next view layer click. Field log 2026-09-14 15:01:49 (verify blend, Scene tier passes down): "layers cleared on Suzanne" with no reconcile line; healed three seconds later only because Cube's own Alt+I released the take. New action_bind.unbind_action nulls slot + action and leaves the layers; the revert uses it, clear_action calls it. Guard: dev/tests/test_revert_keeps_parent_layers.py. Full account: doc/troubleshooting/revert_last_key_strips_parent_layers.md. 7. 🟢 Deleting a last key that the parent tier also keys releases the emptied take like any other last key. The revert subtracted extra_animated_channels from the witnessed loss BEFORE deciding on rule 1, and gated both rule 1 (unbind) and rule 2 (tier release) on the reduced lost set — so a slot whose only key was on a parent-keyed channel read as "nothing lost": the empty take stayed bound to the object and named on the tier (the trap state). Now the witnessed loss (gone) drives the unbind and the release; the reduced set drives the snap alone. Same test file, second case. 8. 🟢 Clearing a key on a channel a parent tier also keys lands on that parent in one move instead of flicking through the rest value. Ordering inside _revert_unkeyed_to_rest_deferred: the snap ran first and Empty Action Unassign rule 2 last. Releasing the emptied take clears its tier, and a tier property re-resolves the cascade synchronously from its own update callback (panels/context/properties.py::_on_tks_action_update → apply_overrides), binding the tier above — so the rest value written in step 1 was replaced by the parent's own curve in step 4, two visible values for one gesture. The release (and the mirror suppression) now run before the snap loop, so _snap_one_target sees the newly bound parent action among the keyed sources and leaves its channels alone; channels nobody answers for still go to rest. No tier-value resolution was added — the revert only decides whether to write. Measured with dev/scripts/probe_parent_landing.py (rest 1.0 / parent 7.0 / take 2.0 on location[0], six Parent State variants). Guards: test_a_channel_the_parent_tier_keys_is_never_written_to_rest (asserts the WRITE COUNT — the settled value is right either way) and test_a_channel_no_parent_keys_still_lands_on_rest. Trap recorded in the troubleshooting doc: a tier write arms the snap-suppression window, so a test calling the revert straight after watches it abort and passes on broken code. 9. 🟢 Leaving a borrowed parent action no longer shows the Rest pose until the playhead moves. panels/inspector/handlers.py::_poll_slot_removal snaps a target to Rest when it sees ad.action go to None (the native template_ID "X" fires no depsgraph update). Ending a borrow makes the same transition for a different reason: the sweep unassigns the borrowed action and rebuilds the owned TKS Parent N strips, so the target keeps animating from the layers. The poll's exclusion set was the VL keyed cache alone, which lists what cascade ACTIONS key and knows nothing about NLA strips — so every layered channel looked unanimated and took the rest value. features/silence/operators.py already ends a borrow with scene.update_tag(refresh={'TIME'}) (the 2026-09-10 "I must scrub a little" fix), so the pose was restored correctly and then overwritten by the poll on its own timer, with nothing left to re-evaluate. Fixed by folding core/keyed_extra.extra_animated_channels into the poll's exclusion — the One Keyed Answer site list in that module's docstring named the inspector, but this poll never called it. Log fingerprint: a sweep line reading SNAP=0 followed by SLOT POLL: action cleared on Object::… snapping to ref. Guard: dev/tests/test_slot_poll_keeps_parent_layers.py (layered channel untouched + a control that still snaps when nothing animates it). Full account: doc/troubleshooting/slot_poll_snaps_over_parent_layers.md.

    1. 🟢 A parent layer whose action starts on a fractional frame no longer runs that fraction ahead of the parent. features/parent_state/layers.py::sync_layers created the owned strip with track.strips.new(action.name, int(fr[0]), action) — strips.new only takes a whole frame — and then set action_frame_start = fr[0] unrounded. For an action whose first key sits at 1.5 the strip began at 1 while its action frames began at 1.5. The strip maps its scene range onto its action range, so scene frame 1 showed action frame 1.5: the whole parent animation ran half a frame AHEAD of the curves it was built from, and its tail ended half a frame early under HOLD. Direction measured in factory Blender 5.2, 2026-09-17 (buggy vs fixed strip, same action: buggy leads by up to 0.88 of a 10-unit move at mid-ramp). _strip_matches compared only action_frame_start/end (±0.5) and never strip.frame_start, so the freshness check called the strip in place and no later sweep corrected it. Fix: strip.frame_start = fr[0] after the action frames are set (a float assignment moves the strip and keeps its length), and _strip_matches now rebuilds when strip.frame_start is off its action start by more than 1e-3. Found by the 2026-09-15 re-audit of the parent feature (doc/roadmap/_dev/rest-parent-state-followups.md). Test: dev/tests/test_parent_state_layers.py:: test_parent_strip_starts_where_its_action_starts_even_on_a_fraction. Record: doc/troubleshooting/parent_state_strip_subframe_offset.md. Verified on the tests at the user's explicit request (2026-09-17), not by hand: reproducing it needs a key on a fractional frame, which the interface only reaches through retiming or a typed value. Evidence: the test is red on main's file and green with the fix; the merged-main run of 2026-09-16 carried it (301 passed); the direction was measured in factory Blender 5.2.

    2. 🟢 A view layer switch that lands on the row borrowing a parent action no longer ends the borrow. Two doors end a borrow. The tree click calls parent_borrow/state.py::end_if_row_changed (row comparison, stands down while TKS_VL_STATE.is_undoing/is_redoing or a batch render). The VL_SWITCH_POST_CASCADE subscriber parent_borrow/__init__.py:: _on_vl_switch_post — the door for the native view layer dropdown, a script setting window.view_layer and sequencer follow — still called state.clear() unconditionally, a leftover of the WindowManager-note design. A switch landing on the borrowing row ended the borrow for nothing, and a clear inside an undo replay would have edited the step just restored (the detector guards undo today, so that half was latent). Fix: the subscriber reads scene.name / view_layer.name from the event and calls end_if_row_changed, refreshing the tree only when a borrow actually ended. Found by the 2026-09-16 re-audit (doc/roadmap/_dev/rest-parent-state-followups.md). Tests: four new in dev/tests/test_borrow_toggle_in_undo.py (own row keeps, other row ends, undo stands down, both doors share the rule). Record: doc/troubleshooting/parent_borrow_two_end_doors.md. Verified on the tests at the user's explicit request (2026-09-17), not by hand: no click reaches the blunt door today — the tree click already carried the row rule — so this is a guard for every other switch path and for an undo replay. Evidence: 3 of the 4 new tests are red on main and green with the fix; the merged-main run of 2026-09-16 carried them (301 passed).

    3. 🟢 Saving a file opened from an older add-on version clears its Cache Version Mismatch warning. core/cache_version.py stamps every scene with ADDON_VERSION from a save_pre handler (_stamp_on_save), so the instant a save lands the .blend is version-coherent and the next load will not warn. Nothing recomputed the two WindowManager flags that drive the banner (tks_cache_stale, tks_cache_stale_from) — they were set once at load_post / register() and only ever cleared by restamp_active_scene() from tks.rebuild_cache. A session therefore kept a red badge over a file that was already current, and the only way out was the Rebuild Cache button, which disables and re-enables the whole add-on. Fix: new @persistent _check_on_save on save_post calling _refresh_flags(), plus signal_redraw() (Constitution rule 3 — never area.tag_redraw() direct) so the N-panel repaints instead of holding the old paint until a mouse move. save_post and not save_pre deliberately: save_pre would read the stamp the same tick it is written and clear the flag even for a save that then fails. signal_redraw is imported inside the handler body under except ImportError — core takes no module-scope utils.process_monitor import, and the handler can fire mid-teardown. Registered with the Process Monitor as "Cache Version Refresh" alongside the two existing entries and removed in unregister() before the load_post one. Constitution rule 2 does not apply: WindowManager props sit outside the undo stack, this is not a depsgraph/frame handler, and the sibling load_post handler already makes the same write. Tests: dev/tests/test_cache_version_banner.py — the save pair clears, save_post alone does not (pins the ordering against anyone moving it to save_pre), both handlers are registered, and a view-layer switch does NOT clear the banner. That last one guards the original question this came from: only load, register, save and Rebuild Cache may move the flags, because a banner that vanishes on a take switch leaves the user working the old cache believing it was dealt with. Card: doc/roadmap/active/cache-warning-persistence.md.

    4. 🟢 Rebuild Cache drops generated names and the cached preset list, which it used to leave behind. Found by measurement rather than by reading: dev/tests/test_rebuild_cache_reaches_everything.py clears, warms every draw path reachable headlessly, and clears again, then asks whether each module-level cache came back to where the first clear left it. Two did not. core/naming_utils._NAME_CACHE is keyed on (template_key, separator, tokens) and has had reset_label_cache() since it was written, wired only to the naming-template preference update= callbacks - so a file an older version shaped kept its generated names through a rebuild and the next cascade served them back out. features/render_presets/serialization/crud._LIST_CACHE is the third preset cache (after utils.preset_cache and the preset engine, both already cleared) and is not on cache_registry either; its 1.5 s TTL means it heals on its own, and it is cleared anyway because a rebuild should be finished when the button returns. Both now run in _clear_in_memory_caches. NOT cleared, deliberately: naming_utils._EFFECTIVE_TEMPLATE_CACHE, which stores (raw_template, effective_template) and compares the raw string on every read, so a stale entry can never be served - it is in the test's _EXEMPT map carrying that reason, rather than cleared to make a count go green. The check also treats a raised dirty/force flag as invalidation: the warning-bar cells keep their payload and gate it behind the flag (panels/navigation/panel.py:476), and a first draft that demanded an empty payload produced 16 false positives. The baseline is a clear rather than an add-on reload for a measured reason - cycling the add-on mid-suite re-enables it under the bare takes_for_blender name instead of bl_ext.user_default.takes_for_blender, and an earlier draft that did so broke test_render_version_lock and test_render_version_notes two files later, both green again the moment this file was deselected. Why it matters beyond the button: this is what lets the stage-2 add-on disable/enable eventually go, which is the question doc/roadmap/ideas/cache-rebuild-automation.md hangs on - a cache flush on file open is safe to do unasked, a teardown from a load handler is not. Gate: 4662 passed, 13 skipped, 1 xfailed, 0 failed (full run; the spike file under dev/experiments/ is unattributable and forces one). Card: doc/roadmap/active/rebuild-cache-completeness.md.

    5. 🟢 Shift+RMB on an inspector row opens that list's own menu. TKS_OT_TreeContextMenu._menu_for picks a menu with self._MENU_OF.get(key) and, on None, returns self.MENU — the takes tree menu. _MENU_OF (takes_for_blender/operators/context/ops_tree_context_menu.py:123) held two entries, TAGS and VARIANTS. The three inspector lists were absent, so INSPECTOR_OBJECTS, INSPECTOR_ACTIONS and INSPECTOR_SLOTS all fell through and the reader got the tree's menu, header and all. Added the three missing entries pointing at TKS_MT_watchlist_row_menu, TKS_MT_inspector_action_row_menu and TKS_MT_inspector_slot_row_menu (panels/context/tree_context_menu.py:644-690), all three of which already existed, registered correctly and declared the matching LIST_KEY. The fall-through itself is kept: it is correct for the CONTEXT family, where the tree and its five SPLIT_* views share one menu deliberately. Why no existing guard saw it: each menu has a SECOND door — the watchlist's is a column button at panels/inspector/inspector_sections.py:162 — so the classes are registered, referenced and live, and every reachability, orphan and registration check passes. The defect was a missing key in a dict, which is only a defect because a class in another file declares that key and expects to be routed by it. Guards: test_every_list_menu_is_reachable_by_its_own_key asserts every menu declaring a LIST_KEY outside the CONTEXT family appears in _MENU_OF, and test_menu_of_names_only_real_menus refuses an entry pointing at a menu that no longer exists — both pure source tests in dev/tests/test_list_row_menu.py, RED before the fix with all three names in the failure message. The general auditor rule, so this shape is caught in any add-on rather than by a user noticing the wrong menu, is carded at doc/roadmap/ideas/menu-reachable-by-its-key.md (compare CORR-08, the same exhaustiveness idea one layer down). Reported by the user 2026-09-18. Impact-selected suite: 1339 passed, 8 skipped (1347/4692 selected).

    6. 🟢 Each split view's row menu offers only what its own rows can do. Two faults, one cause. _MENU_OF (operators/context/ops_tree_context_menu.py:123) routed nothing for the five SPLIT_* keys, so Shift+RMB in any split view opened TKS_MT_tree_context_menu. That menu resolves its row with _active_item("CONTEXT"), which reads tks_all_viewlayers and tks_all_viewlayers_index — the TREE's list, which a split view does not draw — so the header could name a row the reader never clicked. And _row_actions fell to _context_row_actions, the tree's hand-written set, so every split list offered all eight entries. Six of those can never fire for their row type: Group on either group list (can_group accepts only SCENE/VL — user ruling 2026-09-18, "grouping a group makes no sense"), and Retarget, Group and Ungroup on Takes. They greyed themselves, which is not good enough: a greyed entry still tells the reader the action belongs to that list. The five menus already existed with the right LIST_KEY (panels/context/tree_context_menu.py:589-630) and were reachable only from their column buttons in panels/context/draw_split.py — the same half-wired shape as Fixed 14, found by sweeping the registry after that fix. Added the five _MENU_OF entries and five _FAMILY_ENTRIES rows built from the operators' own polls: TKS_OT_DuplicateTreeItem.poll (SCENE, VL, TAKE), TKS_OT_RetargetTreeItem._typed_op (SCENE, VL, SCENE_GROUP, VL_GROUP — the last two as merge), groups.ops_manage.can_group (SCENE, VL) and _in_a_real_group, which does let a group header disband itself, so Ungroup stays on both group lists. Copy/Paste collection visibility is view-layer only. Table entries gained an optional third element ({"text":…, "props":…}) so the Duplicate PAIR can live in the table — the thing a two-element table could not express, and the original reason the split views borrowed the tree's set. _draw_entry replaces the inline loops in _table_actions. Because a setattr onto a property an operator does not have is silent and kills the rest of the panel, test_table_only_sets_properties_the_operator_has reads every props name and checks it against that operator's declared annotations. Guards: three more pure tests in dev/tests/test_list_row_menu.py — test_every_split_view_has_its_own_entries, test_no_split_view_offers_what_its_rows_cannot_do (the six forbidden pairs) and test_split_views_keep_what_their_rows_can_do (the mirror, so trimming cannot take a working action away). The reachability test from Fixed 14 was tightened at the same time: only the literal CONTEXT key may fall through now, not the whole CONTEXT family. Two existing shape guards were re-pointed, not relaxed — _table_actions now unpacks entry rather than idname, icon, so they grep the new wording for the same invariant.

    7. 🟢 Diff State no longer calls every animated object inherited in a file that assigns no actions to any tier. features/diff_state/states.py::_target_keyed_source classified a bound action with one test — OWN if name in own_names else ABOVE — which reads absence as evidence. With no tier assigning anything, own_names is empty, so every action failed it: measured on dev/scripts/build_diff_state_kinds_blend.py, 25 marked objects and 25 of them pink, none blue. The same fault hit a stray hand-bound action beside a real chain. Fix: _row_action_names(scene, view_layer) returns TWO sets built from core.cascade.cascade_levels (the same six-tier walk the cascade uses, so they cannot drift) — own for the tiers at or below the row plus the Rest action, above for the tiers above it — and ABOVE is now claimed only for a name a tier above really holds, or for parent layers on the object, which nothing but a parent tier builds. Anything in neither set is the user's own. Re-probed on the catalogue: 25 marked, 0 above, 25 own. Tests: two corrected, four added (test_diff_state_states.py), 247 passed across the Diff State files. Record: doc/troubleshooting/diff_state_pink_without_a_parent.md.

    8. 🟢 The Diff State empty mark no longer grows or shrinks with an object's scale. features/diff_state/draw.py::empty_extent sized the mark from obj.dimensions — the bound box with the object's scale ALREADY applied — and the points were then drawn under gpu.matrix.multiply_matrix(obj.matrix_world), which applies scale a second time. Measured in factory 5.2 on a 2 m cube (dev/scripts/probe_diff_state_sizing.py): the mark drew at 0.062 against a box of 0.250 at scale 0.25, and at 9.000 against 3.000 at scale 3 — out by exactly the scale factor, in both directions, with only an unscaled object agreeing. That is why every hand test passed. It now reads obj.bound_box, which is local, the way box_matrix already did and says so in its own docstring.

    9. 🟢 Lights, speakers and light probes get a box sized against the view. display_size(obj) preferred obj.data.display_size and fell back to obj.empty_display_size. A camera has the first and an Empty's is its real size, but EVERY object carries empty_display_size and on anything else it never leaves its 1.0 default — so a light, a speaker and a light probe all boxed at a flat half-extent of 1.0 whatever the scene (measured, same probe). No honest world size exists for them: a sun's angle is not a size and an area light's size is the emitter, not the gizmo. So display_size answers None for them, and box_matrix(obj, view) falls to a new view_extent() that asks the same question marker_matrix already asks — eye distance in a perspective view, zoom in an orthographic one — through logic.marker_size. They KEEP the box: swapping the mark the user switched on for a different one would be a setting quietly ignored. First attempt did exactly that (returned None and fell through to the marker) and was rejected for it. Tests: 6 added (test_diff_state_states.py), 253 passed across the Diff State files, impact gate 1529 passed. The three existing box-scale tests are untouched and still green. Record: doc/troubleshooting/diff_state_marks_measured_the_object_twice.md.

    10. 🟢 The debug log always lands in the shared Blender profile's log folder, even when Blender runs on a redirected profile. utils/logger.get_log_dir() ended on bpy.utils.user_resource('SCRIPTS', ...), which resolves against the profile Blender was STARTED with. The Worktree Launcher (blender-dev-launcher/launcher/worktree_launcher.pyw, L756) sets BLENDER_USER_RESOURCES to .sandboxes/profiles/<repo>--<worktree>/, so every worktree session wrote its log inside its own sandbox. Nobody looks there: on 2026-09-18 an agent asked to read "the log" checked %APPDATA%/Blender Foundation/Blender/5.2/scripts/presets/takes_for_blender/logs, found nothing and reported no trace — a full round trip lost. The FILENAME half already solved the mixing problem (utils/log_source tags a worktree run with its worktree name), so one folder can hold every session; only the directory was wrong. Fix: two new private helpers in logger.py sit BETWEEN the debug_log_path preference and the user_resource fallback, so the documented precedence is unchanged. _default_profile_root() builds the un-overridden user profile path per platform (%APPDATA%/Blender Foundation/Blender/<ver> on Windows, ~/Library/Application Support/Blender/<ver> on macOS, $XDG_CONFIG_HOME|~/.config/blender/<ver> elsewhere), reading the version off bpy.app.version rather than hard-coding it, and returns None when the base folder is missing. _shared_profile_log_dir() returns None — meaning "keep the profile's own answer" — unless one of BLENDER_USER_RESOURCES, BLENDER_USER_SCRIPTS or BLENDER_USER_CONFIG is actually set. That gate is deliberate: an ordinary install and a portable Blender never set one, so they are byte-for-byte unaffected, and the sandbox path can only ever arise WITH one. TKS_TEST_CONFIG_DIR still wins over everything, which is the regression that would have mattered most (see the _test_log_dir and _log_destination_key docstrings for the flake it caused once) and is asserted rather than trusted. _log_destination_key() is unchanged: the new answer depends only on env vars and bpy.app.version, none of which move while Blender runs. resolve_source_suffix and the filename are untouched. Guard: dev/tests/test_log_dir_shared_profile.py, 8 tests — the sandbox folder does NOT get the log, the shared folder does, no override means no change, the shared root is the machine's real one, TKS_TEST_CONFIG_DIR beats it, an explicit debug_log_path beats it, the worktree suffix survives, and folder and suffix meet in one path.

    11. 🟢 Opening a file whose take resolves no action no longer strips it. _deferred_load_apply resolved the cascade action and handed it to apply_vl_switch_unified whatever it was, including None. The sweep's STEP 1 clears every target whose action is not the target action, so a None target walked the scene and unbound all of it - the state every file the add-on has never seen is in. Measured on a first-contact .blend built by dev/scripts/build_heavy_repro.py: sixty objects wearing their own actions and slots across twelve view layers went in and none came out bound; with the guard, sixty do. Both sibling paths already refused this - the undo re-fire returns before the sweep when nothing resolves (vl_lifecycle_undo.py), and cascade_apply clears only when it has applied something to that scene before. Its memo is no help here: _last_applied_action is module-level session state and is empty right after a load. The guard wraps the CALL, not the function, so the variant cascade, the READY status, the inspector invalidate, the preload kick and the is_applying release in the finally all still run. Guards: dev/tests/test_first_open_keeps_actions.py, plus dev/scripts/probe_heavy_repro.py for the end-to-end measurement. Card: doc/roadmap/ideas/first-open-strips-actions.md.

    12. 🟢 Drift now shows at any frame, so moving an object a second time after autokey keyed it is seen again. features/rest_state/drift_scan.py compared a KEYED channel against fc.evaluate(0) - its own key at frame 0 - which is the expected value on frame 0 and nowhere else. Off it the scan had to skip keyed channels outright (if is_keyed and not _keyed_check: continue) rather than report every animated object as drifted. The guard was right; the reference under it was not. Field report: first nudge shows drift (channel still unkeyed, rest is a flat frame-0 hold and valid anywhere), autokey keys it, second nudge reports nothing. _take_keyed_value takes a frame and evaluates there; get_rest_drifts passes the playhead, and _keyed_check is deleted because the reading now holds at every frame. snap_single_to_rest follows the same reference through a new _playhead(context), so a snap lands on the curve where you are standing instead of the frame-0 key - a teleport that was unreachable before only because drift was never reported off frame 0. diff_state.logic.drift_reading_valid answers True always now, kept and kept called for the Overlays honesty line. Tests: 2 added (test_diff_state_states.py - the reported three steps end to end, and the snap destination), 2 rewritten (test_diff_state_logic.py - they pinned the old rule). 560 passed across Diff State and Rest State, impact gate 1876 passed. Record: doc/troubleshooting/drift_only_read_at_frame_zero.md.

    13. 🟢 Clear Add-on Data and the property scan reach every ID type, not the twenty-three somebody wrote down. CORR-30, the fifth hand-written ID list in this codebase. preferences/cleanup_ops.py carried FOUR identical copies of a 23-entry data_collections literal - in TKS_OT_ClearAllCustomProperties.execute, _clear_properties_by_matcher, get_all_unique_property_keys and TKS_OT_ClearAddonData._count_addon_properties. Blender 5.2 has 39. The sixteen missing - annotations, brushes, cache_files, hair_curves, libraries, lightprobes, linestyles, masks, movieclips, paint_curves, palettes, pointclouds, screens, sounds, window_managers, workspaces - were invisible to all four: a tks_* key on any of them was never counted, never listed by the scan and never cleared. New utils/id_collections.py asks bpy.data.bl_rna.properties instead, the same mechanism as core/anim_utils.iter_animdata_holders, and all four walks become for _coll_name, collection in iter_id_collections(). Near-miss worth keeping: bpy.data declares FORTY collection properties, and the fortieth is all_ids - every datablock in the file again. Walking it counted every key twice and made skip a lie, since a skipped collection walked back in through the aggregate. A test caught it before the commit. The guard is generic rather than a name check: an aggregate's fixed_type is the ID base class, a real collection's is its own, which leaves exactly the 39 the auditor counts. Guards: dev/tests/test_id_collections.py (12 tests), of which test_no_module_hand_writes_a_list_of_bpy_data_collections is an AST contract over the whole package - three or more bpy.data.<x> in one literal fails it, so the sixth copy cannot land. Doc: doc/troubleshooting/hand_written_id_collection_lists.md.

    14. 🟢 Assigning an action to a Volume, Metaball, Grease Pencil or Point Cloud no longer reports "not found". Same rule, second site. operators/inspector/ops_action_assign.py::_resolve_target answered the DATA/MESH/CAMERA/LIGHT/ARMATURE types out of a six-collection tuple (meshes, cameras, lights, armatures, curves, lattices), so every other object-data type fell through to None and execute reported Target '{name}' ({type}) not found. The branch is now find_id_by_name(name, skip=('objects', 'scenes', 'worlds', 'materials', 'node_groups')) - the five the branches above already answered, skipped so a mesh sharing a scene's name cannot win here. Names are unique only WITHIN a collection, so a typeless lookup can still pick the wrong one of two same-named blocks; that is the price of the resolver having a name and a free-form target_type: StringProperty(), and it is strictly better than the old answer of None for every type nobody listed.

    15. 🟢 The adoption card's save handler joins the Process Monitor. REG-06, found on the 2026-09-19 rescan - registered 46, unregistered 1. core/take_mode_adopt._stand_down_on_save is appended to bpy.app.handlers.save_post in register() and never announced, so it was invisible to the perf audit and the debug viewer - the two places somebody looks when a save feels slow. Registered as "Adoption Card Stand-Down" (HANDLER / CORE, feature_group="core") with the matching unregister_process, both in the try: ... except ImportError: pass the sibling handlers in cache_version.py and camera_native_sync.py already use.

      Two internal cleanups ride with it, both from the same merge and neither visible to a reader:

      • CORR-07. TKS_OT_AdoptedPrompt and TKS_OT_AdoptedObjectToTake were the two adoption operators left without a poll(). Both dereference context.scene / context.view_layer / the window manager exactly like their four siblings, so both join _AdoptedCardOp. All six adoption operators now share one gate.
      • MAINT-09.
