Five unused imports: MODE_ICON in operators/inspector/ops_adopted.py, a bare import bpy in panels/navigation/warnings/adopted_list.py (which imports what it needs from bpy.types / bpy.props directly), and the whole ALL_TAKES, MODES, MODE_ICON line in panels/navigation/warnings/adopted_objects.py.

    16. 🟢 Two Multi-Cam clearers were a dialog a script walks past. AI-05. Blender routes a confirm dialog straight back into execute(), so invoke_confirm protects a click and nothing else: bpy.ops.tks.multicam_clear_cuts() and tks.multicam_clear_orphans() from an MCP-bridge timer wiped the take's cut list and deleted every orphan marker with nothing in the way. Both now carry the two-state shape from utils/confirm_gate.py: confirm: BoolProperty(default=False, options={'SKIP_SAVE'}), self.confirm = True at the TOP of invoke() (before any branch, so the preference-off path still passes), and if not self.confirm: report(confirm_required(self)); CANCELLED as the first statement of execute(). SKIP_SAVE is load-bearing - without it Blender remembers the last value and the second scripted call inherits the first one's True.

      TKS_OT_MultiCamCutAdd was the rule's third hit and is NOT gated: it adds, it never removes, its confirm is a heads-up about where the marker lands when the frame is taken, and it is skipped entirely when the preference is off. A gate there would refuse every scripted caller for a notice. Waived in the class body with # AI-05-OK: and a reason.

      Tests: +3 in test_multicam_markers.py - the gate's five parts, that the refusal is the FIRST statement of execute() (a gate under the work is not a gate), and that the waiver exists and gives a reason. test_confirm_gate_internal_calls.py already polices the other side and stays green, so no in-addon caller hits its own new gate.

    17. 🟢 tks.msw_remove_slot could only reach the highlighted row. AI-03. _target() read _selected_entry(context) - the row the Swap List happens to be sitting on - so a script could say WHICH SLOT via slot_index but never WHICH OBJECT, and had to arrange the selection first. New entry_name: StringProperty(options={'HIDDEN'}) and a _named_entry() lookup; empty keeps the highlighted row, which is what a click means. Same shape _OrphanTarget already uses for the warning-panel buttons.

      The rule's other two hits, tks.msw_settle_orphan and tks.msw_settle_slot, are NOT changed - they already carry their whole address (scene_name / vl_name / object_name / index, and scene_name / object_name / slot), and action plus slot_index are the dialog's only fields, so a scripted call reaches execute() with nothing left to ask. Both carry # AI-03-OK: in the class body saying so. Worth a look in the auditor: props_dialog is already in _ROUTING_INVOKERS, so these two should have landed in the rule's conditional bucket rather than unreachable.

    18. 🟢 A log gate named a topic that was renamed away. INFO-14. utils/logger.py builds its gate's attribute name from the call's own arguments - f"log_topic_{topic.lower()}" - and reads it with a default of True. The default has to stay: a logger that goes quiet because a name was mistyped loses the output somebody is reading. But a name nobody declared then FAILS OPEN - the line logs whatever the switches say, no switch in Preferences can silence it, and nothing warns.

      Commit 269e6dcf renamed the topics ("name log topics after the symptom, not the folder") and features/material_swap/paint.py was left on the retired FEATURES / msw pair. Its neighbour in the same feature, common.py, was already on VARIANT / swap - the pair whose preference is literally named "Material Swap". Moved. A census of every call site builds 70 names against 68 declared preferences, and the two missing were both this one line.

      New dev/tests/test_log_topic_names_exist.py (4) is the part that lasts: it reads every tks_log / tks_log_active call, builds every name it can build, and demands a matching BoolProperty. Verified by reintroducing the defect - it failed and named the file and line. It also pins tks_log's own default topic (the loudest version of this bug: every call that names no topic goes ungateable at once) and pins the positional-argument map, because the two functions put topic in different places -

      tks_log(msg, level='INFO', topic='CORE', subtopic=None, force=False)
tks_log_active(topic='CORE', subtopic=None)
      • and a first pass of the census read tks_log_active("REST", "state") as having no topic at all, inventing 35 phantom findings.

      All twelve gates the rule lists carry # INFO-14-OK: with a reason. Each fails open in the safe direction: the logger stays loud, a missing confirm preference ASKS, a missing visibility flag SHOWS, a missing expand flag WALKS the rows.

      Found while gating this, diagnosed after, and not caused by it: a full suite run dies partway - no failure, no message, no Windows error report, no Blender crash file - whenever a SECOND Blender is running. Traced to cross-session interference, not to the suite and not to worktrees: this checkout is shared by several agent sessions, and the guarded run that proved it logged INTRUDER pid=24292 appeared at 21:11:30 and died at 8%. Runs on a quiet machine pass - 4862 passed, three times over, in the same worktree that had just crashed.

      Two wrong turns are recorded because each cost an hour. The first baseline ran from the main CHECKOUT while the branch ran from a worktree, which is not a comparison and sent the hunt after worktrees. The second was an instrumented harness whose while (-not $p.HasExited) never waited, so it stacked four runs on top of each other and produced the very interference it was measuring.

      TKS_TEST_CONFIG_DIR isolates the addon's own prefs and log, but not Blender's userpref.blend, which every run inherits and which the addon autosaves into on a preference change. That is the leading mechanism; BLENDER_USER_CONFIG per run would test it. Until then the rule is operational: check Get-Process blender before a full run.

      Also checked and NOT a defect: REG-09's three "unresolved" handlers. features/sync/_on_file_load and _on_depsgraph_update both carry @bpy.app.handlers.persistent on their definitions in handlers_viewport.py; the rule could not follow the hv. alias across the module boundary. utils/state.py:67 re-appends handlers it removed earlier, which keep whatever decorator they already had. The rule reports missing: 0, so it is honest about not knowing - nothing to fix here, and the same cross-module resolution would close it. 28. 🟢 Two of the four Diff State states had settings nobody could open. Diff State grew from two states to four (Take, Parent, Rest, Drift) and the state table generates a complete set of preferences per state - the marks table, the look, the empty style and size, ~113 properties apiece. preferences/draw_interface.py was never taught about the new pair: its loop still read (("keyed", ...), ("drift", ...)), so Parent State and Rest State had every setting saved, read and obeyed by the overlay, and no row anywhere to change them.

      The page now runs the same _draw_diff_state_block once per state, in the state table's own order. Two new fold switches (expand_diff_state_parent, expand_diff_state_rest) join ACCORDION_GROUPS and ACCORDION_NESTED beside their siblings, so Ctrl+Click on the Diff State topic still takes every state along and Shift+Click still folds the states against each other rather than against the topics above. EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 1095 -> 1097.

      This is the SHORT road, chosen knowingly (user ruling 2026-09-20): four full folds make the settings reachable today at the cost of a ~105-row page. The one-screen page - a tab per state, the look behind a pencil popover grouped by the mark it paints - stays its own card, doc/roadmap/ideas/diff-state-prefs-on-one-screen.md. 29. 🟢 The first-contact dialog drew no text at all. Its only explanation went through styles.wrapped_info_box(..., kind='warning'), and that kind returns None BEFORE layout.box() when the global show_warning_details preference is off. The reporter's was off (read from their prefs: show_warning_details = False, show_tip_boxes = False). Recorded draw output was exactly two calls - separator and prop(answer, expand=True) - so the dialog opened with a title, two bare answers and no question. Changed to kind='status', the never-gated kind, which is what this actually is: live state the reader needs for the choice in front of them. A dialog that opens UNASKED, once, to someone meeting the add-on for the first time must not be silenceable by a preference they set months ago for something else. Ruled out along the way, recorded so nobody re-chases them: the answer enum registers fine and its labels are non-empty ('Keep them all, nothing changes' / 'Let me decide, object by object') - an earlier reading of cls.bl_rna.properties said otherwise, but operator properties do not live there and a minimal throwaway operator reads the same way; the UI language is en_US with use_translate_interface off; and _pending.py is a test baseline, never fed to bpy.app.translations. takes_for_blender/operators/inspector/ops_adopted.py. FOLLOW-UP, same report: with the box drawing, two more faults showed. context.region is None inside invoke_props_dialog, so draw_wrapped_paragraph fell back to its 240px guess and wrapped a 460px dialog into a 13-character column - width_px added to it and to wrapped_info_box, and the operator names its own width once (_DIALOG_WIDTH) for both the popup and the wrap. And prop(answer, expand=True) drew two squat unlabelled bars although the RNA reports correct item names, so each answer is now drawn explicitly with prop_enum(..., text=...) at scale_y = 1.4, reading the labels back off the REGISTERED property. They stay INLINE in items=[...]: lifting them into a module tuple made all four invisible to i18n_extract and test_pending_baseline_has_no_dead_entries caught it - regenerating the baseline would have passed the test by dropping the strings from the catalogue for good. SECOND FOLLOW-UP: "Let me decide" did not open the sidebar or switch to the Takes tab. _open_the_panel is correct - measured from a shut sidebar on the View tab, one call, open on Takes - but it ran INLINE in execute, which fires while Blender is tearing the popup down, on the very screen it is being asked to rearrange. The sidebar work is now _reveal_takes_sidebar, deferred onto a one-shot timer_safety.safe_register at 0.05s, reading windows off bpy.data.window_managers[0] so the timer body borrows no context. Falls back to an inline call if no timer can be had. Also repaired a Constitution rule 3 breach I introduced here: the helper called area.tag_redraw() directly instead of signal_redraw(). THIRD FOLLOW-UP: the two answers read as BUTTONS, so a reader expects clicking one to act - it only selects, and OK confirms. Each row is flat now (row.emboss = 'NONE'; prop_enum takes no emboss argument, so it goes on the parent) with a RADIOBUT_ON / RADIOBUT_OFF glyph driven off self.answer. RADIOBUT and not CHECKBOX although the report said checkbox: the two answers are mutually exclusive and a checkbox invites ticking both. FOURTH FOLLOW-UP: the paragraph still filled only ~60% of the box, the answers sat centred, and the popup was too wide. width_px was read as REAL PIXELS, but a popup only knows the UI UNITS it handed invoke_props_dialog, and blf measures in real pixels - so on a scaled UI the budget came out ui_scale times too small. Measured at the reporter's scale (1.5): popup 460 units = 690px with a 420px text budget, 61% filled. The helper multiplies width_px by ui_scale now (the region.width branch already is real pixels and must NOT be scaled), the popup drops to 320 units, and the budget is 290 units = 435px of 480px, 91% filled. Adding one verification probe turned an impact-selected run (1454 tests, ~3 min) into a full scan (4870, ~6:20): anything outside the addon package, the test tree and INERT_PREFIXES is “not attributable to any test” and widens the run to everything. Right for an unknown file, wrong for dev/scripts/, which is mostly probes nothing under dev/tests/ has heard of. A BLANKET inert rule would have been wrong the other way, and that is the part that needed care: test_changelog_split imports the guard out of release_cut.py and is NOT in always_run, so marking the directory inert would let a real break through. So _is_unreferenced_script asks per FILE - if no collected test file contains the script's stem, no test can import, exec or read it. Measured: release_cut.py and blender_crash_audit.py still force one, today's probes do not.     19. 🟢 Split-view list rows left dead air between the icon strip and the row's right edge. row_main had exactly two children and NEITHER could absorb the row's surplus width: left carried alignment = 'LEFT', which makes a layout shrink-wrap rather than stretch, and right carried an absolute ui_units_x = right_side_width(...) reserve. The name prop lived inside left, so it shrank with it; every pixel the row had over that total simply stayed behind the strip. It is width-proportional, which is why it read as a small margin in a narrow sidebar and a hole in a wide one - measured on a real 5.2 session with the reader's own prefs (collapse NEVER, all nine columns shown): 51px of dead air at an 800px sidebar, 12px after the fix, 12px being the ordinary button padding. Fix: the name prop moves into name_row = row_main.row(align=True), a child of row_main between left and right, making it the row's ONE flexible child - the shape the 2026-09-11 comment already claimed ("the NAME is the only thing that should grow") but did not have. Second pass: with the name gone, left is empty on every row that is not in multi-select, and an empty row still costs its own padding - it indented every name by a unit. So the four tick-only lists now BUILD left inside the if wm.tks_multiselect_list == ... branch; TKS_UL_SplitTakes keeps it unconditionally because its ordinal label lives there. Files: panels/context/lists_split.py (SplitSceneGroups, SplitVLGroups, SplitTakes), panels/context/lists_context.py (ContextScenes, ContextViewLayers). The tree drawers carry the same shape and are NOT touched here - see doc/troubleshooting/split_view_icon_strip_dead_air.md. Cross-ref CHANGELOG_UNRELEASED.md Fixed 35.

    20. 🟢 The Variants tree left a hole between its last row icon and the row's edge. Not the same bug as Fixed 35, though it looks identical: the variant rows already have a flexible child (name_cell asks NAME_ASK_UNITS = 100.0, which keeps the row over-subscribed so the two-unit cells above are never the ones Blender scales), and moving that cell onto row_main changed the gap by 0px - measured, then reverted. The hole is INSIDE the last cell: right_cell pins a cell at ICON_CELL_UNITS = 1.5 while the icon button it holds is about a unit, and the glyph sits at the cell's left. Between icons that spare width IS the even spacing; after the last icon it is a gap against the row's edge. Fix: right_cell(..., flush=True) sets alignment = 'RIGHT' on that one cell, and the four row renderers pass it on their final cell - _draw_product (collection), _draw_state (tag), _draw_part and _draw_material (collection). Measured at an 800px sidebar: product 30px -> 10px, state 35 -> 14, part 30 -> 10, with every other column unmoved. dev/tests/test_vsw_right_cluster.py kept the two-unit rule and gained the new half: a right-aligned cell anywhere but last is still a cluster and still refused, the last one must be right-aligned, right_cell(flush=True) is checked in isolation, and each renderer's source must carry exactly one flush=True, on its last right_cell. 139 vsw tests pass. Files: features/variant_switch/ui_helpers.py, features/variant_switch/ui_row_renderers.py. Cross-ref CHANGELOG_UNRELEASED.md Fixed 36.

The twin of first-open-strips-actions, one domain over. World and Camera read a WITNESS first (_last_cascade_*.get(scene.session_uid) - native differs from the last applied value = user intent); the compositor wrote its tracker but never read it. Both arms now do: the no-winner arm adopts a witnessed native onto the configured tier (Scene by default) or follows the tree when the scene holds exactly the last applied value; the winner arm lands a witnessed hand-pick on the most specific of (winner tier, adopt tier), with the Comp.001 duplicate-suffix echo falling through. Third row in _ADOPT_KINDS, _last_cascade_compositor_source beside its siblings, _compositor_reconcile_guard() on the three callbacks that re-entered apply_overrides unguarded. doc/troubleshooting/compositor_cleared_on_first_open.md. Now an elif clears the WindowManager name when the file has none; the saved-name-restored-even-if-gone contract is untouched and guarded. dev/tests/test_rest_action_restore_clears.py (3), doc/troubleshooting/rest_action_name_leaks_across_files.md. Branch fix/rest-action-leaks-across-files.
    24. 🟢 The camera pass cleared a marker-bound camera on first open. core/cascade_apply.py, no-winner arm: "not witnessed" has two causes - the tree lost a camera the cascade applied (scene.camera.name == _prev_applied_cam), or the native camera is the one a timeline marker governs (_marker_bound_camera, correctly never a pick) - and one else: served both. On a file the cascade had never touched the marker case hit the clear: scene.camera = None, ledger None; Blender's marker rebinding restored the camera at the next frame evaluation, so the viewport looked right while no tier held it and the drift row read "expected None, actual CAM-01" on every rebind. From the user's log (four-camera shot, 2026-09-20): DRIFT Camera exp_name='None' act_name='None' at 21:02:05, act_name='CAM-01' at 21:02:11. The clear arm is now elif _prev_applied_cam and scene.camera.name == _prev_applied_cam; the marker case owns nothing - no clear, no record, both trackers popped so the drift detector stays silent. A marker camera the tree really lost is still cleared (test). dev/tests/test_camera_marker_bound_first_open.py, doc/troubleshooting/camera_marker_bound_cleared_on_first_open.md. Branch fix/marker-camera-first-open.

    25. 🟢 "Cut camera(s) hidden from the render" warned on a parked take. multicam_panels.draw_warnings read the cut cameras' LIVE hide_render flags - which belong to the take on screen: Isolate (Multi Camera + Hide Others) hides every camera the active take does not use and puts them back on arrival. A single-camera take with no camera keeps nothing, so a parked Multi-Cam take's popover read "3 cut camera(s) hidden" with a Show button about the active take's hides (user report 2026-09-20). Same disease as the 2026-09-14 timeline-conflict warning: draw_warnings(..., is_active=True) now draws the render-hidden block only for the take on screen, the popover passes _mc.on_screen(context, scene, vl); the missing-camera warning stays for all. Second report the same hour: the cut ROWS went red for the same reason (row.alert read obj.hide_render) and were editable for a take not on screen - draw_cut_rows(..., is_active) now locks the rows (layout.enabled = False) for a parked take and reads neither the render flags nor the timeline's stacked markers for it; a cut naming a gone or non-camera object stays red everywhere. Third report: the TREE badge (draw_layers._get_vl_cascade_status, multicam_hidden) read the same flags - it now takes is_active (None asks on_screen(bpy.context, ...)), and the per-take status cache the sync timer wipes makes the badge follow the active take. Two source guards in test_multicam_markers.py widened their needle to the call's new shape. dev/tests/test_multicam_hidden_warning_is_for_the_take_on_screen.py (4), doc/troubleshooting/multicam_hidden_warning_parked_take.md.

      test_the_diff_state_topic_names_every_section_it_holds reads the _topic call from the source, resolves its _dst.* names and compares against the titles the page draws between this topic and the next; verified by reintroducing the defect. The banner topic gets the same check. The auditor learnt the general shape as CORR-33, Search Cannot Reach a Section.

    Changed¶

    1. 🟢 Borrowing a parent action, and letting it go, is a step in the undo line like any other change. The borrow note lived on the WindowManager (features/silence/state.py), deliberately: WM properties cannot be saved, and the note must not outlive the session. They are also invisible to Blender's undo, which snapshots the main database — while everything a borrow DOES (action assignments, owned TKS Parent N strips, rest snaps) is ordinary data that undo walks back normally. So undo unwound the work and left the note claiming the row was still borrowing; the panel and the viewport disagreed, and the next click acted on the wrong one (user ruling 2026-09-16). The four fields move to the MASTER scene — the Value Lock pattern, utils/master_scene.get_master_scene(), which resolves by data rather than sort order so a rename cannot hand the note to another scene, always answers (first scene when nothing carries anything) and never allocates. forget_on_load, a @persistent load_post handler registered in the Process Monitor, keeps the other half of the promise: the note is written into the .blend and dropped the moment one is opened. Both verbs take 'UNDO' in bl_options so the click owns its step rather than riding the mutation queue's timer push seconds later, and both call note_gesture_carried_by_operator — the seam the gesture macro uses — so the queue does not land a second step on top (One Gesture, One Step for a click). Solo / Cascade moves with the rest of the note and rides the same step. Guards: dev/tests/test_borrow_toggle_in_undo.py; test_silence.py::test_the_note_lives_where_undo_can_see_it replaces the test that pinned the old home.
    2. 🟢 Going to another take or view layer ends a borrowed parent action. Nothing in core/ cleared the note; the cascade only ASKED silence.borrowed_tier_for(scene, vl), which answers '' for any other row — so a borrow went quiet when the user walked away and woke up again on the way back, a state nothing on screen explains (user ruling 2026-09-16). state.end_if_row_changed(scene_name, vl_name) clears the note when the active row is not the borrowed one, called from operators/context/ops_crud_switch.py right where Variant Live is already told, and for the same reason: that operator suppresses the handler emitting the switch event and runs the cascade itself. The rule compares rows rather than ending on any switch, because the borrow's own bind switches to the row it borrows ON. It stands down during undo/redo (CRASH-01: clearing from inside a replay edits the step the user just stepped back to) and during a batch render, which walks every row itself — but NOT on is_applying, which is set for the whole length of the switch this is called from.
    3. 🟢 The borrow feature is named Parent Borrow everywhere, including its script names. The code carried a second name for the feature — silence — that appeared in no button, no tooltip and no wiki page, so the module, the operator ids, the properties, the providers and the text constants all said one thing while every reader saw another (user ruling 2026-09-16; "Parent State" was offered and refused because that name already belongs to the tier-inheritance feature). Renamed: features/silence/ → features/parent_borrow/, texts/tooltips_silence.py → tooltips_parent_borrow.py with its *_SILENCE_* constants, tks_silence_* Scene props → tks_parent_borrow_*, providers silence.* → parent_borrow.*, TKS_OT_Silence{Borrow,Release} → TKS_OT_ParentBorrow{,Release}, cascade._silence_tier_for → _borrowed_tier_for, parent_state.silence_says_solo → borrow_says_solo, the tree cell key silenced_from → borrowed_from, the Process Monitor group key and label, and dev/tests/test_silence.py → test_parent_borrow.py. The four internal property name= strings changed with them and de_DE was re-keyed in the same commit. The ordinary English word "silence" is left alone where it means silence (autokey_guard, diff_state/logic, sequencer/operators), and the released CHANGELOG_DEV.md is not rewritten — it records what the names were when those entries shipped. Gate: impact-selected 4378 passed; the 3 test_overlay_prefs_layout failures reproduce on plain main.

    4. 🟢 The Cache Version Mismatch warning opens by itself, folds when you click its badge, and the badge is always there. Reworded and back to unverified: what the user confirmed was an earlier shape. "Do not hide it" was first built as "draw it unconditionally", which is a different thing - a notice you have read and cannot put away is its own nuisance. The fold is back, tks_show_cache_warning now defaults True and carries no _make_warning_callback, and it is out of WARNING_TOGGLE_PROPS so opening any other warning cannot close it. The badge lost its and not _store_locked: every other badge stands down for a pending take-data restore because a second opinion on a doomed tree is noise, but this one is not a second opinion - it says the readings themselves came from an older version's caches, which is true of the restore offer too. Also: folding cache_locked into _store_locked made the panel RETURN at the take-data guard, a hundred lines above the lock card, so the lock greyed everything and explained nothing - two flags, two exits now. The rebuilt-cache note is boxed, matching draw_restored_strip. Superseded text: 🟢 The Cache Version Mismatch warning is always on screen while it applies, and its badge stays red throughout. The box in panels/navigation/panel.py was gated on tks_cache_stale AND tks_show_cache_warning like every sibling warning; the second term is gone. The siblings earn that gate because they report on scene data the user can choose to look at later. This one reports that the add-on's own runtime state was built from a file an older version shaped, which makes every other reading on the panel suspect — one click away it was routinely ignored for whole sessions (user ruling 2026-09-17). The badge stays in the warning bar on the user's call, but its alert is now unconditional True rather than not tks_show_cache_warning: the sibling convention colours a badge red only while its panel is closed, and this panel is never closed, so that rule would have painted a permanently calm badge over a live warning. Known wart, accepted: the badge is still a real toggle, so a click fires _make_warning_callback and closes the OTHER warning panels while doing nothing visible to this one. The follow-up, if it grates, is a plain label indicator plus dropping tks_show_cache_warning from WARNING_TOGGLE_PROPS (panels/navigation/logic.py), its BoolProperty (panels/navigation/__init__.py) and its manual_map anchor. Guards: two pure source-contract tests in dev/tests/test_cache_version_banner.py — no test can see a drawn panel, so the draw condition is the only observable. Card: doc/roadmap/active/cache-warning-persistence.md.

    5. 🟢 Diff State names its two states Take State and Drift State. Keyed Slot and Drifted named the mechanism — how an answer is stored, and what happened to it — and neither said where the value came from, which is the only question the overlay answers. The states are named for their tier now, so the colours read as the cascade (user ruling 2026-09-17, alternatives and their reasons in doc/roadmap/_dev/diff-state-prefs-tabs.md).

      A second pair went with them. The dropdown, the pie, the mode row and the Overlays popover said "Slot Marks" and "Drifted Marks" — a suffix that only existed because the state names did not say what a state was. One vocabulary now (user ruling 2026-09-19): LABEL_DIFF_SLOT_MARKS → LABEL_DIFF_TAKE_STATE, LABEL_DIFF_DRIFT_MARKS → LABEL_DIFF_DRIFT_STATE.

      Three byte-identical copies of the state label had to move together: texts/tooltips_diff_state.py (STATE_KEYED_LABEL/STATE_DRIFT_LABEL), preferences/prefs_search.py SEARCH_INDEX, and dev/tests/test_overlay_prefs_layout.py TITLES. Four more places had duplicated the chooser label as a literal and could not drift together — features/diff_state/operators.py _STATE_ITEMS, panels/mode_toggles.py, preferences/addon_prefs_constants.py MODE_PIE_SLOT_ITEMS (pinned equal to mode_toggles by test_mode_pie) and features/diff_state/properties.py — all four read the constants now. props_logging.py carries the two fold labels.

      German re-keyed in the same change, because the English text IS the key: Take-Zustand and Drift-Zustand. Take and Drift keep their English nouns and hyphenate, the way Take-Daten and Take-Wechsel already do; Abweichungszustand was unavailable because it is already the German for Diff State, the feature these two states belong to. Orphans 0, untracked 0.

      NOTHING identifying changed: the KEYED/DRIFT enum ids, the DIFF_DRIFT/DIFF_KEYED pie slot ids and their slot numbers, the saved _DIFF_STATE_ITEMS preference values, the keymap tokens and the ~200 generated diff_state_keyed_* / diff_state_drift_* property names all stand, so no saved preference and no keymap breaks. test_diff_state_switch::test_the_tooltip_names_the_state_on_show renamed with its asserted words. Wiki prose updated in four pages (the UI manifest is CI-generated and follows). Impact gate 1652 passed.

    6. 🟢 Diff State reads one table for which states exist and which one claims an object that is in several. classify_states, visible_states, dominant_state and split_marks each spelled out KEYED and DRIFT in their own body, so a third state meant editing four functions, both call sites and every test that touched them. New logic.STATE_ORDER - one tuple, most dominant first - now carries which states exist, precedence, and the order the draw plan lists them in. Signatures follow the table: classify_states(flags) takes a mapping, visible_states(states, shown) takes the set of states switched on (built in draw.py from STATE_ORDER + the tks_diff_state_<id> window-manager switches), and split_marks(states, marks_by_state, priority) takes the marks each state would draw - draw.py already had that dict as wanted. split_marks generalises "drift takes what it draws" to "each state takes what the ones above it did not", which is the same rule for two. Six tests add a state that does not exist and assert the helpers carry it with nothing else changed; test_the_shipped_table_still_reads_drift_first pins the real order. 259 passed across the Diff State files, impact gate 4501 passed. NOT moved, with a comment saying why: resolve_mode / mode_pair are a two-BIT scheme - four exclusive choices out of two switches - and their choice ids are saved (props_mode_row._DIFF_STATE_ITEMS) and live in keymaps (operators._STATE_ITEMS). Absorbing a third state turns the chooser into per-state toggles, so it moves with that interface, additively. Verified by evidence, not by hand, at the user's request (2026-09-20): this change has no surface of its own. The six monkeypatch tests add a state that does not exist and assert the helpers carry it; and Parent State and Rest State, which are nothing but two new rows in that table, were confirmed working in-app on the same day (Added 9). A table that did not drive the helpers could not have produced them.

    7. 🟢 The uncaptured-values list follows the list-height setting. MAINT-16. preferences/draw_data_storage.py drew TKS_UL_CaptureCoverage with rows=6, maxrows=10 - the only literal list height left in the tree. Now get_list_rows('capture_coverage'), with rows and maxrows both set to it, the same shape draw_data_tools.py already used for the patterns list. No dedicated preference row was added for it: it is a diagnostic list, and get_list_rows answers list_rows_default for a key with no override_* of its own, which is the behaviour wanted here. Adding a row would mean a new IntProperty, a new BoolProperty, an entry in props_list_heights._LIST_KEYS, a Preferences > Interface row, a tooltip constant, a de_DE key and an EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT bump - a product decision, not a cleanup.

    Two internal changes ride with it and have no user-facing line, because nothing a reader can see changes:

    • CORR-07. The four adoption-card operators - TKS_OT_AdoptedKeep, TKS_OT_AdoptedToOneTake, TKS_OT_AdoptedDrop and TKS_OT_ActionlessToAuto - dereferenced context.window_manager, context.scene and context.view_layer with no poll(). New _AdoptedCardOp mixin states the gate once, with poll_message_set on each branch. Deliberately does NOT require the card to be open: a script that knows it has adopted objects may answer for them without the panel having drawn (Constitution rule 7).
    • MAINT-01. operators/cascade/_helpers.draw_inherited_field had no caller anywhere - not by name, not by string - and was a 31-line copy of the block already inside draw_action_field (lines 813-824). Every helper it used keeps another caller, so removing it strands nothing. Recoverable from git if the assign-row-of-their-own popovers it was written for ever arrive.

    • 🟢 Diff State preferences are a tab row, not four folds. Every state generated ~113 preferences and preferences/draw_interface.py drew one full block each - 26 rows a state, about 105 with four. Worse, its loop still read (('keyed', ...), ('drift', ...)), so Parent State and Rest State had every setting saved, read and obeyed by the overlay and no row anywhere to change them. diff_state_prefs_tab picks one state; _draw_diff_state_block draws that one. The four expand_diff_state_<state> fold flags retire with the folds. Page length is now flat in the number of states.

    • 🟢 Each tab carries its state's colour as a painted dot. UILayout.prop_enum takes no icon_value (checked against 5.2.0 LTS), so a static enum drawn with expand=True can only show a stock glyph and no stock glyph follows a user's colour. diff_state_prefs_tab became a DYNAMIC enum whose items hand back an integer icon id, retained through utils.enum_cache; it loses its default= (Blender allows none on a callback enum) and the first item - the first state in the table - is the default. New preferences/diff_state_icons.py paints one 32x32 dot per state into a preview collection, repainted only when that colour moves, freed in unregister. Pixels are PREMULTIPLIED: measured four ways side by side (dev/scripts/probe_dot_icon.py), straight alpha arrives as a dot sitting on a solid square of its own colour, because the icon buffer does not honour a zero alpha beside a full colour.

    • 🟢 The look moved into a pencil popover, grouped by mark. New preferences/diff_state_popovers.py: Every Mark (colour, random), Box (line width, opacity), Outline (its own width mode + slider, opacity), Fill (opacity), Empty (style, size). A group whose mark is off says "not drawn" and greys its heading but stays editable - people set a look before switching a mark on. One INSTANCED panel per state and per state x object kind, GENERATED, and built at register() rather than import: _build_panels reads features.diff_state.logic for the kind rows, and a feature imports preferences back for get_list_rows, so building at import time was a cycle that made variant_switch fail to load with one line in the console. A test pins the module scope free of feature imports.

    • 🟢 Search had to be solved before the tabs could ship. Three parts. The per-state sections in prefs_search.SEARCH_INDEX are GENERATED from the state table - hand-listing them is what left Parent and Rest unsearchable. A query matching a state the tab row is not showing switches the tab (_ds_visible_tab reads the section flags, so with no query nothing moves and it can never disagree with the dimming). And while a query runs the pencil's contents are drawn FLAT on the page from the same body the popover uses - a popover cannot be opened from code, so a hit inside one would otherwise point at a row nobody can reach.

    • 🟢 Wording and spacing. The topic heading is plural, "Diff States", since it holds four. PREFS_TITLE_GAP above the master default row so the tab row reads as a header rather than another line of the block, and separator(type='LINE') under it - everything below is an exception to that row. EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 1095 -> 1097 -> 1094 across the branch (+2 fold flags, then -4 flags +1 tab).

    • 🟢 Scene.use_nodes is left alone. Deprecated for removal in Blender 6.0 - a DeprecationWarning on every read or write, measured 2026-09-20 on 5.2 with a headless probe. The cascade forced it True on every switch that resolved a node group; core/vl_preload_snapshot.py captured, compared and restored it. Both dropped; in 5.x the node group being set enables the compositor. A test holds the cascade and the snapshot capture warning-free. Needs the in-app check that a comp still renders.

Writing tree state during undo replay creates phantom steps - the World's and the Camera's rule, now the compositor's.

Nothing changes., Decide one by one.) and one preference name in preferences/props/props_undo.py over the label length (Skip Compositor-Clear in Post-Undo Cascade). Nothing removed; tks.um_log_files moves from #debug-log-monitor to #undo-redo where it is documented now.

The member sat in the enum and in all three property maps (_VL_OVERRIDE_PROPS 'tks_preset', _SCENE_BASE_PROPS None, _GLOBAL_PROPS 'tks_global_preset') marked "Future: render presets", and no pass ever branched on it - render presets got their own system instead. CORR-34.2's one finding on this codebase (a domain the cascade names but never applies), confirmed by a re-scan reporting 0 findings after the removal. Nothing else in the addon or the tests referenced the member or those three property names; the class docstring's - PRESET: (Future) line went with it. core/cascade.py. Impact gate 4747 passed.

    [0.8.5] - 2026-09-14¶

    Fixed¶

    1. 🟢 _picker_props handed the View Layer Group picker a vl_name. A VL Group has members, not one view layer, so TKS_OT_VLG*Popover declares no such property — setattr raised inside the draw, and Blender drops every widget after a raise without a word. The trailing button and the whole Rule + Preset box vanished; the popover looked perfect whenever the tier held a value of its own, because that state takes the prop_search branch and never reaches the loop. Found by drawing the traceback into the popup itself, there being no System Console on this build. Guards: dev/tests/test_cascade_picker_props.py asks the REGISTERED operator what it declares, and auditor INFO-20 blind_setattr reports a setattr in a draw whose name is not a literal (6 sites on Takes). Full account: doc/troubleshooting/cascade_popover_silent_truncation.md.
    2. 🔴 Five icons in panels/context/draw_collections.py set group_name and not scene_name. A cascade popover resolves its target by name and returns on its first guard, so the popup opened empty. The twin block 100 lines below and the one in lists_split.py always passed both. Guard: dev/tests/test_cascade_popover_addressing.py, and auditor INFO-20 half_address.
    3. 🔴 A VL Group records its scene twice — a scene pointer and a scene_name string — and the pointer survives a rename while the name does not. The tree has always preferred the pointer (_resolve_row_group); every cascade popover matched on the name alone. Eleven sites now go through vl_group_is_in.
    4. 🔴 _NEW_OPS in operators/cascade/_picker.py held no group tiers at all and no Global for World, so the same icon one row up the tree had nothing to click. Twelve cells added; Compositor was already complete in its own _COMP_NEW_OPS, which auditor INFO-20 now also reads (cascade_menu_table takes a list — asking about one table reported Compositor as missing Create at five tiers it offered it at).
    5. 🔴 Camera and World at Global and Scene, and the Automation Rule cascade at all five of its tiers, drew their own assign row. The Rule cascade sat outside CASCADE_TYPES entirely — a rule is a library tag, not a datablock — so a parity rule that compares a kind against itself was blind to it. Its registry entry carries tag_category instead of a bpy.data collection, and draw_assign_row learned to search a library category. Auditor INFO-20 whole_kind now reports a kind that routes a shared part nowhere while every peer routes it everywhere.
    6. 🔴 TKS_OT_VLWorldPopover kept the older form while Camera at the same tier had moved. One cell out of nineteen, found by drawing every cell of the grid and comparing the field shape.
    7. 🔴 draw_inline_controls drew both controls always and set enabled = bool(own_action). Now drawn only when the choice is real: the tier holds an action of its own, or parents_with_an_action counts two or more tiers above holding one. An empty tier above is a pass-through, not a parent. A Scene Group has only Global above it and so can never reach two. Guard: dev/tests/test_parent_controls_visibility.py.
    8. 🔴 on_mode_changed in features/cameras/multicam_engine.py asked the view layer for a camera, then the scene, and stopped — so a take inheriting from a VL Group, a Scene Group or Global answered "no camera" and seeded nothing, while the read-out directly above the list named a camera because it resolves the cascade. Now resolved through resolve_cascade. Measured: 1 cut at VL, 1 at Scene, 0 at Global before; 1 everywhere after. Guard: dev/tests/test_multicam_seed_inherited.py.
    9. 🟢 draw_single_conflict reads the conflict off the SCENE's timeline markers, and those belong to whichever take is on screen - the switch writes them. So another take's popover showed a warning about somebody else's cuts and offered a button that cleared them. The Add row in the same popover already had this rule ("shut on a take that is not on screen"); the warning below it never got it. Now gated on engine.on_screen, and TKS_OT_MultiCamClearSceneCuts refuses off-screen callers outright rather than trusting the button to be hidden. Guard: dev/tests/test_multicam_conflict_is_for_the_take_on_screen.py.
    10. 🔴 TKS_OT_SGOutputRulePopover.draw had been given the View Layer Group's body and read self.scene_name, which a Scene Group does not declare - it spans several scenes and names none. That raises in a draw, and Blender drops every widget below the failing line without a word. Guard: dev/tests/test_operator_reads_only_its_own_props.py reads all 114 drawing operators and asks whether each self.<name> is declared by the class or one of its bases; proven by putting the fault back.
    11. 🔴 The View Layer World box named its inherited rule via get_cached_inherited(..., CascadeProperty.OUTPUT_RULE) - a different cascade from the row it belongs to. Folded onto draw_rule_and_preset, whose parent comes from _rule_parent('WORLD', ...).
    12. 🔴 Camera, World and Automation Rule at the TAKE tier drew a bare prop_search. A Take DOES inherit its value - it sits at the top of the chain and falls through to the View Layer below it - so the empty field was hiding a real answer. All three now use draw_assign_row. Their RULE is still their own only, which is a separate question: draw_rule_and_preset is handed parent=None at TAKE.
    13. 🔴 draw_rule_and_preset never took a vl, so from the View Layer tier down preset_selector_row resolved against context.view_layer. It takes one now, and passes vl_name to tks.clear_rule_override, which declares it. draw_assign_row also gained middle(row) for a tier carrying a control between the field and the trailing button - the View Layer camera's Multi-Cam toggle. INFO-20 on this tree: own_row 9 -> 0, blind_setattr 6 -> 0, everything else already 0; the two cells that cannot fold carry an INFO-20-OK sentinel with its reason.
    14. 🟢 Five separate Alt-click handlers - Camera, World, Action and Automation Rule at the VL tier, plus the shared popover_invoke - cleared the ACTIVE TAKE as well as the view layer, while the report named only the view layer. The reasoning was real (a take sits above the VL in the chain, so clearing only the VL can leave the take's value still winning and the click looks inert) but the answer is that a take is cleared from its own icon, and Shift+Alt is the deliberate way to reach down a chain (user ruling 2026-09-14, after "alt+click on vl cam icon has removed the take's cams"). Guard: dev/tests/test_alt_click_clears_only_its_own_tier.py scans every tks.vl_* operator's invoke for a WRITE to the active take - narrowed from a first version that also flagged the camera icon reading it to resolve the cascade, and the Take variant icon clearing its own take.

    [0.8.4] - 2026-09-14¶

    Added¶

    1. 🟢 Twin marking: which view layers ASSIGN the ACTIVE view layer's action. panels/context/draw_layers.get_twin_state() answers it once per draw cycle; find_action_twins() is the single lookup behind the marks, the tooltip and the popover's jump list.

    An empty assignment is not a share (user ruling 2026-09-10, after seeing it in the app). The lookup first compared the RESOLVED action, so every row inheriting the same thing from a tier above counted as a twin -- and a Global or Scene action reaches nearly every row, so the mark lit up almost the whole tree. That is precisely the noise the active-relative ruling exists to prevent, arrived at from the other direction. A row that sets nothing has nothing of its own to share.

    It reads cheaper too: one tks_action per view layer instead of a full cascade resolve, so the pass no longer touches get_cached_inherited() at all. The filter stands down entirely when the active row assigns nothing -- hiding every row would read as a broken tree, not as an honest empty answer.

    The mark is ACTIVE-RELATIVE by ruling. A stable colour per action was built first and rejected the same session — with many shared actions on screen it trades one visual irritation for another (roadmap _dev/see-who-shares-your-action.md, ruling (a)). The rest action never counts as a twin: it is assigned nearly everywhere by design and would light the whole tree up.

    Resolution goes through get_cached_inherited() for every view layer — the cache the cascade popovers already fill, so the pass adds no resolve the tree was not already paying for, once per ~200 ms cycle rather than per frame (ARCH-05).

    _twin_state is keyed by the ACTIVE (scene, view layer), not a bare sentinel. The switch operator (operators/context/ops_crud_switch.py) redraws synchronously while the cascade caches clear on a ~200 ms timer, so a timer-only cache paints the previous row's twins and corrects them a fifth of a second later — the disease doc/roadmap/ideas/diff-state-stale-after-switch.md describes. A tuple compare per row covers every route into a switch, including Blender's own view-layer dropdown, undo, and scripted calls that never reach our operator.

    1. 🟢 Two hint styles, and NEITHER costs a column (tks_twin_mark: OFF / BUTTON / LINE, default BUTTON).

    ONE colour paints every marked row, the active one included. Borrowing tks_active_vl_color for the active row tied two settings together, and the Colors box could then no longer say which switch owned which swatch.

    • LINE repaints the row's tree-line strip — the same strip the tag colour uses — and overrules the tag (user ruling 2026-09-10). New twin_prop argument on tree_layout_calc.draw_tree_line(), tested BEFORE the tag branch, painting at TAG_STRIP_UNITS. Reusing the tag strip's own width is what makes it free: a tagged row is already that wide, and an untagged one gives back exactly the untagged_gap it would otherwise have padded with, so a marked row is the same pixels as an unmarked one.

      untagged_gap() had to learn about it. The compensating pad asked only whether TAG COLOURS were on, so with tags off and the mark on, marked rows were wide and every unmarked row beside them a hair narrow -- the tree stepped sideways as the mark moved (user report 2026-09-10). It now pads while EITHER owner can widen a strip. - BUTTON fills the action chip (emboss + depress). That is the rest action's look, and the two can never land on one row because the rest action is excluded from the twin set outright — asserted, not assumed.

    What this replaces, and why. The first build gave the mark its own far-left column and put the count beside the action icon. Both were wrong, and both were reported from the app the same day:

    • The tree shifted on every switch. The column was reserved on whether anything happened to be shared, so it appeared and vanished as the user walked the tree. Reserving it on the setting fixed the shift but left a permanent column nobody asked for. Riding the tag strip removes the column entirely — the correct answer, and the user's.
    • The count pushed the icon cluster out of column. The right cluster is right-aligned inside one shared width; TWIN_COUNT_UNITS = 0.5 did not cover a digit plus its button padding, and no value would have been right, because the right-hand strip has no room to give.

    TWIN_BAR_UNITS, TWIN_BAR_R_PAD, TWIN_COUNT_UNITS, draw_twin_bar() and twin_count_units() are all gone; dev/tests/test_action_twins.py::test_no_column_of_its_own fails if any returns.

    1. 🟢 The count moved to the action chip's tooltip (TKS_OT_VLActionPopover._describe_twins, folded into the STATE half of compose_tooltip).

    Blender cannot put a number inside an icon from Python. Its C side can — UI_icon_draw_ex takes a number and the Outliner uses it — but nothing exposes it. Probed against the real RNA in Blender 5.2, not documentation: operator, prop, label, menu, popover, template_icon and template_node_socket were listed in full, and a search of EVERY UILayout function parameter for number / count / badge / digit returned zero hits. The only Python route to a real badge is painting our own pixels (bpy.utils.previews → ImagePreview.image_pixels_float → icon_value=, verified writable on 5.2) and hand-drawing digit bitmaps. Parked as too much machinery for one number; the tooltip answers the same question on the row the user is already pointing at.

    1. 🟢 Twin list in the view-layer action popover (operators/cascade/ops_viewlayer_action.py). Rows in another scene are labelled scene / view layer; each is a tks.switch_viewlayer operator, so the jump reuses the existing switch path.

    2. 🟢 Settings, both halves of the mirrored pair. Live WindowManager.tks_twin_mark / tks_twin_action_color (panels/context/__init__.py) and saved default_twin_mark / default_twin_action_color (preferences/props/props_list_heights.py), on BOTH sync maps — preferences/ops_addon_ui.py (WM→prefs) and preferences/persistence_io.py (prefs→WM); the colour rides the explicit list() conversion beside default_active_vl_color, since _TREE_MAP cannot carry a FloatVector. EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT bumped 853 → 855 (the guard refused the whole addon at register time when it was missed — working as designed). Drawn in the Tree View Design popover (operators/misc/ops_tree_design.py) and Preferences → Interface → Tree (preferences/draw_interface.py), categorised in preferences/draw_data_inspector.py.

    ONE enum, not a master bool plus a style enum — the Camera Visibility pair taught that a second setting lets the answer move behind the user. tks_twin_mark's update callback drops the twin cache, so throwing the switch bites on the next redraw instead of waiting out the sync timer (the "Mark Shared Actions has no effect" report).

    Texts are centralised (INFO-09): texts/tooltips_context.py and texts/tooltips_preferences.py, with texts/locales/de_DE.py re-keyed in the same commit — twelve new sources, verified with python dev/scripts/i18n_extract.py takes_for_blender --locale de_DE.

    1. 🟢 A third filter axis: show only the view layers carrying the active one's action (tks_twin_filter, in the Filter popover beside Render Icon and Filter by Tag; panels/context/tree_filter_engine.py mirrors the render-filter shape exactly -- pre-computed VL / scene / SG / VLG sets, then one membership test per row).

    It reads find_action_twins(), not get_twin_state(). The state collapses a lone carrier to "nothing shared" because there is no mark to draw; a filter answering that with an empty tree would just look broken. The raw lookup always returns the active row itself, so the worst case is a tree holding exactly the row you are standing on. Deliberately independent of tks_twin_mark: someone who turned the marking off may still want to ask the question once. The sidebar Filter button lights for it like it does for the other two axes.

    1. 🟢 Still Mode is the Tree Icon Pie's eighth slice (South-East, which shipped empty). It is the only row icon that is NOT a cascade property: it is absent from ops_cascade_overflow._ORDER and always was, so the pie's vocabulary is now that order PLUS one. dev/tests/test_tree_icon_pie.py carries the addition as an explicit _EXTRA_SLOTS set rather than loosening the equality, so a prop that goes missing from _ORDER still fails.

    Two spellings for one tier. A tree row calls its tier SCENE_GROUP / VL_GROUP; tks.still_popover calls the same thing SG / VLG. New _STILL_TIERS in the pie mirrors _TIER_MAP from the overflow operator -- copied, not imported (panels may not import from operators, ARCH-01), and held to its original by a test, exactly as _LEVEL_EXCLUDES is.

    force_popover had to reach a ninth operator. TKS_OT_StillPopover forks three ways in invoke (Alt clears to Inherit, Shift opens the full Timeline Options popup, a plain click opens the quick mode dropdown), and a pie dispatches no modifiers, so the slice would have opened the quick list while its seven neighbours opened their editors. Same house shape as the other eight: if self.force_popover or event.shift:. The property carries options={'SKIP_SAVE'}, which the older eight do not -- an operator property Blender remembers between invocations is exactly the leak test_every_forcing_operator_declares_the_property warns about. features/still_mode/operators.py joins _FORK_FILES.

    The master lock still wins: invoke returns {'CANCELLED'} while engine.master_active(), so the slice no-ops exactly as the row icon does.

    1. 🟢 The slice resolves its own glyph. New features/still_mode/panels.still_row_icon() -- the winner-to-glyph mapping lifted out of draw_still_button, which now calls it, so the two cannot drift. The other seven slices carry a constant in _ICONS; STILL is deliberately absent from that table, with a comment saying why, because a constant there would sit reading PREVIEW_RANGE while the row it points at reads Still.

    _targets_active_vl() answers the is_active half: the master lock's depressed badge belongs to the ACTIVE view layer row and to no other (Fixed entry 6), so the pie has to ask the same question or the two disagree the moment the lock is on.

    The import is guarded. Still Mode is an optional feature bundle (features/__init__.py catches its ImportError), so a session where it failed to load gets seven working slices and a neutral eighth, not an empty wheel.

    1. 🟢 Silence — borrow a parent tier's action for one row (features/silence/). A take can hold its own action while a tier above it holds another, and the one above was then unreachable from that row: the take's action wins, so the parent could only be edited by leaving the take and going to the tier that owns it.

    The borrow is a WindowManager note — the row by NAME, the tier, and ONLY/CASCADE. WindowManager because it must not survive a save; that choice also removes the migration and the load-time clean-up, since a fresh session simply has no note. No PointerProperty, no as_pointer().

    resolve_cascade gains the skip beside the Rest State Mode short-circuit (core/cascade.py), in the same shape and gated on not raw: while the note names a row, the ACTION walk starts AT the borrowed tier, so every tier from the row's own down to just above it is silenced and the borrowed action becomes the resolution. Stored assignments are never written. raw=True consumers — batch render, the CLI worker, the drift scan — see the real chain, as they do for Rest.

    The tier is stored as the label cascade_levels itself produces. action_tiers() is the one public helper the borrow check and the popover both read, so the list drawn for the user and the chain the resolver walks are the same walk. Public rather than a feature importing _VL_OVERRIDE_PROPS, which would be a private cross-package import (ARCH-03).

    Rest still wins over a borrow inside the resolver even though turning Rest on releases the borrow. The release makes the overlap impossible; the ordering makes it guaranteed.

    NOT features/parent_state, which keeps doing per-channel inheritance through NLA layers and is untouched. The two are siblings: every read across goes through core/providers, every write through bpy.ops (ARCH-02).

    The list is drawn by features/silence/panels.draw_parents, called from the view layer action popover ABOVE the row's own field — the same shape as parent_state.panels.draw_parent_keys. It gets its own heading because the picker in that same popover greys an inherited action to mean "do not assign this" and these rows mean the opposite; a tier holding nothing is left out entirely rather than drawn as a dead row.

    Ending it: VL_SWITCH_POST_CASCADE clears on a take switch, TKS_OT_RestModeToggle's enable branch clears through query("silence.clear"). Both drop "vl_cascade" before signal_redraw(), or the tree waits for a mouse move (Fixed entry 5, 2026-09-10).

    Phase 1-2 of doc/roadmap/active/silence.md; Solo/Cascade (which decides whether the Parent State layers are built under the borrowed action), the tier lock and the blast-radius line are phases 3-4. Twenty-four new strings, de_DE in the same commits. Tests: dev/tests/test_silence.py (42).

    1. 🟢 The borrow is given back on its own. Split from entry 7 because it is its own user-visible promise: nothing has to be remembered to switch off, and nothing can be left silenced by accident. Three doors — the Release button, a take switch, and Rest State Mode coming on — and the note cannot outlive the session either way.

    2. 🟢 Solo / Cascade — one switch for the whole list, because only one parent is ever borrowed at a time (user ruling 2026-09-10). The two differ in exactly one thing: whether the Parent State layers are built under the borrowed action. parent_state.engine_bpy.silence_says_only() empties resolve_stack for ONLY, after the Rest gate and scoped to the borrowing ROW — another take's borrow must not flatten this row's stack. CASCADE needs no branch at all: the borrow has already made that tier the winner, so the stack walks the tiers above it exactly as it always did. The switch is WindowManager.tks_silence_view with an update callback that re-runs the bind, since the layers are built during the bind. A property callback is the user's own click inside their own undo step, not a handler (Constitution 2).

    3. 🟢 The lock and the blast radius. state.locks_assignments() is true only for the row that borrowed; panels.lock_assignment() sets layout.enabled = False on the assignment row — enabled, not active, because this one must really refuse input — in both binding popovers, the take row and the version row. Reassigning a tier mid-borrow would move the ground under the keys being set with nothing on screen to explain it. The blast-radius warning that shipped with this entry was taken back out on 2026-09-11: two red lines inside the box for a state the depressed button and the dimmed rows already announce. The tier is named on the row in play; the words were noise. INFO_SILENCE_BLAST and its second line stay in texts/ with their German, so a one-line version can return without a re-key.

    4. 🟢 Reach. The version row binds too, so it gets the list with own_tier="Version" — every other tier is a parent to it. The tree marks the borrowing row with LINKED, depressed, from a new silenced_from key on the cell state read through query("silence.borrowed_tier_for"). Unlike the Rest badge it stays the PICKER operator with force_popover, so one more click reopens the list that lets go; a status chip there would be a dead end. Scene, group and Global popovers deliberately get NO list. The borrow is keyed by (scene, view layer) because a view layer is what BINDS, and those tiers are not binding rows — there is nothing to borrow for.

    5. 🟢 The camera popover's Add row has its own frame field, so a marker lands where you type instead of where the playhead sits WindowManager.tks_multicam_add_frame, seeded in the popover's invoke() -- a draw may not write, and opening the popover is exactly when "the current frame" is the answer the user expects. Transient by design: a thought in progress must never reach the .blend.

      It settles itself on every path that takes a frame -- `settle_add_frame()` after the mode toggle seeds a cut, after Select hands a marker over, and one frame past its own marker after an Add. It counts the take's ROWS as well as the scene's markers, because a row is written first and its marker only follows when the cascade re-applies.

    6. 🟢 Select says how many markers are waiting in it, so opening an empty list is never a wasted click free_markers() filtered to what this take has not already claimed, counted onto the button text. Claimed is matched BY NAME, not by frame, so a marker dragged away from its row's frame is still spoken for and cannot appear in two places.

    7. 🟢 A cut row with no camera yet offers a + that makes one and binds it, in place of the rename pencil tks.multicam_cut_camera_new. An empty field is a question; there is nothing to rename yet, and the one thing the row waits for is a camera. Naming goes through naming_utils.generate_viewlayer_camera_name, so the whole add-on keeps one naming policy.

    8. 🟢 Discard List throws a parked cut list away, after saying how many cuts go and that the cameras are untouched tks.multicam_clear_cuts, drawn ONLY in the parked state -- the one place the edit is already inert. Beside a live cut list it would put a delete next to the buttons that build one. Clearing also switches Multi-Cam off: "I do not want this list" and "I am not cutting" are the same sentence.

    9. 🟢 A take set to Still still shows its cut list, greyed, with a line saying how many are parked and what brings them back Switching Multi-Cam off never deleted anything, but markers vanishing from the Timeline with nothing said looks exactly like losing work -- and a user who believes an edit is gone rebuilds it by hand. A sentence promising the edit is safe is worth far less than the edit itself sitting there to be counted.

    10. 🟢 Multi-Cam Follows Animation Mode, on by default, lets the two modes settle each other instead of leaving it to you Preferences, Workflow, Automations, Cameras. On: pressing Multi-Cam on a Still take animates it and turns the mode on in one press, and setting a take to Still parks its Multi-Cam. Off: the conflict is flagged and left to the user. The Still side goes through _reapply() -- the one seam a per-tier edit and the global lock both pass -- and asks cameras by name through the cameras.still_changed provider, never a sibling import (ARCH-02).

    11. 🟢 A warnings panel lists takes whose cuts cannot play, and every frame in the file carrying more than one marker Red on a tree chip says THAT something is wrong; a user with twenty takes still has to go looking. still_conflicts() and stacked_conflicts() behind one subpanel and one nav-bar button -- two red buttons for two rare states would cost more room in the bar than they are worth. The paused rows carry Animate; the stacked rows carry Separate.

    12. 🟢 Separate moves one marker off a shared frame, and a marker with no camera is the one that gives way tks.multicam_unstack_frame. The one left behind keeps the frame, so the fix never changes which camera is on screen at that moment. Deliberately NOT held to the active take, unlike the marker operators inside the popover: a marker belongs to the SCENE, the panel row says which scene, and a user fixing a listed problem should not have to go and stand somewhere else first.

    13. 🟢 Batch render skips a take with a camera problem and says which, instead of writing a render that only looks finished Four reasons, one shared predicate so the queue's draw-time marker and the start-time gate can never disagree: two CAMERA markers on one frame (Blender picks one and the cut list keeps the other), Multi-Cam pinned to a single frame, a cut naming a camera that is not here, and a cut to a camera hidden from the render. An empty marker beside a cut is deliberately NOT one of them -- only camera markers decide the camera. Asked through cameras.render_block rather than a fifth slot in cameras.render_api, whose tuple is unpacked by index in three places.

    14. 🟢 A confirmation says which frame a new marker will land on when the one you asked for is taken, and can be switched off confirm_marker_moved, Preferences, Interface, Confirmations, Context. A button that quietly uses a different number from the field beside it is what this stops; a confirm nobody reads any more is just a click in the way, so it comes off. A scripted caller never sees it.

    15. 🔴 Still and Render become real columns with real switches. New utils/tree_columns.py names all nine icon columns once — TreeColumn(key, icon, pin_default, editor) — and column_visible(wm, key, collapsed) answers the one question every drawer used to answer for itself. Ten places hand-listed the columns before this and disagreed in five ways.

    tks_show_still was never registered: every read site spelled it getattr(wm, 'tks_show_still', True), so the column was forced on forever and the Tree Design popover had no property to offer. Registered now, along with tks_pin_still and tks_pin_render, both defaulting True — reproducing the "always outside collapse" both columns were hard-wired to, so no existing profile changes on upgrade.

    The Tree Design popover (operators/misc/ops_tree_design.py), its Preferences mirror (preferences/draw_interface.py), PREF_TREE_MAP (used by ops_addon_ui.py and persistence_io.py) and the preferences search index all walk the table now. Retired with them: tks_show_rest_state / tks_pin_rest_state and their two preference defaults — registered, saved, and drawn by nothing.

    Lives in utils/ because operators/ owns the Tree Design and overflow popovers and may not import panels/ (ARCH-01). Imports only typing, holds no RNA, takes wm as an argument (Constitution 7). Auditor after the shape commits: ARCH-01/02/03/05 all 0.

    1. 🔴 Split view reaches full parity, not Hide-only (user ruling, revising the plan's own recommendation). _is_collapsed moved from TKS_UL_AllViewLayers to tree_layout_calc.is_collapsed(context) — the UIList delegates, so one definition — because split view stacks its lists as full-width layout.box() sections in the same region (draw_split.py:60-110, 160, 228, 306, 391), so region.width is the right measure with no scaled threshold and no new preference.

    2. 🔴 The cascade overflow popover hosts Still. Making Still pinnable without this would give the reader a switch that hides the column with nowhere to reach it. _PROP_ICONS / _PROP_KEY / _ORDER in operators/misc/ops_cascade_overflow.py are derived from TREE_COLUMNS; tks_overflow_active_prop gains an appended 'STILL' item (Blender stores that enum as an int — never reorder).

      The editor moved to features/still_mode/panels.draw_still_editor: ONE definition, called by tks.still_popover and by the overflow popover. The Mode control is the only part needing a live operator — it is an EnumProperty whose get/set read self.tier, and _call_inline_draw renders through a types.SimpleNamespace where that cannot work — so without op= it draws the same three values as three tks.still_set buttons.

      Render joins as a plain button after the strip (_PLAIN, _draw_plain_columns, _RENDER_OPS): a bare toggle with nothing to edit, excluded at the TAKE tier which has no render operator.

      Two comments asserting the opposite — "Still Mode is not a cascade property and is not in the overflow popover", in panels/pie_menus/tree_icons.py and in dev/tests/test_tree_icon_pie.py — are rewritten. The pie had already contradicted them via force_popover.

      Not done, deliberately: no RENDER slot in the Tree Icon Pie. Every slice there opens an editor and the machinery assumes it; Render flips instead. A slot means six more per-tier operator maps for a toggle the row already offers, and a pickable slot that does nothing is worse than none. Reasoning recorded beside TREE_ICON_PIE_SLOT_ITEMS.

    3. 🟢 Material Swap — a standalone per-slot swap feature. New features/material_swap/ (properties, operators, logic) storing rows on the World that carries them (utils/store_world.SWAP_STORE, path tks_material_swaps). A row is (object_name, slot_index, original, swap_to, enabled, link_flipped).

    Reference types split deliberately. The object is a StringProperty (Constitution rule 1 — a stale object pointer crashes undo). The two materials are PointerProperty(type=Material), matching TKS_VSW_PoolMaterial.material: the pointer keeps a user, so the stored ORIGINAL cannot be purged out from under a revert, and it survives a rename. Materials only — never widened to objects or actions.

    1. 🟢 Every slot is listed; there is no row to add. panels/inspector/swap_view.py draws two template_lists bound STRAIGHT to the store — no WindowManager mirror. The Watchlist needs a mirror because its membership is computed; a swap row is the user's own record, so the store is the list. Nothing to sync means nothing to go stale.

    2. 🟢 Revert assigns the captured original. logic.add_row() reads the slot's material once, at creation. revert_row() writes it back. No per-object idprop stamp (the shape Shot Manager Pro's rule book uses and this design rejected), no snapshot, nothing to unwind.

    3. 🟢 The overrule: ownership, not ordering. features/variant_switch/cascade_engine._apply_pool() hoists providers.query('material_swap.owned_slots', default=frozenset()) once per pass and skips any (obj.name, slot_idx) in it. pool_resolve._collect_collapse() reads the SAME provider, so a warning can never disagree with an apply (that module's stated contract).

      Wired through core/providers.py, never a sibling import — ARCH-02. Argument-free on purpose: an arg-taking provider fetched with query() answers None without a word. Absent feature ⇒ empty set ⇒ the apply behaves exactly as before.

      Ownership ignores enabled. A row claims its slot on or off; otherwise "swap off" would hand the slot back to the variant pool and the original would be repainted anyway.

      No handler, no timer, no re-apply pass. Because the variant apply skips owned slots, the written material simply stays. Writes happen in operator execute() and property update callbacks only — direct RNA, so variant_ui_block_corruption.md never becomes reachable.

      No cache either. A dirty-flag set was specced in the activation ruling and dropped during the build: undo restores the store without passing through any writer, so a cached set would outlive the undo it described and the switch would skip the wrong slots. owned_slots() rebuilds — a pure read over a hand-made list, hoisted by both callers.

    4. 🟢 Shared-mesh protection. logic._protect_shared_mesh() flips slot.link = 'OBJECT' only when obj.data.users > 1, then assigns (the object-level slot starts empty). A single-user object keeps the plain DATA link, so the common case carries no side effect. Never flipped back on revert — the object-level assignment may hold the user's own work by then; the row records link_flipped and the UI badges it.

    5. 🟢 The Swap List is the third exclusive Inspector content. wm.tks_inspector_show_swaps + mode SWAPS on tks.toggle_inspector_mode, short-circuiting in panels/inspector/panel.py like tks_inspector_show_channels. Turning one of the two on now turns the other off explicitly — both booleans could previously be true at once, showing whichever the panel tested first. The view carries its own depressed toggle as the way back.

      Its own object list is what dissolves the membership conflict: an object with rows is listed here whether or not it holds an action, so the action-driven Watchlist needed no fourth membership source.

      _draw_index_box() moved from features/variant_switch/ui_helpers.py to utils/index_box.draw_index_box() so the Inspector draws the same boxed slot number without a private cross-package import (ARCH-03); the variant tree re-imports from there and keeps its own spelling.

      Tests: dev/tests/test_material_swap.py (21 cases) — round-trip, disabled rows still claiming, provider publication, the variant-switch skip, shared-mesh isolation, single-user objects keeping DATA, stale rows writing nothing, and reads never raising on a deleted object.

    6. 🟢 Rows belong to a VIEW LAYER, not the file. bpy.types.ViewLayer.tks_material_swaps (precedent: ViewLayer.tks_camera_cuts, features/cameras/multicam_properties.py:150). The World carrier added in the first cut is gone from utils/store_world.py. swap_entries(), find_entry(), ensure_entry(), remove_entry() and owned_slots() all take a view_layer.

      Note this is per VIEW LAYER, not per TAKE: a take is a record inside the take set of a view layer (ops_versions._TAKE_COPY_FIELDS), so takes of the same view layer share its swaps — the same granularity the Watchlist has.

    7. 🟢 The write-once model is retired; there is a switch pass. A material slot is file data, so "per view layer" has to mean the active layer's rows are the ones written. logic.apply_for_view_layer(scene, vl) reverts every OTHER layer's rows to their stored original, then applies this layer's on top. Total and idempotent, still no snapshot and no cache — every row carries its own original, so the pass needs no memory of what the last layer did. Never raises: it sits in the switch path.

      Hooks: VL_SWITCH_POST_CASCADE (after the cascade, so the swap has the last word), plus batch_pipeline.py and batch_render_phases.py right after their apply_variant_cascade calls, so a render of many layers is correct per layer.

      true_original() closes the trap this opened. A row created while ANOTHER layer's swap is on screen would otherwise record that material as its original, and the two layers would slowly trade looks. A sibling row for the same slot already knows the answer, so it is asked first.

      Both providers now take arguments, so every call site uses get_provider() and its own try/except — query() would invoke them with none, swallow the TypeError and answer None, which reads as "feature torn down" and would paint over every swap (the trap test_cameras_feature_seam pins).

    8. 🟢 The switch seam the first per-VL cut missed, and a trace to see it. operators/context/ops_crud_switch.py switches the view layer through the operator, which sets is_applying=True and so ABORTS the depsgraph handler — VL_SWITCH_POST_CASCADE is never emitted there and the feature's subscriber never ran. A swap made in one view layer stayed on screen in every other. Still Mode is called from that same block for exactly this reason; the swap pass now sits beside it, after the variant apply.

      Pinned by test_every_switch_path_applies_the_swaps (parametrised over the operator switch and both batch paths) and test_the_providers_are_fetched_not_called_by_name, which reads the source rather than the behaviour — a forgotten seam leaves every behavioural test green.

      New trace: topic VARIANT, subtopic swap (pref log_sub_variant_swap, Preferences ▸ Debug ▸ VARIANT ▸ Material Swap). logic._mlog() records the pass entry with the layer and scene, every revert and apply with the slot, both materials and the slot link, and every reason a write was declined. Both entry points announce themselves, so the log says whether the event or the operator drove it.

      EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 856 → 857 for the new pref; the annotation guard in preferences/__init__.py caught the omission at register time.

    9. 🟢 Rows mirror the object's material slots. logic.sync_rows_to_slots() gives an entry exactly one row per slot; the add-object operator calls it, and tks.msw_refresh_slots re-reads after the object gains or loses a slot. Growing the list from draw would be a write from draw code, so rows_match_slots() reports the mismatch and the view offers the re-read instead. tks.msw_add_row / tks.msw_remove_row are gone.

      A row is therefore not a claim. owned_slots() counts only rows that name a material AND are switched on.

    10. 🟢 BEFORE is a live reading, not a keepsake. User ruling: "the before state should always show the material that was applied manually or by the variant switch". logic.base_material(obj, row) reads the slot itself whenever this row's swap is not the thing on screen, and falls back to the stored original only while it is (when the slot can only answer with the after). refresh_base() records it during the pass, at the one moment every other layer's swap has just been taken off.

      This is why a switched-off row had to stop claiming its slot: the Variant Switch has to be able to paint it, or there is nothing for the BEFORE to follow.

      take_swap_off_screen() replaces the pass's blind revert_row(): it puts the original back only when the slot actually holds THIS row's swap material. The blind revert would have clobbered whatever the user or the Variant Switch put there while the row's swap was not even on — the exact material the new rule exists to keep.

    11. 🟢 Funnel filter. TKS_UL_MSWRows.filter_items() honours wm.tks_msw_only_swapped; every slot being listed is what makes a swap one click, and the funnel is what keeps a heavy object readable.

    12. 🟢 Drift badge. The row alerts when the slot holds neither the base nor the swap material — something outside the feature repainted it, and both halves of the pair would otherwise be lying.

      EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT unchanged here: tks_msw_only_swapped is a WindowManager property, not an addon preference.

    13. 🟢 The rows follow the slots by themselves. panels/inspector/sync.sync_swap_rows() runs from the Inspector's sync TIMER (handlers._sync_timer, the same place _poll_slot_removal already writes) and from force_sync_inspector, gated on the Swap List being the visible content. A timer is not a depsgraph handler, so this does not breach Constitution 2, and sync_rows_to_slots compares two counts and returns at once on every call but the rare one.

      The "material slots changed" warning and tks.msw_refresh_slots are gone with it. The funnel moved from the Materials header into the list's own sidebar column, where the object list keeps its buttons.

    14. 🟢 A base is a reading, never a keepsake — the bug that broke variants. Reported: "If I switch vl and then make a variant switch, the other 'before' material is still overriding the variant switch." Two causes, both now fixed:

      • true_original() handed a NEW row whatever base some other view layer's row had stored. That burned one take's old material into the new row, and it was later written back over the material the Variant Switch had just painted. It now reads the slot, and consults another layer's row only when that layer's swap is the thing on screen this moment.
      • sync_row() wrote the stored base back unconditionally when a swap was switched off, repainting whatever the user or the Variant Switch had put there.
