Every such site (sync_row, remove_row, remove_entry, the shrink half of sync_rows_to_slots) now goes through take_swap_off_screen(), which writes only when the slot actually holds THIS row's swap material.

      Pinned by four tests, including test_leaving_a_take_does_not_repaint_a_variant_material, which walks the exact reported sequence.

    15. 🟢 A stale row is now a blink, not a state. The row sync sat behind _cache._inspector_dirty in handlers._sync_timer, and removing a material slot does not always trip that flag — so a row whose slot was gone simply stayed, reading "Slot is gone - fix the row" next to no way of fixing it (there is no per-row button, by design). It now runs BEFORE the gate: two integer comparisons per listed object, cheap enough per tick. Wording is plain "Slot removed", since it clears itself.

      test_the_timer_syncs_the_rows_even_when_nothing_flagged_it_dirty reads the source and fails if the call drifts back behind the gate.

    16. 🟢 A deleted object is the one case the sync cannot clear — there is nothing left to compare its rows against. The view says so once, above the list, and names the cure (the object list's minus). Previously every row drew its own identical error and none of them named a way out.

    17. 🟢 A moved slot carries its swap. logic.detect_slot_move() reads the reorder by the material each row expects to find - a slot carries no identity of its own, so that is the only handle there is. When every slot matches exactly one row the move is unambiguous and apply_slot_move() rewrites the rows into the new order; when it is not (two slots holding the same material) it answers None and nothing moves, because a half-read reorder would point a swap at the wrong surface.

      panels/inspector/sync.sync_swap_rows() now walks EVERY view layer of the scene, not just the one on screen: the slot belongs to the object, so one reading of the move is applied to all takes at once or they end up disagreeing about which row owns which slot. It also does the count-sync for every layer for the same reason.

      logic._suspend_row_updates guards the rewrite - the row properties carry an update callback that writes the object, and without the flag it would have repainted the mesh halfway through the shuffle from values not yet in their final places.

    18. 🟢 Both lists are in List Heights. list_rows_swap_objects / list_rows_swap_rows (+ their override_ toggles) under Inspector, and swap_view.py resolves both through get_list_rows(). EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 857 → 861.

      Guarded from the other side too: the auditor gained MAINT-16 (List Height Not Configurable), which reads every template_list call and flags a literal or missing rows=. It scans 22 lists in Takes and names the one that is still frozen (preferences/draw_data_storage.py:280).

    19. 🟢 A removed slot takes its row with it. The shrink half of sync_rows_to_slots dropped the LAST row, so removing a slot in the middle left every later row describing its neighbour's slot - a swap set on the removed slot appeared to survive, one row up.

      detect_slot_move generalised into detect_slot_mapping(): one entry per CURRENT slot, naming the row that belongs there or -1 for a slot no row describes yet. Rows nobody names are the removed ones. apply_slot_mapping() rebuilds the rows from it, so a move, an insert and a removal are one mechanism. sync_swap_rows reads it once per object and applies the same answer to every view layer; when no take can read it (two slots holding the same material) the count-only sync runs instead - dumb about identity, never wrong about it.

    20. 🟢 tks.msw_remove_slot names the blast radius. logic.takes_swapping_slot(obj, slot_index) lists the view layers with a swap there; the operator opens invoke_props_dialog ONLY when more than one would lose one, since one take or none is a plain edit and a dialog would be noise.

      Blender's own minus button is NOT intercepted. Overriding object.material_slot_remove would take that operator away from every other add-on. The Swap List's own remove is the way in that can warn; the native path still drops the swaps cleanly (entry 28) and logs it, and Ctrl+Z is the recourse.

    21. 🟢 One picker, four contents, drawn everywhere. inspector_sections.draw_content_toggles() + active_inspector_content() are the single source; panel.py (both channel modes) and swap_view.py call it instead of drawing one button each. Watchlist had NO button at all (it is what shows when the flags are off), Slotted was a separate toggle, and each view drew only its own way back - so the third content was two clicks away.

      tks.toggle_inspector_mode gained WATCHLIST and SLOTTED and now SETS the content for all four instead of flipping a flag: clicking the content you are in is a no-op rather than a way to blank the panel.

    22. 🟢 The native Move Up did nothing to the swaps. detect_slot_mapping() refused to read anything when two entries looked alike, and two EMPTY slots look alike - which is most objects. Rewritten to read ONE GESTURE: identity, a two-place exchange (move), a vanished place (removal) or a new place (insert), each by prefix/suffix comparison. Duplicates elsewhere in the list no longer block it; several changes at once still answer None, because that is not a gesture and a guess would move a swap onto the wrong surface.

    23. 🟢 IndexError from the shared slot mapping (user-reported traceback, once per sync tick). The mapping is read once and shared with every view layer - correct, since a take whose swaps are not on screen cannot read the change itself - but its values index the rows of the entry it was read FROM. A take that joined the list later holds a shorter row list, and the lookup walked off the end.

      sync_swap_rows now records the source entry's row count and shares the mapping only with entries that match it; the rest fall back to the count-only sync. apply_slot_mapping bounds-checks each index and treats an out-of-range one as a fresh row - a function reached from a timer must not be able to throw.

      Full write-up: doc/troubleshooting/material_swap_mapping_index_error.md.

    24. 🟢 A removed slot parks its swap instead of discarding it. TKS_MSW_Object.orphans holds rows whose slot went, and apply_slot_mapping moves a dropped row there whenever it carried a swap material (a row with none is a slot nobody touched — nothing to ask about). Per view layer, so three takes swapping one slot park three.

      Blender's own minus button still cannot be intercepted, so the swap cannot be SAVED from the removal. Throwing it away is a decision though, and it belongs to the user — the Swap List shows the parked swaps as a pending change rather than reporting the loss after the fact.

    25. 🟢 Two ways out. logic.accept_orphan() / tks.msw_accept_orphan lets it go; logic.reassign_orphan() / tks.msw_reassign_orphan copies it onto another slot's row and applies it, asking which slot through invoke_props_dialog (a scripted caller names slot_index and reaches execute() directly — Constitution 7).

    26. 🟢 The lost-swap report moved into the nav warning system. First cut drew its own strip at the foot of the Swap List, which only reached a user already looking at that view - and a swap can be lost in a take that is not on screen. It is a pending change like any other, so it follows the house pattern: warnings/material_swap_orphans.draw_material_swap_orphans beside variant_conflicts, badge tks_show_swap_orphans in the nav header, collected by logic.collect_orphans() (pure read, never raises), grouped per view layer, with the same row_label / diff_pair / value_button_row widgets every other warning uses.

      The operators gained scene_name / vl_name / object_name (_OrphanTarget): a warning row can name a take that is not selected, and the Swap List's own selection says nothing about it. Names, never pointers (Constitution 1).

    27. 🟢 Restore is the strongest answer to a lost swap. logic.restore_orphan() grows the material list by one, shifts the tail down by plain assignment and drops the parked material back at its old index, then re-attaches the swap. Clearing the list and rebuilding it would be shorter and would discard every object-level material and link flag on the way. When the object has since shrunk past that index it lands at the end - restored somewhere is honest; refusing because the old place is unreachable is not.

    28. 🟢 Bulk pair in the title row. tks.msw_restore_all / tks.msw_accept_all walk collect_orphans() and settle index 0 until the list empties (walking by position would skip every other entry as the list shortens). Placed right-aligned in the warning header with alert=False, the house position for panel-level actions.

      The reconcile moved into the feature. follow_slots() now lives in features/material_swap/logic.py; panels/inspector/sync.sync_swap_rows is a forwarder. Restore needs the same reconcile to give every take a row for the returning slot, and a feature reaching up into panels is the ARCH-01 violation the guard catches.

    29. 🟢 One dropdown per warning row. tks.msw_settle_orphan replaces the three per-row operators, drawn with operator_menu_enum so the chosen answer rides on the operator and the row's scene / view layer / object ride with it - a Menu or a popover carries no target of its own.

      Its items are a literal tuple, never a callback: a dynamic enum has to keep its strings alive or Blender dereferences freed memory (CRASH-07), and there is nothing here to build at runtime. test_the_answers_are_static_enum_items reads the AST and fails if that ever becomes a callable.

      invoke() opens a dialog only for MOVE; RESTORE and ACCEPT are the whole answer already, and a scripted caller reaches execute() directly in every case.

    30. 🟢 The warning groups by the lost SLOT, not the take. orphan_groups() gathers the parked swaps by (scene, object, slot); the panel draws one box per group with the takes inside. A removed slot is one event however many takes were swapping it, and reading it take by take made five takes look like five problems.

    31. 🟢 And restoring it put the slot back once per take. restore_slot() restores through the FIRST take and re-attaches the rest to the slot that came back, so the object grows by one whatever the count. accept_slot() / move_slot() are the same shape. tks.msw_settle_slot carries the group answer in the box header; the per-take dropdown stays inside for the rarer split decision. The panel-wide Restore All / Accept All route through the groups too - they had the same duplication.

    32. 🟢 Settling travels to the take that owns the swap, and nothing paints from outside it. _go_to_its_take() sets window.scene / window.view_layer before RESTORE and MOVE (ACCEPT paints nothing, so it stays put); guarded on a window, since a scripted caller has none.

      entry_is_active() now gates EVERY write: restore_orphan, reassign_orphan and the row update callback. A slot is file data, so applying a row that belongs to another take puts a material in front of the user their take never asked for. test_a_swap_is_never_painted_from_another_take caught exactly that in the update callback, which the first pass had missed.

    33. 🟢 Settling a lost swap goes to the take that owns it first. _OrphanTarget._go_to_its_take() in features/material_swap/operators.py points the window at the swap's own scene and view layer before the settle writes anything.

      Why: a material slot is FILE data, so a swap can only be SHOWN in its own take. Settling one from the warning panel while standing in another take recorded the change and showed nothing - or worse, wrote a material the take on screen never asked for. The warning rows name a take that is often not the one in front of you, which is exactly when this bites.

      Never forced on a caller without a window: a scripted caller has none (Constitution rule 7 / AI-02), so the move is skipped and the settle still records correctly - it just does not paint.

    34. 🟢 An empty slot cannot carry a swap. logic.row_can_swap() reads the BASE, not the live slot - a slot holding an applied swap is not empty, and asking the slot directly would say so. apply_row() refuses when the base is None, and the row draws its picker disabled.

      Why: with nothing in the slot there is nothing to replace and nothing to put back. The "before" half would be blank and the "after" half would be a plain assignment, which is not a swap - and switching it off would leave the slot holding a material the user never put there.

      A swap left on a slot that was emptied afterwards keeps its picker reachable (or it could not be cleared) and draws an alert icon, since it can no longer be applied.

    35. 🔴 The Silence empty state was written and never drawn. features/silence/panels.no_parents_note() existed, three tests in test_silence.py pinned the sentence, the icon and the translator call it uses - and nothing called it. The auditor found it as a MAINT-01 orphan, which is how the gap surfaced at all.

      Wired at both action popovers in operators/cascade/ops_viewlayer_action.py (the ViewLayer tier and the Take tier), on the not _has_parents branch each of them already computed for its own layout decision. A popover with nothing above it drew a bare field, which reads as one that failed to load rather than one with nothing to show. A plain INFO line, the shape the Multi-Cam block uses for "No cuts yet" - never enabled = False, which swallows the tooltip with it.

      The text constant INFO_SILENCE_NO_PARENTS was already in texts/tooltips_silence.py, so de_DE needs no new key.

    Changed¶

    1. 🟢 The Colors box shows a colour only while something uses it (operators/misc/ops_tree_design.py). One shape throughout: a switch, then its colour directly beneath, drawn only when that switch is in a mode that paints. The child row is always labelled "Color" -- it sits under its owner, and repeating the owner's name is what truncated every label to "Active View La...". The width row is now "Strip Width" and sits under both its owners, because the tag strip and the mark both paint at it.

    Preferences greys instead of hiding, and that difference is deliberate (preferences/draw_interface.py): that panel has a search box, and a row that is not drawn is a row the search can never turn up. The old "hiding it would make the section jump height" note is superseded for the popover only.

    1. 🟢 "Width" is now "Strip Width", and it is shared. The tag strip and the shared-action mark both paint at TAG_STRIP_UNITS, so the row belongs to neither one: it sits under both and stays live while either does. Same reasoning as the untagged_gap() fix in Added entry 2 -- one width, two owners, and every place that asked about only the first was wrong.

    2. 🟢 The Tree Icon Pie acts on the ACTIVE VIEW LAYER by default (tree_icon_pie_source, ACTIVE_VL | TREE, default ACTIVE_VL).

    It shipped reading active_item(wm, "CONTEXT") -- the tree's blue bar -- which was a deliberate choice and is still the richer answer, since the highlight reaches Scene, Group and Take rows too. But the pie is thrown in the VIEWPORT, where the reader's "current thing" is the layer Blender is showing them and the sidebar may not be open at all. The tree answer becomes the opt-in.

    The ACTIVE_VL path never looks at the tree. _active_vl_values() builds the whole target from context.scene / context.view_layer: tier is always VL, the layer names itself, its scene names itself, and group_name / take_index / group_type are empty because a view layer belongs to no group row and holds no take index. Those are the only five fields any of the eight popovers can ask for, so no row lookup happens and there is nothing to miss -- hence no fallback entry, and a test (test_the_active_view_layer_path_never_touches_the_tree) that fails if an active_item or tks_all_viewlayers walk creeps back in.

    (A tks_all_viewlayers walk would in fact have worked -- tree_sync builds every row and collapsing only sets is_expanded -- but it is work the answer does not need.)

    poll and draw share one resolver. Both go through _pie_target(). Two sources make "polls open on the tree's row, then draws the view layer's" easy to write by accident; a test asserts draw resolves no row of its own. On ACTIVE_VL the poll effectively always passes -- there is always an active view layer -- so only TREE can still answer no.

    1. 🟢 _slot_label reads TREE_ICON_PIE_SLOT_ITEMS, not tks_overflow_active_prop. The wm enum names the seven cascade props and never will name Still Mode, which is not one. The slot-items list is the same table the eight preference dropdowns are built from, so a slice and the dropdown that configures it now read one word by construction. The old enum lookup stays as a fallback. All eight labels were already in de_DE.

    EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 855 -> 856 for the new preference (preferences/__init__.py); the guard caught the omission on the first headless run, as designed.

    dev/scripts/i18n_extract.py learned to read the new item table. An enum items= constant only resolves by NAME inside the module that assigns it, and every preference item list lives in addon_prefs_constants.py while the properties using them live in preferences/props/. Most of those labels happen to be written somewhere else too, so the gap had stayed invisible; "Tree Selection" and the two source descriptions are written nowhere else, and their German went straight to test_no_orphan_translations. TREE_ICON_PIE_SOURCE_ITEMS is registered in _TEXT_TABLE_CONSTANTS with slots (1, 2) -- the mechanism that exists for precisely this. Catalog 4306 -> 4309 strings, missing unchanged at 48.

    1. 🟢 Every action popover is 300 px and every row opens with a label column (operators/cascade/_helpers.POPOVER_WIDTH, ui/styles.popover_label_column). 250 px could not hold a label, a field and its button without cutting the name — which is the one thing the row exists to show. Blender takes any width in invoke_popup and the add-on already opened several popovers at 280 and 300, so nothing new is asked of it. The split factor (0.3) and the right-aligned label live in ui/styles because features/parent_state and features/silence both draw the shape and a sibling import between them would be ARCH-02; ui/ is the layer they may both read. popover_spacer() holds the trailing-button column on rows that have no such button, so every field ends on one line — Blender's own popovers do this with a disabled BLANK1.

    2. 🟢 The inherited value moved inside the field (_helpers.draw_action_field). An empty tier used to get an empty field plus a line underneath naming what it inherits: two rows to say one thing, with the answer below the question. Now the empty state swaps widget — a disabled prop() whose placeholder is "NAME (Tier)", plus the picker button that already exists. Disabling it is what keeps it safe: prop_search refuses a name that is not in its list, a plain enabled prop would take anything typed, and that guarantee is worth more than the typing. Checked on 5.2 rather than assumed: UILayout.prop takes placeholder, UILayout.prop_search does not; the argument landed in 4.1, well under the 5.0 floor in the manifest. Applied to ViewLayer, Take, Scene, Scene Group and VL Group; Global has nothing above it, so it keeps the plain search field.

    3. 🟢 Inherit Keys and Pass Down ride the row they govern (features/parent_state/panels.draw_inline_controls). They are settings OF a tier, not facts about the chain, so they sit on that tier's own field row instead of costing a row each: prop_menu_enum(text="", icon=…) for the three-state Inherit — a plain prop insists on printing its value beside the icon, and the icon IS the value — and prop(text="", toggle=True) for Pass Down. draw_parent_keys and its stacked pair of full-width buttons are gone. Global draws no Inherit (nothing above it) and a take no Pass Down (nothing below it), as before.

    4. 🟢 The action popover is the chain, top down. No box around the parents and no heading on it: the popover is already a frame and every row names its own tier, so features/silence/panels.draw_parent_rows draws them straight onto the layout. This row's own tier follows under a hairline (0.15), named by its tier like the rest — TIER_LABELS spells ViewLayer as "View Layer", because core.cascade's labels are identifiers first and a row is read by a person. Under it, one box for everything that ACTS on the chain: Solo / Cascade (draw_view_row) and Push to Selected (_helpers.draw_push_row). A take with no parent above it gets neither the chain nor the box — there is nothing to solo and nothing to inherit, and an empty frame is worse than no frame. Drawn against the concept at https://claude.ai/code/artifact/34d9489c-0b27-4531-bb62-6dea4ea74254

    5. 🟢 Multi-Cam moved onto the camera row (features/cameras/multicam_panels.draw_mode_toggle). It is a setting OF a take, like Inherit and Pass Down on the action row, so it rides that row as an icon toggle instead of costing a labelled Mode row for two states.

    6. 🟢 The camera field becomes a read-out while cutting. A take that cuts has no ONE camera to set, but it has a camera right now: the field is drawn disabled, showing engine.active_camera_name() — rules.camera_at_frame over this take's cuts, falling back to the scene camera when no cut has happened yet, which is what Blender would be showing anyway.

    7. 🟢 A cut is drawn as what it is: a marker (draw_cut_rows). The row label is the marker's OWN name (engine.marker_name_at), not an invented "Cut 3" that would drift the moment somebody renamed it in the timeline. Right-aligned like every other row label, because Blender cannot right-align a text field and one column reading differently costs more than a click. No unbind button either: prop_search draws its own clear X, and a cut with no camera is exactly an orphan marker again. No end column: a cut runs until the next one starts, so the end was the number on the row below.

    8. 🟢 Orphan markers get a menu, not a popup (TKS_MT_OrphanMarkers). A popup would close the popover it was opened from, and this list is read while looking at the cut list beside it; context_pointer_set hands the menu its take the same way the Inherit menu is handed its tier. A marker outside the take's frame range can be deleted but never added — a cut there would never play. tks.multicam_orphan_add writes the cut straight onto the collection with an EMPTY camera, because set_cuts normalises empty cameras away (correctly: a cut with no camera must never reach the timeline).

    9. 🟢 Clear All confirms first (tks.multicam_clear_orphans). invoke_confirm(title, message, confirm_text, icon) — checked on 5.2, and its icon enum is a different one from prop()'s, which is why WARNING is valid there and not in a layout. Cuts are untouched; the count is in the title.

    10. 🟢 One rename for both names (tks.multicam_rename_cut). The camera object and the marker are two names for one moment in the edit. Renaming the object goes through repair_cascade_refs, which now ALSO repoints tks_camera_cuts[].camera — before this, renaming a camera silently broke every cut pointing at it: the take kept a name no object answered to and the render just skipped the cut. That bug predates this branch.

      No Adopt button anywhere: a marker with a camera bound to it IS a cut, so the list shows it. Concept: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/34d9489c-0b27-4531-bb62-6dea4ea74254

    11. 🟢 A popover only ever changes the row it was opened on. Every camera operator called apply_for_switch unconditionally, so editing a cut on a take that is not on screen stamped that take's cuts over the timeline in front of the user. The timeline is written only when the addressed take is the active one; everything else is a record change. The four that touch markers directly refuse and name the take to switch to, because a marker can only exist on the timeline you are looking at. Silence had the same fault and worse: reapply() rebinds what the WINDOW shows, not the row the operator was given, so a borrow aimed elsewhere set a note nothing applied AND re-swept the active take.

    12. 🟢 Multi-Cam settles itself on a switch (engine.demote_if_single). Multi-Cam means cutting BETWEEN cameras; a take left with one camera -- or none -- is a single-camera take wearing the wrong hat, with its camera field hidden behind a read-out of cuts that cut to nothing. Switching away is when the user is done with that take, so that is when the flag is settled: after adopt_markers has read its own timeline edits back, so a second camera added in the Timeline counts. Distinct CAMERAS, not cuts -- A to A is not a cut. The take being entered is asked the same question, which clears a flag left on by an earlier session.

    13. 🟢 Multi-Cam counts markers, not different cameras, so two cuts to one camera stay a real edit Counting DIFFERENT cameras threw the user's work away: one of those markers is usually about to be repointed, and cutting back to a camera you already used is ordinary film grammar. Counted on the RAW collection and not cut_list(), which normalises every cameraless row away -- so two fresh markers had counted as none.

    14. 🟢 Adding a marker binds no camera, except the first one on a take, which opens on the camera you are looking at Binding the current camera to every marker made each one a cut from A to A, which is not a cut, and the user then had to undo a choice they never made. A take still has to start on something, and that something is already chosen.

    15. 🟢 Cut markers are named cut_ wherever they are made, not after the camera bound to them A marker called after its camera is a name that is wrong the first time the row is repointed. Worth saying because it LOOKS like a rename and is not: the Timeline draws a camera-bound marker with its camera's name whatever the marker is called. The stored name is untouched, and it is the stored name every list in the add-on shows.

    16. 🟢 Add lands on the next free frame when the one asked for is taken, instead of refusing Blender would stack the new marker invisibly under the old one. The user asked for a marker, not for an argument. Forward and not nearest: a moment being moved is being moved LATER far more often than earlier, and a rule that sometimes went back would be impossible to predict from the number you typed.

    17. 🟢 Typing a frame on a cut row steps it over another row on that frame, and a row with no camera takes its marker with it normalise_cuts keeps one cut per frame, so two rows sharing one meant a cut thrown away the next time the timeline was written -- silently, which is the worst way to lose one. Plain markers are still not in the way: a camera outranks a note.

    18. 🟢 Opening the camera popover reads the timeline back, so a marker dragged there shows up in the list straight away adopt_markers() in the popover's invoke(). Not a handler: Constitution rule 2 keeps handlers read-only, because a persisted write from inside one desynchronises the undo stack. It also pulls any stacked markers apart FIRST -- camera_markers keeps one cut per frame, so reading a stacked timeline quietly threw a cut away and left a tidy list that was wrong.

    19. 🟢 Every tier popover draws a line under its title, and the Multi-Cam list has one above and below it Nineteen seams, one shape: Action, Camera, World, Compositor at every tier, plus Automation Rule, Timeline Settings, Variant, Tags and the preset editors. A folder-shaped search found only the cascade ones, so dev/tests/test_popover_title_seam.py is shaped like the RULE instead -- it walks every file in the add-on and lists by name the seven message lines that are not headings.

    20. 🔴 The Global popover row draws the canonical column order. panels/popovers/draw_global.py kept its own order — Still, Render, Variant, … — putting Render two columns from the left while every tree row draws it last, and reserving nothing for the tag column. It sits directly above the tree and sizes itself with _right_side_width(wm) for alignment, so the mismatch was visible. Now walks TREE_COLUMNS; guarded by test_global_popover_row_matches_the_tree.

    21. 🔴 The split take row's note button moved into the tag column. Takes carry no tag, so the tree lends that column to the feedback note (draw_layers.py:draw_take). TKS_UL_SplitTakes drew the same button LAST instead, so the identical control sat in two different places depending on which view was open.

    22. 🔴 Six column buttons that the row menu already reached are gone. Round 2 gave the row actions a home in the menu and trimmed the takes tree's own column to +, - and move. Five other columns kept their copies, so each duplicate sat directly beside the row-menu button that contained it:

    23. tks.merge_scene_group, tks.retarget_scene, tks.retarget_vl_group, tks.retarget_viewlayer — panels/context/draw_split.py. All four are the menu's Retarget entry: tks.global_retarget routes to tks.retarget_tree_item, whose one _typed_op table maps SCENE → retarget_scene, VL → retarget_viewlayer, VL_GROUP → retarget_vl_group and SCENE_GROUP → merge_scene_group. Merge was not a gap in the menu; it was the scene-group branch of Retarget all along.

    24. tks.tag_retarget_group — panels/tag_library_ui/draw.py. The TAGS family lists tks.global_retarget, which routes to it. Its enabled bookkeeping went too: the dispatcher's poll asks the same question.
    25. tks.vsw_duplicate_product — features/variant_switch/panel.py. The VARIANTS family lists tks.global_duplicate, which routes to it.

    The column button was also the WORSE door: only a Menu entry prints the shortcut, so each duplicate taught nothing and the menu entry stayed the one nobody found.

    tks.group_scenes and tks.group_vls were examined and KEPT — both draw with icon='ADD' and are their list's + button, not a second Group door. tks.multiselect in the variant panel was examined and kept too: it is a depress= mode indicator, and a menu entry cannot show state.

    Guarded by dev/tests/test_list_row_menu.py::test_no_panel_redraws_a_dispatcher_target, which walks the dispatcher chain TRANSITIVELY (Ctrl+G → global_group → group_or_ungroup → group_scenes; one hop would have missed it) and fails on any panel button drawing a routed operator that is not in _COLUMN_KEEPS. A companion test fails on a stale exemption.

    1. 🔴 Shift+Alt clears a child's rule and preset, and reaches its takes. User ruling 2026-09-14, both halves. The eight Camera and World popovers each carried their own invoke(); they now call _helpers.popover_invoke(), which the Compositor popovers already used.

      What the copies disagreed about, settled: (a) the World copies cleared the rule and preset on children, the Camera copies cleared neither - now both do; (b) none of the eight reached the per-take overrides, while the shared path always did - now all of them do.

      tier_override_props() is the single answer to "which properties does this tier own", read from _registry.CASCADE_TYPES rather than spelled out at each call site. clear_tier_override() clears the triple and counts ONE DATABLOCK ONCE; the old World copies incremented per property and could report three children where one scene had changed.

      _registry.py was stale and is now the source of truth. It said WORLD had no rule property while the World code cleared tks_world_rule on four tiers. It also gained preset_prop, with a note on where presets actually live.

      Phantom properties found, not yet removed. tks_scene_camera_preset, tks_scene_world_preset, tks_global_camera_preset and tks_global_world_preset are registered on nothing - no Scene, no ViewLayer, no master scene - and nothing ever writes them. Presets exist only on the PropertyGroup tiers (SG, VLG, TAKE). Every read of those four names is therefore always empty, which makes the matching clauses in core/cascade_queries.py (scene_has_camera, scene_has_world, global_has_camera, global_has_world) dead branches. The new tier_override_props() does not carry the phantoms forward; the stale reads in cascade_queries.py are left for their own change so this one stays inside the twins card.

    2. 🔴 The clear report is the shared sentence. Twenty per-property English strings retired in favour of the three parameterised ones the Compositor tier already used ('Cleared {lower} override', 'Cleared {lower} on {count} child' / children). The twenty matching German entries went from texts/locales/de_DE.py in the same commit - test_i18n_guard.py::test_no_orphan_translations fails otherwise, and caught exactly this.

      Cost: the report no longer names the group or scene it cleared ("Cleared camera override", not "Cleared camera on Scene Group 'Hero'"). That is the wording every other cascade tier already gave.

    Fixed¶

    1. 🟢 The Diff State marks scan is dropped when the take switch finishes. features/diff_state/states.py cached the marked-object scan under (dirty, frame), and invalidate_scan() had exactly one caller in the addon: the depsgraph handler in features/diff_state/cache.py. Diff State subscribed to no event-bus event, while VL_SWITCH_POST_CASCADE already had four listeners. The switch defers its cascade (vl_switch.py registers _deferred_post_switch on a 0 ms timer), so the viewport repaints with the new view layer before the actions are swapped; that repaint marked objects still wearing the previous take's actions and set dirty = False. Whether a later depsgraph_update_post arrived before the next repaint was a race, hence the intermittency. Second defect: the view layer was absent from the key although the scan documents itself as scoped to one — probed directly, scanning TAKE_A then setting window.view_layer = TAKE_B returned the identical dict object. Same family as af41a8f (stale watchlist). Fix: subscribe _on_vl_switch_post() to VL_SWITCH_POST_CASCADE in features/diff_state/ __init__.py (invalidate + signal_redraw(), never area.tag_redraw()), and add 'where' = (scene.name, view_layer.name) to the scan key — names, not as_pointer(). Gating the store on TKS_VL_STATE.addon_is_mutating was tried and dropped as unnecessary: guard 1 covers the same window, and the flag is held across a file load until _deferred_load_apply lowers it 200 ms later (a documented LOCK-OK gate, cited by the auditor's own CORR-18 rule text), so the gate would only have cost a per-draw rescan while it was up. See doc/troubleshooting/diff_state_stale_marks_after_vl_switch.md.

    2. 🟢 Picker: the Rest Action and the tier's inherited action are drawn disabled, not removed. operators/cascade/_picker.forbidden_action_names() is the single rule; menus_picker.TKS_MT_CascadePicker.draw() renders a forbidden entry into a row.enabled = False sub-row, keeping its alphabetical place. Icons come from the meanings the addon already assigns: GHOST_ENABLED for the Rest Action (features/rest_state/panels.py:34, ops_action_rest.py:42), LIBRARY_DATA_INDIRECT for an inherited value (37 existing uses). Per-row tooltip text comes from a dynamic TKS_OT_SetCascadeProp.description() classmethod — layout.operator() takes no tooltip argument, so that classmethod is the only route, and a disabled button still shows a tooltip.

    Removal was the first shape and was rejected. An action that disappears from the picker reads as an action that was deleted; that trades one confusion for a worse one (user ruling 2026-09-10).

    Only the cascade WINNER is marked, not every action assigned further up the chain (user ruling 2026-09-10). With Global=Idle and Scene=Walk, a VL row's only no-op pick is Walk; pinning Idle at VL is a legitimate explicit choice and hiding the whole ancestor chain would remove it. forbidden_action_names() therefore returns the inherited entry ONLY when the tier's own prop is empty — with an override present, _helpers._resolve_effective_name() returns that override, and greying it would grey the row's own current value.

    The refusal is {'WARNING'} + CANCELLED, not {'ERROR'}. {'ERROR'} makes bpy.ops raise RuntimeError, which none of the three sibling refusals in the same execute() do and which would surprise any caller not wrapped in a try. Caught by the first test run.

    bl_description was dropped from TKS_OT_SetCascadeProp. Blender always calls description() once it exists, so the constant became unreachable text — dev/tests/test_tooltip_key_names.py::test_no_new_shadowed_constant caught it (46 vs baseline 45).

    Constitution rule 7 (agent drivability): ai/api._write_override() calls forbidden_action_reason() before dispatching to the operator, so a scripted caller reads the reason plus a hint naming clear_override(), rather than engine setter returned ['CANCELLED']. Its op_kwargs keys map 1:1 onto the helper's parameter names, so **op_kwargs is the whole call.

    Auditor delta: no new scored finding. One new Merge-Candidates row (operators/cascade/_action_props.py, R-TINY-LONELY + R-STUB) that duplicates the identical existing row for _camera_props.py — the house pattern this file mirrors. Score unchanged at 7.4.

    1. 🟢 The six action prop_search fields search a filtered collection. _helpers.action_prop_search() mirrors camera_prop_search(): refill WindowManager.tks_filtered_actions (new TKS_ActionItem PropertyGroup in operators/cascade/_action_props.py) at draw time with only the names the tier may take, then prop_search against that instead of bpy.data.actions. Sites: ops_action_levels.py GLOBAL/SG/VLG/SCENE, ops_viewlayer_action.py VL/TAKE.

    No hand-typed hole — measured in 5.2, 2026-09-10. The plan carried an accepted hole here on the belief that prop_search writes whatever is typed, matched or not, and a write guard on all six tks_action properties was scoped as the eventual fix. Probed in-app instead: typing the Rest Action's exact name into the field shows no match and Enter does nothing. Blender's prop_search REFUSES a value absent from its collection, so filtering the collection IS the guard and no property-level write guard is needed. Every route through tks.set_cascade_prop (picker click, ai/ facade, scripted bpy.ops) was already airtight; the field now matches it.

    Tests: dev/tests/test_picker_forbidden_actions.py (17 cases across the rule, the greyed list, the icons, the tooltip, the refusal, the facade, both fields). Roadmap card doc/roadmap/active/picker-hides-inherited-and-rest.md.

    1. 🟢 Rest State Mode's ghost badge belongs to the ACTIVE view layer row. Rest State Mode is a read-time override: core/cascade.py:324-334 short-circuits resolve_cascade(ACTION, …) to the rest action for EVERY view layer before the tier chain is walked. panels/context/draw_layers._get_vl_cascade_status() derived is_ref from that overridden answer, so while the mode was on every VL row read as "assigned the rest action": GHOST_ENABLED plus depress=True on all of them (draw_layers.py chip, and lists_context.py for the alternate VL list). The tree stopped saying what each tier actually held — the one thing the action column is for.

      Fix: the row's OWN assignment is the RAW resolution (raw=True skips the override). _get_vl_cascade_status now also publishes is_ref_raw, rest_mode and own_icon — per-row facts only. The badge decision itself is rest_badge_for_row(cs, is_active_vl): true when the row really holds rest, OR the mode is on and this is the active view layer row. Non-active rows fall back to own_icon (the Parent State glyph via tree_layout_calc.row_state_icon, else ACTION) with sub.active = False.

      Active-ness is decided at the DRAW site, never cached. _vl_cascade_cache is keyed (scene.name, vl.name) with a ~200 ms TTL and no notion of which view layer is active; folding is_active_vl into the cached dict would survive a VL switch and badge the wrong row for a redraw or two. is_active_vl was already computed at draw_layers.py:707, in scope at the chip — no hoist, no new parameter.

      Cost. The second resolve_cascade runs only while the mode is on (with it off the raw and overridden answers are identical by definition), and only on a cache MISS, reusing the already-resolved gctx. row_state_icon is now called unconditionally, which is exactly what the mode-off path already did for every row, so the worst case does not grow (ARCH-05).

      cs['is_ref'] is deliberately unchanged — lists_context.py:224 reads it, and retiring the key silently is a cross-module break nothing would catch.

      Both VL drawers go through the one helper; a fix in only draw_layers.py would have been half a fix. Non-VL tiers (take, scene, scene group, VL group, global) were never part of this: they test their own stored string, so they ghost only where the user assigned rest by hand, which IS their assignment.

      The driven row is its own STATUS CHIP (tks.rest_badge, in features/rest_state/mode.py), reached after two wrong turns in the same session. _RestModeGatedPopover.poll returns False for every cascade action picker while the mode is on, so click and Shift-click were inert already — but Blender draws the ICON of every button whose poll refuses dimmed, and layout.active = True does not undo that. First attempt: force active = True on the picker chip — still dim. Second: draw label(text="", icon='GHOST_ENABLED') — bright, but a label cannot carry the blue depressed look, which is what makes it read as the mode's badge. The chip is therefore an operator with NO poll: bright, depress=True, and it answers a click with {'CANCELLED'} plus the sentence the pickers put in their poll message (Constitution 7 — the scripted caller gets the same answer). Its wording moved from an inline literal to texts/tooltips_rest_state.REPORT_REST_MODE_LOCKED with a de_DE entry. rest_drives_row() gates it, narrower than rest_badge_for_row() — a row holding rest by its OWN assignment is not being driven and keeps its picker, as does a row whose rest action is broken (the chip cannot carry the alert state). Rejected: ungating _RestModeGatedPopover so every picker stays bright and refuses on click, the way the Still master lock behaves — it would turn the action chip bright on all five other tiers and flip test_cascade_action_popovers_disabled_in_rest_mode.

      The inheriting tiers ghosted too, and that was the same root cause. draw_scenes (:143, :234) and draw_collections (:166, :251, :447, :537) fall back to get_cached_tier_action(...) when the tier holds no action of its own — the RESOLVED value, which the mode answers as rest for every tier. tree_layout_calc.rest_mode_driving(wm) now gates all six fallbacks. A tier whose own string IS the rest action still ghosts; that is its assignment, not the mode. draw_tree_nodes, the take rows and lists_split read their own string only and were never affected.

      rest_mode in the cell state means "the mode is DRIVING this row" — is_rest_mode() AND a rest action name resolves. With the flag on and no rest action, resolve_cascade never short-circuits, so the tree resolution is the honest one and no badge is owed.

      test_multicam_switch.py::test_every_multicam_icon_name_exists_in_this_blender walks every string constant inside an assignment whose target ends _icon, so the first draft's _own_icon = row_state_icon(vl, 'VL', …) or 'ACTION' reported VL and own_icon as unknown Blender icons. Real guard, not a false positive — the tier argument and the dict key are split onto their own lines rather than the check being loosened. New tests: dev/tests/test_rest_badge_active_row.py (21). Card: doc/roadmap/active/mode-badge-active-row-only.md phase 1; plan doc/roadmap/_dev/mode-badge-active-row-only.md. Confirmed in-app 2026-09-10 on fix/rest-badge-active-row. See doc/troubleshooting/rest_mode_badge_on_every_row.md.

    2. 🟢 The Rest State Mode toggle drops the tree read-model before it repaints. TKS_OT_RestModeToggle called signal_redraw(), but nothing invalidated _vl_cascade_cache — the ~200 ms per-(scene, view layer) read-model the tree icons come from. The repaint therefore re-read the pre-toggle answer, and the tree only caught up when the sync timer next fired, which in practice meant "when the user moved the mouse". The toggle now calls cache_registry.invalidate("vl_cascade") and ("rest_state") before signal_redraw(). Through the registry, not a direct import: features/ must not reach up into panels/. Confirmed in-app 2026-09-10.

    3. 🟢 The Still master lock badge belongs to the ACTIVE view layer row. The Still twin of Fixed entry 4, and the same shape of bug. features/still_mode/panels._row_winner() short-circuits to the locked value whenever engine.is_still_global() / is_anim_global() is on, and draw_still_button() drew the blue depressed lock chip unconditionally under engine.master_active() with no row identity available at all. So the lock flattened the whole timeline column: Global, scenes, groups, view layers and takes all showed one value.

      _row_winner gains raw=False, mirroring resolve_cascade(raw=True) — with raw the two global short-circuits are skipped and the tier chain answers. draw_still_button gains is_active=False; only the view-layer row passes it (panels/context/draw_layers.py:1018), and every other call site — draw_scenes (2), draw_collections (4), draw_tree_nodes (2), the take row, panels/popovers/draw_global.py — keeps the default. Under the lock: the driven row gets today's blue chip, every other row resolves with raw=locked and draws sub.active = bool(own) and not locked, i.e. its own answer, dimmed.

      Unlike the Rest chip, this one needs no status-chip operator: TKS_OT_StillPopover has no poll, so the button was never drawn dim and the lock is enforced inside the popover instead. Nothing about that changed.

      TKS_OT_StillGlobalToggle.execute also never called signal_redraw() — it relied on whatever repaint _reapply() happened to cause. Since the lock now MOVES the badge between rows and takes the other rows from live to dim, it asks for the repaint explicitly (Constitution 3 — never area.tag_redraw()).

      Tests: dev/tests/test_still_lock_active_row.py (9), including a guard that exactly ONE call site claims the active row — two claimants would light two badges, none would light none. test_jit_fold_preserves_bystanders and test_still_global_tier_split::test_master_toggle_from_off_comes_on_as_still fail under a -k still subset; both fail identically on main, so they are pre-existing subset order/state pollution, not this change. Card: doc/roadmap/active/mode-badge-active-row-only.md phase 2. Confirmed in-app 2026-09-10.

    4. 🟢 The Still lock toggle asks for the repaint. Split from Fixed entry 6 because it is its own user-visible effect. TKS_OT_StillGlobalToggle.execute relied on whatever repaint _reapply() happened to cause; now that the lock MOVES the badge between rows and takes the other rows from live to dim, it calls signal_redraw() explicitly (Constitution 3 — never area.tag_redraw()). No cache invalidation is needed here: the Still icons are resolved live per draw, not out of _vl_cascade_cache. Confirmed in-app 2026-09-10.

    5. 🟢 Multi-Cam can be switched on again. Toggling it ran the same check that turns it off on a take with one camera apply_for_switch runs the moment the mode comes on, when the take has one camera at most, so the demotion undid the toggle under the user's finger. It now lives inside the "did the take actually change?" branch, and the second half of the rule -- give it up when it never got a second camera -- happens on the popover's cancel(), which is the moment the user has finished deciding.

    6. 🟢 Every marker button in the camera popover works again on the take you are standing in The "is this take on screen?" guard compared Python objects. Blender hands out a fresh wrapper for the same data whenever it likes, so the guard answered "not on screen" for the take the user was in: the row greyed out and the operators refused, naming the take already in front of them. One shared on_screen() compares NAMES, which survive the wrapper being rebuilt.

    7. 🟢 A row with no camera keeps its marker when you drag it in the Timeline or type a new frame The row knew only its frame, so a moved marker was lost and the row handed back to Select for nothing. It records WHICH marker it claimed and follows that name; two markers sharing a name -- which Blender allows -- is ambiguous and handed back rather than guessed at. Typing a frame now moves the marker too: cut_list drops cameraless rows before the timeline is written, so nothing else could.

    8. 🟢 Answering a row's camera question uses the marker already there instead of making a second one on the same frame The pair then sat stacked -- one in the cut list, one still offered in Select. A bare row IS a marker the take made and the user has now answered, so the camera binds to it. Keyed to the row's own recorded marker: a cut may take over the marker its row holds and no other, because a marker made by hand is not ours to eat. Its name is left alone.

    9. 🟢 A marker you made yourself is never moved or taken over when a take's cuts are written to the timeline A camera outranks a note, so the CUT still goes in -- a cut that silently does not play is worse than two markers on one frame -- but the user's marker stays exactly where they put it, appears in Select, and wears the overlap button that moves it if they want. separate_stacked_markers counts only OUR markers as duplicates for the same reason.

    10. 🟢 The tree's camera chip stops going red on a take that is still being built It counted cut_list(vl), which drops every row with no camera yet -- so a take with markers collected and cameras not chosen read as empty. It counts what the take HOLDS.

    11. 🟢 The parked cut list keeps its row names after Multi-Cam is switched off The labels read the marker on that frame, and switching the mode off takes every marker off the timeline, so the whole list fell through to bare frame numbers and read as a different list. Each row remembers what its marker is called -- recorded for camera rows too -- and the label falls back to that before it falls back to a number.

    12. 🟢 The camera chip turns red the moment a take starts holding cuts it cannot play, instead of after the next unrelated click The tree's per-row status is cached on the "vl_cascade" topic and neither the Still edit nor the Multi-Cam toggle ever fired it. Opening the camera popover happened to wipe the cache, which is why the flag only appeared AFTER clicking the very icon it exists to send the user to. Both seams invalidate before asking for a redraw: a redraw without an invalidation only repaints the stale answer.

    Open, deliberately — design notes on the twin-marking entries in Added, parked here by mistake as a heading; a ### line reads as a new SECTION to release_cut.py and split this list in two.

    • Take rows are not marked. The question this answers is whose action matches the ACTIVE VIEW LAYER's; a take's own action is a separate one.
    • Inherited versus own override both count as carrying the action. A row that merely inherits from a tier above still moves when you key, so it is a twin.

    • A painted number badge stays possible (see entry 3) if the tooltip proves too quiet in daily use.

    • 🔴 The tree counted a 'lock' column that no tier draws. count_icons() in panels/context/tree_layout_calc.py added +1 for getattr(wm, 'tks_show_lock', True), and tks_show_lock is the Inspector's property (panels/inspector/__init__.py, name="Show Lock", default True). No row drawer has ever drawn a lock glyph — grep -n "lock" panels/context/draw_*.py returns comments only. So _right_side_width() reserved one ICON_SLOT_UNITS too many on every row of the tree, and the reserve silently tracked an unrelated Inspector toggle.

    • 🔴 has_unpinned_icons() could never return False. _PIN_MAP carried ('tks_show_lock', 'tks_pin_lock'), and tks_pin_lock was never registered anywhere. getattr(wm, 'tks_pin_lock', False) therefore read False forever while tks_show_lock read True, so the "any visible icon not pinned" test always short-circuited True. The … overflow button was drawn in every collapsed row even with every icon pinned, and count_collapsed_icons() always added its +1. Both flags are gone from the layout maths; dev/tests/test_tree_row_columns.py::test_all_pinned… and ::test_no_phantom_lock_column are the regressions.

    • 🔴 The split-view lists read no visibility flag at all. TKS_UL_ContextScenes, TKS_UL_ContextViewLayers (lists_context.py) and TKS_UL_SplitTakes (lists_split.py) hardcoded their icon strips: no tks_show_*, no tks_pin_*, no collapse, no overflow button, and three different column sets (scene rows lacked Still and Render, VL rows lacked Still, take rows lacked both). All three now guard every column with column_visible(wm, key, collapsed) and carry the … button.

    • 🔴 The split-view rows split their width PROPORTIONALLY, so a narrow panel squeezed the icons to nothing. Every row used layout.split(factor=0.45) (0.55 for the two context lists), which hands the icon strip a SHARE of the row; the icon buttons inside are flexible children dividing that share between them. Inside a template_list, already narrowed by its side button column, the share collapses and the buttons render as nothing at all — reported as "the groups have nothing at all". Every tree row has reserved ui_units_x absolutely since 2026-09-05 for exactly this reason (utils/tree_metrics.py header); the split lists never got the fix. _right_side_width joins _is_collapsed as a module function tree_layout_calc.right_side_width(wm, collapsed) (the UIList delegates), and all five rows now set right.ui_units_x from it.

      Two of the five then read wm and collapsed in that reserve BEFORE assigning them — a NameError on every draw of those rows, which neither an import nor py_compile can see. Guarded now by test_split_lists_assign_before_they_reserve.

    • 🔴 TKS_UL_SplitSceneGroups and TKS_UL_SplitVLGroups were missed entirely. Both shipped with no Still column, no Render, no Hide/Pin obedience and no overflow button while the other three lists had all four. They were missed because _SPLIT_LISTS in test_tree_row_columns.py was HAND-WRITTEN and named three of five — the same failure this change set exists to end, reproduced inside the test meant to enforce it. The test now discovers every class TKS_UL_*(UIList) in lists_context.py and lists_split.py, and its overflow check reads each class's own op.item_type and asserts the popover's _TIER_MAP knows it.

    • 🔴 The split-view multi-select tick grew with the panel. left is a plain row(), and a plain row divides its width EQUALLY between its children — so an unsized checkbox took half the left side and pushed the name along with it. The takes tree never had this: it wraps its tick in ui_list._icon_slot(left), which sets ui_units_x. The five split-view lists drew left.prop(item, "tks_selected", text="") bare. Each now wraps it in a row pinned to ICON_SLOT_UNITS, so only the NAME flexes.

      Measured, not eyeballed (dev/measure/capture_tree_widths.py at 340 / 360 / 400 / 440 / 560 px, worktree build loaded via BLENDER_USER_EXTENSIONS).

      What the rig did NOT reproduce: a growing indent strip in the takes tree itself. A coloured block on the active row measures 14 → 32 px across those widths, which looks like the reported symptom — but it reads IDENTICALLY with tks_vl_icon_style set to BOX, whose marker is a fixed-width icon operator rather than template_node_socket. A metric that cannot tell those two apart is measuring Blender's own row-selection paint, not our widgets. Every left-side element in the tree (open_marker_slot, icon_slot, _gap/reserve_gap, draw_tree_line) already sets ui_units_x on every path, so there is nothing there to fix by inspection either.       left = row_main.row(align=True) has no width of its own, so it grows with the panel — and an EXPANDING row hands its surplus to the items inside it. Every child already sets ui_units_x, which is exactly why this survived so long: by construction the columns are absolute, and they still drifted, because the CONTAINER stretched them. Each fixed column walked right and every gap opened up.

      left.alignment = 'LEFT' makes the row pack at natural size instead. 14 sites: the six takes-tree drawers, the five split-view lists, both inspector object lists and the render queue list. The NAME is the only thing that should grow with the panel, and it still does.

Before: the take row's tick sat at x≈265 at 800 px and x≈395 at 1300. After: identical at both. Worktree loaded via BLENDER_USER_EXTENSIONS so the rig shot this branch.

      Guarded by test_tree_row_columns.py::test_every_left_cluster_packs_instead_of_stretching, which fails on any left = row_main.row(align=True) in panels/ without the alignment beneath it.

      Four trees name their container differently, and one lives in features/: the Variant Switch tree (features/variant_switch/ui_row_renderers.py, 8 row renderers), the Tag Library tree (panels/tag_library_ui/lists.py, 2), and the Process Monitor and Profiler lists (panels/navigation/monitors_pm.py, monitors_profiler.py). It now asks SEMANTICALLY: find every container passed to reserve_gap / _gap, in any module that draws tree indentation, and require <container>.alignment = 'LEFT' in the same function. Scoped to files that import the layout helpers, because _gap is a common enough name that core/camera_link_scan.py has an unrelated one about camera coverage. Verified to bite: all four files had zero alignment = 'LEFT' at the previous commit.

    • 🟢 A tree line points at the chevron it refers to. Two conditions, and entry 23 only met the first.

      Every indent column is one chevron wide. INDENT_PAD_UNITS is derived, (ICON_SLOT_UNITS - STRIP_UNITS) / 2, and both pads are drawn, so a level costs exactly ICON_SLOT_UNITS whatever strip it holds. That retired untagged_gap(), which added the same difference on ONE side.

      The chevron occupies a column of that same width, and a row with nothing to expand RESERVES it. New utils/tree_strip.chevron_slot(). The takes tree already did this via _icon_slot; the Variant Switch tree and both monitor lists drew an unsized row.operator(...) that took its natural width, and the Rules list let a plain tag skip the column entirely while a group header beside it drew a chevron -- which is the report: two rows at the same depth starting at different x, with the line above pointing between them. The separator(factor=3.0) the tag had there instead was proportional as well, so it grew with the panel.

      TAKE_CHEVRON_PAD was the last hand-tuned number in the tree -- INDENT_PAD_UNITS * 1.2, commented "tune to align under VL chevron" -- and therefore wrong the moment the pad was derived. It is 0.0 now: the shared helper places the line in the chevron column by construction.

      Measured (dev/measure/capture_tree_widths.py, 800px). Depth 1 was already right after entry 23. Depth 2 was 40px off and is now 3px: the take row's second strip sits at x=313 against the view layer chevron at x=310, where it sat at x=350 before.

      Two guards: every tree chevron must be drawn into chevron_slot(...) or _icon_slot(...), and no tier may scale a shared metric by hand.

      Not measured: the Rules tree itself. The capture rig only shoots the takes tree, so that half rests on the code change and the reader's eyes.

    • 🟢 One glyph-to-name distance, in every list. The reader asked several times for "the same distance everywhere", and it kept not being one because there was no shared definition: the takes tree had icon_slot plus draw_name_gap, and every other list hand-rolled its own version of the pair.

Callers now: the Rules and Tags list, the variant tree (its three section headers), the process monitor, the profiler, the inspector object list (4 rows), and the takes tree, whose draw_name_gap delegates rather than keeping a second copy.
