    • 🔴 The Variant Switch row icons are a counted, pinned column again. User report 2026-09-12, from a side-by-side with the takes tree: "on the tree list the icons are fixed and right aligned; on the variant switch list they are not all on the right side and not fixed — they change width when I widen the list." Both halves were the traps already recorded in doc/troubleshooting/tree_row_column_alignment.md, which the panel tree learned and the features/ tree never shared.

      Three causes, and the third took a day and a measuring rig to find.

      (0) The cluster's children were PINNED. Every cell inside the fixed cluster carried its own ui_units_x. Each pinned child makes its own size request; those add up beside the cluster's, and the panel's surplus or shortfall is then shared over all of them -- so the block tracked the panel instead of holding, and a narrow panel crushed the six part toggles into one smear. Measured at the reader's REAL scale (effective 1.5: view.ui_scale 0.75 x DPI 108 -- the rig had been forcing 1.0 all day), part-row strip across a 437/587/737px panel: 216 / 265 / 351px.

      The takes tree never does this because its cluster children are UNSIZED -- one plain right.row(align=True) per icon, only the cluster itself sized (panels/context/draw_layers.py). Blender keeps that block whole and divides it. Uncollapsed, at the same scale, its strip measured 376 / 390 / 408 / 389px across a 501..1119px panel: flat. The part row now has that shape -- seven unsized cells (six toggles + collection), cluster = 7 x RIGHT_BUTTON_UNITS, no gap cells -- and its toggles are six clean glyphs from 426px up. Rows of MIXED cell widths (product, material) stay pinned-and-summed; they cannot be divided evenly and were never the smear.

      Two dead ends on the way, both reverted: a separator_spacer() between the halves (3f033742 / 572bbdc6; a third flexible child, the state row landed 624px short at 1300px), and ONE shared width for every row (it paid the difference with a blank cell INSIDE the block, so narrowing squeezed the icons while the pad sat unspent).

      And the comparison itself was wrong for most of the day: tks_collapse_width defaults to 600, not 380 (380 is only the getattr fallback in is_collapsed). Every narrow takes-tree screenshot was the COLLAPSED tree showing three icons. Lists compare only at >= 600px.

      (a) Every renderer opened its cluster with a hand-tuned ui_units_x — 7.5 (PART), 5.5/3.0 (MATERIAL), 7.2/2.5 (PRODUCT), 1.0 (STATE) — none of them derived from the cells drawn inside. A right-aligned box wider than its contents does not push the icons right; the slack is shared out among them. (b) The cells were unsized children, and a row splits itself by what each child asks for. The PART cluster held exactly two: one holding six visibility props, one holding the collection icon. Blender gave each half — six glyphs crushed into 3.75 units, one glyph rattling around in the other 3.75. That is the hole in the screenshot. Same lesson as ICON_SLOT_UNITS in the takes tree's left half. Plus four separator() calls inside the clusters, which size relative to their row, all but vanish inside align=True, and are therefore the only spacing that did move with the panel.

      features/variant_switch/ui_helpers.py gains open_right_cluster() / right_cell() / right_gap() and the units they spend (RIGHT_ICON_UNITS is utils.tree_metrics.ICON_SLOT_UNITS, so both trees pack identically). ui_row_renderers.py rebuilds all four clusters on them; _stats_units() prices the stats block once for the two rows that draw it, and the PART row's six toggles became the _PART_TOGGLES table because the cluster now charges len(_PART_TOGGLES) * RIGHT_ICON_UNITS. The PART toggles and the MATERIAL pool index reserve their columns even when the data does not resolve, or those rows would pull their collection icon left of their neighbours'.

      Not one union width across tiers, the way the takes tree does it: that works there because every tier draws the same icon set, and the Variant Switch tiers genuinely differ (six toggles, a pool-index input, a "LIVE" text badge). Their union is wider than a sidebar. The rows share the right EDGE instead, so the last column lands in the same x on every row and the rest packs leftward.

      Measured by dev/tests/test_vsw_right_cluster.py, which drives the real renderers against a recording layout — reserved == drawn for 4 row types × 4 flag combinations. PART is now 8 cells of 0.85/0.35 summing to 6.30, where it was two children splitting 7.5. These are layout-tree units, not pixels; ui_units_x is a request, and the ~340 px wall documented in the tree record still applies.

      Deliberately out of scope: the rows' LEFT half still pads with separator(factor=) inside align=True rows. Same trap, but the cluster is fixed-width and right-anchored so nothing there can move it, and the report was about the icons. Record: doc/troubleshooting/vsw_right_icon_cluster.md.

    • 🔴 Variant Switch names are SIZED from the region width; the pool selector fills its row. Reader, 2026-09-13: "use the full space available to display the name" -- Pro... trimmed with 190px of empty row beside it.

      Why nothing simpler works, all measured at the reader's scale, 500..1300px: a packed left half (Fixed 14) hands the name a share that scales with the panel and leaves the rest empty; a ui_units_x floor on the name inside it is inert (pixel-identical on/off); unpacking the row with a packed chrome sub-row walks the columns (default 212 -> 258px between 800 and 1000); pinning that chrome to the sum of its columns still walks them (marker 145/150/175px). A pinned child inside an expanding row takes a share of the surplus too. "Columns hold still" and "the name takes the slack" cannot both come from layout flags.

      So the name is computed (_size_name / _name_units in ui_row_renderers.py): region width in units (context.region.width / (20 * system.ui_scale)) minus ROW_OVERHEAD_UNITS (what the region spends around the row: tab strip, list insets, sidebar buttons, scrollbar -- measured a constant 306px across four sidebar widths, 7.65 units at the rig's 40 px/unit, plus half a unit of safety) minus the row's chrome (_chrome_units: every column before the name is already an absolute unit) minus the cluster's price. The left half stays packed, so Fixed 14 holds. Outside a region the name stays unsized. The takes tree built this once (RowBudget) and reverted it as not worth ~50 call sites; this list needs four.

      Calibration lesson. The first pass divided 306px by an ASSUMED 30 px/unit, got 10.2 units, and clamped every name to its minimum. The rig now logs system.ui_scale and px/unit; the constant is derived from the logged value. Same mistake had inflated the toggle price (1.6 -> back to the 1.3 floor). Result at 800px: Product_0 full where it read Prod...; at 1300px base part full where it read base...; default at the same x across 800/1000/1300.

      Overhead sized for the reader's panel, not the rig's. The reader's sidebar has no vertical tab strip (every screenshot ends at the panel's grip); the rig's has five tabs, and that strip is the largest piece of the 7.65 units it measured. ROW_OVERHEAD_UNITS = 5.0. Where a tab strip IS present the name overshoots a little, and Blender trims the pinned name first and leaves the natural-width icons alone -- verified on the tabbed rig 650..1300px: names full from 800px, base part from 1000px, columns still, icons untouched.

      Pool-material row: the selector sits inside the packed row in its own unsized sub-row (the takes tree's name pattern). As a SIBLING of the packed row it did not take all the slack -- a packed container still grows as a container -- and the gap opened between the index box and the field. Verified 650..1300px: the field reaches the list edge and the gap after the index box holds.

      Also: every cluster cell unsized on every row (df6e2b7d), icon_only on the six part toggles, scale_x on the pool-index number field (natural ~2.75 units, priced 2.0), one label for the empty in-use badge. Guards in dev/tests/test_vsw_right_cluster.py. Full suite 4025 passed.

      Superseded the same day by the two-unit rule (1a158f7a). The computed budget failed both ways on the reader's panel: a lower overhead squeezed the icons and changed nothing about the name, the same overhead left a hole, stats on trimmed the product name early, stats off let the material row's folder icon flex. interface_layout.cc explains it: an over-full row scales each child in proportion to its ask, except that no child goes below min(2 units, its own width) -- so a child of two units or less is NEVER scaled, and a cluster wider than that is. Now every right-side icon is its own pinned direct child of the row at <= 2 units (right_cell raises above CELL_MAX_UNITS; a stat's glyph and its number are two cells, 1.05 + 0.55, because an over-full container makes the number OVERLAP the glyph rather than shrink it, and their widths come from shooting main itself at the reader's 30 px/unit -- digits 50px apart in both; the Live column is two cells; the in-use badge spends the same two cells, blank, when unused) and the name asks for NAME_ASK_UNITS = 100 through name_cell(), so the row is always over-subscribed and the name -- the one child Blender may shrink -- is handed exactly the remainder. open_right_cluster, right_gap, cell_units, the _*_units price functions, _size_name, the overhead constant and the budget log are gone. Rig, 600..1300px, stats on and off: folder icons 210-212px from the edge from 850px up, names wider at every width. dev/tests/test_vsw_right_cluster.py rewritten around the rule; the rig gains TKS_RIG_STATS=1 and per-shot overhead / shape arguments. Record: doc/troubleshooting/vsw_right_icon_cluster.md, root cause 6.

    • 🟢 The nav panel stopped drawing halfway down. TKS_PT_Navigation.draw read swap_orphans while nothing bound it - Blender answers a NameError in a draw by ending the panel there, so the sidebar looked partly removed. The assignment never landed: the anchor text a replacement was matched against differed in whitespace, the replace was a silent no-op, and that one was not asserted while the two reads were.

      Guard: dev/tests/test_panel_draw_names.py walks the draw bodies of the navigation and inspector panels for any plain local name read while nothing binds it. Verified by re-deleting the assignment and watching it name the line. Pure AST, no bpy, runnable outside Blender.

      Write-up: doc/troubleshooting/nav_panel_truncated_draw.md.

    • 🟢 The removal warning never fired from another Inspector content. handlers._sync_timer and force_sync_inspector both called sync_swap_rows only while tks_inspector_show_swaps was set, so a slot removed with the Watchlist on screen was never noticed, nothing was parked and the nav warning stayed empty. Parking a swap is DATA, not a view - the gate is gone from both.

      It therefore runs on every tick now, so sync_swap_rows leaves at once unless some view layer in the scene carries swap entries, which is the common case.

      test_the_row_sync_is_not_gated_on_the_swap_list_being_open reads the source: a gate like this is invisible from behaviour whenever the test happens to have the Swap List showing.

    • 🟢 tks.msw_remove_slot raised "Index out of range" (user traceback). Two faults in one line. It took the index from entry.rows_index - a POSITION in the rows list, not a slot - and it guarded on len(obj.material_slots) while popping from obj.data.materials. Near enough to look right, and wrong the moment the two lists differed for a tick.

      Now it reads the highlighted row's own slot_index, guards the collection it actually pops, and reports rather than raising if the pop still refuses.

      And it settles what it removes - by being TOLD, not by detection. Removing from the Swap List is deliberate and the confirm already named every take that would lose a swap, so the row goes with the slot in every take and nothing is parked.

      The first attempt ran follow_slots() and accepted the group it created. That still left the swap on screen: follow_slots() has to work the change out from the materials it can see, and when that reading comes back unreadable - two slots holding the same material, rows that had already drifted - it falls back to trimming the LAST row, so the swap landed on a surviving row and no group was ever parked to accept.

      logic.drop_slot_rows(obj, slot_index) replaces it: the row at that index goes in every take, the rows below renumber, nothing is parked. We removed the slot, so there is nothing to deduce.

      Blender's own minus button is unchanged: nothing there warned anybody, so those swaps are still parked and reported.

    • 🟢 The swap forbade the variant instead of painting after it. "Material Swap overrules" shipped as a veto: _apply_pool skipped every slot material_swap.owned_slots claimed. On a ONE-SLOT object that leaves the Variant Switch nothing to paint at all, and it starved the feature's own rule - the row's BEFORE is defined as what the variant put there, which a slot the variant may not touch can never supply.

      _apply_pool now skips nothing. It calls material_swap.lift_for_view_layer first, pool-swaps, then material_swap.apply_for_view_layer. The LIFT is required: the pool only recognises slots holding a pool material, so a slot wearing a swap from outside the pool is invisible to it and the variant loses that slot for good. pool_resolve dropped its matching exclusion.

    • 🟢 "Is my swap on screen?" was answered by comparing materials, which says yes whenever the variant paints that same material - so the pass kept a stale base and wrote it back over the variant's fresh one. TKS_MSW_Row.applied records it outright; notice_overwrite() clears it when the slot no longer holds our material, the one direction that is safe.

      And the rewrite guard never fired. _suspend_row_updates was a module global, and this feature's logic is held TWICE at once - the flag set in one copy read False in the other, so every update callback ran mid-shuffle and rewrote original from the slot the row had just left. Proven by printing id(module) from both sides after three wrong guesses from the source. The guard now lives on WindowManager.tks_msw_rewriting.

      Write-up: doc/troubleshooting/material_swap_vs_variant_switch.md.

    • 🟢 The shared-mesh protection cut the wire the variant came down. Field case: three objects share one mesh, and _apply_pool reaches only ONE of them - the log shows pool: drawer_S_front[0] ... -> ... and never a single line for .002 or .003. The twins get the variant purely through the mesh.

      _protect_shared_mesh moves a swapped slot to the OBJECT so the swap cannot leak to those twins. That part is right. But base_material() then read the OBJECT side, which is where OUR material sits - so the base froze at whatever the slot wore the day it was flipped, and every variant switch afterwards changed a mesh the row no longer looked at.

      A slot with link_flipped now reads its base from obj.data.materials, where the Variant Switch still writes. refresh_base() follows it there and apply_row() records through base_material() so there is one answer, not three.

      Found by tracing, not by reading: three fixes reasoned from the source were wrong, and the pool: line that names which slots the pool paints settled it in one reproduction.

    • 🟢 The revert wrote a stale base - the "seems not to work all the time" half of the field report. refresh_base() only runs for the ACTIVE take's rows, so a row whose swap was lifted from another take, or was off screen while the Variant Switch painted, kept a row.original from two variants ago. revert_row() then wrote that onto the object.

      It now restores base_material(obj, row) - the base AS IT IS, read from the mesh for a slot this feature moved - and catches row.original up on the way, logging when it does.

      Pinned from both directions: test_leaving_a_take_puts_back_the_variants_CURRENT_material and test_a_take_without_swaps_shows_the_variants_current_material.

    • 🟢 Nothing tagged the object after a swap write. The field log showed the data correct end to end - base following the variant, revert writing the current material - while the user still saw the old material. A material written at DATA level tags the mesh by itself, which is why the Variant Switch never needed this; a material written at OBJECT level, where this feature writes once a slot is moved to protect shared mesh, does not always reach the viewport on its own.

      _tag_object() after every apply and revert, and one signal_redraw() at the end of a pass. Both guarded - this sits in the view-layer switch path.

    • 🟢 Putting a swap away PINNED the object instead of releasing it - the actual field bug, and the reason the log read perfectly while the screen did not.

      _protect_shared_mesh moves a swapped slot to the OBJECT so the swap cannot reach the twins. revert_row then wrote the base onto that object-level slot and left the link flipped - so the object wore the material it had the moment the swap came off, and every variant painted on the MESH afterwards never reached it. The row was correct throughout; the object was pinned.

      A revert now hands a flipped slot back: slot.link = 'DATA', link_flipped cleared. The object follows the mesh again exactly as it did before the feature touched it, and apply_row re-flips when the swap goes back on.

      test_putting_a_swap_away_hands_the_slot_back_to_the_mesh reproduces the scene shape and fails on the old code. 38. 🟢 The Global row's icon strip was not anchored right. Reader screenshot 2026-09-14: every tree row's icons sat against the right edge and the Global row's sat where the word "Global" ended -- 420px inside it at a 1000px sidebar (rig, dev/measure/capture_tree_widths.py, scale 1.125 = 30 px/unit).

      Cause. A tree row is [left (packed), right (fixed ui_units_x)], and what actually holds the strip against the edge is the NAME's own sub-row: the left half is alignment = 'LEFT' (the Fixed 14 rule), so a widget drawn straight onto it shrink-wraps and nothing in the row absorbs the panel's slack. Every other drawer draws its name into n = left.row(...); draw_tree_nodes.draw_global_item drew left.label(text="Global"). One line.

      draw_layers.draw_take's fallback branch (left.label(text=item.name), the path taken when the take index cannot resolve) had the same shape and is fixed with it.

      Second, smaller thing in the same row: its 16 right-side cells were right.row(), not right.row(align=True). draw_tree_nodes.py was the only file in panels/context/ opening its cells bare, and an unaligned cell carries Blender's own inter-widget padding, so that strip read wider per icon than the rows under it.

      Measured before/after at 700 and 1000px: the Global row's last icon now lands on the same x as the row below it at both widths.

      Guards (dev/tests/test_tree_row_columns.py): test_every_row_puts_its_name_in_its_own_sub_row and test_every_right_side_cell_is_aligned, both across all six row drawers.

    • 🟢 The confirm gate refused the addon's own buttons. Reader 2026-09-14, Ungroup on a scene-group header: TKS_OT_delete_group is destructive and refuses an unconfirmed scripted call.

      utils/confirm_gate.py sets confirm = True in invoke() and refuses in execute() when it is False — that is what makes a bridge or a timer say it means the deletion. But the addon calls its own operators, and those are scripted calls: tks.group_or_ungroup routes a group header to bpy.ops.tks.delete_group('EXEC_DEFAULT', ...), EXEC_DEFAULT skips invoke(), and the operator refused the user's own key press. The gate was added per operator; the callers were never swept.

      An AST scan found five: four delete_group calls in operators/context/groups/ops_manage.py (Ungroup, single and multi) and one tag_group_delete in operators/tags/ops_groups_query.py. All five take confirm=True rather than INVOKE_DEFAULT, because in each the human has already agreed — Ungroup's own invoke ran, and its multi branch loops over every selected group; the tag dispatcher had already shown its own invoke_confirm() dialog, so handing the gesture on would ask twice.

      Pre-existing, not from this branch: the same four calls are on main. Guard: dev/tests/test_confirm_gate_internal_calls.py walks the package's AST and fails on any in-addon call to a gated operator that neither passes confirm=True nor uses INVOKE_DEFAULT, plus a second test so the sweep cannot pass by the gate being removed. Record: doc/troubleshooting/confirm_gate_refuses_own_button.md.

    • 🟢 Ungroup died on a file that has no "Ungrouped" group. Reader 2026-09-14, straight after the confirm-gate fix let the call through: RuntimeError: Error: Main group not found.

      tks.ungroup_scenes looked the default group up BY NAME, and properties/groups.reconcile_topology only creates it when the file has NO scene group at all -- so a file whose first group the user made themselves never had one, and the lookup came up empty on an ordinary file. Finding it would not have been enough either: the scene needs somewhere to land, so the group has to exist.

      properties/_groups_shared gains DEFAULT_GROUP_NAME, ensure_ungrouped_scene_group() and ensure_ungrouped_vl_group(scene): find it, or add it. A fresh group is already named "Ungrouped" (the property default) and the name is written through the IDProperty so the rename callback cannot renumber it to "Ungrouped.001". tks.ungroup_scenes, tks.ungroup_vls and tks.delete_group's view-layer branch -- which carried its own copy of the create -- now go through the one helper.

      Pre-existing, not from this branch. Tests: dev/tests/test_ungroup_without_ungrouped_group.py (3), which build the reader's state: one user-made group, no Ungrouped, and a scene inside it. Record: doc/troubleshooting/confirm_gate_refuses_own_button.md.

    • 🟢 The scene default group was being renamed to "Ungrouped.001". Reader 2026-09-14: a group by that name appeared and could not be deleted. This is the ROOT of Fixed 39 -- "Main group not found" was this bug seen from the other end.

      A group name's update callback enforces uniqueness across scene groups AND view-layer groups (_on_sg_name_update: one flat namespace, on purpose). Every scene owns a VL group called "Ungrouped", so when reconcile_topology created the SCENE default with an RNA assignment (default_sg.name = "Ungrouped") on a file whose VL groups already existed, the callback renumbered it. Everything downstream reads that group by name, so it went missing -- and the stray sat at index 0, the one group tks.delete_group refuses to delete. Neither usable nor removable.

      The per-scene VL default had always dodged this by writing the IDProperty directly (default_vlg['name'] = "Ungrouped"); the scene default now does the same. reconcile_topology also heals a file that already carries the renumbered name: in any scope with no plain "Ungrouped", an "Ungrouped." is renamed back, once, through the IDProperty. A user group of that name beside a real default is left alone.

      Reproduced and fixed headless (dev/measure-style probe: clear the scene groups on a file whose VL groups exist, reconcile, read the name). Tests: dev/tests/test_default_group_never_renumbered.py (3). Record: doc/troubleshooting/confirm_gate_refuses_own_button.md.

    • 🟢 A created default group landed at the END of the list, so the user's own group could not be deleted. Reader 2026-09-14: "there is one group I can't remove". Their log said why -- sync: SG 'g' first, SG 'Ungrouped' second.

      Index 0 IS the default in this data model: tks.delete_group refuses to delete groups[0] ("Cannot delete the default group") and reconcile_topology adopts every orphan scene into it. Fixed 39's ensure_ungrouped_scene_group() appended the group it created, so on a file that had none the user's own group stayed at index 0 -- undeletable -- while the new default, sitting below it, could be deleted.

      The helper now moves what it creates to index 0, and reconcile_topology moves an "Ungrouped" that sits further down back to the front, so a file already in that state repairs itself on load. Scene groups only: VL groups are scoped per scene inside one flat collection, where position means nothing.

      Tests: two more in dev/tests/test_default_group_never_renumbered.py (created-first, and the heal), and the expectation in test_ungroup_without_ungrouped_group.py updated to the rule.

    [0.8.3] - 2026-09-10¶

    Added¶

    1. 🟢 auto_camera_visibility_mode: one enum, three values, replacing a master bool plus a four-value timing enum. The old pair asked when the automation ran (SWITCH_STILL / SWITCH / MANUAL / PLAYHEAD) and then let the take's own Still-or-Animation mode decide how many cameras survived -- one on a Still take, the whole cut list on an animating one. Two questions in one setting, and the second answer moved behind the user whenever a take changed mode. OFF / SINGLE / ALL answer only what you see, identically on every take. rules.isolates_to_one() is the fork; new engine._visibility_plan() returns (keep_names, viewport_only) together because they are ONE decision -- SINGLE is the only branch that hides cut cameras and therefore the only one forbidden to touch hide_render, since Blender's switch skips a render-hidden camera. New engine.apply_for_take() is the single entry point for the deferred switch drain, the Isolate operator and the preference callback. gate_on_switch() and on_pref_changed() lost their is_still callable, so the switch hot path no longer resolves the six-tier Still cascade (MAINT-12). visibility_enabled() is now the whole switch-time decision and applies_on_switch() is gone. apply_camera_visibility() gates on the two RULES rather than on visibility_enabled, because it is the writer every MANUAL caller comes through and On Request must work while the mode is OFF; every automatic entry point asks visibility_enabled before reaching it. TKS_OT_ApplyCameraVisibility.poll follows. Config migration in _migrate_config_dict (master off or MANUAL -> OFF, PLAYHEAD -> SINGLE, SWITCH/SWITCH_STILL -> ALL) with both retired keys in _LEGACY_CONFIG_KEYS so they drain on save; the last row maps to ALL deliberately, because a settings migration may never hide MORE than the user had. EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 832 -> 831. Row menu drops the master checkbox and its mode.enabled gating (OFF IS the off state) and names the mode in force with a pgettext_iface-composed label; Preferences collapses to one draw_split_prop_row. de_DE: twelve sources dropped, seven added -- one of the twelve was a dead duplicate key of the Sequencer's own Follow the Playhead, which had been shadowing the camera entry since it shipped. Behaviour change to call out: a single-camera take in ANIMATION mode is now isolated, where the old SWITCH_STILL default left it alone. 11 pure tests in dev/tests/test_camera_vis_mode.py (replacing test_camera_vis_trigger.py), 6 migration tests, the test_multicam_switch.py assignment block rewritten mode-driven; 1169 impact-selected pass; auditor 9.5 / 18 findings, none in a changed file.

    2. 🟢 Apply When gained a fourth value, PLAYHEAD. (Superseded by entry 1 before release: the mode survives as SINGLE, the timing enum does not.) The other three isolate ONCE, on a take switch, so a cutting take keeps every cut camera visible for its whole length. This one follows the frame. rules.TRIGGER_PLAYHEAD; engine.apply_for_frame() computes the cut's camera with camera_at_frame(cuts, scene.frame_current) and passes it as an explicit keep_names set, bypassing assigned_cameras() -- whose whole-cut-list answer exists to stop a RENDER hide killing a cut, which this mode never makes. apply_camera_visibility(..., viewport_only=True) therefore writes hide_viewport and the per-view-layer eye and NEVER hide_render: Blender's own switch skips a render-hidden camera, so hiding one would delete the cut the mode exists to show. New features/cameras/handlers.py adds a frame_change_post handler that only DECIDES and parks (Constitution rule 2); schedule_playhead / _drain_playhead do every write from a one-shot timer, the same shape the switch path uses. _last_playhead_camera (keyed by session_uid) makes a frame inside the same cut cost one dict lookup and no writes, which is what makes it affordable during playback. Leaving the mode calls release_playhead_hides(), which may reveal where the automation as a whole may not: its scope is exactly this take's cut list and only the viewport flag, so nothing of the user's is guessed at. New cameras Process Monitor group (REG-06). 18 tests in dev/tests/test_camera_vis_playhead.py; 3184 impact-selected pass; auditor 9.5, no new findings.

    3. 🟢 TKS_MT_PIE_TreeIcons (panels/pie_menus/tree_icons.py), Ctrl+Shift+F, off by default. Eight slots in Blender's W/E/S/N/NW/NE/SW/SE draw order over the seven props of ops_cascade_overflow._ORDER; the eighth is pie.separator(), there being no eighth thing a row can hold. Row identity is list_focus.active_item(wm, "CONTEXT") — the key named as a constant, never "which list was clicked last", which is stale whenever the reader clicks an already-highlighted row. poll returns False with no focused row, so the chord is inert rather than opening an empty wheel. Each slice draws that icon's OWN popover, resolved per tier from _POPOVERS, a 6x7 table extracted from the five panels/context/draw_* modules rather than guessed; test_pie_draws_exactly_the_popovers_the_rows_draw compares the two sets in BOTH directions. Three spellings in that table are irregular and all three are real: Tag is tks.assign_tag_popover, ONE operator for every tier told which one it is by group_type/vl_name; Output Rule at Scene tier is tks.output_rule_popover with no scene_ in the name; Variant is tks.vsw_<tier>_variant_popover over in features/variant_switch/. (An earlier pass reported these as three HOLES and routed every slice through tks.cascade_overflow_popover instead — a grep artifact, now reverted; ops_cascade_overflow.py is byte-identical to main again.) Labels are read off tks_overflow_active_prop's enum rather than hand-written, so the seven props cost no new English string. _LEVEL_EXCLUDES is MIRRORED in the pie, not imported (panels ↛ operators, ARCH-01), with a test comparing the two tables. layout.operator_context = 'INVOKE_DEFAULT' before menu_pie() is load-bearing: a popup layout defaults to EXEC, every one of these operators does its work in invoke, and their execute correctly refuses a scripted call — without the line every slice draws, clicks and does nothing, the trap that took out "Show Overrides…" on 2026-08-31. Prefs: tree_icon_pie_enabled + expand_pie_tree_icons, a Hotkeys section with the rebindable chord centre but no slot grid, a prefs_search entry, and ACCORDION_GROUPS membership — CORR-25 caught that last one missing, where TKS_OT_ToggleAccordion falls back to a group of one and the section's fold gesture dies silently. EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 832 -> 834 (the 30 operator properties below do NOT count; that guard reads TKS_AddonPreferences.__annotations__). Ctrl+Shift+T was the obvious mnemonic and collides twice in the 3D View (object.data_transfer, mesh.quads_convert_to_tris), measured against Blender 5.2's own blender_default.py. Ctrl+Shift+L was free but right-handed; the chord had to suit the LEFT hand alone (user ruling), so it is Ctrl+Shift+F - index finger, home row, pinky on both modifiers, and unbound anywhere in Blender or this addon. Ctrl+Shift+Q is free and left-handed too but wants the busy pinky; Ctrl+Shift+D and +G are free in the 3D View but taken in the Node Editor. Ctrl+Alt+* stays banned (German AltGr). 21 pure tests in dev/tests/test_tree_icon_pie.py; full pure suite 341 pass / 3 skip. Auditor 9.51 and -0.49 total deduction, identical to main at dbe83327, no finding naming tree_icons.py. Headless impact-selected suite against the branch point: 1599 passed, 1767 deselected, 0 failures.

    4. 🟢 force_popover on 30 popover operators, 25 forks rewritten. Action, Camera, Compositor, World and Output Rule each fork in invoke — if event.shift: opens the editor, otherwise open_picker_menu drops a list of names at the cursor (ops_camera_levels.py:116 is the canonical shape; ops_compositor.py:434 is the same fork inside _comp_picker_or_popover_invoke, shared by all six compositor tiers and therefore reading op rather than self). A pie dispatches NO modifiers, so those five slices would have silently opened the picker — the one thing this pie exists to skip. Each class gains force_popover: bpy.props.BoolProperty(default=False) and each fork now reads self.force_popover or event.shift; the pie sets it for the props in _FORCED. Tag and Variant never fork and carry no such property, so setting it on them would raise — hence the set rather than a blanket write. Per-operator, not a flag on the window manager: a WM flag would survive a pie the reader opened and dismissed, so the next plain click on a row icon would open the editor instead of the picker. Files: ops_action_levels, ops_camera_levels, ops_world_levels, ops_compositor, ops_viewlayer_{action,camera,world}, ops_output_popovers. Two tests hold it: every if event.shift: immediately above an invoke_popup( must accept the flag, and every class that forks must declare it.

    5. 🟢 tree_icon_pie_enabled defaults False. Carries the mode pie's ruling that an opt-in pie claims a viewport chord, and a key the reader never asked for is a key they will meet by accident. Reachable at Preferences → Hotkeys → Tree Icon Pie. The pie deliberately ignores tks_show_* / tks_pin_* — the same ruling _show_in_popover already carries for the comprehensive view: those say how crowded the ROW should be, and eight slots that rearrange themselves as icons are hidden defeat the muscle memory a pie exists to build. Known cost of dropping the overflow route: the pie no longer inherits that popover's icon row, so switching prop is a second keypress rather than a click.

    6. 🟢 TREE_ICON_PIE_SLOT_ITEMS + TKS_TreeIconPiePropsMixin: the eight slots become preferences. Nothing new had to be built - _draw_pie_grid, tks.reset_pie_grid and _pie_dedup.resolve_pie_duplicates are all prefix-driven, so the section is one _draw_pie_grid(col, self, "tree_icon_pie_slot_", center_pie_id="TKS_MT_PIE_TreeIcons", center_key="Ctrl Shift F", reset=True) call over a mixin of eight EnumProperty slots, each with its own update= running the shared de-dup under its own lock key ('tree_icon' - two pies sharing a lock would let an edit in one abandon a de-dup in the other). The items table reuses the LABELS of tks_overflow_active_prop verbatim: a slot's dropdown entry, the pie slice it configures and the ... popover's icon row are one vocabulary, so one translation covers all three and the seven property names needed no new German. Item descriptions are empty for the same reason they are empty there. Defaults reproduce the previously hard-coded layout, and _SLOTS survives in the pie as the fallback for a session whose preferences have not loaded (registration, or headless); _slots_for(context) reads the prefs and maps 'NONE' to None so the draw has one shape for "empty slot". test_slot_defaults_match_the_built_in_layout holds the two together - a reader must not meet one layout before their prefs land and a different one after. EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 834 -> 842. Search index gains the eight names; dev/tests/test_prefs_search_index.py asserts every name is real RNA, so a rename cannot rot it silently.

    7. 🟢 WindowManager.tks_show_tree_lines hides the neutral indent strips without moving anything. The switch is honoured in ONE place, the new utils/tree_strip.draw_tree_strip(strip_row, wm), which fills a row the CALLER has already sized. Hidden is drawn, not skipped: the same prop(wm, "tks_tree_line_color") goes down with enabled=False, active=False, emboss=False -- the shape panels/context/draw_layers.py (~L361, ~L715) had already been using for its deepest grouped-take strip. A blank label was rejected outright: scale_x multiplies a widget's OWN natural width, so a label and a colour prop at the same factor are different pixels, and every row would have shifted -- the same trap utils/tree_metrics.TAG_GAP_UNITS documents for the width setting, and the reason untagged_gap() is in ui_units_x. tree_metrics.tree_lines_visible(wm) is the predicate (pure, no RNA, beside untagged_gap); tree_strip.py is the only module that draws. Eight call sites routed through it: both _draw_tree_line twins (panels/context/tree_layout_calc.py -- note the name is draw_tree_line, no leading underscore -- and features/variant_switch/ui_helpers.py), plus the hand-drawn strips in panels/navigation/monitors_pm.py, monitors_profiler.py and panels/tag_library_ui/lists.py x3. The TAGGED branch is untouched by design (user ruling: hide the lines, keep the tag colours), and ops_tree_design.py's own colour swatch is excluded -- it EDITS the colour, so the switch has no business hiding it. Both draw_layers placeholders stay as they are: already invisible, nothing to toggle.

      Preferences twin is default_tree_lines, deliberately NOT default_show_tree_lines: draw_data_inspector.py (~L121) files prefs by prefix and default_show_tree_* already belongs to the per-column icon toggles, so that spelling would have filed the row under Columns instead of Tree. Wired into both sync tables -- ops_addon_ui.py (~L325, WM -> prefs) and persistence_io.py (~L784, prefs -> WM) -- plus prefs_search.py "Tree", draw_interface.py's Tree section and two manual_map.py entries. EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 832 -> 833; the register-time assertion in preferences/__init__.py caught the omission on the first headless run, which is exactly its job. Three new de_DE keys (98.8% coverage held).

      9 tests in dev/tests/test_tree_row_left_cluster.py, including a repo-wide sweep that fails on any raw prop(wm, "tks_tree_line_color") outside the drawer, and a check that untagged_gap() is byte-identical with the lines on and off -- if hiding lines moved that number, the tag column would shift. 1952 impact-selected pass; auditor 9.5 / 10.0, no finding on the new code. 8. 🟢 Parent State — features/parent_state/. The cascade applied per channel. Per tier tks_parent_keys (AUTO/ON/OFF, static EnumProperty) and tks_parent_keys_pass_down (Bool; Global carries only Scene.tks_global_parent_keys_pass_down on the master scene); group tiers declare theirs in properties/groups_*.py from the shared item table properties/parent_keys.py. Pure resolver engine.py (resolve_stack(tiers): winner's ancestors with actions, bottom first; ON pulls, OFF cuts the chain below, AUTO inherits iff an ancestor passes down with no action-holding OFF in between; empty tiers transparent; same action never stacks under itself). bpy side engine_bpy.py builds the tiers from cascade.cascade_levels(...), returns [] while Rest State Mode is on or when the sweep's target is not the tier winner. Layers layers.py: one owned NLA track per depth (TKS Parent 1..N), one strip each (blend_type REPLACE, extrapolation HOLD, action_slot matched label→name→identifier through a session_uid-keyed slot index), use_nla forced on, ensure-or-rebuild (frame-range drift rebuilds), tweak-mode targets skipped, foreign tracks never touched. Hooked into the ONE action door: bind_action(..., target=, parent_stack=) calls provider parent_state.sync_layers; clear_action calls parent_state.clear_layers (action or not) — so the sweep, the legacy writer, the CLI worker, the pinned/no-slot/no-action clears and clear_actions_on_watched all agree; both doors resolve the stack ONCE per pass via parent_state.resolve_stack. Preload's restore drops owned layers before writing the other window's action back (vl_preload_snapshot.py). Layers are keyed everywhere through core.keyed_extra (owned_strip_channels registered as a source) — rest snap, revert, drift, Value Lock, Diff State, inspector. A setting change re-sweeps the window's take and bumps the cascade token (vl_switch.bump_cascade_token) so undo replays it. UI: two rows in every tier's action popover (features/parent_state/panels.py), a LINKED action icon on take and view-layer rows while a layer is active (_row_inherits provider seam in draw_layers.py), texts in texts/tooltips_parent_state.py + 18 de_DE entries. AI verbs set_parent_keys / set_parent_pass_down (ai/api.py). Take duplication copies the setting. Spike dev/spikes/parent_state_nla_spike.py 18/18 on 5.2. Tests: test_parent_state_engine.py (pure, 16 cases), test_parent_state_layers.py (registered, both doors, keyed answer, foreign track, rest mode). Not in this pass: a target with no slot in the winner but one in a parent gets no layer (documented follow-up); token-based slot matching for parents. Post-merge fix (fix/parent-state-strip-range): a strip made from a MULTI-slot parent came out one frame long (strips.new sizes from the not-yet-assigned slot); the strip range is now set from action.frame_range after the slot — doc/troubleshooting/parent_state_multi_slot_strip_range.md. Post-merge fix 2 (fix/parent-state-slot-cache): the per-action slot index cached ActionSlot OBJECTS across ticks; Rest State Mode keying / undo recreated slots under the same count and the cache served freed memory ("This slot () does not belong to the assigned Action"). Names -> identifiers only, live action.slots.get() per call — doc/troubleshooting/parent_state_stale_slot_cache.md. Trace lines under SWITCH/cascade and ANIM/slots ship with the feature (feat/parent-state-trace).

    8. 🟢 Undo Monitor — core/undo_trace.py records a tape of PRESS / STEP / HANDLER / WRITE / SEAL / STATE / ORPHAN rows: every Ctrl+Z and WHO took it, every drain with the DOOR it came through (inside the gesture vs timer), every seal and every REFUSED seal with _push_block_reason() in words, a state line before and after each press, and a 3 s orphan sweep counting writes that never reached a step. panels/navigation/panel_undo_monitor.py

    9. monitors_undo.py (TKS_UL_UndoMonitor) + monitors_props.py (TKS_UndoStepItem), a UIList like the Debug Monitor, WM props tks_undo_items / tks_undo_items_index / tks_um_show_*, Record / Clear / Copy in operators/ui/ops_undo_monitor.py, UNDO button in all four monitor headers. Built because four rounds of log-reading failed: the log says WHAT happened, never WHICH suppression window was standing.

    10. 🟢 Its own log file — takes_for_blender_undo_<date>.log beside the debug log, same rotation, written whether or not the panel is open.

    11. 🟢 Named steps — _STEP_LABELS / _label_for / _pending_step_label in core/mutation_queue.py; the FIRST meaningful label of a gesture names it ("Takes: fold key into take" / "snap to Rest" / "release empty action"), reset after the seal. User ruling 2026-09-07: name it, do not hide it.

    12. 🟢 The Undo Monitor list is file-backed. core/undo_trace.py has always appended every step to its own dated log via _write_line, and nothing ever read it back: panel_undo_monitor.draw_undo_monitor called undo_trace.sync_collection(wm), which mirrors the in-memory _events list that arm() clears on every Record press. So the one artefact that survives a crash was thrown away on the next press. New utils/undo_reader.py parses the file instead — _STEP_RE is the exact inverse of _write_line's f"{t:7.3f} {phase:<8} {label}" (+ [detail]), and _BANNER_RE picks up the === … === line arm() writes. It lives beside log_reader.py deliberately: _read_tail_lines, the dated+tagged filename grammar in log_source.py and the source filtering are all shared, and a second copy of any of them would drift. sync_undo_collection caches on (mtime, size) like log_reader.sync_log_collection, so an unchanged file costs one os.stat per draw (ARCH-05); the active-row jump to the newest step now happens only on a cache MISS, so a reader can click a row and keep it selected. undo_trace.as_text() delegates to undo_reader.rows_as_text() so the clipboard reads identically from either source.

    13. 🟢 tks.um_settings_popover — invoke_popup(width=220), mirroring tks.dm_settings_popover. Holds the new tks_um_line_limit enum (default '50', not the debug default of 25: one press produces 10-20 rows) and the three tks_um_show_* bools that used to be loose toggle buttons in the sidebar. execute() is refuse_scripted behind the _tks_invoked marker (AI-01), with AI-03-OK on the class.

    14. 🟢 tks.um_log_files — click opens the tape picker, Shift+Click opens the log folder in Explorer, copied from TKS_OT_DebugMonitorLogFiles including both error reports. Backed by tks_um_log_file, a dynamic enum whose callback _get_undo_file_items in monitors_undo.py is wrapped in @retained_enum — an unretained dynamic enum is an EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION in uiBut, not a cosmetic bug (CRASH-07). The tks_um_all_sources opt-in is drawn only when undo_reader.has_other_sources() is true. Panel also gained the open-file row (basename with the shared stem stripped, ERROR icon when file_source(name) != get_source_suffix()), the same shape panel_debug_monitor uses.

    15. 🟢 [s<pid>] on every log line, and a "This session only" filter on both monitors. Every open Blender appends to ONE file and they interleave line by line, so the Debug Monitor was showing another window's work as if it were yours. A banner cannot fix that - it is written once per file, and the next line may be another session's - so logger.session_tag() stamps every line and undo_trace._session_tag() stamps every tape row and banner. The field is OPTIONAL in both regexes: a line written before the stamp existed still parses, reads as "session unknown", and is never claimed by whoever happens to be filtering. read_log_entries / read_undo_entries / both sync_* take session=, and the mtime+size caches are keyed by it so two sessions cannot serve each other's rows. The tape reads a WIDER tail when filtering (limit * 6), or a tail full of another session's rows would hand back fewer than limit of ours. The toggle is drawn DISABLED when the panel is showing a file this session is not writing: on yesterday's log it would hide every row and read as a broken panel. Follow-up the same day: the boolean became an ENUM in the FILE popover, not a tick in the display settings - one file can hold several sessions and reading someone ELSE'S is a real reason to open the monitor, so "mine" is a default rather than the only choice, and the control belongs beside the file it narrows. log_reader.list_sessions() / undo_reader.list_sessions() fold a file into [(id, first, last, count)] through the shared fold_sessions(), cached on (mtime, size) because the enum callback runs on every redraw while the popover is open and the log can be 18 MB. Only a BANNER carries a wall clock on the tape - a step's stamp is seconds since Record and restarts each recording - so sessions are ordered by banner time there. build_session_items() is shared by both pickers and always leads with ALL / MINE: stable identifiers, so a file change that replaces every other item cannot take the two useful choices away. Both session_filter()s fall back to MINE on an empty read, which is what a dynamic enum returns once its items change under a stored index. Hoisted to utils/session_pick.py before merge: written per monitor it was two near-identical session_filter()s plus two copies of the item list - three new clone pairs, and the exact drift that had already made the two stats bars diverge. Only two things differ per monitor (which WM property holds the choice, and how "is this my file" is answered), so both are arguments now. SESSION_ALL / SESSION_MINE / build_session_items() / resolve_session_choice() have one home and 5 tests of their own. Ordering fix: MINE now leads the item list. Blender gives a dynamic enum no default= - it selects the FIRST item - so with ALL in front the shipped default was "every session", exactly what the stamp was added to stop. The order IS the default, and a test pins it.

    16. 🔴 tks.dm_copy — the Debug Monitor's Copy button. Mirrors the Undo Monitor's, and copies what the panel SHOWS: same file, level filter, session and line limit. log_reader.entries_as_text() rebuilds the lines from the parsed fields rather than keeping raw text, so the clipboard matches the list exactly and the session stamp - machinery, not content - is left off. Sidebar order now matches the Undo Monitor's: settings, gap, logging + refresh + copy, gap, files.

    17. 🟢 One keyframe, one Ctrl+Z — the gesture macros. The answer to the card's question is a seam that already exists in Blender: bpy.types.Macro. Blender runs a macro's sub-operators in sequence, stays modal while one is modal (the transform drag), and pushes ONE undo step at its end — object.duplicate_move is one step for this reason. The last sub-operator, tks.settle_gesture (operators/ops_gesture_macro.py): context.view_layer.update() so the mirror handler enqueues (read-only, the Handler Mutation Ban holds), revert_snap.flush_revert_now() so the debounced snap joins the queue instead of firing after the push, mutation_queue.drain() in an operator's execute — outside evaluation, before the macro's push — then note_gesture_carried_by_operator() so the seal adds nothing on top. undo_trace learns the label prefix carried so those writes are not orphans.

      Why not the 0.7.11 way: that drained inside the autokey handler, from inside scene_graph_update_tagged, and crashed Blender in deg_update_eval_copy_datablock (removed 2026-08-20, 9f29d8c0). The macro writes where every operator writes.

      Measured in the launcher sandbox, 2026-09-09: fold + mirror + snap all drain (inside the gesture) (23–46 ms with a fresh action, ~5 ms for a follow-up move), no seal, one press per gesture both ways, six fast moves undone in six presses each landing on the previous position, and the material-value key — the August crash spot — settled with no crash. Headless: dev/tests/test_gesture_macro.py (the seam, the orphan accounting, the keys, the preference). Two harness traps met on the way and fixed in conftest.py: a headless ed.undo leaves TKS_VL_STATE.is_undoing True (no timer runs to clear it) and refuses every later seal; and the harness holds two package instances whose ownership of a registered operator flips — the tests resolve modules through bl_rna_get_subclass_py.

      Keys: tks.key_move on G and tks.key_insert on I in Object Mode, tks.key_insert_button on I in the 'User Interface' keymap — plain I over a value field is anim.keyframe_insert_button, a different operator ("Ctrl+Shift+I on material values will not set a key"). Addon-keyconfig items are consulted before Blender's own. Items are matched by idname + key in both directions, never via kmi.properties. Scripted callers keep bpy.ops.transform.translate (timer path, two steps); the macros are reachable as bpy.ops.tks.key_move(TRANSFORM_OT_translate={"value": ...}).

    18. 🟢 Preference undo_gesture_macro (User Options, ON, badge Recommended) — binds and unbinds the keys at once through the keymaps.sync_gesture_macro provider, same shape as the Smart Undo hijack. EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 848 → 849; texts in tooltips_misc.py / tooltips_preferences.py with de_DE for every new string; manual-map rows for the four operators and the pref. Still to write: the hotkeys wiki page section (INFO-04 lists the four operators until it exists).

    19. 🔴 Shift+D reaches the Inspector's Actions list. tks.duplicate_action existed and was drawn only in the datablock popover; the key never reached it (auditor CORR-28, INSPECTOR on TKS_OT_GlobalDuplicate's cannot-reach set). New _INSPECTOR_DUPLICATE table beside the _INSPECTOR_DELETE / _INSPECTOR_NEW pair already in operators/ops_global_shortcuts.py, keyed on the EXACT list (_focused_key) because the INSPECTOR family names three lists and only Actions has a duplicate — an object row is a reference to a scene object (Blender's own Shift+D owns that) and a slot is copied by Split/Duplicate on its row. Alt+D reports that an Action copy is always unlinked rather than silently doing what Shift+D does, mirroring the product branch above it. TKS_OT_DuplicateAction gained a description() that composes OP_DUPLICATEACTION_KEYS with live_shortcut('tks.global_duplicate') — required, and caught by the auditor: routing a key to a panel button that never names it is MAINT-14, which went 0 -> 1 on the first scan after the wire-up and back to 0 after the tooltip. de_DE gained both new strings.
    20. 🔴 Ctrl+T reaches the Inspector's Slots list. Same shape: tks.retarget_slot was popover-only. New _INSPECTOR_RETARGET table, and the branch calls INVOKE_DEFAULT so the key opens the same "which action?" dialog the row's button opens. Objects and Actions are absent from the table on purpose — neither has a second home to be moved into.

    21. 🟢 Every keying and transform key is a macro door. operators/ops_gesture_macro.py is table-driven: _MACROS = (macro class, native RNA operator, bindings), _KEYS derived from it, one define() loop in register(). Nine doors join tks.key_move / tks.key_insert / tks.key_insert_button: tks.key_rotate (TRANSFORM_OT_rotate, R), tks.key_scale (TRANSFORM_OT_resize, S), tks.key_delete (ANIM_OT_keyframe_delete_v3d, Alt+I), tks.key_delete_button / tks.key_clear_button (ANIM_OT_keyframe_delete_button Alt+I / ANIM_OT_keyframe_clear_button Shift+Alt+I, 'User Interface'), tks.key_insert_dopesheet / tks.key_delete_dopesheet (ACTION_OT_keyframe_insert I / ACTION_OT_delete Del, 'Dopesheet'), tks.key_insert_graph / tks.key_delete_graph (GRAPH_OT_keyframe_insert I / GRAPH_OT_delete Del, 'Graph Editor'). Keys harvested from blender_default.py (5.2) and pinned in dev/tests/test_every_key_through_the_door.py (8). Modifiers ride in the table; _our_items matches idname + key + alt/shift/ctrl so Alt+I and I on the same key stay apart; no Ctrl+Alt (AltGr). Polls are context.mode in {OBJECT, POSE} or "a window exists", never stricter than the native op. K (anim.keyframe_insert_menu) stays native: a menu returns before the key exists. Texts (texts/tooltips_misc.py), de_DE (18 keys) and utils/manual_map.py in lockstep. Merge 6d54f7e0.

    22. 🟢 Pose keymap rows for the viewport doors. G / R / S / I / Alt+I bind in 'Pose' as well as 'Object Mode', so a bone key gets the one-step undo. Caveat, written in doc/roadmap/_dev/every-key-through-the-door.md: tks.catch_rest seeds the rest cache at the OBJECT level (rest_cache.catch_selection); bone channels are not object transform paths, so the pre-gesture rest catch does not cover them yet. Whether a posed bone can leak into Rest the way Suzanne's rotation did is open until the pose tape says.

    23. 🟢 A scripted key gets one undo step. The twelve gesture macros give a KEYPRESS one step; a script got none of it - it writes through RNA, Blender pushes nothing, and the add-on's share of the key (folding it into the take, snapping the untouched channels to Rest) lands ~0.8 s later in a step of its own. ai/gesture.py is the macro's three links said as a with: enter runs bpy.ops.tks.catch_rest, exit runs bpy.ops.tks.settle_gesture and then ONE ed.undo_push labelled AI: <what>. The links are the registered operators, called rather than imported - ai/ and operators/ are siblings at the top layer, and one source of truth means the scripted path cannot drift from the key the user presses; both carry {'REGISTER', 'INTERNAL'} and no 'UNDO', so neither adds a step. The guard must not hold the mutation lock, and that is the design: the lock gates the reactive layer, and the reactive layer is what NOTICES the key, so an ai_session around an animated write would be seen by nobody. It refuses inside a held session and says why. Order is pinned by test: catch -> body -> settle -> push (a rest value caught after the write IS the written value; a push before the settle leaves the share outside the step, which test_undo_write_after_push.py measures). tks.catch_rest gains target: StringProperty - the catch walks the SELECTION and a script has none, and a named object that is not here is refused rather than passed over. ai/verbs_keys.py is the bridge-callable front: key(target, path, value=None, index=-1, frame=None) and unkey(...), name-addressed, envelope-returning, in _MUTATING_VERBS (they change the project even without the lock) and in _verb_modules() so help() lists them; path is Blender's own RNA path, so nothing here keeps a list of what is keyable. AI_GUIDE.md section 4, de_DE +1, dev/tests/test_the_scripted_way_in.py (23). The rest half was missing on the first real run ("but rest state was not created"): the mirror's keyed branch skips any Object not in the SELECTION - a drag mask - and a script has none, so the key folded into the take and the Rest action gained nothing (measured on the same object: unselected 18 -> 18 curves, selected 18 -> 21). The gate stays; a scripted gesture names its objects instead. mirror_logic gained a naming window beside the two suppression windows - name_gesture_targets(names, seconds=2.0) / forget_gesture_targets() / named_gesture_targets(now=None), additive and never-shortening, expiring on its own so a gesture abandoned between the catch and the settle leaves nothing in scope - and the gate reads {o.name for o in sel_objs} | named_gesture_targets(). tks.catch_rest names when given a target, tks.settle_gesture forgets once the writes have gone out. After: unselected but named, 18 -> 21, the same as a selected object. Fix 3169a1d0; dev/scripts/check_scripted_key_one_press.py measures all three halves now, and keeps its run-1 record in driver_namespace because a scene property is in the .blend and the Ctrl+Z being measured took it back. Two test traps met: cls.bl_rna.properties on an operator subclass answers the BASE struct (it lists macros, not one declared property) - use bpy.ops.<x>.get_rna_type(); and a headless session starts with is_applying SET, so every gesture refused BUSY until the file cleared it. Merge 7d61ea7f.

    24. 🔴 state_outline_mode/px/pct — the outline gets the width setting it never had. state_width_prop feeds one uniform, lineWidth on the POLYLINE shader (features/diff_state/draw.py), which reaches the BOX, EMPTY and camera-frame line layers and nothing else. The outline is an inverted hull — a SURFACE pushed along its normals — so no line width can size it, and its thickness was logic._HULL_FRACTION = 0.018, a constant no preference read. Three new properties per state in preferences/props/props_diff_state.py, beside state_width_prop in the same for _state loop: an enum (SCREEN/OBJECT, default SCREEN), a PIXEL float (2.0, 0.5–16.0) and a PERCENTAGE float (0.6, 0.05–5.0). EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 847 → 853 in preferences/__init__.py — the guard caught the omission on the first run, which is what it is for.

    25. 🔴 Screen mode: a custom vertex program, because there is no state call for this. New features/diff_state/shader.py. gpu.state exposes no polygon-offset and no triangle-reaching line width, so a rim can only be sized in the program. GPUShaderCreateInfo + gpu.shader.create_from_info (both verified present in Blender 5.2's binary before writing a line). Two push constants decide the layer: localOffset moves a vertex along its own normal in OBJECT units, widthPx pushes the silhouette outward AFTER projection, scaled back by clip.w so the perspective divide cannot shrink it — which is what makes 2px read as 2px at any distance. The direction is the normal as it lands on screen, guarded with length > 1e-6 because a normal pointing at the eye projects to nothing and normalize() would return NaN; those vertices are interior and never on the silhouette, so skipping them is correct. ModelViewProjectionMatrix is pushed explicitly (proj @ modelview @ matrix_world) rather than trusted to auto-bind, so the two geometry layers no longer use gpu.matrix.push_pop(); the line layers still do.

    26. 🔴 Object mode, and a floor that follows the user. logic.hull_offset_percent() + logic.layer_uniforms() — the whole layer/mode decision in one pure function, so all 14 tests in dev/tests/test_diff_state_outline_width.py run without a GPU. _HULL_MIN scales with the chosen percentage: a fixed floor silently ignored a deliberately thin rim on any small object, which reads as the slider not working — the exact complaint the setting answers. layer_uniforms takes screen_ok (the machine's answer, not the user's wish) and falls back to OBJECT when the program will not build; test_the_fallback_matches_what_object_mode_would_have_drawn pins that the fallback is not a third behaviour.

    Changed¶

    1. 🟢 The take's Still-or-Animation mode no longer selects the camera set. assigned_cameras() used to branch on still_mode.resolve_still through the provider seam: one camera on a Still take, the whole cut list on an animating one. So the number of cameras a user saw changed behind them whenever a take changed mode, and no control said it would. _visibility_plan() asks the visibility MODE instead, and the probe is gone from both the chooser and the switch gate. Pinned by test_the_takes_still_mode_no_longer_changes_the_answer, which asserts a Still take and an Animation take with identical cuts assign identical cameras. Saved settings carry over through _migrate_config_dict (see Added entry 1 for the table).
    2. 🟢 TKS_OT_ApplyCameraVisibility polls on the two rules, not on the mode. On Request stopped being an enum value and stays as the operator it always really was -- tks.apply_camera_visibility, its Shift Alt H binding and its row-menu entry. Gating its poll on OFF would have deleted the value the retired MANUAL trigger carried while claiming to keep it, so the poll now refuses on exactly one condition: both auto_camera_show_assigned and auto_camera_hide_others off, with the same sentence the execute path reports. apply_camera_visibility() dropped its visibility_enabled guard for the same reason -- it is the writer every manual caller comes through. The old "cancels when both sub-flags are off" test drove that branch through bpy.ops, which the poll now blocks; it asserts the CANCELLED/FINISHED pair at the source instead, since execute is still the scripted entry point (Constitution rule 7).
    3. 🟢 The tree row menu names the mode in force. tree_context_menu lost layout.prop(prefs, "auto_camera_visibility") and the mode.enabled gating -- OFF IS the off state, and a disabled chooser is one you cannot use to switch back on. The master checkbox was the only thing that answered "is it on?" at a glance, so the layout.menu row carries the answer itself, its label composed from the enum's own enum_items name with pgettext_iface on each half (an f-string text= never reaches the catalogue as one source string). One walk over three items in a draw path: a real call, not a heavy one (ARCH-05). TKS_MT_CameraVisibilityMode.bl_label Apply When -> Camera Visibility; the class name keeps its ...Mode suffix, which is an identifier and not a label. Three tests replace the greying assertion.

    4. 🟢 Tree Design's menu icon SETTINGS -> OUTLINER (panels/context/tree_context_menu.py, ~L501). The wrench is also the tks_show_output_rule glyph in ops_tree_design._PIN_ITEMS, so one icon named two unrelated things; OUTLINER is unused elsewhere in that menu (IMAGE_DATA, CAMERA_DATA, THREE_DOTS, HIDE_OFF are the neighbours). bl_idname stays tks.icon_visibility_settings -- manual_map.py (~L1073) and the wiki anchors resolve on it, and the file already carries a comment saying so. The popover's Colors box header moved OUTLINER -> COLOR so the tree glyph names one thing. Both literals are asserted present in the running Blender build.

    5. 🟢 The tree-line colour became a sub-row under its own switch. Same checkbox-then-detail shape as Tag Color / Width directly above it, in ops_tree_design.py and preferences/draw_interface.py alike; the label on the swatch row is now Color, and Tree Line names the checkbox. In prefs the colour row also greys with self.default_tree_lines rather than hiding, so the section keeps its height.

(the six-tier list resolve_cascade walks) and vl_switch.bump_cascade_token(scene) (the undo-boundary bump the VL switch performs). apply_overrides' ACTION branch and the per-object tks_action callback stay on the legacy writer (its empty-action guard, test_empty_action_never_clears.py, is a behaviour the sweep does not have).     8. 🔴 Empty Action Unassign (user ruling 2026-09-06). Four rules. (1) cascade_apply.apply_overrides ACTION branch runs apply_vl_switch_unified instead of the legacy writer, so creating/assigning a tier action drops the parent's action from the objects at once (the legacy guard "an action that animates nobody must not unassign everybody", the 84-object wipe, is RETIRED in cascade_actions.apply_action_to_watched — what it protected, parent keys surviving, is Parent State's job). (2) An empty slot is not an assignment: both doors bind populated_slots only; sync_jit._rest_action_has_slot counts a slot only when it has keys so an empty slot never blocks the fresh-action fold. (3) revert_snap: a target whose bound slot lost its LAST key gets clear_action (slot, action and Parent State layers) before the snap. (4) _release_actions_that_lost_their_last_key: an action in the modified set with no keyed fcurve in any slot leaves every tier prop naming it (_tier_holders: global, scenes, view layers, takes, groups) and drops its fake user — never bpy.data.actions.remove; stands down in Rest State Mode and under Value Lock; the Rest action is never released. A fresh, never-keyed action is untouched (nothing was witnessed lost). Tests: dev/tests/test_empty_action_unassign.py (replaces test_empty_action_never_clears.py). Post-merge (user rulings 2026-09-07): the revert pass opens mark_undo_recovery() before it writes, so unbind + release + snap attach to no push of their own and ONE Ctrl+Z restores key, binding and tier; a released action with users == 0 is bpy.data.actions.remove()d (never-auto-delete exception, recorded in memory). The empty-action tests close the queue's recovery windows after each test — in a tight -k selection they otherwise leak into test_mutation_queue_single_push.

    22. 🔴 Generated channel census in the coverage probe. dev/scripts/channel_coverage_probe.py gains a census block: it walks bl_rna.properties from every root Takes routes (Object, Mesh, Material, ShaderNodeTree, World, Scene, ParticleSettings, Key) to depth 3 and records every struct owning an animatable FLOAT/INT/BOOLEAN that is a real value (not a select/is_/lock_/mute/hide_/show_/tag flag) as a FAMILY keyed by its address prefix (OBJECT:modifiers[…].). ID-typed pointers are roots, not sub-paths — that is the routing boundary. A pruned name list (channel_coverage_core.CENSUS_SKIP_POINTERS & co.) drops the animation system's own bookkeeping, thumbnails, alias pointers (active_*, parent, child, bone, relative_key), raw geometry arrays, editor state and this addon's tks_* PropertyGroups; pruning can only hide a family, never mark one covered. One member per family is keyed (generic factories for modifiers, constraints, pose bones, particle systems, force field, collision, soft body, rigid body (+constraint, +world), GP material, particle fluid, shape keys, shader nodes and inputs), routing is re-driven per owner object AFTER keying, and classify_census diffs. First 5.2 run: 41 found / 41 built / 38 surfaced / 3 fell through / 0 unbuilt. The three are real routing gaps, left as findings for their own cards: particle_systems[…].* object-side keys vanish once the ParticleSettings also carries an action (PARTICLE retargets to settings, OBJ excludes the prefix); root props of a ShaderNodeTree (NODE requires nodes[); root props of a Key such as eval_time/use_relative (SHAPEKEY requires key_blocks). Also adds the modifier hand builder (Subsurf + a Geometry Nodes socket keyed through modifiers["X"].properties.inputs.Socket_N.value, the 5.2 shape). It now builds build_log_filename(undo_reader.undo_base_name(), date, get_source_suffix()), so main keeps takes_for_blender_undo_<date>.log (empty suffix reproduces the historical name, and old tapes therefore still list and still parse) and a worktree writes …_<date>_<suffix>.log. undo_base_name() derives from log_base_name(), so renaming the debug log renames its tape in lockstep. One preference therefore names the pair and they cannot drift. build_log_filename / parse_log_filename are untouched — the kind rides in the base, exactly as the tape's _undo already did. Both panels now strip only the SHARED stem plus the extension, so the rows read debug_2026-09-08_worktree and undo_2026-09-08_worktree. _cleanup_old_logs globs the shared stem, so its 7-day sweep reaches both.

    28. 🟢 One-time rename of the logs already on disk (utils/log_migrate.py). The alternative — teaching both pickers a second, legacy name — leaves two schemes in the code forever, and a log the panel can no longer open is a log that is gone; these are the files a bug report is rebuilt from. migrate_legacy_log_names() walks the log dir, parses each name under the legacy bases (takes_for_blender.log, then takes_for_blender_undo.log — undo FIRST so the order does not depend on _STEM_RE's date anchor continuing to reject undo_<date>), and os.renames it. Never overwrites an existing target (it may be the file a live session is writing), never raises (an open file on Windows just fails the rename and keeps its name), runs at most once per session. The pure _plan() half is what the tests drive. Called from a first_interval=0.0 one-shot in register_logger(), not from register_logger itself: it reads a preference, and add-on preferences are not reliably reachable during registration. The same one-shot rewrites debug_log_filename when it still holds the legacy default — reads already map it (_raw_base_name, raw_base_name), but the Preferences field would otherwise keep showing a filename nothing writes. 9 tests in dev/tests/test_log_migrate.py.
