It used to be glued onto the label with an em dash, so a long detail pushed the label out of view. tks.value_chip_info gained an icon_only flag: drawn as a label Blender prints the value at the top of the tooltip, but drawn as an ICON there is no label, so the value has to come through description() - which the class now defines (and its bl_description had to go with it, per test_no_new_shadowed_constant). The cell is drawn even when empty so the timestamp column does not jump.

    35. 🟢 The waiting-writes line moved into the stats bar. As a status row under the list it appeared and vanished with the number, and every appearance shoved the whole panel down a row. stat_filter_bar gained notes (trailing non-filter cells, drawn through the same info chip so the sentence has somewhere to live) and alerts (bucket values painted red - ORPHAN, which is the number this monitor exists for). The old orphan sentence is dropped outright: the Orphan bucket already carries that count.

    36. 🟢 styles.LIST_ICON_UNITS = 1.35, shared by all four monitor UILists. One unit fits the glyph and nothing else, so the text started hard against it. Shared because the four lists are one row design wearing four sets of icons. Undo's phase icons are line-style only per the user's ruling (2026-09-09) - BLENDER, GREASEPENCIL, LOCKED, INFO and ERROR became DRIVER, DECORATE_KEYFRAME, DECORATE_LOCKED, STATUS_INFO and STATUS_WARNING - the OUTLINE TWINS Blender ships beside the filled ones, not substitutes for them (STATUS_INFO / STATUS_INFO_FILLED, and the thin DECORATE_* family). Only the Blender logo and the grease pencil have no outline twin at all. The detail chip is INFO_LARGE, user's pick: not INFO (filled) and not STATUS_INFO, which the STATE phase already wears - two different things must not share a glyph. The phase icon sits beside the TIMESTAMP, where its column always was; the label keeps the full width to its left. dev/tests/test_undo_monitor_icons.py pins four things: every literal exists in this Blender (they drift between versions), no solid glyph is back, every recorded phase has an icon, and no two phases share one - the icon is the only place the phase is named now.

    37. 🟢 The rest snapshot no longer walks every Rest slot per channel. _rest_has_path walked every Rest slot's fcurves for every channel of every selected object - 31 ms for 50 selected objects, 346 ms for 200, on EVERY selection change (measured on the real code, dev/measure/bench_rest_catch_before_gesture.py). rest_cache.rest_tracked_index() builds slot name -> {(path, index)} once, keyed on the Rest action's name and slot count, dropped by note_rest_changed() after every rest keyframe write (keyframe_write._note_rest_changed), on undo/redo invalidation and on a full clear: 1.6 ms and 18 ms (dev/measure/bench_rest_catch_indexed.py). Same answers, one dict lookup each.

    38. 🟢 Smart Undo retired. operators/ops_smart_undo.py (tks.smart_undo / tks.smart_redo, the 'Screen'-keymap hijack, hijack_status) is gone, with the undo_smart_hijack preference and its callback, the Hotkeys "Undo" section (expand_hotkeys_undo), the texts / de_DE / manual-map rows, flush_pending_push (only the hijack called it), the tape's press-owner counter (set_press_owner / next_press_step), and test_smart_undo_pair.py / test_smart_undo_press_bounds.py. EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 849 -> 847. It existed because one autokey gesture cost two Ctrl+Z: it pressed once, then checked whether the press had landed between Blender's two snapshots and pressed again. With every keying and transform key running through the gesture macros (Added 21-22) the add-on's share lives inside the user's own step, so Blender's own Ctrl+Z is one press and a second one skipped a step - field report 2026-09-09, "with smart undo enabled it's not working well". Two things stay: a give-back net in ops_gesture_macro.register(), because up to v0.8.2 the hijack switched the user's native ed.undo items OFF and kmi.active is saved in userpref.blend; and the six Required Core Strategies, which govern what happens AFTER a press (the post-undo cascade, the seal refusal inside the recovery window), not how many presses a gesture costs. The Undo Monitor's status row reads the doors now - door_status() = (pref on, rows bound, rows in the table). Merge 4319c6a0.

    39. 🟢 Viewport Tool Settings sync ships on. All eight toggles under Workflow > Sync - the master plus its seven groups - defaulted to False, so a fresh install carried the whole feature dark and the user had to tick eight boxes before one tool setting followed them between scenes. preferences/props/props_sync_viewport.py; only default= moved, so Blender's stored values still win and the flip reaches fresh installs and Reset to Defaults only. Merge 40e3ec8d.
    40. 🟢 Both sides of a tier's type glyph are padded from one number. The Context tree drew each name flush against its icon, which already had 0.5 units on its LEFT (KIND_L_PAD) and nothing on its right. utils/tree_metrics.ICON_SIDE_PAD_UNITS is now the single source and every tier calls the same draw_name_gap() at the same point in the row - right after the icon slot, right before the name column - so one tier cannot start its name in a different column from its siblings. Reserved in absolute ui_units like the rest of the tree metrics: a separator() collapses inside an align=True row and a scale_x shrinks with the panel. All six tiers. Merge 0f3cae4b.
    41. 🟢 The undo strategy rows lost their prose and their badge glyph. Eight strategies x two lines of RNA description turned one accordion into a wall of text at exactly the moment a user needs to scan it. A row is now [toggle] Name [i] [badge], the same words behind the [i] on hover - nothing lost, because the checkbox already carried that description as its own tooltip. TKS_OT_PrefHelp is a GENERIC carrier: prop names any add-on preference and the tooltip is read from that property's RNA description, so the next page that wants this adds a draw call, not a ninth operator. The [i] sits OUTSIDE the locked zone on purpose - a user who cannot flick the switch is the one who needs to read what it does. The badge glyph went with it, and badge_color with that (a parameter kept past its only reader is a dead thread-through). Merges 3ad05a41, 2adfeedb.
    42. 🟢 The Required Core Strategies rationale is a house warning box. It was six loose labels drawn straight into the accordion - the one piece of real warning text on the page, and the only one without the frame. Now styles.wrapped_info_box(kind='warning'), so it also sits behind the same Show Warning Details switch as every other warning. The unlock button stays OUTSIDE the box on purpose: hiding the rationale must never hide the control. Merge 637ba0b2.
    43. 🟢 Info boxes gained vertical inner padding. INFOBOX_INNER_PAD in wrapped_info_box, not at the call site: design guide 11.8 makes padding part of the info-box STYLE, so a site tuning its own would be the bug - which is why this reaches every info box in the add-on. Vertical only: the wrap budget is an ESTIMATE of region width, so indenting the body horizontally would eat space the wrapper does not know it lost and long lines would clip. Merge 8b583039.

    44. 🔴 Default rim 1.8% → 0.6%. 36 mm → 12 mm on a 2 m cube. Nobody has the property saved, so every existing file lands on the new default; that is the intent, not a migration gap.

    45. 🔴 PROP_DIFFSTATEPROPSMIXIN_DIFF_STATE_LINE_WIDTH reworded. It claimed "the box and outline marks" and never touched the outline. Reshaping the English orphans its de_DE entry (the English IS the key), so texts/locales/de_DE.py was re-keyed in the same commit: 1 reworded, 7 added, 0 orphans left. Written on bytes with CRLF preserved and ast.parsed before the write, per the two traps in the locale mechanics. First attempt used «…» around Screen/Object as quotation marks — those are TERM placeholders resolved from a vocabulary, and test_i18n_vocabulary failed on three counts. Removed.

    Fixed¶

    1. 🟢 Register-path keymap walks are gated on UI:HOTKEYS logging. The full scan reported a recovered access violation; three parallel replications of its exact launch caught it once with a stack: keymap_audit.snapshot_user_kc (the is_user_defined read) from _keymap_shared.register_pie_keymap, inside register() during a re-enable — where addon_utils.enable() has just run unregister() (operator types removed) and register() has just written new add-on-keyconfig items, leaving Blender's keyconfig rebuild pending until an event loop that a --background session never enters. The scan's named landing spots (store_snapshot.py, the German fixture teardowns) were incidental innermost frames. All fifteen register/unregister-path walks only fed the hotkey debug log, off for every user, so they were pure cost and the whole crash surface. New choke point register_phase_snapshot() (walks only when _audit_logging_enabled()), None-tolerant dump_snapshot/diff_snapshots, fifteen sites in five files routed through it; the same gate the load/save handlers got on 2026-09-01. Guard test dev/tests/test_keymap_audit_register_gate.py (structural: no raw snapshot_user_kc() outside the audit module; behavioural: zero walks with the topic off, unchanged with it on). 3169 impact-selected pass; the scan launch ×3 on the branch: 0 faults vs 1 in 4 before. Auditor 9.5 / 17, identical to main. Write-up: doc/troubleshooting/register_keymap_walk_access_violation.md.

    2. 🟢 assigned_cameras() returned the whole cut list even for a STILL take. (Superseded by Added entry 1 before release: the take's Still mode no longer selects the camera set at all -- _visibility_plan asks the visibility MODE, and the still_mode.resolve_still probe this fix added was removed with the rest of the Still fork.) The set contract was written for an ANIMATING take, where hiding a cut camera deletes its cut (Blender's switch skips hide_render cameras). A still take is pinned to one frame, so only one cut can ever apply and the rest are assigned to nothing -- which made Isolate a near no-op on exactly the takes the default Apply When value (On Still Mode) exists to isolate. Reported from the sample file: Still_MultiCam (cuts at 1 and 48, pinned to frame 1) left both CAM_A_Top and CAM_A_Wide visible. assigned_cameras now asks still_mode.resolve_still through the provider seam (sibling feature, ARCH-02; a torn-down Still answers False, which keeps cuts alive -- the safe way round) and returns only camera_at_frame(cuts, scene.frame_current) for a still take. Animating takes are untouched, pinned by their own test. Three tests in dev/tests/test_multicam_switch.py; 1144 impact-selected pass; auditor 9.5 with no new findings.

    3. 🔴 TKS_MT_CameraVisibilityMode kept its own copy of the trigger list. draw() looped a hand-written ('SWITCH_STILL', 'SWITCH', 'MANUAL'), so PLAYHEAD shipped in the EnumProperty and stayed invisible in the tree's row menu -- the only place most users reach it -- and the mode could not be turned on from there at all. Reported from a screenshot. The menu now iterates prefs.bl_rna.properties['auto_camera_visibility_trigger'].enum_items. test_the_mode_submenu_offers_every_trigger used to ASSERT the three identifiers appeared in the source, which enforced the very copy that drifted; it now asserts none of them do and that enum_items is read. Also swaps the Multi-Cam mark from CAMERA_STEREO to CON_CAMERASOLVER (user's call, reads better at chip size) in the row chip and both popover rows, with test_every_multicam_icon_name_exists_in_this_blender checking every icon= literal against the running build's own enum -- an unknown name draws blank and says nothing. 1516 impact-selected pass.
    4. 🟢 Fresh action orphan after undo. _process_fresh_actions merged the fresh {Object}Action at once but removed it on a 0.1 s timer, outside the fold's undo step; Ctrl+Z after a later delete restored the orphan. action_queue._schedule_action_cleanup now removes a zero-user source action immediately (same drain / step) and defers only an action still in use; the deferred test stays as it was — its users == 1 and not fake_user clause would remove an in-use action, so it is not used for the immediate path. doc/troubleshooting/fresh_action_orphan_after_undo.md, dev/tests/test_fresh_action_cleanup_now.py.
    5. 🟢 Rest-revert no longer gated by auto_mirror_keyframes. The mirror handler returned at the preference gate before scheduling revert_snap.schedule_revert, so with the mirror off a deleted last key neither snapped to Rest nor unbound the object (Empty Action Unassign rule 3 rides on that revert). _schedule_key_loss_revert is the one helper both the keyed branch and the gate call. Suite hygiene shipped with it: conftest.py pins auto_mirror_keyframes / auto_snap_on_clear ON for every bpy test (the run inherits the live userpref.blend). Record: doc/troubleshooting/revert_gated_by_mirror_pref.md.
    6. 🟢 Tree highlight stranded on the timeline after a Scene Follow return. _sync_timer_payload step 2 (panels/context/handlers.py) follows the window's view layer only when it CHANGES, keyed on the _last_active_vl memo. The memo was stamped BEFORE the 0.5 s move guard was checked, so a switch observed in the same tick as a tree rebuild (which arms the guard) was recorded as handled and never retried - the bar stayed on the layer the window had left. Reproduced headless: the first look after a rebuild consumed the memo with the guard up (dev/tests/test_seq_follow_tree_highlight.py, red on main at the OUT leg, green with the fix). Fix: a change seen under the guard is left unstamped and completes on the next tick; only a FIRST look (memo None - load, undo, session start) is still stamped under the guard, which keeps test_tree_index_snap.py's no-tug-of-war contract. Two new latched DEBUG lines (UI:SYNC "highlight follow: ...") name what the follow did or why it waited. doc/troubleshooting/tree_highlight_lost_under_move_guard.md.
    7. 🟢 "Came from" button did nothing. TKS_OT_SequencerGoBack.invoke (features/sequencer/operators.py) guards on context.area.type == 'VIEW_3D' for the MOUSEMOVE binding - but the sidebar button is drawn in the SEQUENCE_EDITOR sidebar, so every press was refused as "a return is pending, but the mouse is over SEQUENCE_EDITOR" and passed through. The existing button test called bpy.ops without INVOKE_DEFAULT, so it only ever exercised execute(). Fix: an empty trigger (a press) runs execute() first and still returns PASS_THROUGH; new latched line back: button: pressed. Test test_sequencer_go_back.py::test_the_sidebar_button_works_from_the_sequencer_area invokes with a SEQUENCE_EDITOR area override (red on main, green fixed). doc/troubleshooting/seq_go_back_button_refused_by_area_guard.md.
    8. 🟢 Hover loop after "Came from". With the Hover rung on, pressing the sidebar button returned the window and the very next MOUSEMOVE over that same sidebar fired tks.sequencer_focus_switch (trigger HOVER) and sent it out again. Ruling (user, 2026-09-07): the N panel is not "using the sequencer". TKS_OT_SequencerFocusSwitch.invoke now passes a HOVER through when context.region.type == 'UI'; every other rung is untouched. A stateful "hold Hover until the mouse leaves" was drafted first and dropped for this region rule. Test test_sequencer_go_back.py::test_hover_does_not_fire_from_the_sequencer_sidebar (invoke called directly with UI vs WINDOW region overrides). doc/troubleshooting/seq_go_back_button_refused_by_area_guard.md (follow-up section).
    9. 🟢 Re-fold after redo. Redo replays the key insert (fresh {Object}Action recreated and worn) but not the fold, which ran on a timer with no undo step, and fresh-action detection is depsgraph-driven + suppressed 0.5 s after undo/redo, so nothing folded until the object moved. sync_jit.refold_fresh_actions (provider inspector.refold_fresh_actions) is called by _settle_recheck_redo 1.5 s after a redo. doc/troubleshooting/fresh_action_not_refolded_after_redo.md, dev/tests/test_refold_after_redo.py.

    10. 🟢 One Gesture, One Step. Blender's memfile step holds Blender's half of a gesture; the addon's half (fold, bind, Parent State layers, release) ran on timers outside it, so redo restored only Blender's half and each earlier patch replayed one piece. core/reconcile.py::reconcile(scene, view_layer) recomputes that half from the tree, idempotently: fold fresh {Object}Actions (synchronous sync_jit.jit_merge_now via provider inspector.refold_fresh_actions), unified sweep, release_empty_tier_actions (slots-no-keys: released everywhere + removed at zero users; no slots: released only where its tier is not the window's active tier). Both settle hooks in vl_lifecycle_undo call reconcile_after_undo_redo inside mark_undo_recovery(); revert_snap delegates to the same release rule. Sweep: a slot is populated only with a KEYED F-Curve (a channelbag outlives Alt+I), and a target wearing the target action with an unpopulated slot is unbound. dev/tests/test_one_gesture_one_step.py (real memfile stack: key → delete → undo → redo → undo), doc/troubleshooting/undo_redo_one_gesture_one_step.md. Card: active/one-gesture-one-step.md.

    11. 🔴 Unresolved channel paths become rows, not silence. Both Channels row builders ended their resolve step with a bare continue: panels/channels/channels_helpers.py::_collect_items and the inline loop in sections.py::TKS_PT_ChannelModifiers.draw. A path that core/channels.py::rna_path_resolve could not split into (parent, prop) produced no row, no report, no log line — while get_key_count_for_target still counted it, so the badge and the list disagreed. Field report 2026-09-07 ("Takes does not see my modifier keys") turned out to be panel STATE (Slotted mode + Current-frame view), and a sweep of all 83 Modifier.type values in 5.2 resolves clean — but the exit stays a latent trap for the next data_path reshape (5.2 already moved GN inputs from IDProperties to modifiers["X"].properties.inputs.Socket_N.value). Fix: both builders append {'unresolved': True, 'parent': None, 'prop': None, 'sort': UNRESOLVED_SORT} carrying the raw path; _render_item_groups gained a target= kwarg and paints them last under an Unresolved group via new _draw_unresolved_row (row.alert, prop(target, raw_path) attempt — the same shape as draw.py's General Properties fallback — else an ERROR label). Search matches the raw path; NATIVE/ADDON source filters hide it (unclassifiable). The Modifiers loop was extracted to module-private _collect_modifier_items(target, active_paths, search_term) so it is testable; groups whose first item is unresolved get the ERROR icon. Companion field tool dev/scripts/diag_channel_coverage.py prints, for the active object, every F-Curve Blender holds vs. what each Takes channel type surfaces, plus a file-wide action scan — run it FIRST on any "missing key" report. dev/tests/test_channel_unresolved_row.py (4 tests); 1353/3496 impact-selected pass. Follow-up card: a generated is_animatable census to replace the hand-typed CORR-09 _ANIMATABLE_SURFACES.

    12. 🟢 Ctrl+M dispatched on the list FAMILY, which cannot name a list. TKS_OT_GlobalMultiselect.poll compared _list_context(context) — that is core.list_focus.current_family(wm) — against a hand-kept ('CONTEXT', 'TAGS', 'VARIANTS'). FAMILY_INSPECTOR was not in it, so the chord was inert over tks_inspector_objects / _actions / _slots. Since Ctrl+M is what turns multi-select ON, tks.global_select_all (Ctrl+A) and tks.global_invert_select (Ctrl+I) were unreachable there too — not broken: TKS_OT_MultiSelect._walk_visible has always handled OBJECTS, ACTIONS and SLOTS, and their polls only require a non-empty wm.tks_multiselect_list. Nothing could set it by keyboard.

      The poll's comment claimed the inspector lists "do not announce themselves". That stopped being true when tks_inspector_{objects,actions,slots}_index were given claimer('INSPECTOR_*') callbacks — they claim focus on every row click. The stale comment is what made the gap read as deliberate.

      Fix: new core/list_focus.MULTISELECT_TYPE_OF, mapping each registry KEY (not family) to the list_type its button carries, with None for the render queue, which has no tick boxes. current_multiselect_type(wm) reads it through current_key; ops_global_shortcuts._multiselect_type() wraps that and both poll and execute dispatch on it. Deliberately a separate table rather than a sixth column on LISTS: the two vocabularies do not match key for key (SPLIT_SCENE_GROUPS → SCENEGROUPS, INSPECTOR_ACTIONS → ACTIONS), and a column would have implied they do. dev/tests/test_multiselect_key_routing.py asserts every key in LISTS appears in the table, that nothing stale remains, and — the invariant the whole fix exists for — that every list_type drawn anywhere in the package is reachable by the key (AST-read from op.list_type = "X" and styles.list_stats(..., list_type='X')). See doc/troubleshooting/list_keys_and_bulk_duplicate.md.

    13. 🟢 All five split lists share FAMILY_CONTEXT, so a family dispatch named the tree for every one of them. Ctrl+M over the split Scenes list ran bpy.ops.tks.multiselect(list_type='CONTEXT') and toggled the tree's selection. Not reported — found while fixing entry 12, and cured by the same move from family to key. Pinned by test_each_split_list_toggles_itself_not_the_tree.

    14. 🟢 TKS_OT_DuplicateAction's poll and execute disagreed about what a selection is. The poll returned any(item.tks_selected for item in wm.tks_inspector_actions) under tks_multiselect_list == "ACTIONS", so the button un-greyed for a whole ticked selection — and execute read only wm.tks_inspector_actions_index, copied that one action and returned {'FINISHED'}. Tick ten, press, be told it worked, get one. TKS_OT_RemoveAction, twenty lines below in the same file, has always collected the ticked names.

      execute now collects [item.name for item in wm.tks_inspector_actions if item.tks_selected] when multi-select is on, falls back to the highlighted row (the delete twin's shape), sets use_fake_user = True on every copy per the house action policy, and reports a count for a batch. Multi-select is NOT cleared afterwards — delete clears it because the ticked rows are gone, duplicate leaves the sources in place. dev/tests/test_duplicate_action_bulk.py parks the highlight on an UNTICKED row, so an index-reading regression fails on the name it copies rather than on a count.

      Found by the auditor rule written for it first: CORR-29 Poll-Only Bulk Mode, on blender-addon-auditor branch feat/list-key-dispatch-rules. One finding on the whole Takes tree, and this is it.

    15. 🟢 The tooltip's Shortcut: gate was a second hand-kept copy of the same three names. TKS_OT_MultiSelect._KEYED_LISTS decided whether compose_tooltip prints the chord; it held ('CONTEXT', 'TAGS', 'VARIANTS') beside the dispatcher's identical tuple. They agreed with each other and were both wrong: the button is drawn on ELEVEN lists. It now derives from core.list_focus.KEYED_MULTISELECT_TYPES, which is itself derived from the dispatch table, and test_the_tooltip_names_the_key_on_every_reachable_list asserts the two are equal so they cannot drift again.

      Remaining, deliberately out of scope: CORR-28 List Family Dispatch Coverage reports eight dispatchers in operators/ops_global_shortcuts.py that cannot reach the INSPECTOR and RENDER_QUEUE families. This branch fixes one (Ctrl+M). The other seven — Del, F2, Ctrl+G, Alt+G, Ctrl+N, Ctrl+T, Shift+D — need a target operator and a confirm story per list, which is a feature, not a fix.

      i18n: Duplicated {count} Actions and This list has no multi-select added to texts/locales/de_DE.py (verified with dev/scripts/i18n_extract.py --locale de_DE: missing count 50 → 48). 16. 🟢 Shortcuts resolved the CLICK, never the hover. _list_context read current_family(wm), which prefers tks_active_list_key (the last row click) - so hovering a list and pressing a key acted on wherever the reader had last clicked, until they clicked inside the new list once. hovered_key(context) was already exact and already used by the row menu; the shortcuts never asked it. New core/list_focus.focused_key / focused_family / focused_multiselect_type(context): hover, then click, then the ambient family. Over a list that is NOT ours focused_family answers FOREIGN_LIST - a real string, not "", because every dispatcher reads "" as "use the tree", and that default firing over the debug log is Del deleting a take. Pure tests in test_list_focus.py. Needs in-app confirmation that the Window keymap hands context.property to a KEY event the way it does to Shift+RMB. 17. 🟢 _walk_visible fell through for SCENEGROUPS / VLGROUPS / TAKES to return True - Select All and Invert reported success over nothing on the three split-view group lists (Constitution rule 7). Each branch now mirrors its UIList: Ungrouped (no tick box) is skipped, VL groups and takes follow tks_context_scenes_index / tks_context_viewlayers_index through a shared _split_target_scene. TestTheSplitGroupLists in test_multiselect_walk.py. 18. 🟢 Hover only counted ON A ROW. hovered_key read context.property, which Blender sets for the row button under the cursor and NOT for the blank space below the last row - there only context.ui_list is set, and with no way to map a UIList class to a key that read as a foreign list, so the keys refused. New UILIST_OF (key -> UIList bl_idname) and hovered_key falls back to ui_list.bl_idname when no row is under the cursor. test_every_drawn_list_is_recognised_by_its_uilist_class walks every template_list(...) in the package against the table. 19. 🟢 OP_MULTISELECT_KEYS named Ctrl+M and the two clicks, never Ctrl+A / Ctrl+I. compose_tooltip has one {key} hole and this button has three keys to name, so TKS_OT_MultiSelect.description now translates the gesture block itself and fills {key_all} / {key_invert} from live_shortcut before the composer sees it; an unbound chord drops out with its locale joiner (re.sub(hole + r"\s+\S+\s+", "") - "or" / "oder"). de_DE re-keyed in lockstep. Found by asking the auditor's new CORR-28 matrix for the full picture: it lists 4 keyless buttons beside the inspector lists (remove_from_watchlist, add_to_watchlist, remove_action, delete_slot), left standing as routing features. 20. 🟢 Del over the inspector. TKS_OT_GlobalDelete gains an INSPECTOR branch that resolves the EXACT list through focused_key (the family is three lists wide) against _INSPECTOR_DELETE - remove_from_watchlist / remove_action / delete_slot - and invokes with INVOKE_DEFAULT, so the key shows the same confirm dialog as the button. Poll delegates to the target's poll. dev/tests/test_inspector_key_routing.py. 21. 🟢 Ctrl+N over Objects -> add_to_watchlist via _INSPECTOR_NEW; Actions and Slots have no "new" beside the list (popovers), so the key stays quiet there. The four routed operators grow a composed description() with a live {key} (OP_*_KEYS in tooltips_inspector.py / tooltips_slots.py, de_DE re-keyed), which is what MAINT-14 requires of a routed button. These are the four keyless buttons the CORR-28 matrix reported; the seven family-level findings for Rename/Group/Ungroup/Retarget/Duplicate stay, as their lists draw no such button. 22. 🟢 One gap under the minus, everywhere. styles.row_menu_button already adds its own separator; Objects and the tree added a second one above it, and Variants and the five split lists wedged move/merge/retarget buttons between the minus and the menu. Now every column reads add, minus, menu (own gap), separator, the rest - the Actions column, which the user named as the reference. Layout-only: inspector_sections.py, draw_tree.py, variant_switch/panel.py, draw_split.py.

    16. 🟢 The shutdown log flush read add-on preferences. Field crash 2026-09-08, Blender 5.2, EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION (0xc0000005), read of address 0x0, on a normal GUI quit. Stack: BLI_ghash_lookup ← BKE_addon_pref_type_find ← Addon_preferences_get ← RNA_property_pointer_get ← pyrna_prop_to_py ← PyObject_GetAttr ← … ← PyUnstable_AtExit ← WM_exit_ex ← wm_exit_handler. Chain: keymap_audit._atexit_marker → _flush_now → the captured _FLUSH_SYNC_AT_REGISTER (= logger._flush_sync) → _log_destination_key (called unconditionally) → prefs.preferences. Blender frees the add-on preference type registry before Py_Finalize runs atexit handlers, so that GHash lookup dereferences NULL. It is a C-level fault, so the except (AttributeError, KeyError, RuntimeError) guarding that read cannot catch it, and addons.get(...) returning a live wrapper is not evidence the type registry is alive — only the .preferences pointer-get touches it. Intermittent because _flush_sync returns early on an empty _log_buffer: it needs unwritten lines at exit. Same family as the 2026-05 atexit crash, different mechanism — that one was a re-import after purge_modules() (signature: stacked PyImport_ImportModuleLevelObject frames ending in pyrna_srna_Subtype); this one has no import frames at all. _LOG_PATH_AT_REGISTER / _FLUSH_SYNC_AT_REGISTER exist because of that fix, and the gap they left is the lesson here: capturing a callable does not make its body finalize-safe. Fix: new logger._flush_cached_only() — drains _log_buffer to _log_filepath_cached, no bpy, no lookup, writes nothing when no path was learned; logger._flush_sync(*, allow_prefs=True) delegates to it when False, and the live default still recomputes so a mid-session Log File change (or TKS_TEST_CONFIG_DIR) keeps moving the log at once. New keymap_audit._flush_now_finalize() calls the separately captured _FLUSH_CACHED_AT_REGISTER; _atexit_marker calls that instead of _flush_now. The two flush entry points are deliberately separate functions rather than one branching function, because _flush_now names _flush_sync in its lazy-import fallback and an AST guard cannot see past a branch. dev/tests/test_logger_exit_safe.py (4 tests): the finalize flush writes with _log_destination_key/get_log_filepath monkeypatched to raise; it is a no-op with no cached path; the default path still follows a moved destination; and a contract test walks every function reachable from _atexit_marker across both modules and fails if any mentions .preferences — it named all three offenders (_log_destination_key, get_log_filepath, get_log_dir) before the fix. Not reproducible headless: --background exits clean on both the old and new code (verified A/B), because the GUI wm_exit_handler path tears down more before Py_Finalize. Confirmation needs a real GUI quit with a warm buffer. doc/troubleshooting/log_flush_exit_access_violation.md. Card: active/log-flush-exit-crash.md.

    17. 🟢 Object-side particle keys had no reader. Particle animation lives in TWO datablocks: count/show_unborn on the ParticleSettings ID, and seed/use_hair_dynamics on the ParticleSystem, which is stored in the OBJECT's action as particle_systems["Name"].prop. Both collectors pick target = ps.settings the moment the settings carry an action, then read only that action; OBJ excludes "particle_systems[" in p. So the object half vanished — but ONLY once the settings were also animated, which is why the hand-built probe never saw it and the generated census did. Fix: new core/channels.py::object_side_particle_filter(obj) (active system by name AND index, mirroring the existing ps_filter), and a PARTICLE union pass at the end of BOTH get_inspector_keyed_paths and get_key_count_for_target that appends whichever half the earlier passes did not read, de-duplicated by data_path. channels_helpers._collect_items now points resolve_target at the Object for a particle_systems[ path when the routing target is not the Object — otherwise the row resolved to nothing and landed in the new Unresolved group.

    18. 🟢 A property of the node TREE carries no nodes[. default_group_node_width (and custom props on the tree) are keyed on the tree's own action, and the NODE / WORLD_NODE filter is "nodes[" in p.

    19. 🟢 eval_time carries no key_blocks. Absolute shape keys are animated through it; the SHAPEKEY filter is "key_blocks" in p or "shape_keys" in p. Fix for both: new core/channels.py::is_own_path(p) — true when a path names no nested container (nodes[, key_blocks[, particle_systems[, modifiers[) and no data. prefix — plus a separate own_filter applied ONLY to the target's own action in both collectors. path_filter stays strict because the second try reads a PARENT's action, where the same bare path belongs to the parent; two guard tests pin diffuse_color out of the Nodes view and location out of Shape Keys. _path_passes_type_filter in channels_helpers follows for NODE/WORLD_NODE/SHAPEKEY.

Card: active/channel-census-gaps.md.

The revert reads that generator and resolve_id_type instead of its own list and its own id_type literals, so the revert and the snap engine can no longer disagree about what exists. Third occurrence of this disease after core/channels.py and core/vl_targets.iter_anim_targets.

Without layers it lands on 1.0. Both correct; a resolver in rest_state would have recomputed an answer Blender already had and then had to avoid fighting the NLA stack. Three earlier measurements each lied first (the take action emptying and being released; a single-key parent producing a zero-length strip; view_layer.update() not re-running the anim system after a direct write) — all three are written up in the troubleshooting doc.

    25. 🔴 The addon sealed undo steps that held no change — field tape 2026-09-09: a redo at 78.21 and an undo at 82.81 both landed on a state identical to the one before them, and four more presses in the tape before it did the same. The user pressed Ctrl+Z, nothing moved, the press was gone — reported as "one step is being ignored or lost". The step was there; it was empty. A drain counted as work because a callable RAN, and a callable that looks at the scene and decides there is nothing to do ran too.

    REVERTED the same day. Nine undo behaviour changes landed on 2026-09-09 with no soak time and the user's verdict on the set was "it got worse". This and entry 38 both decide WHETHER A STEP EXISTS, so they went back together — neither disproven, neither judgeable while the other moved.     _execute_pending now returns True only when the DATA changed. _data_fingerprint() covers exactly what this queue's callables write: slots, F-Curves, keys and users per action, plus the action every animation holder wears — holders from iter_animdata_holders, so a value keyed inside a material's nodes counts like any other.

    Safe in the dangerous direction by construction: a fingerprint that cannot be taken returns None, and a None NEVER suppresses a seal. Suppressing a real fold would be far worse than the empty step this removes; test_an_unanswerable_fingerprint_never_suppresses holds that.

    Self-limiting, because it is on the hot path. One walk of every action's channel bags costs 0.64 ms against 800 F-Curves (measured; the whole-file fingerprint 1.17 ms, holders half 0.27 ms), it runs twice per drain and a keyframe drains about three times. The first walk over _FP_BUDGET_MS (2.0 s → 2.0 ms) switches the check off for the session with a WARNING and a tape row. Losing the fix on a heavy rig costs a wasted Ctrl+Z; keeping it would cost frame rate while the user animates. Asking get_slot_fcurves per slot re-walked layers and strips per slot — 1.36 ms; the single walk replaced it.

    The WRITE tape row moved to AFTER the work. undo_trace._account treats a WRITE as something a seal still owes a step to, so announcing the drain up front made every no-change drain surface later as an ORPHAN that never happened. A no-change drain gets a HANDLER row instead.

    The first attempt named location, rotation_euler, scale on Object, and the user answered it in one line: "What about all other value types for all other object types?" Reading them all back was then MEASURED, not argued: walking every animatable RNA property on every holder costs 3.69 ms at factory startup, 65.31 ms with 100 objects, 74.83 ms with 4000 keys on top — twice per drain, three drains per keyframe, against a whole-undo budget of ~0.5 ms — and it still could not see a node socket.

    So the queue stops asking the file. _revert_unkeyed_to_rest_deferred already counted what it snapped and now RETURNS that count; _execute_pending treats any non-None answer from a callable as authoritative and keeps the fingerprint for the rest. Exact, free, and complete for every value type on every datablock type, because the function that wrote the value is the one being asked. A callable added here that writes values MUST return a count — pinned by a test on the real function, not a stand-in.

    1. 🟢 _handle_undo_pre had lost its @persistent — undo-chain audit, 2026-09-09. The decorator sat one function above where it belonged, on _note_reconstruction, a plain helper that is never registered as a handler and where it does nothing.     For the record: @persistent marks the function by SETTING _bpy_persistent — to None. Presence is the signal, truthiness is not (measured, Blender 5.2); the first version of the guard test read it as True and failed on correct code. dev/tests/test_undo_handler_persistence.py covers all three handlers plus the helper that must NOT be marked.

This and entry 38 both decide WHETHER A STEP EXISTS, so they went back together — neither disproven, neither judgeable while the other moved. What returns: a gesture whose work changed nothing can seal a step that holds nothing.     1. 🟢 A refused seal named the next gesture — same audit. _settled_undo_push reset _pending_step_label only on the success path, so a gesture whose seal was refused handed its label onward and Blender's undo list called a fold "Takes: snap to Rest". Also removed there: the step-naming gate read A or (B and A), which is A — the second clause could never change an outcome.

    2. 🟢 Two questions the Undo Monitor could not answer — the tape recorded structure (positions, worn actions, key counts, the take) and could not say whether the scene MATCHED the take, which is the whole of "a step on undo is not being reconstructed correctly".

    _note_reconstruction() asks the addon's own four health checks after every press settles — cascade drift, broken tier pointers, slot mismatches, values drifted from Rest — and writes ONE row naming what disagrees, so the tape and the panel agree by construction. The two arg-taking ones are fetched with get_provider, never query(), which passes no argument and answers None in silence.

    undo_trace.remember_state / check_landing / seen_states add the landing check the user asked for as a "replay": every state a gesture SEALS is remembered, and a press may only land on one of them. A press that lands somewhere the user has never been did not restore a state, it built one. Bounded at 300; reported once then counted as seen; recorded from the seal only, never from a press, so a wrong landing can never teach the check that wrong is normal. dev/tests/test_undo_landing_check.py (8) and test_tape_checks_reconstruction.py (5).

    1. 🟢 The Undo Monitor's two new answers, and the two shapes that were wrong first. The tape recorded structure and could not say whether the scene MATCHED the take, nor whether a press had gone too far.

    Drift, named. _note_reconstruction() asks the addon's own four health checks after every press settles — cascade drift, broken tier pointers, slot mismatches, values drifted from Rest — so the tape and the panel agree by construction. The first row said "3 value(s) drifted from Rest": true and unusable. It now names each one — Suzanne.location[1] is -0.04, neither rest nor keyed (0.0) [keyed] @frame 3 — with the frame, because the keyed half of that test only holds at frame 0 or in Rest State Mode.     Landing, third time right. Two earlier shapes both cried wolf on the field tapes, and the header of test_undo_landing_check.py names both so neither is re-derived: - MEMBERSHIP ("has this state ever existed") cannot see a skipped step — the state a skip lands on is a real one — and reported every state the addon had never SEALED as one the user had never been in; - DISTANCE in a first-seen list cannot see one either. A user who walks back and forth builds a list ordered by when a state was first MET, not where it sits in the stack, so an ordinary redo read as "skipped 2".

    The stack POSITION needs no guessing: the running sum of the ed.undo / ed.redo calls that actually went out, counted in _step_twice at the only two places one completes. check_landing asks the user's own question — coming back to the same point in history must give the same scene — and puts BOTH scenes plus the step number in the row. First visit only learns; new work truncates the forward record exactly as Blender truncates the redo chain. test_undo_landing_check.py (13), test_tape_checks_reconstruction.py (7).

The user had already chosen the safer half of that trade (entry 33: never MAKE an empty step); adding the other half back was a mistake. The one proven collapse signal stays — a Blender-default {Object}Action the press brought BACK — and the "changed nothing" row stays as a reading, not a decision. test_smart_undo_crosses_empty.py → test_smart_undo_press_bounds.py, its crossing test inverted with the reason in the docstring.

Impact-selected run: 3670 passed, 0 failed. 50. 🟢 The rest-snap's ARRAY branch never cast the F-Curve float. Found by the auditor, not in the field: the CORR-09 clear-key probe (scan 2026-09-09) reported one wrong family — OBJECT: parent_vertices, expected 1.0, actual 0.0, "no gate identified — the write itself failed". Every revert gate had passed; the write itself threw. A rest value comes out of an F-Curve and is therefore always a float, and Blender refuses a float on an int RNA property (expected an int type, not float). coerce_rna_value has fixed exactly that since the CyclesWorldSettings.max_bounces bug — but only on the SCALAR branch. _snap_one_target (features/rest_state/snap_engine.py) and _apply_value (features/rest_state/logic.py) both wrote the raw float into an array element, Object.parent_vertices is an int array of 3, and the TypeError was swallowed by the loop's own except as a WARNING. New core/path_utils.coerce_rna_value_for_path(root, data_path, value) — the same cast, addressed by RNA data path instead of by owner + property name, because a data path is the only form an F-Curve carries; it rpartitions the path, resolves the OWNING struct and defers to coerce_rna_value. An unresolvable path returns the value untouched, so a caller fails as it did before rather than differently. Float arrays (location, scale, colours, node vectors) pass through unchanged, which is why this survived so long — those are the arrays the addon actually touches. _apply_value could not simply absorb the array case: it setattrs a whole array, and the snap writes one index at a time on purpose so components that kept their keys are never disturbed. Six tests appended to dev/tests/test_rest_rna_value_coercion.py, including the pin that obj.parent_vertices[0] = 1.0 raises. Full record in doc/troubleshooting/clear_key_landing_int_array.md.
