    52. 🟢 The Rules and Tags sections drew nothing, and nothing said so. panels/globals_panel.py calls tag_library_ui.draw_tag_library_mode(...) through the PACKAGE, and the large-file split had trimmed panels/tag_library_ui/__init__.py down to from .draw import TKS_MT_TagAddMenu - so both modes raised AttributeError on every draw. Blender SWALLOWS what a panel's draw raises and shows an empty panel, so no test, no log line and no error reported it; it was found by a reader navigating to a panel that was not there. Present on main BEFORE this branch merged (git show 99c0d419:... has the trimmed line) and carried through the merge, which took main's side of that hunk. The export is restored with a note saying why it is public. New dev/tests/test_panel_package_exports.py walks every <package>.<attr>(...) call in panels/ and fails when the package does not export the name - the check that could have caught this the day it broke.

    Changed¶

    1. 🔴 Internal: six duplicated code paths collapsed to one implementation each; verified dead code removed. Behaviour-neutral except where noted. operators/inspector/ops_slots.py — select_all/invert_selection were mirror twins over their first two thirds (= True vs = not <lvalue>); folded into _walk_visible(context, list_type, decide) with a module-level _FILTER_TO_CAT (the two copies were byte-identical) and the cloned dead categories_with_matches deleted. The CONTEXT tails stay separate — invert's seen_* dedup bookkeeping is required semantics, not duplication. ai/api.py — five verbs (switch_take, delete_take, rename_take, create_take, explain) opened with the same scene+VL resolution; _resolve_scene_vl returns (scene_obj, vl_obj, None) or (None, None, envelope) with BYTE-IDENTICAL codes/messages/hints (facade contract AI-04). _resolve_tier_target's near-miss (dict-wrapped envelope, different wording) is pinned as deliberately separate. core/cascade.py — _write_world_record/_write_camera_record were verbatim twins apart from the recursion flag, resolve_world_adopt_target/resolve_camera_adopt_target apart from a pref name and two prop names; now _write_tier_record(..., flag_attr=) + _resolve_adopt_target(kind, ...) over a 3-string table, all four public names kept as wrappers (external callers in ops_apply_scene_camera.py/ops_apply_scene_world.py). is_world_reconciling/is_camera_reconciling stay DISTINCT — a shared flag would let one write silence the other's callback. Everything stays module-local (R-HOT-PATH-COHESION). panels/context/draw_layers.py — draw_take and draw_vl each spelled their 7-column icon cluster twice; AST-compared with the pin conjunct/overflow/import-placement stripped (draw_vl identical; draw_take differed only in where take_has_variant is imported), then merged behind wm.tks_show_X and (_draw_all or wm.tks_pin_X) with _draw_all = not collapsed per row — same two attribute reads per column, no new call, no string building on the draw path. -138 lines. take↔vl NOT merged (~0.40 similar: different data sources, idnames, alert logic). features/batch_render/process_manager.py — 107 identical lines across BGRenderManager.poll/FastBGRenderManager.poll (incl. a 30-line byte-exact run) hoisted to _drain_stdout/_apply_engine_line/_apply_status_line on the base, with _on_task_start/_on_task_done/_on_task_error hooks carrying the real deltas (Fast learns active_task from the worker's start line, pops the queue, clears on done/error) and _LOG_LABEL keeping "BG"/"Fast BG" distinct in the render log. The process-exit tails stay separate — genuinely different lifecycles. Dead code swept: preferences/persistence_io.py (unused webbrowser/Operator/StringProperty/4 OP_* constants, duplicate function-local import json, write-only _project_prefs_warning global — get_project_prefs_warning() checks the path on disk each call; ops_addon_ui.py:391 had a second copy with no reader either), core/vl_lifecycle.py (commented-out V1 sequential pipeline; seven from .event_bus import emit, X lines collapsed to one), duplicate import lines in mirror_logic.py/sync_viewport.py/ops_action.py/ops_camera_levels.py, panels/inspector/handlers.py's import of three names it never used, ops_crud.py's zero-caller _get_existing_override stub, tag_library.py's dangling "Rebuild full tag cache" comment (no cache in that module; the rename already propagates every reference), and 84 try: <call> except ImportError: pass guards whose try body contains no import — a call raises NameError, never ImportError, so the guard could never catch anything (persistence_io.py:381 already made the same call unguarded two lines above a guarded one). Unwrapping used an AST filter restricted to a verified-safe callee set; every one of those callees either imports nothing or handles its own ImportError internally (event_bus.emit, providers.query), and any try containing an import was left alone. KEPT by prior decision: _apply_preview_cascades, the preview_bg plumbing (lost-feature suspect, own ticket), rename_scene_in_ledgers + its caller. New characterisation tests land BEFORE each fold: test_multiselect_walk.py (7), test_ai_scene_vl_preamble.py (4), test_cascade_world_camera_twins.py (7), test_bg_poll_dispatch.py (10). Auditor AST-only scan, main -> branch: CORR-20 Impossible Except Guard 85->1, CORR-19 Phantom Deferred Import 47->44, CORR-21 Never-Filled Collection 2->1, CORR-22 Loop-Variable Capture 1->0, CORR-23 Write-Only Local 2->0, CORR-24 Unknown ID-Type Literal 1->0, MAINT-11 Clone Code 2269->2225, MAINT-09 Import Hygiene 829->805, MAINT-10 Commented-Out Code 2->1, MAINT-03 135->133; quality score 2.05 -> 3.00.     2. 🟢 The preset change tip says that Accept or Revert resolves the change, not saving the file. (In-app confirmed 2026-08-27.) texts/infoboxes.py's INFOBOX_PRESET_CHANGES_SCOPE read "Changes are kept per scene until saved or reverted.", drawn by panels/navigation/warnings/presets_changes.py:63. "saved" reads as Ctrl+S, which resolves nothing: there is no pending-change store at all — features/render_presets/preset_state.get_preset_diffs:479 recomputes the diff on every redraw from the preset JSON (load_preset_cached → serialization/crud.load_preset:242) against live RNA (preset_engine._capture_for_type), and features/render_presets/ registers no save_pre/save_post/load_post handler (the only save_pre registrants are core/cache_version.py, core/store_guardian.py, core/vl_lifecycle.py:511 and utils/keymap_audit.py, none of which touch preset state). So wm.save_mainfile is a strict no-op for preset dirtiness and the warning returns byte-identical after a reload. The only writers are tks.update_render_preset (ops_manage_crud.py:117) and tks.save_all_dirty_presets (ops_manage_sync.py:104), both overwriting the JSON in the preset's own tier (decode_preset_key → find_preset_tier → 'USER'), so Accept carries cross-scene / cross-file blast radius; tks.revert_to_preset re-applies the preset onto the scene. New wording names both buttons. texts/locales/de_DE.py re-keyed in lockstep (a texts edit that leaves the old key behind trips test_i18n_guard); the entry keeps its alphabetical slot and reuses the button translations Übernehmen / Zurücksetzen. Commit 0388c101.
    3. 🟢 The changelog is split into a working pair and an append-only archive, and the release cut is a script. The 0.8.0 cut was a ~400-line manual text move and it went wrong: the ## [0.7.11] - 2026-07-12 heading ended up ABOVE the last twenty dev Fixed entries instead of below them, so six weeks of August work sat under a July release with no ### Fixed header, numbered 90-109 a second time — Fixed 90 named two different fixes in one release. Neither file looked wrong while reading it. The split. Entries are written in CHANGELOG_UNRELEASED.md / CHANGELOG_UNRELEASED_DEV.md. CHANGELOG.md / CHANGELOG_DEV.md keep their names (GitHub and the shipped ZIP expect a complete CHANGELOG.md) and become append-only, with a pointer where their Unreleased block was. The cut. New dev/scripts/release_cut.py is the only thing that appends to an archive: it refuses unless the working pair is a valid mirror (same sections, same counts, contiguous 1..N), inserts one dated block into each archive, empties the working pair, and re-stamps the freeze lock. --dry-run prints without writing. The freeze. check_changelog_mirror.py digests every released block into dev/changelog_archive.lock; a shipped block that no longer matches fails the commit with "shipped notes were edited after release". The mirror and numbering checks moved onto the working pair, where drift starts and a fix is still cheap. check_changelog_terse.py defaults to the working file and falls back to the archive for an older checkout. 11 tests in dev/tests/test_changelog_split.py cover all three, including the 0.8.0 failure itself as test_editing_a_shipped_release_fails.

    4. 🟢 The unreleased user entries are a TIGHT list again. A blank line between two items makes Markdown render a LOOSE list - each entry wrapped in its own paragraph, with a gap around it. Every block before 0.8.0 is tight; 0.8.0 itself shipped with 39 blank lines between entries and the unreleased block had drifted to spaced throughout, so one document rendered two ways. 14 blank lines removed, and check_changelog_terse.spacing_offences() now refuses a commit that puts one back. The archive was normalised in the same pass — 44 blank lines out of CHANGELOG.md (39 in 0.8.0, which shipped spaced while every older block was tight, plus 5 strays among the pre-marker **Bold** entries), with all 1175 entry lines asserted byte-identical before and after and dev/changelog_archive.lock re-stamped. That is a deliberate one-off: the freeze refused it first, which is the guard working. The rule is pointed at the user file only: the dev mirror's entries are multi-line paragraphs that Markdown would run together without the blank line. +3 tests.

Follow the Playhead is what applies the strip's take under the playhead (handlers.poll_follow + on_frame_change); shipping it off read in the field as "the merged feature does not work" — the in-app report that triggered this was scrubbing with no view-layer switch, traced to the pref being off, not to a defect. The caution that shipped it off is covered elsewhere: sequencer_cache_off (ships ON, consulted only while the follow is on) guards the stale-frame footgun, and the write paths honour the mutation locks. Existing profiles keep their saved value — the autosave JSON overrides the default, so only fresh installs see the change. New pin test_sequencer_follow.py::test_the_follow_ships_on (red before the flip, green after, verified against the worktree code via BLENDER_USER_EXTENSIONS); no test pinned the old default.

    8. 🔴 UI vocabulary pass: INFO-18 197 findings -> 0. Every edit driven by the rule's own findings (file+line+literal), so only the exact reader-facing strings it named were rewritten - no property identifier, no bl_idname, no RNA path moved (naming standard section 7). Terms: View Layer (was ViewLayer/VL/View-Layer, 93), Folder (Directory), Configuration (Config), Settings (Options), Data-block (datablock), Watchlist (Actions List), Autokey. Verbs: 27 Create X -> New X; Drop & Re-apply -> Revert & Re-apply (Revert already names that act in the same feature's drift warning). Collisions settled by MEANING, not by picking one word - Clear empties an assignment, Remove takes a thing out of its list, Delete destroys it: Remove Action said permanently in its own docstring so it is now Delete Action (matching the confirm pref already named that); Delete Selected/Clear Selected keep their verbs but name their object (... Items / ... Properties); Delete Item -> Delete Tag or Group; token keeps both words for its two acts. tks.remove_slot RETIRED - it duplicated tks.delete_slot (same confirm gate, same multiselect, same targets) and was drawn nowhere and bound to no key; class, registration and manual-map row removed. Five tooltips stopped leaking a property name at the reader (vl.use -> 'render icon'). Protected, not renamed: {viewlayer} naming-template tokens and the 'directory' option identifier - added to the glossary allow list, since renaming those breaks what the user must type. Glossary also gained verb_collision_allow (auditor commit 0568fad) for the three legitimate pairs. de_DE re-keyed in the same commit for all ~150 changed strings (orphan+untranslated guards green). Suite 2762 passed; INFO-18 re-scan 0 findings / 7 exempt over 4134 strings. Field rounds after the first build closed four interaction defects the unit tests could not reach: the viewport route never followed at all (sync_viewport sets the row inside the _syncing_objects_list guard, which silenced the index callback - the sync now runs _follow_selection itself); Scene/World rows could not be clicked (Pass 2 re-pointed the watchlist whenever the row name differed from the active object, and a synthetic name never matches - it now reacts to _last_synced_active changing); a World animated on its NODE TREE looked unanimated (_animated_target prefers the row's own action, else walks iter_anim_targets_only, the same list the button walks); and a plain click died on a Scene/World row after that row deliberately cleared the viewport (_selected_special_row_id supplies the source, active object otherwise).     9. 🔴 Report messages brought onto the glossary, and their plural glue split. INFO-18 read only declared labels, so a clean 0-finding scan said nothing about the status line an operator writes into the info area — a string a reader reads exactly like a label. The rule gained a report_msg harvest site (auditor branch feat/info-18-report-terms, e520a81; terms only, since a status line is a sentence: "Created 3 takes" is not a Create button), and Takes immediately reported 29 findings over 4892 strings where every other site kind reported none. All 29 fixed here across 15 files: VL(s) 13, directory 7, ViewLayer 5, config 1. Fourteen of those sites carried (s) plural glue, which [[project_multi_language_support]] bans — a translator cannot inflect a phrase around it. Each is now an explicit pair chosen at the call site, pgettext_rpt('… {count} View Layer') if count == 1 else pgettext_rpt('… {count} View Layers'), both literals visible to dev/scripts/i18n_extract.py (a helper would have hidden them: the collector and INFO-10 key on the pgettext_* call-site NAME). Two judgement calls: Rendering {len} VL(s) ({skipped} non-VL ignored) became … ({skipped} ignored) — non-View-Layer re-introduces a banned variant (View-Layer), and a second count in the same sentence would need four templates for one status line; and Removed ViewLayer: {vl_name} merged onto the Removed View Layer: {vl_name} key that already existed, closing the duplicate the German second-witness pass first exposed. de_DE re-keyed in the same commit (section 13.5, no grace period): 27 keys, 13 of them split into a German singular/plural pair, which also removed the mirror-image Ansichtsebene(n) glue. Every German VERB is left exactly as the translator settled it — entfernt where it said entfernt, gelöscht where it said gelöscht — so the act-split ruling merged on main is untouched; only the noun and the plural move. Four German values still reading {count} VL(s) are fixed as a side effect. Guards: orphans() 0, untracked() 0; INFO-18 re-scan 29 → 0 over 4906 strings; suite 2652 passed, 1 skipped, with the four known worktree collection errors. NOT touched, and worth a later card: sibling messages abbreviate VLG and SG (View Layer Group, Scene Group), which the glossary does not know, and (s)/(n) glue survives in strings the rule never looked at, e.g. Cleared action on {count} child(ren).

The glossary gained View Layer Group (banning VLG, VL Group, VL-Group, ViewLayer Group) and Scene Group (banning SG), plus the same rows in doc/standards/naming_conventions.md §13.2. Same ruling as the parent term: the short forms only ever appear in a status line or a popover header, never anywhere a reader could learn them. INFO-18 then reported 20 findings, all fixed here. Eight of the twenty were invisible until the rule learned to read a text= that is an EXPRESSION rather than a literal (auditor 6ab9139): four cascade popover headers draw pgettext_iface("Action -- VL Group '%s'") % name, which _str_kwarg could not see. The same pass caught VL Switch Profiler and Timeline Options (→ Timeline Settings, Options is banned) — neither is a group name, both had been drifting in plain sight behind the same blind spot. layout.label(text=f"ViewLayer: {vl.name}") in ops_cascade_layers.py was BOTH the wrong word and the only popover header in its family that was never translated. It is now pgettext_iface("View Layer: %s") % vl.name with a de_DE key, matching its four siblings — a term fix and a translation gap closed in one edit, which is why it is not a separate entry.     11. 🔴 Plural glue swept out of every translated template. Entry 9 split the 14 sites the vocabulary rule happened to report; a tree-wide AST sweep for (s) / (es) / (ren) inside a pgettext_* template found 68 more sites / 62 distinct templates, at labels, confirm dialogs and status lines the rule never looks at. [[project_multi_language_support]] bans the glue outright — a translator cannot inflect a phrase around slot(s), and German has to agree an adjective and a case ending with the same number. (verb agreement), nicht erfasster Wert / nicht erfasste Werte (adjective ending), %d leeren Slot entfernen? (accusative), and Ruhezustand-Kanal (the translator had written only the plural).     12. 🟢 Build Syntax popup widened: TKS_PT_TokenBuilderPopup.bl_ui_units_x 30 -> 36. (In-app confirmed 2026-08-30.) The token grid is a grid_flow(columns=4, even_columns=True) inside that fixed width, so the four columns split whatever the panel is given and cannot grow past it — a token wider than a quarter of the panel clips to an ellipsis with no other symptom. Shortening the region names bought headroom but left [resolution_percentage] (23 characters with brackets) sitting on the edge, which is the residual shift the user saw. 36 units gives each column ~9 units instead of 7.5. Chosen over the render_jobs_popup_width treatment (a preference plus _apply_panel_width’s unregister/re-register dance in features/batch_render/jobs_popover.py) — that is a real feature with a prefs row, German text and an EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT bump, and is worth its own card if the fixed width ever chafes. The two halves of the bargain are now written down together: the class comment says to raise the width or shorten the name, and test_no_grid_token_name_is_too_long_to_render fails the moment a name outgrows resolution_percentage.

    13. 🟢 resolution_x / resolution_y now report the RAW scene setting; the percentage-scaled value moves to the new _scaled pair. Semantic correction, not a rename. Both tokens have always resolved through the legacy cluster names res_x / res_y, whose bodies are int(r.resolution_x * (r.resolution_percentage / 100)) — so [resolution_x] silently returned the SCALED size while its own registry description said "Resolution X", Blender's property of that name holds the raw value, and Blender's native {resolution_x} (the token ours is declared to BE, via BLENDER_NATIVE_NAMES) resolves raw too. Three sources of truth disagreed with the code. Now resolution_x / resolution_y dispatch on themselves and return str(r.resolution_x); _LEGACY_TOKEN_ALIASES maps resolution_x_scaled → res_x / resolution_y_scaled → res_y instead, so the cluster bodies are untouched and — importantly — a saved path containing the legacy [res_x] keeps resolving to the scaled value it always did (test_legacy_res_x_alias_keeps_the_scaled_meaning pins exactly that, and it was the one test GREEN before the implementation). User-visible risk, stated plainly: a saved render path using [resolution_x] at a resolution percentage other than 100 will now produce a different folder/file name. At 100 % (the default, and what the alias test's other cases cover) nothing moves. test_blender_native_tokens.py's exact-equality assertion on _LEGACY_TOKEN_ALIASES and test_token_builder.py::test_categorized_tokens_search_filters were updated for the new names. (Verified 2026-08-30 by the same live probe: at 1920x1080 and 50 %, resolution_x answered 1920 and resolution_x_scaled answered 960, while the legacy res_x still answered 960 — the back-compat promise holds in the shipped code, not only in a unit test.) Branch feat/more-builtin-tokens, merged 84dfb21a.

    14. 🔴 MAINT-12 keeper audit: 8 dead parameters removed, 3 marked # PARAM-OK. The auditor's Dead Parameter Thread-Through inventory reported 15 sites and its dev take warned "some are documented keepers, and at least one is a lost feature". Read all 15. THREE are deliberate and now carry # PARAM-OK with the reason in place, all from the same rule - never traverse kmi.properties, which segfaults inside rna_builtin_properties_lookup_string once the operator's SRNA is torn down: utils/keymap_audit._kmi_props_string(kmi) (the function returns "" on purpose, so dropping the parameter would leave a helper that reads like dead code and invites the crash back), utils/keymap_audit._is_ours(props_str) (its docstring already said "kept in the signature so callers don't need to change"), and panels/pie_menus/keyframe_keymap._find_existing_pie_kmi(pie_id) (matches on idname + kmi.alt precisely to avoid reading properties.pie_id). EIGHT are plain leftovers, deleted with their call sites: _vl_fingerprint(vl), _get_property_source(scene) (8 call sites), _get_effective_collections(variant_idx), _draw_inherited_source(group_name), _first_scene_in_sg(wm), _first_vl_in_vlg(wm), _draw_global_row(item_count, row_count) - whose caller computed len(bpy.data.scenes) on every redraw for a value nothing read - and _draw_batch_progress_bar(wm). THREE are NOT cleanup and are deliberately left for their own cards: _render_preview(preview_bg) drops a colour the UI collects and the CLI carries five files deep; _draw_inherited_source(take_index) is unused while the body calls get_active_take, so a row popover can answer for a different take; _check_warning_state(scene) reads bpy.context instead of the scene it was handed. Headless suite 2783 passed, 1 skipped; the single test_ai_call_log failure (test_the_sync_flush_rolls_to_todays_file) is the known log-flood flake - a baseline run against main failed TWO DIFFERENT tests in that same file (test_an_opted_in_ai_line_survives_the_info_level_gate, test_a_crash_traceback_is_never_muted), which is what a tail-window race looks like.

    15. 🟢 17 cascade popovers stop answering a modifier in silence — and a fourth gesture nobody could have known about. Card phase, doc/roadmap/active/tooltip-single-source.md. Scanning operators/cascade/ for "does invoke() branch on a modifier, and does the tooltip say so?" returned 17 buttons with a shipped, documented-nowhere gesture and only 1 that named its key. Reading each invoke() to write truthful text turned up more than the Alt+Click clear: the if event.alt: branch contains a nested if event.shift: that clears the level AND every level below it, so Alt+Shift+Click is a cascade wipe that appeared in no tooltip, no label and no docs. Leaf tiers (View Layer, Take) have no nested shift — nothing below them — so they take a three-key block; parent tiers (Global, Scene Group, View Layer Group, Scene) take four. Two shared templates in texts/tooltips_misc.py, TIP_CASCADE_KEYS_PARENT / TIP_CASCADE_KEYS_LEAF, with the keys as holes filled from texts/keys.py. The state logic is untouched. Rather than rewrite 17 bespoke bodies, each description() was renamed to _describe_state() byte-for-byte and the class given a new description() that returns compose_tooltip(purpose, state, gestures) — a new helper in operators/cascade/_helpers.py that joins purpose, state and the gesture block with the house blank line.     17. 🟢 Tooltip house style — explanation first, shortcuts last, one Key: effect line each. (In-app confirmed 2026-08-30.) Each function should get its own line. All hotkeys should be at the end of a tooltip." Blender renders \n in a tooltip as a real line break but never wraps a long line — it clips at the popup width — so a one-liner that buries Alt+Click mid-sentence is unreadable by construction. The standard. doc/standards/tooltips.md (normative, sibling of naming_conventions.md): purpose first, shortcut block last, key first then ": " then the effect, one shortcut per line; §2 line length, §3 no trailing period on a line, §4 dynamic tooltips, §5 the # TOOLTIP-OK opt-out for prose that names a gesture rather than offering it, §6 the i18n lockstep, §7 what the guard checks.     24. 🟢 A Tooltips page in Preferences: two switches and a value style, with a worked example built by the real composer. (In-app confirmed 2026-08-31.) Blender gives an add-on no bold, no colour and no markup inside a tooltip, so line order and omission are the only levers there are; this turns both into the reader's choice instead of one decision made for everybody. show_tooltip_explanation (default True) drops the purpose line and tooltip_state_style (VALUE_FIRST default, PLAIN) chooses whether the state reads above the purpose; both are read lazily through bpy.context.preferences.addons rather than by importing preferences/, since texts/ sits below it and the import would be upward (ARCH-01). The explanation survives whenever nothing else would remain — an empty popup reads as a broken button, not a tidy one. texts/compose.example_tooltip(style, with_keys, with_purpose) builds the preview through the same composer the real tooltips use, so it cannot promise a shape the add-on does not produce. The cascade popovers needed a fix to benefit: operators/cascade/_helpers.popover_description pre-joined purpose and state into one string, so the two beats arrived as one and the order could never be swapped — the style did nothing on exactly the buttons it was built for. A QUOTED style is deliberately absent: compose_tooltip receives the state as one finished string and cannot tell the datablock name from the source that won it, so quoting wrapped the whole line; it returns when the 28 state builders become templates with a {value} hole (doc/roadmap/ideas/half-german-tooltips.md). EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 583 → 586 with each bump's reason recorded in place. Caught by the suite: the eight new strings had no i18n decision, and one of them still described the cut quoted style — English corrected first, German written against the corrected wording.     25. 🟢 The synonym backlog INFO-18 was blind to, plus two rulings that changed the standard. Card ui-vocabulary-standard, phases 4 and 5. A fresh scan opened at 9 findings over 5463 strings — Options in nine cascade gesture tooltips, everything else already clean. That number was never the work: the real backlog was the ~15 SYNONYM pairs the German second witness had exposed, which the term check cannot see because neither spelling is banned. Blind spot four: plural forms. The term patterns compile as \b<banned>\b, so ViewLayers walks straight past a ban on ViewLayer. Adding the plurals to the glossary turned a 0-finding scan into 112 findings — ViewLayers 11, VLs 2, VIEWLAYERS 1, datablocks 4, plus the two new terms below. Every banned list now carries its plurals, and §13.2 says a new entry must too. This is the fourth blind spot in the series (declared labels → report_msg 29 → ui_text_template 8 → plurals 14): a clean scan has never once been proof the words were clean. Ruling 1 — Add-on, not Addon (76 sites). Blender writes the hyphen everywhere in its own interface, so Blender's word wins beat the add-on's own 76:2 majority. The Autokey precedent (dominant form wins) does not apply, because it is explicitly conditional on Blender being inconsistent, and here Blender is not. File Name over Filename (18) on the same footing, with the German Dateiname already covering both. Ruling 2 — Select, and the Select/Pick split withdrawn. User ruling: if Pick and Select do the same thing, we choose Select. Measured against the code they do: Pick Existing Camera, Pick Scene, Pick Tag and Select Render Preset all choose one entry from a chooser, and only tks.select_scene_camera touches Blender's own selection. The German translator had already written wählen for every one of them — the same conclusion reached from the other side. So the nine preset choosers keep Select and six Pick … labels move to it; §13.3's two-verb definition is gone rather than nine labels being wrong under it. Pick and Choose join the banned list. The ban reaches labels only: TIP_VL_CAMERA_KEYS reads {click}: pick a camera three lines above {ctrl_shift_click}: select the assigned camera, and collapsing those would rebuild exactly the ambiguity the German entfernen/lösen split removed. Prose is judged on terms, never verbs — the same line already drawn at layout.label(text=…) and report(). The other judgement call closed itself. Is Open Config Folder the same concept as a saved Configuration? — the Config → Configuration rename had already landed, every reader-facing string says Configuration, and the button opens exactly the folder holding the Configuration File. One concept chain, nothing to rename. Synonym pairs settled (each a glossary term now, so a regression reports): Add-on Prefs→Add-on Preferences, File Out Preset→File Output Preset, Color Mgmt→Color Management, Tags Filter→Tag Filter, Into Group→To Group (one target_group property drawn four times, named two ways), Top Middle→Top Center, Preserve→Keep, Safety Copy→Snapshot on the two log-topic labels. Unassign is banned as a fourth verb for the get rid of a thing act — the cautionary case, because the collision pass can only see verbs the glossary declares, so four Unassign … labels sat invisible beside the Clear/Delete/Remove triple it does police. Unassign Slot→Clear Slot, Unassign the action slot→Clear the action slot assignment, Unassign Slotless→Clear Slotless, Unassign Action→Clear Action Override (its own docstring already said clear the manual action override, and Override is the house word). NOT verified by an actual render. 78. 🟢 A written frame is not a finished job. render_write_handler fires once per FRAME WRITTEN; it stamped DONE and cleared shared._pending_render_vl every time, so an animation take read as finished after its first frame and every later frame reported nothing at all — the sample handler bails when _pending_render_vl is None. It now compares sc.frame_current against sc.frame_end and only finishes on the last frame (a cancel still finishes immediately, since the engine wrote a partial file). render_complete_handler gained a guard with it: moving it to render_complete (entry 76) put it AFTER the last write rather than before, so its POST stamp would have walked DONE back a step. A probe against a real Blender pinned the firing order and counts — three frames give three render_post, three render_write, one render_complete. 79. 🟢 The in-flight bar reads the frame counter for a sequence instead of guessing from time. update_live_progress fills the bar from elapsed / tks_last_render_time until the render_stats handler takes over on the first real sample. For an animation take that recorded time was measured on ONE frame, so the ratio reaches its 0.99 cap within seconds and the monotonic guard then pins it there for the rest of the sequence — and on an engine whose stats lines never match _RE_FG_SAMPLE, nothing ever takes over. A multi-frame job needs no guess: sc.frame_current IS progress, so it now feeds job_progress(...) with a zero within-frame fraction, stepping once per frame. Single frames keep the time curve unchanged. prev hoisted above the branch, since the one-shot diagnostic below logs it either way. 80. 🟢 Every render bar formats its percentage to two places. One frame of a 250-frame job is 0.4% of that job and a fraction of that across the batch, so int(x * 100) left both bars reading the same whole number for minutes. job_snapshot.total_bar and progress_display now format .2f, and the Render Queue tab's two copies (render_queue_panel total, render_queue_lists RENDERING row) call those helpers instead of formatting their own, so the popover and the queue cannot drift apart. 81. 🟢 The whole-batch bar moves during an animation take. Its in-flight slot only uses a take's own progress when that progress is REAL — _has_real_progress, set by the sample handler — and falls back to wall-clock projection otherwise. Frame-counter progress (entry 79) is measured too, so a new TKS_OT_BatchRender._has_frame_progress is set beside it when a multi-frame take's bar is driven by sc.frame_current, reset per take alongside _has_real_progress, and get_batch_progress accepts either. 82. 🟢 Real progress wins the in-flight slot outright. The slot took max(elapsed / snapshot_estimate, real_progress), capped at 0.99. That max() was right while every take was one frame and the only risk was an estimate running LONG. An animation take inverts it: the snapshot estimate can still hold a single frame's measured time, so the wall-clock ratio reaches the cap within seconds and max() locks the slot there — the batch bar read 14.14% (0.99 of one slot in seven) while the take itself showed 0.80%. Real progress is now taken alone when present. 83. 🟢 The sidebar render button stops becoming the cancel button. _draw_render_mode_control returned early down three busy branches, each drawing an X in the render button's place — which put cancel exactly under the pointer that had just started the render. The menu button is now always drawn first and merely disabled while busy (it could never start a second render), with the matching cancel operator (tks.calibrate_render_times, tks.batch_render, tks.batch_render_bg_fast) in a row beneath it. The already-cancelling state keeps its greyed, non-alert CANCEL icon. 84. 🟢 The whole-batch bar is weighted by duration, not by an equal share per take. overall = (completed + in_flight_fraction) / total gave every take the same slot, so a one-frame Still counted as much as a 250-frame animation and finishing it moved the bar an eighth — 15.71% with one Still done and the first animation at zero. New pure job_snapshot.weighted_overall(weights, done, in_flight, in_flight_fraction) divides the finished takes' estimates plus the in-flight take's share by the sum of all estimates, and get_batch_progress feeds it the same frozen estimates snapshot the bar already used for monotonicity. It returns None when no estimate exists, which is when the old count-based formula still runs. DONE only, never FAILED or CANCELLED — unchanged, and for the same reason: a cancelled take never rendered, so counting it would send the bar to 100% on cancel. 85. 🟢 Borrowed estimates are scaled to the borrowing take's own length. Weighting the bar by duration (entry 84) only helps if the durations differ, and they did not: a 250-frame animation estimated ~20s beside a one-frame Still at ~14s, so the Still still took 8.68% of a seven-take batch. _estimate_vl_render_time falls back to the median of its SIBLINGS' measured times, and to the tks_estimated_render_time probe — both measured on ONE frame (cli_probe_worker renders a single frame), both handed over as raw seconds. Both are now multiplied by _frame_count(sc, vl), and the two sibling pools (_refresh_display_estimates, get_batch_progress) store PER-FRAME values so the median is a per-frame number to scale. A take's own history and tks_last_render_time are untouched — they were measured on that take's own range. 86. 🟢 A missing frame counter is inserted BEFORE the extension. Blender appends the frame number to the end of the output path, so a name that already carries its own extension — which Smart Output produces, and which apply_render_overrides then confirms by switching use_file_extension off — writes 'hero.png0001'. New pure job_snapshot.ensure_frame_number(path, ext) inserts a #### run ahead of a trailing extension, and apply_render_overrides applies it for multi-frame jobs only, skipping movie formats (one container, no counter). A path that already holds a # run is left alone — where the counter goes is the user's choice — and so is a path with no extension, where append-number-then-extension is already right. It sits OUTSIDE the tokenised-path branch, which never ran for a plain filename. Both engines get it, since the CLI worker calls the same apply_render_overrides; the background path's later normpath on the filepath keeps the hashes but is NOT verified by a real background render. 87. 🟢 The inserted counter carries a separator. ensure_frame_number produced hero####.png; it now produces hero_####.png, skipping the underscore when the stem already ends in _ - . / or a backslash so a deliberate separator is never doubled. 88. 🟢 The Image column resolves the counter, and drops it for a Still. apply_render_overrides writes the numbered path onto sc.render.filepath, which is per SCENE — so every take sharing that scene, Stills included, showed a raw #### while a sequence was in flight. New pure job_snapshot.preview_path(path, still, frame) zero-pads the hash run to the job's first frame, and for a Still strips the run AND a leading _/- with it, since a Still writes no counter at all. build_job_snapshot puts it on the path key, so the folder tooltip and the disk scan see the same string the reader does. 89. 🟢 A recorded render time now says how many frames it covered. Estimates borrowed from tks_last_render_time — the take's own, and the sibling medians — were measured when the batch rendered ONE frame, so a 250-frame animation still estimated ~20s beside a one-frame Still at ~14s and took a twelfth of the batch bar (entries 84, 85 weight correctly; the weights themselves were wrong). record_render_actual stamps vl['tks_last_render_frames'] (a plain ID property — session bookkeeping, not a setting, so no preferences count to bump), and _recorded_frames(vl) reads it back with a default of 1, which is exactly right for every value recorded before this. The estimator rescales the take's own last time by frames_now / frames_recorded, and both sibling pools divide by the frames the time was MEASURED on rather than what that sibling would render today. 90. 🔴 Diff State ships with the outline + fill on, box off, and half-strength box/outline opacity. preferences/props/props_diff_state.py: _OPACITY_DEFAULTS is now box 0.5 · outline 0.5 · fill 0.25 (was 1.0 · 1.0 · 0.25) and the master-mark default reads from a new _MARKS_ON_BY_DEFAULT = {outline, fill} instead of mark == 'box'. Both states (keyed and drift) get the same defaults; colours, line width, empty style/size and the whole per-kind table are unchanged. Only default= values moved, so a saved user_preferences.json still wins - existing users see no change, fresh installs and Reset see the new look. dev/tests/test_diff_state_prefs.py pins the new defaults (outline + fill on, box + empty off, box/outline at 0.5).

    Fixed¶

    1. 🟢 Camera Visibility writes deferred out of the depsgraph tick — intermittent EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION in deg_check_base_in_depsgraph on switch-then-transform. (In-app confirmed 2026-08-20.) apply_camera_visibility (Show Assigned / Hide Others) wrote hide_viewport / hide_render / hide_set(view_layer=…) INLINE from apply_overrides inside depsgraph_update_post; hide flags rebuild depsgraph relations and per-view-layer Bases — the structures evaluation is walking (dump: null Base lookup while workers copy the Scene in SceneBackup::init_from_scene). Found by a four-level seeded bisect: six handlers → only VL Switch Handler off stops it; handler phases → the whole fast sweep off STILL crashes, apply_overrides off does not; inside it → camera/world pointer writes innocent, apply_camera_visibility off survives every run; prefs dependency confirmed (factory startup survives — auto_camera_visibility defaults off). Fix: per-scene coalesced requests applied by a one-shot timer (_schedule_camera_visibility / _drain_camera_visibility in core/cascade.py). Failed approaches (recorded): a view-layer membership guard in the sweep (wrong hypothesis, crashed with guard in place), and routing through enqueue_mutation (vl_switch_scope drains that queue in its finally, still in-tick — crashed attempt 1). Verification: 2-step repro (seed 48291: switch_vl → rotate) 28+ runs clean vs died-on-attempt-1 before; suite 2408 passed. doc/troubleshooting/vl_switch_transform_deg_base_crash.md. Commit 49780182.
    2. 🟢 The way back is bound where events actually arrive. Both 3D View keymap items registered live and active (MOUSEMOVE ANY trigger='HOVER', LEFTMOUSE PRESS trigger='CLICK'), the outbound switch fired twice in the same session, the origin was remembered - and tks.sequencer_go_back logged ZERO arrivals. Registered, correctly scoped, never matched: verbatim the SequencerCommon failure from the outbound campaign, unrecognised in the other direction. Now bound on the global Frames map too - the one this feature has MEASURED to deliver, since PLAY and all four arrows come from it - with the operator's context.area.type == 'VIEW_3D' check, the area under the mouse, as the filter that makes a global binding safe. The Frames LEFTMOUSE does not repeat the entry removed in 0.8.0 Fixed 118: that one was tagged as the PLAYHEAD rung, so an ordinary click claimed to be a scrub; here the rung IS CLICK. The 3D View entries stay - correct home, no cost, and a return is idempotent because the first clears the origin the second would read. The two extra field rounds were spent on INSTRUMENTATION, not the keymap: invoke had two deliberately silent early returns (it rides MOUSEMOVE, and an unlatched log there writes hundreds of lines a second), so an empty log meant three different things and named none. Replaced with a latched verdict - log only when the answer changes - which is the same pattern that cracked the scrub detector. The origin check also moved ahead of the area lookup: one module-global against None, on a binding that now sees every mouse move in the application. See doc/troubleshooting/sequencer_scene_autoswitch_triggers.md.
    3. 🔴 Metaball cascade slot lookup could never match, and the miss path CLEARS the action. core/cascade_actions.py's inlined ID-type chain mapped bpy.types.MetaBall to 'METABALL'; Blender's enum member is 'META' (probed live on 5.2.0: slots.new('METABALL', ...) raises TypeError, and the member list has META and no METABALL). Both cascade paths build the slot table from Blender's own slot.target_id_type — ('META', name) — then probed it with ('METABALL', name), so EVERY metaball lookup missed. cascade_actions.py:405-415 treats a miss as "this target should not be animated by this action" and unassigns ad.action_slot then ad.action — the same path the file's own comment calls catastrophic (84-object incident). Silent: the diagnostic log at :394 only fires for SCENE/WORLD/NODETREE/MATERIAL/LIGHT/CAMERA. Reachable: core/vl_targets.py:58-61 yields id_data.data for any object with data, and metaballs are a supported animated case (naming template naming_utils.py:592). Core fix + features/rest_state/assimilation.py's unreachable GENERIC_NAMES key shipped on main as 9b7db0fe with dev/tests/test_metaball_id_type.py; doc/troubleshooting/metaball_id_type_spelling.md. This entry records it — it had no changelog line.
    4. 🔴 slots.new(id_type='OBJECT') for metaball and particle data produced a slot Blender then REFUSES to bind. core/path_utils._TYPE_MAP and core/anim_utils._SLOT_ID_TYPE_MAP (byte-for-byte twins, class-name keyed, .get(cls, 'OBJECT')) listed neither MetaBall nor ParticleSettings. 'OBJECT' is a real enum member so slots.new SUCCEEDS; binding then raises RuntimeError: ... not suitable for this data-block type (MB) one step away from the wrong answer. Reached via features/rest_state/keyframe_write.py:73 and panels/inspector/sync_jit.py:245. Same pass: panels/inspector/sync_actions.py's data sub-target tuple asked for 'METABALL' — but tracing what FEEDS target_type showed the tuple was not even the reachable half. The two isinstance chains in panels/inspector/sync_viewport.py (_sub_id_type :418, _id_type :563) had no MetaBall branch, so a metaball arrived as 'OBJECT' and could never reach that case however it was spelled; the sub-target chain was also missing Curve/Armature/Lattice, which both the tuple and the sibling chain already expected. That same value goes straight to merge_action_into_cascade(id_type=) -> slots.new(). Tests probe the LIVE enum rather than hard-coding it, put a real datablock through every callable resolver, prove the wrong id_type really does refuse to bind, and sweep the tree for the invented spelling in STRING TOKENS only (a naive grep failed on its own explanatory comments). Follow-up in the same branch closed the class: all four resolvers merged into core/anim_utils.resolve_id_type (memoized chain), with path_utils/vl_switch_fast re-exporting and cascade_actions calling it — _ID_TYPE_MEMO re-exported too so it stays one dict. NOT neutral in one direction: the dicts also had no TextCurve/LightProbe/Speaker entry, so those answered 'OBJECT' and now get their real types; TextCurve keeps answering 'CURVE' (pinned by test_sweep_round2.py:127, not a fix). doc/troubleshooting/metaball_id_type_residue.md. Commits 8545ed22, 5c66606c.
    5. 🔴 _process_target tagged the sweep's loop variable, not the datablock it wrote — and NameError out of the sweep when the object loop yields nothing. core/vl_switch_fast.py — the closure's snap step ended if hasattr(obj, 'update_tag'): obj.update_tag(), where obj is the free variable of for obj in scene.objects:. Three call sites: the object sweep (right by luck), the scene+world loop and the instance-source loop (both refreshed whichever object the sweep saw LAST). With no objects at all — an objectless scene, or TKS_STRESS_SKIP=objects — obj is never bound (the instance-source discovery loop iterates scene.objects too, so it does not rescue the empty case) and a world snap raised NameError: cannot access free variable 'obj' where it is not associated with a value in enclosing scope at :575. NameError is not in the snap block's except list and the enclosing try has only a finally, so it escaped the whole sweep. Fix: tag target and getattr(target, 'data', None) — identical to the old code when target IS the object. Tests: a structural one (the code object must have no obj free variable) plus the end-to-end objectless-scene world snap. Test gotcha recorded: core/mutation_queue.is_snap_suppressed is a 1-SECOND WALL-CLOCK gate on a module global, so any earlier undo-path test in the suite armed it and the new test passed alone / failed in a full run for reasons unrelated to the defect — it now holds that gate open explicitly. doc/troubleshooting/sweep_tagged_the_wrong_datablock.md. Commit ce4472b3.
    6. 🔴 _on_variant_select imported three names from a module that defines none of them. features/variant_switch/properties.py:650 — from .operators import parse_multi_cascade, build_multi_cascade, apply_variant_cascade. Real homes: core/variant_queries.py:42,54 and cascade_engine.py:81 (re-exported by ops_cascade.py:17). operators.py mentions apply_variant_cascade only in a function-local import inside one of its own operators, which is what made it look plausible. The callback IS armed (update=_on_variant_select at properties.py:821) and has stayed quiet only because nothing writes wm.tks_vsw_sel_variant — the sole reader is a getattr at ops_cascade.py:470. First write from anywhere, script included, would raise ImportError instead of applying the variant. Imports stay function-local: the picker resolves its menu through a deferred import to break a proxy<->menu cycle. Test gotchas: setting the real enum is refused (enum "2" not found in ('0') — retained dynamic items do not have to rebuild for a synthetic world), so the callback is driven directly with a stub context; and the guard at :644 returns before the import while addon_is_mutating holds, which is a computed property with NO setter — the test clears is_applying/is_undoing/is_redoing, since a headless suite leaves is_applying standing after a file read. No UI is re-surfaced; the callback stays dormant, just no longer armed with a broken import. Auditor CORR-19 flags this class and 44 more sites remain — their own campaign. doc/troubleshooting/variant_select_phantom_import.md. Commit 11ebae19.
    7. 🔴 Cached VL-switch rest-snap silently dropped ENUM and INT properties. features/rest_state/cache.py's snap_cached_diffs — the path a view-layer switch actually runs — re-inlined the value writer instead of calling the shared logic._apply_value:836-884 that _snap_one_target (:237,:242) and snap_single_to_rest's _write (:769-773) already use, and had fallen THREE fixes behind: (a) hasattr(prop, '__len__') instead of core/path_utils.is_array_value — a dropdown reads back as its identifier STRING, which answers __len__, so enums were routed into the array branch and died on 'str' object does not support item assignment; (b) no coerce_rna_value, so an INT property refused the float the rest cache holds (expected an int type, not float); (c) no known-boolean safety net for hide_viewport/hide_render/mute. All three raise inside the ladder's bare except (...): pass at :427-428, so the property kept its old value with nothing reported — Alt+I and the per-object path were fine, which is what made it look switch-specific. The fork also carried a verbatim duplicate of its own boolean-cast block (:397-409 == :413-425). Fix replaces the generic branch's write mechanics only; the fast-path transform ladder and per-site logging are untouched, and the scalar diff check now COERCES before comparing so a dropdown already at its rest value is not rewritten. The swallow stays (rest-state is autokey/undo hot territory; removed fallbacks stay removed). Repro: obj.rotation_mode stuck at 'XYZ' when rest wanted 'ZXY', obj.pass_index stuck at 0 when rest wanted 7. doc/troubleshooting/cached_rest_snap_dropped_enums_and_ints.md. Commit 75fc54b8.
    8. 🔴 Inspector rest-snap queue that nothing ever filled. panels/inspector/sync_actions.py — _pending_rest_snaps was declared (:14), cleared on every VL switch (:150) and read by a 132-line drain engine _process_rest_snaps (:159). No line in the addon appended to it (grep: clear + read only). handlers.py:6 imported both names and called neither. Reads as the remnant of a deliberately removed fallback, and the standing ruling is that rest-snap fires only on witnessed key-count loss (69ba211) — removed fallbacks stay removed — so deleting agrees with that ruling rather than quietly reopening it. Also collapses the doubled module-level _pending_fresh_actions binding (:15 and :134; the second replaced the list object after the module body had run, harmless only because handlers.py imports later). dev/tests/test_no_dead_rest_snap_queue.py pins the absence, so a queue like this can only return WITH a producer. Auditor CORR-21 Never-Filled Collection 2->1. Commit eef69432.
    9. 🔴 Seven more deferred imports named a module that does not define what they ask for. Same class as Fixed 6, found by sweeping rather than reading. SIX pointed at features/variant_switch/operators: ops_manage.py:125 (get_cascade_target, apply_variant_cascade) and ops_variant.py:35/51/210/258 (get_world, get_variant_display, parse_multi_cascade, build_multi_cascade, apply_variant_cascade). Real homes: core/variant_queries.py for the four query helpers, features/variant_switch/cascade_engine.py for the apply, utils/store_world.py for the world resolver. The callers are a tooltip (description() at :35), a popover draw (:51), two operator execute paths and a bulk-apply branch — every one an ImportError waiting for a user to reach it. The SEVENTH: panels/inspector/__init__.py:115 asked .handlers for mark_inspector_dirty, which lives in .cache, and the same file already imports it correctly from .cache twice. get_world had to be CHOSEN, not just repointed: features/variant_switch has two wrappers with that name and opposite semantics — ops_crud's calls get_or_create_vsw_world (its docstring: "NOT draw-safe - allocates bpy data. Operators only.") and panel's calls get_vsw_world ("Draw-safe."). Both sites here are draw paths, so both take get_vsw_world straight from utils/store_world. The tooltip also gains a if world: guard: get_variant_display dereferences the world for a single-product cascade, so making a never-run site reachable without it would swap ImportError for AttributeError. All imports stay function-local (the picker's proxy<->menu cycle). New guard dev/tests/test_no_phantom_deferred_imports.py walks every function-local from ... import ... in the addon and resolves it for real — deliberately a RUNTIME check, because panels/popovers/__init__.py re-exports through import * and a name can be resolvable without appearing in any import line a static scan can see. That distinction is not academic: the auditor's CORR-19 reported 44 sites here, and probing each pair in a live Blender showed 7 real and 26 that resolve fine through that hub. The check was fixed on the auditor side (build_namespace_table now follows readable star sources to a fixed point; blender-addon-auditor commit 999c03e, doc/troubleshooting/corr19_star_import_false_positives.md) and CORR-19 now reports 0 against this branch, with quality 3.00 -> 3.88. doc/troubleshooting/phantom_deferred_imports_sweep.md. Commit e2c14507.
    10. 🟢 _poll_slot_removal snapped to rest DURING undo - the last undo step showed the action pose instead of the rest pose. The poll exists to catch USER-initiated clears (the native template_ID 'X' fires no depsgraph event), but an undo also turns ad.action from set to None and the poll had no addon_is_mutating / grace-window check at all. Field log 2026-08-26 14:24:59: Aborting _handle_autokey_mirror: addon_is_mutating (undoing=True ...) immediately followed by SLOT POLL: action cleared on Object::Suzanne_MESH action:'01-01_blue'->'None' ..., snapping to ref - the flag was visibly up and the poll fired anyway, painting ref=0.0816 over the live=-0.0299 state Blender had just restored. Its sibling honours the window (_revert_unkeyed_to_rest_deferred: ABORTED (Undo/Redo grace) in the same log); the poll predates that discipline. Fix: after the clear is detected AND the tracker is updated, consume the event without snapping when TKS_VL_STATE.addon_is_mutating or mutation_queue.is_snap_suppressed() holds. The tracker update stays unconditional on purpose - an early return would leave the stale pair and the first poll after the window would late-fire the very snap that was suppressed (test_the_suppressed_clear_is_reobserved_not_postponed pins it; re-observe-never-snap is rest_cache's own documented rule). 6 tests in dev/tests/test_slot_poll_undo_guard.py; a genuine user clear still snaps. FOLLOW-UP FILED, not fixed here: the snap showed the ACTION pose because the rest baseline itself was poisoned - the autokey mirror re-captures insert_rest_keyframe baselines from the LIVE pose (log shows captures at frame 6 with the cascade action posing the object) after the rest slot's keys are removed by undo (they were written in undo-recovery windows with skipped undo_push). That capture-while-posed defect also skews Alt+I revert and needs its own pass. doc/troubleshooting/slot_poll_snapped_during_undo.md.
    11. 🟢 The rest cache snapshotted the ASSIGNED action's pose as the neutral baseline - "rest state is being poisoned". rest_cache._snapshot_id_block captures live values as neutral, and the cache is cleared + re-snapshotted on every undo (invalidate_and_rebuild -> _initial_snapshot_timer), on selection change and on file load. Nothing asked WHO was posing the object: a re-snapshot at frame 6 with cascade action 01-01_blue assigned read location = 0.0965 - the ACTION's output - and cached it as neutral. The autokey mirror prefers the cache (get_cached_value, source tag REST-CACHE) when writing insert_rest_keyframe baselines into the Rest action, so the action pose became "rest"; every revert then restored the action pose and the drift panel agreed with it (zero drift against a poisoned reference). The log shows the baseline re-captured repeatedly - 0.102... action-era at 14:24:25, -0.009... true rest at 14:24:54 - last capture wins. The existing _rest_has_path guard only protects channels the Rest action ALREADY covers; the vulnerable ones are exactly those not yet in it (they keep falling out because rest keys written in undo-recovery windows carry skipped undo_push and vanish with the undone step - that durability question is its own follow-up). Fix: driven_paths = the assigned action's slot-fcurve (data_path, array_index) set, skipped in both capture loops; a live value is only neutral if nothing is posing it. Undriven channels still cache from live; the Rest action posing itself does not populate the set, so rest-mode behaviour is byte-identical (rest-covered channels were already skipped as the Rest action's business - a test pins that expectation, corrected during TDD). Rejected: skipping the whole snapshot while any action is assigned - too broad, it would starve the mirror of correct baselines for undriven channels. NOTE for already-poisoned files: the fix stops NEW poison; re-store rest state from a clean pose to overwrite old poison. 4 tests in dev/tests/test_rest_cache_not_poisoned_by_action.py. doc/troubleshooting/rest_cache_poisoned_by_action_pose.md.
    12. 🟢 Value Lock did not hold across scenes — the flag was per-scene while every other mode row is global. (In-app confirmed 2026-08-27: lock in scene A holds in scene B, first-entry capture snaps a nudge back, unlock restores autokey everywhere.) Scene.tks_value_lock_enabled lived on each scene: locking scene A left scene B unguarded, and the header/pie read context.scene, so the button showed UNLOCKED after a scene switch (the reported symptom). A mode-storage audit confirmed the lock was the odd one out (Rest = master-scene flag, Still master = master scene, Autokey = written to ALL scenes by tks.toggle_autokey, Timeline Sync + Variant Live = WindowManager). Fix, the rest-mode pattern: the flag is now read/written on the MASTER scene (properties.is_lock_enabled(scene=None) / set_lock_enabled), tks_value_lock_enabled joins master_scene._SECONDARY_MARKERS so consolidate_global_records() heals stray per-scene flags from pre-fix files on load. The heavy baseline STORE stays per scene and fills LAZILY: the toggle captures only the current scene (properties.capture_scene, which sets the new persisted Scene.tks_value_lock_captured marker), and the feeder handler schedules engine.ensure_scene_captured via a one-shot timer on the first depsgraph tick of an uncaptured scene (engine.schedule_scene_capture — Handler Mutation Ban; the timer waits out the VL-switch settle window so half-applied cascade state is never baked into baselines). Entry capture also pauses that scene's autokey; the toggle now pauses/restores autokey on ALL scenes (per-scene tks_value_lock_autokey_was_on), matching the all-scene tks.toggle_autokey. New provider seam "value_lock.is_enabled" replaces every direct RNA read outside the feature (core/vl_preload ×3, rest_state mode/mirror_logic/revert_snap, panels mode_toggles/navigation/process_overlay) so lower layers never import the feature upward (ARCH-02). New prop tks_value_lock_captured + tooltip; de_DE re-keyed in lockstep (INFO-09). test_rest_mode.py::test_rest_mode_value_lock_conflict_helper rewritten to the provider contract (the old test pinned the per-scene semantics). 9 tests in dev/tests/test_value_lock_global_scenes.py (master-scene flag, provider, lazy capture + no-op paths, all-scene autokey pause/restore, all-scene release, stray-flag consolidation). doc/troubleshooting/value_lock_not_global_across_scenes.md.
    13. 🔴 Preset verbs for the facade (list_presets, apply_preset). Reading precedes applying because an agent cannot apply what it was never shown — the same reason list_variants precedes switch_variant. Each entry carries key (the sanitised filename it is addressed by), name (what the user typed) and tier, because the same name can live in several of PROJECT/LOCAL/SHARED/ADDON and "apply the HQ preset" is otherwise ambiguous — an agent picking the wrong tier is silently wrong, the failure mode with no symptom. An unknown kind is REFUSED with the real kinds rather than answering empty, which is why PRESET_KINDS is named rather than discovered: an empty list for a typo reads as "no presets exist". apply_preset is deliberately NOT gated behind confirm=True, unlike delete_take — the click path (tks.apply_render_preset, no invoke()) asks nothing, so gating the agent path would make clicking and asking disagree about the same action; the undo step carries reversibility. The answer reports which tier won. Tests: test_ai_presets.py (7), test_ai_apply_preset.py (8). TWO test traps are recorded in the fixture because both cost a debugging pass: resolution is captured by the OUTPUT kind, so a render preset round-trips cleanly while changing no resolution at all (green test, opposite of its name); and LOCAL/SHARED/PROJECT are preference-driven, so a REGISTERED operator resolving the addon module under a different name than the caller reads prefs as None and those tiers collapse to '' — a preset the test can see is invisible to the operator applying it, so any save-then-apply test must use ADDON (bpy.utils.user_resource, no prefs involved). AI-04 clean afterwards: 16 verbs, 16 documented. Commits 46b7bad1, 4e57e340.
    14. 🔴 Render job verbs (render_status, cancel_render). The AI-Ready card's last phase, and TWO verbs rather than the three AI-03's remedy names: starting was already scriptable because the batch operators keep their confirmation in invoke(), so execute() runs from a script. Seeing and stopping were the gaps — a job an agent can start but neither watch nor cancel is worse than one it cannot start, since it cannot know when to stop waiting or report what happened. Nothing is invented: BGRenderManager / FastBGRenderManager already tracked active_task, completed, queue, total_count and had cancel(). BOTH managers are checked — watching one would leave a render started through the other invisible. render_status answers WHILE the engine is busy, since a status call that refused because of a running render would be useless exactly when needed. cancel_render is idempotent (nothing running → cancelled: False, not a refusal), because an agent's commonest failure is retrying a call it believes timed out. It carries NO undo label while still being listed as mutating: killing a subprocess is not something Ctrl+Z takes back, so claiming an undo step would misrepresent what is recoverable. 11 tests drive a fake manager — starting a real render in the suite would be slow, machine-dependent, and would strand subprocesses on a mid-test failure. Commit dd1223c1.

    15. 🔴 create_preset — the facade saves live settings as a NEW preset. Closes the AI-Ready card's last phase. Named create_preset rather than save_preset because it REFUSES a name already in use instead of overwriting: reusing a name destroys saved work silently and with no symptom, while refusing costs one retry — and the refusal lists the names in use so the retry is informed. Delegates to tks.create_render_preset, which already captures across all nine kinds; the facade adds the clash refusal and an answer naming the tier it landed in, since the tiers are not interchangeable. tier defaults to ADDON deliberately — LOCAL/SHARED/PROJECT are preference-driven and resolve to nothing unless configured, so another default would fail on a clean install for reasons an agent could not diagnose (the trap that cost a debugging pass on apply_preset). Kinds needing something present refuse clearly: camera capture needs an active camera, world capture a world, and the message says which. 9 tests including create → apply back → assert the setting returns, so an empty file with the right name cannot pass. Commit 696315af.

Tests: test_rest_seed_memory.py (7: build-refresh, no-resurrection, wipe-keeps-seed, end-to-end re-seed beats live, never-seen captures+remembers, −1/0 parity, clear+load hook).     27. 🟢 Every checkout wrote to one log file, and no line said which wrote it. (Verified 2026-08-30 by automated proof, on the user's explicit "verify by yourself" request — evidence listed at the end of this entry.) Field incident 2026-08-30: a headless suite run against a worktree via the BLENDER_USER_EXTENSIONS override and the user's live Blender (rendering in the background from main) both appended to takes_for_blender_2026-08-30.log — 3.8 GB in which a real render was buried under test fixtures reading as genuine failures ('message': 'out of memory', 'message': 'boom', ai.cancel_render() -> ok). Two causes, both in utils/logger.py: get_log_dir() falls back to bpy.utils.user_resource('SCRIPTS', …), the Blender USER CONFIG root, and BLENDER_USER_EXTENSIONS redirects only where extension CODE loads from — never user_resource(); and get_log_filepath() built <base>_<YYYY-MM-DD>.log, where only the date varies. The collision is not override-specific: two Blender versions on one junction, or a second instance, share a file on the same day too. Fix. New bpy-free utils/log_source.py. resolve_source_suffix(package_dir) reads the parent folder of the takes_for_blender/ package and returns a short filename-safe tag, deliberately returning "" for the canonical Takes-for-Blender folder AND for every ordinary install (_INSTALL_PARENTS = user_default/blender_org/addons/…, plus an _INSTALL_ROOTS grandparent check so a custom extension repo id is still an install) — that empty string is what keeps the historical filename byte-identical for main and for real users, so there is no migration and no churn in the normal case. A worktree (.worktrees/Takes-for-Blender-maint12) or sibling clone (Takes-for-Blender-spike) has the repo prefix stripped and yields maint12 / spike, sanitized to [A-Za-z0-9._-] and capped at 32 chars. build_log_filename(base, date, suffix) holds the naming rule itself so it is provable without Blender. Wiring. logger.get_addon_root() = os.path.realpath(__file__) walked up two levels — realpath is what resolves the extension junction to the real working tree, since __file__ reports the junction path and main and a worktree would otherwise look identical. Cached in _addon_root_cached / _source_suffix_cached; realpath is a syscall and must never run per line. Both helpers swallow everything (# CORR-05-OK) and fall back to "", i.e. to today's exact filename — logging must never break the addon. debug_log_path / debug_log_filename semantics are untouched: a worktree must never edit live user prefs (same reasoning as TKS_TEST_MODE), and a per-run env tag was rejected because the run that caused this is the run nobody would have tagged. Banner. New _session_banner() / _write_lines(): the first write to a given file in a session is prefixed with [SESSION] Addon source: <resolved path> (pid <n>). Emitted lazily by the writers rather than at register time, so a user with enable_debug_logging off never gets an empty file created; both _flush_log_buffer (timer) and _flush_sync (--background, unregister) route through _write_lines, so neither path can lose it. register_logger() resets _banner_path, re-bannering after a disable/enable cycle. The pid separates two sessions running the same code. Untouched by design. _cleanup_old_logs() already globs <name>_*<ext>, which matches a suffixed file (pinned by a test, so a worktree log cannot become immortal); log_reader.list_log_files() already globs *.log, so a worktree log appears in the Debug Monitor as its own named entry. Tests. dev/tests/test_log_source_suffix.py — 13 pytest.mark.pure tests, module imported by path, with an AST check proving it imports no bpy. Pins main to takes_for_blender_2026-08-30.log byte for byte, a worktree to …_maint12.log, a normal install to no rename, a custom debug_log_filename to keeping its extension, and two checkouts on one day to two filenames. Live proof: re-running the suite through the override while the user's Blender ran from main produced takes_for_blender_2026-08-30.log (3702 MB, live) and takes_for_blender_2026-08-30_logsrc.log (105 MB, suite) side by side, the latter opening with the SESSION banner naming the worktree. Suite 2797 passed / 1 skipped under Blender 5.2. Doc: doc/troubleshooting/log_file_shared_across_checkouts.md. Verification. Two headless Blender 5.2 runs of dev/temp/verify_changelog.py, each loading the SAME branch code through a different extension junction, so the only variable is the path realpath() resolves to. Run A (main-shaped path) — a real directory copy at <scratch>/mainsim/Takes-for-Blender/takes_for_blender (a copy, not a junction, since junctions resolve through): addon_root = that path, suffix = '', filename = takes_for_blender_2026-08-30.log, i.e. byte-identical to the historical name. Run B (worktree path): addon_root = .worktrees/Takes-for-Blender-logsrc/takes_for_blender, suffix = 'logsrc', filename = takes_for_blender_2026-08-30_logsrc.log. Both runs additionally proved, live: the resolved root is a real directory and not the junction Blender loaded (root_is_real); the cache is what serves the second call, so realpath cannot run per line (root_cached, via a sentinel); the banner names the resolved root and is emitted exactly once per file (banner_first / banner_repeat = None); a real tks_log line reaches that file (wrote_marker); log_reader.list_log_files() still lists it, so the Debug Monitor is unaffected (monitor_sees); the age-cleanup glob still matches a suffixed name (cleanup_glob); and with os.path.realpath monkeypatched to raise, the filename falls back to today's exact unsuffixed name instead of propagating (fallback_ok). Cross-proof: full headless suite 2797 passed / 1 skipped against the worktree via the BLENDER_USER_EXTENSIONS override; 13 pytest.mark.pure unit tests; and a fresh auditor AST scan with AUDITOR_SCAN_ROOT pointed at the worktree (502 files — exactly the worktree's .py count, so the new module WAS scanned) returns zero findings naming log_source.py. Not covered by automation, and the only thing left for a hands-on look: that the Debug Monitor's file dropdown reads well with two same-day entries in it.

      Out of scope, filed as roadmap ideas: the log FLOODS (3.8 GB on 2026-08-30, 6.4 GB on 2026-08-25 against 0.3 MB on 2026-08-26; one suite run alone wrote 105 MB; commit 89b2123f names keymap_audit as a suspect), and nothing CAPS a log — _cleanup_old_logs prunes by age (7 days) only, so a single day can fill a disk.

    28. 🟢 The cached log filepath was only refreshed on a DATE change, so moving the log was ignored until midnight. _flush_sync / _flush_log_buffer cache _log_filepath_cached and recomputed it only when _log_date_cached != today. User-facing consequence: repointing debug_log_path in Preferences kept writing to the old file for the rest of the session. Test consequence, and how it was found: Blender enables the extension at startup, BEFORE dev/tests/run_tests.py sets TKS_TEST_CONFIG_DIR, so the startup flush cached the real profile path and the override that arrived moments later was never consulted again — the whole suite's output, keymap audit included, went into the developer's live log while the assertions read the isolated one. Diagnostic printed from inside a test: get_log_filepath() ended tks_test_cfg_iks6fzjj/logs/takes_for_blender_2026-08-30.log while _log_filepath_cached still ended Blender/5.2/scripts/presets/takes_for_blender/logs/takes_for_blender_2026-08-30.log (separators shown as / for legibility). Fix: new _log_destination_key() — the tuple (TKS_TEST_CONFIG_DIR, debug_log_path, debug_log_filename) — compared on every flush alongside the date. A dict lookup and two getattrs, no syscall, so the per-line background flush does not pay for get_log_filepath()'s user_resource(create=True). Both flush functions share it, and the existing midnight-rollover test still passes because a date change alone still forces the recompute. Two supporting changes. (a) New _test_log_dir() in utils/logger.py mirrors persistence_io._test_config_dir: same TKS_TEST_CONFIG_DIR, unconditional (NOT gated on TKS_TEST_MODE), checked BEFORE the debug_log_path preference because isolation a test can switch off is not isolation. BLENDER_USER_EXTENSIONS redirects only which CODE loads, never bpy.utils.user_resource, which is why test fixtures had been landing in the live log at all. No change to run_tests.py — it already sets the variable. (b) test_ai_call_log.py's _tail(path, nbytes=8000) replaced by _mark(path) / _since(path, mark): one file load writes ~70 KB of [UI:HOTKEYS] [AUDIT] rows, nine times that window, so a probe line was routinely pushed out of view — and on a shared daily log a match could come from an EARLIER run's identical line, meaning these tests could pass without having written anything. With the isolated log in place but the tail read still there, all four failed deterministically, which is what exposed the caching bug. Reading from a recorded offset asserts THIS test wrote the line. Deliberately NOT done: quietening the keymap audit (keymap-audit-log-noise) would have hidden the tail problem rather than fixed it and touches neither of the other two findings. Tests: dev/tests/test_log_isolation.py (6) plus the four previously-flaky tests. The flake itself is only provable by repetition — full suite three times back to back. Companion to Fixed 27, which landed from another session while this was in flight and solves the adjacent half: a per-checkout filename suffix stops two CHECKOUTS interleaving. It does not replace this one — the suffix is empty for the canonical checkout, so a suite run against main still wrote into the live profile log, and it touches neither the date-only cache invalidation nor the tail read. Both were kept in the merge; _log_destination_key deliberately omits the source suffix, which is resolved once per session from a folder that cannot move. (Verified 2026-08-30 by a live probe, no mouse needed: a session logs a line, then mid-session the debug_log_path PREFERENCE is pointed at a fresh folder. The resolved path follows the preference, the cache follows it, the NEXT line lands in the new file, the old file does not also receive it, and the real profile log is untouched. Before the fix the flush kept the start-up path until midnight.) Card doc/roadmap/active/ai-log-test-flake.md. Branch fix/test-log-isolation.
