Resolved by looking up which texts module actually defines each name. (c) Three composers, not one. compose_tooltip, a private _compose inside _helpers.popover_description, and the VL render toggle hand-building the same block in six returns - so the preference reached neither of the last two. That is what the user saw on the compositor and the render icon. _compose now delegates; the render toggle's six returns use TIP_VL_RENDER_KEYS; and the guard below found 8 more doing the same (variant column popovers, VSW collection, datablock/object action, object slot, cascade overflow, process toggle), now on five small shared blocks. {ctrl_click} was missing from the composer's hole set, caught by rendering the tooltip rather than by reading it. Three new guards, all hard rules at zero: test_a_tooltip_never_names_something_it_did_not_import (the crash class, 38 at once), test_only_one_place_appends_a_gesture_block (any .format() with gesture-hole keywords outside texts/compose.py), and test_no_tooltip_hand_builds_a_key_block. Ratchet MAX_HANDTYPED 15 → 8. German for the new blocks; 0 orphans, 0 untracked. Every tooltip verified by RENDERING it in both switch states rather than by reading the source - which is how (b) and the missing hole were found at all. Full suite 2754 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed.
    30. 🟢 A 3-channel colour preference truncated the whole config file (_serialize_pref_value). (Found while adding the Diff State colours; in-app confirmed 2026-08-24.) FloatVectorProperty(size=4, subtype='COLOR_GAMMA') returns a bpy_prop_array (has __iter__ → converted); size=3, subtype='COLOR' returns a mathutils.Color, which is INDEXABLE but has no __iter__, so it slipped the iterable check and json.dump raised TypeError: Object of type Color is not JSON serializable MID-WRITE — leaving user_preferences.json 30 bytes long, a single { plus half an entry. Latent since the serializer existed; every colour preference until now was size-4. Fix broadens the check to anything sequence-shaped (__len__ + __getitem__), with str/bytes excluded. Process note: the failing guard test was first written off as a worktree artifact because it passed from the main checkout — wrong, because a run launched from a worktree WITHOUT BLENDER_USER_EXTENSIONS still imports the worktree's own code from sys.path. doc/troubleshooting/prefs_three_channel_colour_truncates_config.md. 2 regression tests. Commit 4d4b11c6.

    31. 🟢 Keying one object snapped every drifted object back to rest (keyframe mass-snap). Root cause: _deferred_jit_merge / _deferred_sub_jit in panels/inspector/sync_jit.py call merge_action_into_cascade, whose slots.new/channelbags.new/fcurves.new structurally mutate the SHARED cascade action; Blender then re-evaluates that action for every bound ID on the next depsgraph pass, and a hand-dragged value on a keyed channel is a borrowed value that evaluation discards — scene-wide, in one tick. Proven from the user's live log (2026-08-31): three drift-count collapses to zero, each coinciding to the second with a JIT2 COMPLETE … (merge OK) fold; the long-suspected _revert_unkeyed_to_rest_deferred skipped every target ('no witnessed loss', counts only ever grew) and snap_cached_diffs never ran — both exonerated. Four earlier fixtures were silent because a hand-assigned action is never folded. Fix: both fold bodies snapshot the live values of every keyed channel bound to the cascade action (_snapshot_bystander_drifts — exactly the stompable set, independent of the Rest feature, skipped under Value Lock), then consume the re-evaluation themselves (view_layer.update()) and write the values back by name (_restore_bystander_drifts, mirror-suppressed via arm_suppress(1.0, hard=False), epsilon-gated). Round 2 (sandbox verification failed, same day): the in-app sandbox test still snapped with ZERO JIT lines — a third fold path: _process_fresh_actions (panels/inspector/sync_actions.py, branch 1) merges a queued fresh action into the resolved cascade. The guard became a shared capture/restore pair + preserve_keyed_live_values context manager in features/rest_state/logic.py (snapshots ALL keyed-channel live values scene-wide — no action filter, so every fold is covered; inert under Value Lock and addon_is_mutating), wrapped around every merge_action_into_cascade call site: both sync_jit deferreds, the _process_fresh_actions drain, both ops_action_merge merges, and the ops_watchlist unpin-merge. New test dev/tests/test_fresh_action_merge_preserves_bystanders.py (3) reproduces the sandbox path. New public apply_channel_value in logic.py keeps the cross-package import public (ARCH03). Tests: dev/tests/test_jit_fold_preserves_bystanders.py (4) — reproduces the field bug deterministically in an isolated scene (the harness .blend's live cascade otherwise adopts and snaps bed objects mid-dispatch, which re-demonstrated the bug during test development). Full suite 3035 passed / 1 skipped. Doc: doc/troubleshooting/keyframe_mass_snap_cascade_fold.md. Card doc/roadmap/active/keyframe-mass-snap.md. Branch fix/mass-snap-fold. (Confirmed in-app 2026-08-31, worktree sandbox: six 'fold guard: restored' lines, drift surviving every fold, user-verified no snap.)

    32. 🔴 "Show Overrides…" refused to open, reporting a scripted-call error. Reported from the running addon 2026-08-31: clicking the entry produced "TKS_OT_cascade_overflow_popover opens a UI element, so a scripted call does nothing. This capability has no scripted route yet." Root cause is not in the operator. A popup menu's layout carries an EXEC operator context, so every entry runs execute() and never invoke(); TKS_OT_CascadeOverflowPopover.execute finds no _tks_invoked marker, correctly concludes it was reached by a script, and refuses through refuse_scripted. The refusal was doing its job on a caller that was not really a script. Fix: layout.operator_context = 'INVOKE_DEFAULT' at the top of TKS_MT_TreeContextMenu.draw, which is how Blender's own menus do it (bl_ui/properties_data_curves.py:109) — no Takes menu set it anywhere, so the same latent defect sits in every other menu whose entries open something; only the one with a reported symptom is fixed here. The ten dispatcher entries were unaffected and would have hidden this indefinitely: each one's execute re-enters its own invoke, so they worked under the wrong context. Pinned by test_entries_run_invoke_not_execute, whose fake layout deliberately starts at Blender's real EXEC_REGION_WIN default so a menu that forgets the line fails.

    33. 🔴 Invert Selection did nothing and reported success — since the day it was written. The provider was registered as TKS_OT_MultiSelect.__new__(TKS_OT_MultiSelect).invert_selection(...), and Blender refuses to build an Operator that way: TypeError: bpy_struct.__new__(struct): expected a single argument. Measured with dev/tmp/probe_invert.py. So the provider raised on its first line every time it was ever called, for every list, not just the tree. Two tolerant layers hid it completely: core/providers.query swallows a provider crash by design and returns the caller's default, and TKS_OT_InvertMultiselect.execute ignored the result and returned FINISHED regardless — the exact shape Constitution rule 7 calls the most misleading an addon can offer. The provider returned None on success too, so even a caller that HAD checked could not have told the cases apart. Fix in three parts: the walk helpers became @classmethods (they never touched instance state — only invoke/execute read self.list_type), so a provider can call them with no object to build; both public halves return True; and a shared _run_multiselect reports and CANCELS instead of lying — WARNING when multi-select is off, ERROR when the provider did not answer True. dev/tests/test_multiselect_walk.py passed for the whole life of the bug because it drove the helpers directly and never crossed the seam; its probe copied vars(cls) items passing callable(value), and a classmethod object is not callable, so the fix silently emptied it until the filter learned about descriptors. doc/troubleshooting/invert_selection_did_nothing.md.

    34. 🔴 Select All dragged the highlight to the last row, and so did Invert. tks_selected carries an update= callback, _on_row_ticked, whose whole job is to move the blue bar to the row just ticked — correct for ONE deliberate tick, and what makes the move arrows agree with the selection. A sweep writes every visible row in order, so each write fired it and the bar walked the list, stopping wherever the walk stopped. Nothing was broken in Select All; two correct behaviours met. Not obvious because the coupling is an RNA update= hook — the callback is in panels/, the sweep in operators/inspector/, and neither file mentions the other, so no call graph shows it. test_multiselect_walk asserts which rows end up ticked and never looks at tks_all_viewlayers_index, so it passed throughout. Fix: a bulk_tick() context manager in properties.py that _on_row_ticked returns early under, wrapping the whole body of BOTH sweeps — Invert had the identical fault. The flag restores in a finally, so a raising walk cannot leave the guard up and silently kill highlight-follows-tick for the session. Rejected: suppressing inside _walk_visible alone (the CONTEXT branch writes outside it, so half the rows would still move the bar) and restoring the index afterwards (a number, not the reader's place, and it would flicker through every row on the way). doc/troubleshooting/select_all_moved_the_highlight.md.

    35. 🟢 Switching to the view layer you are already on ran the whole cascade pipeline. tks.switch_viewlayer had no already-active early out, so a click that changed nothing still opened a vl_switch_scope, re-applied the cascade and ended Variant Live. Now returns CANCELLED when context.window already holds that scene and view layer, read defensively because a scripted call may have no window at all. This is what lets the tree draw the SAME widget for the active and inactive marker (see entry 37).

    36. 🟢 A tagged tree line pushed its row's icon and name right of the untagged rows. A tag-coloured strip widens with tks_tree_line_width while an untagged one keeps the thin default, so at MEDIUM / WIDE the columns drifted. Two wrong fixes came first, both instructive. (1) Park the difference beside the untagged strip as a blank label scaled by the same factor - changed nothing, because scale_x multiplies a widget's OWN natural width and a blank label is far narrower than a colour prop(). (2) Widen the untagged strip to the tagged width - aligned correctly, but by changing the tree lines themselves, which the user ruled out: the lines stay, only the spacing moves. Shipped: the untagged strip keeps its thin colour and reserves TAG_GAP_UNITS beside it as ui_units_x, which is ABSOLUTE and so actually is the width it says. Only the tag column compensates - spacing every strip would shift whole rows right instead of lining them up - and that column is NOT the same loop index on every tier: a view layer row draws it with is_last, a take row echoes it one level deeper with is_last off, which is why draw_tree_line takes an explicit match_tag_column rather than inferring it. The first pass had that index wrong in both files. The width table itself had drifted into three copies and now lives once in utils/tree_metrics.py - in utils/ because features/variant_switch/ui_helpers.py needs it too and a feature may not import panels (ARCH-01). Gap values are tuned by eye against the strip widths; one dict, one line to nudge. See doc/troubleshooting/tree_row_column_alignment.md.
    37. 🟢 The active row's marker sat off its own column. It drew a plain label where every other row drew an emboss=False operator, and inside the fixed-width slot the two neither pad nor align the same. Setting alignment = 'CENTER' only moved the error around. BOX style now draws the SAME operator in both states, differing only in glyph and in whether the row is dimmed, so alignment holds by construction - which is what the switch_viewlayer early out in entry 35 exists to make safe. SOCKET is untouched: template_node_socket is a different widget by nature and has never looked out of line.
    38. 🟢 Keymap-audit load/save handlers now honour the UI:HOTKEYS gate. Found by the auditor's speed benchmark: File open · light addon cost scored 3.0 — the addon added 71.82 ms to opening the factory startup file (150.06 ms on vs 78.24 ms off), MORE than its cost on the heavy probe file (32.98 ms). Root cause: utils/keymap_audit.py registered _save_pre/_save_post/_load_pre/_load_post unconditionally, and each event ran snapshot_user_kc() (a full walk of the user + addon keyconfigs) plus a synchronous _flush_now() disk flush — for every user, on every file open and save, even with enable_debug_logging off. The periodic tick in the same file already had the right shape: _audit_logging_enabled() (mirrors tks_log_active(topic="UI", subtopic="hotkeys")) skips the snapshot/diff work when nothing would be logged. All four handlers now early-return through that same gate; with UI:HOTKEYS logging on, the crash-forensics dumps are unchanged. Register/unregister-boundary snapshots and the atexit marker are untouched. Tests: dev/tests/test_keymap_audit_gate.py (4 — gate off skips the snapshot walk and the load_pre flush, gate on still snapshots exactly once). Impact-selected suite 2878 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed. Re-scored 2026-09-01 after the merge: File open · light addon cost 71.82 ms → 13.08 ms, score 3.0 → 9.1; user confirmed on the dashboard.
    39. 🔴 Enabling the Empty mark killed the whole Diff State overlay — NameError on an undefined prefs (auditor CORR-11, its one CRITICAL). features/diff_state/draw.py empty_extent(obj, factor) opened with factor = float(getattr(prefs, 'diff_state_empty_size', 1.0) or 1.0) — prefs is not a name in that scope; a leftover from before the caller passed kind_size(prefs, …) in as the parameter it then shadowed. First Empty mark drawn → NameError → the draw callback's outer guard logs "overlay draw failed" once and aborts the frame, so every mark vanishes while an Empty mark is active. Fix: factor = float(factor or 1.0) — the caller's per-kind size, coerced the same way. No test could see it: the line lives in the GPU draw callback, and the field reports on the branch (dev entry Added 9) all predate the Empty-mark path.
    40. 🔴 The two Diff State handlers were not @persistent — Blender silently drops them on the first file load. features/diff_state/cache.py appended _on_depsgraph (depsgraph_update_post) and _on_load (load_post) bare. Non-persistent handlers are cleared when a file loads, so _on_load could never fire for the event it exists for, and after the first Open the geometry store stopped invalidating: edit a marked mesh and the outline/fill kept drawing the old shape for the rest of the session. Both now carry @persistent, matching core/cache_version.py and every other load/depsgraph handler the addon owns. Found while fixing REG-06 in the same functions — not an auditor finding itself.
    41. 🔴 _on_depsgraph walked depsgraph.updates during undo/redo/cascade (auditor CRASH-01 K1, CRITICAL). Undo and the cascade apply free and rebuild datablocks mid-flight; touching update.id then is the freed-data class the Constitution's handler rules exist for. The handler now early-outs through the house guard (TKS_VL_STATE.addon_is_mutating or is_undoing) — and because anything may have changed shape by the time the flag clears, it drops the whole geometry store (clear() + _dirty_scan()) instead of trusting per-update info it never saw: marked objects rebuild lazily on their next draw, so an undone modeling change can never leave a stale hull. Cheap: the store only ever holds the marked set, and a clear during a long cascade hits an already-empty dict.
    42. 🔴 The [VERIFY] tracer left in panels/inspector/sync_jit.py is demoted to the gated logger. Follow-up to the same benchmark session (Undo · light 5.43 ms, score 7.7). The block's own comment marked it TEMPORARY — forced traces (force=True, bypassing the master switch, topic, and level gates) for in-app verification of the sync.py → sync_jit.py split, to be removed once confirmed; the split shipped with the large-file campaign and the tracer stayed. Cost: every _jit_verify line was written for EVERY user — _is_jit_blocked traced per object per depsgraph tick during undo/redo/VL switches, and a background session flushes each line to disk synchronously (the Fixed 20 behavior). All 10 call sites now go through _jit_log (SWITCH:cascade, normally gated), the helper is deleted, and the redundant COMPLETE trace (already mirrored by an adjacent _jit_log) is dropped — the diagnostics survive for anyone who turns the topic on. Honest measurement note: an A/B probe with logging pinned OFF showed ~0 ms undo delta on this machine both before and after, so part of the benchmark's 5.43 ms may be its own noise; the forced disk writes were real and are gone regardless (verified: 8 forced flushes per undo with the tracer, 0 after). Tests: dev/tests/test_jit_verify_gate.py (3 — no force=True/_jit_verify left in the module, _is_jit_blocked still blocks during undo, and never force-logs).
    43. 🔴 Pass 1b (action-loss detection feeder) removed from panels/inspector/sync_viewport.py. The second half of the Undo · light chase (score 7.7 → the tracer fix only reached 4.77 ms). Profiling ten headless undos with logging pinned OFF showed ~3.2 ms/undo still spent in _handle_viewport_selection_sync: Pass 1b rebuilt EVERY animation target in the scene — objects, materials, node trees, scene, world, each with a template-resolved generate_slot_name label — on every data tick (undo ticks included, by explicit comment), writing _obj_action_tracker. The loss-detection that consumed the tracker was disabled 2026-03-29 ("rest-snaps fight the cascade's own apply_to_watched logic") and never returned; the tracker had no other reader (written and read only inside Pass 1b, cleared on VL switch). Removed the whole pass; kept the _slot_poll_dirty marking that shared its gate; _obj_action_tracker stays defined in sync_actions.py so its VL-switch purge is untouched. Measured after removal: the handler drops 3.2 ms → 0.2 ms per undo and the iter_anim_targets/generate_slot_name frames vanish; ordinary editing ticks shed the same walk. Rebuild-from-history note left in place plus doc/troubleshooting/undo_light_dead_pass1b.md. Tests: dev/tests/test_pass1b_removed.py (2 — a Scene-update tick walks zero anim targets; the dead tracker write stays gone).
    44. 🔴 The batch preview honored preview_transparent and threw preview_bg away (auditor MAINT-12, wired not dropped). The color travels UI (tks_preview_bg_color) → process_manager --preview-bg → cli_worker._render_preview(…, preview_bg, …), which accepted it and read it never — the one picker whose promise the batch path silently dropped, while the interactive vl_preview path composites the same picker's color. Both branches now render film-transparent (the world keeps lighting the scene) and the non-transparent branch composites preview_bg behind the saved png — _parse_bg_color / _blend_pixels_over_bg / _composite_bg_file, the same alpha math as vl_preview's _composite_preview_bg, kept standalone because the worker is a spec-loaded script. A failed composite emits an info line and keeps the transparent png rather than voiding the render. Tests: dev/tests/test_preview_bg_composite.py (4, pure halves).
    45. 🔴 The slot-UI resolver twins had drifted: properties/slot_ui.resolve_id_block did not know PARTICLE (auditor MAINT-11 starter). The slot menu answered None where the slot buttons resolved a real psys.settings block. One authoritative copy now lives as core/path_utils.resolve_slot_target (the operator superset); operators/_slot_helpers.resolve_id_block and properties/slot_ui.resolve_id_block are thin delegates. Same pass: the camera/world promote menus' byte-identical _resolve_target collapsed into operators/cascade/_helpers.resolve_tier_target(context, tier, tier_prop, global_prop). Pinned by dev/tests/test_resolver_twins.py (3).
    46. 🟢 The View Layer Groups stat filter did nothing when clicked. A stat icon's LABEL doubles as the KEY its operator looks up, and that name table existed TWICE - _STAT_TO_TYPE in panels/context/draw_tree.py and STAT_NAME_TO_TYPE on TKS_OT_StatInfo. Main renamed "VL Groups" to "View Layer Groups" in the panel under the UI vocabulary standard; the operator kept the old key, looked up a name that no longer existed, got "" and returned without filtering - a button that looks live and does nothing. One table now, STAT_NAME_TO_TYPE in utils/constants.py, which panels/ and operators/ may both import. It answers BOTH spellings on purpose: panels/context/draw_split.py still passes "VL Groups" and the tag library passes "ViewLayer Group" / "ViewLayer". Renaming those keys to match the newer wording is what would break them next - a label in use is a key that must resolve, whatever the vocabulary standard says about the words. The guard that should have caught this (test_stat_label_linkage_renamed_in_lockstep) asserted exactly one label in one file; new dev/tests/test_tree_stat_filter.py walks every stat_name literal in the package and asserts each resolves, scoped to files that touch tks_multiselect_type_filter because the same operator doubles as a plain tooltip carrier elsewhere ("Currently rendering", "Cancelled") where no mapping is wanted.

Both now go through pgettext_rpt, with their de_DE keys.

Its two siblings - delete_context_item and delete_group - compose the chord from the dispatcher via compose_tooltip(..., key=live_shortcut('tks.global_delete')); the multi-select delete kept a plain bl_description, so the tooltip never named the key that reaches it.     49. 🔴 _draw_inherited_source resolved by the ACTIVE take, not the row (roadmap card answers-for-the-row-you-asked, site 1; auditor MAINT-12). The row's take_index arrived and was ignored; the resolution ran get_active_take, so on a non-active take row the "inherited from" line named another take's inheritance while the same popover's tooltip (popover_description -> resolve_target(..., take_index)) resolved by row - two answers on one popover. Now _get_take(scene, vl, take_index) when the index is a row, get_active_take for index -1 (a VL/scene row reads through the take on top, which is its own inheritance path). dev/tests/test_inherited_source_by_row.py (3) is the card's own test spec: two takes, the second active with a world override, the first inheriting the scene's world - drawing for the first row names the scene's world and never the override. Site 2 (_check_warning_state(scene) reading bpy.context) stays open and is the card's remaining row: the card itself says _prev_warnings being one global for what is really per-scene state must be scoped before starting, and whether query() can take a scene-scoped context is an architect question. MAINT-12 2 -> 1.
    50. 🔴 _check_warning_state(scene) read bpy.context and kept one global memory (roadmap card answers-for-the-row-you-asked, site 2; auditor MAINT-12 2 -> 0). The warning queries take a context, so when the window's scene is not the scene being processed - a cascade walking several scenes, a headless render - the counters described the wrong scene and _prev_warnings compared scene B against scene A's memory. Now: None is a no-op; when bpy.context.scene differs from scene the check steps aside with a DEBUG line instead of journaling a lie; and the memory is a dict keyed by scene name. The query call shape is untouched - the card's open question about scene-scoped contexts stays open, but no wrong answer can be journaled while it is. dev/tests/test_warning_state_by_scene.py (3).
    51. 🔴 The takes tree's Global Still row armed the master lock - Scene.tks_global_still carried both the Global cascade tier and the Rest-Mode-style master override (597ad99c, one day after the 2026-07-09 cascade rework had validated "a take's Animate beats a Global Still"). engine.resolve_still / resolve_still_target / panels._row_winner short-circuited on is_still_global() before the cascade ran, and draw_still_button / TKS_OT_StillPopover.invoke froze every non-Global row on master_active() - so writing the tier WAS arming the lock, and the wiki's own "Global on Still + one turntable View Layer on Animate" setup could not be built. Split: new Scene.tks_still_master is the lock - written only by tks.still_global_toggle (nav header + pie), read by global_master(), listed in _SECONDARY_MARKERS of utils/master_scene.py like tks_rest_mode (never primary, so a lock-only scene cannot claim the master title); tks_global_still stays the plain Global tier get_cascade_winner already resolves last, so old files need no conversion. While the lock is on all SIX tree icons freeze (the Global row lost its escape-hatch exception; the dropdown / pie is the way out); the viewport pill and the nav depress follow the lock. New PROP_MODULE_TKS_STILL_MASTER + de_DE entry, _pending.py regenerated; dev/scripts/diag_still_lock.py writes the lock. dev/tests/test_still_global_tier_split.py (6, headless through the registered namespace - test_still_mode.py spec-loads the engine without bpy and cannot see the cascade): RED 5/6 on the old code, GREEN 6/6 after. Full suite 3114 passed (the impact selector fell back to a full run: the diag script maps to no test). Auditor 548 files, no new REG/CRASH rows, no new findings in touched files. doc/troubleshooting/still_global_tier_armed_master_lock.md. Wiki follow-up: features/still_mode.md says the nav menu sets "the Global tier" - it is the lock now.

    [0.8.0] - 2026-08-20¶

    Verification session 2026-07-21: the open entries above/below were self-verified in-app via a scripted GUI Blender 5.2.0 session against the registered extension (probes + screenshots + full state restore; artifacts in gitignored dev/temp/verify_results.json, verify_shot_*.png, verify_corpus_leaks.json). Highlights: i18n corpus 6790 registered pairs — 6685 resolve to our German, 101 to Blender's own German (native catalog wins on common operator labels), 4 to Blender-owned identity-English editor terms ("Graph Editor" et al.), 0 English fallbacks of addon text; live tooltip pool: 463/464 operators + 53/53 menus draw descriptions that are verbatim texts/ constants, 0 trailing periods; autokey-guard state machine (ASK → consent → borrow → restore → manual-override WITHDRAW) exercised through the real operators with a live German report; tks.datablock_add_slot end-to-end slots 0→1; live bpy.utils.manual_map() resolves both guard ops to interface/navigation_panel/#autokey-is-being-blocked (anchor confirmed on the deployed wiki). Caveats: the consent-popup pixels and nav-warning visuals rest on the earlier in-app pass (d47b636); the guard-buttons grey-out branch (Fixed 5) is unreachable in a healthy session and stays covered by its unit tests.

    Added¶

    1. 🟢 The addon registers per-locale word lists with Blender's translation system — interface strings follow the user's Blender language. (In-app confirmed 2026-07-18 in Blender 5.2: "Kontext" panel title + "Ruhezustand" prefs accordion from our seed; note TKS_PT_Globals is poll-gated behind tks_show_tab_globals, so "Globals" is no verification anchor.) Multi-language support Phase 1. texts/i18n.py: build_dict() assembles {locale: {(context, source): translation}} from texts/locales/ (data modules; de_DE.py starter seed — Globals, Context, Batch Render, Value Lock, Rest State, Variant Switch, Render Presets, UI Sync; the Globals/Context N-panel headers are the visible verification anchors — the feature-group names are overlay runtime strings that stay English until the Phase 3 pgettext pass, and every tks.batch_render draw site overrides its label text); register_translations()/unregister_translations() default the registration name to the root package (__package__.rsplit), hooked early in root __init__.py register()/unregister() beside manual_map, plus _reload_order entries. Static RNA strings (bl_label, bl_description, prop name=/description=, enum item names) auto-translate in C at draw time — zero code changes, zero Python draw cost; dynamic strings (report(), drawn labels) are Phase 3 pgettext work. Verified 5.1 semantics: duplicate register raises ValueError (drives the refresh path), unregister of unknown names is a silent no-op. Tests: dev/tests/test_i18n_plumbing.py (5 — dict shape, real-string seed, name-scoped register/unregister roundtrip, reentrancy, root-init wiring guard). Suite gotcha documented in doc/troubleshooting/i18n_suite_source_tree_registration.md: collection-time module-level addon_enable in test_bookmark_channel_visibility.py enables the SOURCE-TREE addon, keeping a second registration alive — never assert global translation absence in-suite. Commit 2e45691.

    17. 🟢 AI facade — takes_for_blender/ai/, the scripted-caller entry point (read verbs + switch_take). (In-app confirmed 2026-08-10 in Blender 5.2 over the official Blender MCP bridge: status()/describe() read the user's live production file — 1 scene, 11 view layers — and a take switch driven through the bridge landed correctly in the GUI.) Five modules, top layer, never imported upward into: errors.py (the fixed envelope {ok, api, data, error{code,message,hint}, warnings, undo} + plain-string codes an agent branches on — an enum member would serialise as ErrorCode.NOT_FOUND and break that branch — plus guard(), so no exception ever crosses the bridge as an opaque failure; bpy-free and relative-import-free, so the contract is checkable under a bare interpreter); policy.py (pure decisions: busy_reason splits the three independent busy sources — mutation lock, preload, BG render — because one flag cannot tell an agent whether to retry in a second or in ten minutes; is_stale_lock, TTL 5.0s); session.py (ai_session context manager: owner token + monotonic stamp, _push_undo, engine_state(), reset()); api.py (the verbs); AI_GUIDE.md (shipped INSIDE the extension — verified present at the root of the built ZIP, 469 files, with doc/+dev/ excluded — so help() serves it from the install folder rather than the repo). switch_take is deliberately NOT a thin delegate to tks.activate_vl_version: that operator is a TOGGLE, so calling it on the already-active take would deactivate it, and an agent's most common failure mode is retrying a call it believes timed out — a retry that silently turns the take OFF is exactly the AI-01 lying-to-the-agent shape this facade exists to prevent; here it is a no-op that says so. Bug caught in the guard tests' first real run: _depth was incremented only for mutating sessions but decremented unconditionally, so every read-only session drove it negative and ALL later sessions silently skipped locking and undo — __exit__ now mirrors __enter__. Headless fixtures must normalise TKS_VL_STATE.is_applying: the read_homefile load_post handler sets it and its clearing timer never fires under --background. Tests: test_ai_envelope.py (7, pure), test_ai_session.py (14, pure), test_ai_registration.py (5, pure), test_ai_session_guard.py (11), test_ai_verbs_readonly.py (14), test_ai_language_neutral.py (5 — the facade is name/ID-addressed throughout, so a non-English Blender changes nothing). Verified end-to-end 2026-08-10 by two headless spikes: a natively-assigned world survives two facade-driven take switches under the default ADOPT mode and explain("world") attributes it to the SCENE tier (the accident of 2026-08-09, now closed by the world work); and one switch_take costs exactly one bpy.ops.ed.undo(), labelled AI: Switch take to <name>. Commits 04c0aba, 491463b, 12b3e6e.

    18. 🟢 AI facade — mutating and explanatory verbs (create_take, set_override, clear_override, explain, help, reset). create_take delegates to the engine's own new-take path and returns the template-generated name (the agent cannot predict it, so it must be told). set_override/clear_override validate the value against the real datablocks BEFORE storing: the engine setter stores whatever string it is handed — fine for a picker menu that can only offer real datablocks, but an agent TYPES names, and a typo silently stored as a dangling reference is another quiet lie (the assignment "succeeded" while the cascade resolves to nothing), so a refusal carries the actual candidates. help() introspects the LIVE module via _verb_catalogue() rather than a hand-kept list, so a new verb cannot be missing from the agent's own view of the API; it serves AI_GUIDE.md from the install folder. reset() was found missing during the first real bridge run — help()'s gotchas told agents to call it while it lived unexposed in session.py (12b3e6e). Tests: test_ai_create_explain.py (12), test_ai_set_override.py (12), test_ai_help.py (19). Headless- and bridge-tested; not yet exercised by hand in the GUI. Commits 04c0aba, 491463b, 12b3e6e.

    19. 🟢 Shift+Click moves a multi-selection (roadmap: move-multi-selection). Closes the thread that ran Fixed 27 → 30: arrows disabled in multi-select → group auto-exited the mode → auto-exit reverted and arrows decoupled (act on the highlighted row) → now the arrows can take the selection. TKS_OT_MoveAllViewLayerItem gains use_selection: BoolProperty(options={'SKIP_SAVE'}) set from event.shift in a new invoke() (SKIP_SAVE so a shift-click never leaks into the next plain click); execute() tries _move_selection() first and returns None to fall through to the existing single-row dispatch when fewer than 2 rows are ticked. RULED CONSTRAINT (user): same PARENT, not same level — two VLs share depth 3 whether grouped or not, but _move_vl reorders vlg.members, so same-level-different-container has no single correct reading. _parent_key() returns ('SG', group), ('VLG', scene, group) or ('TAKES', scene, vl); a selection with >1 distinct parent refuses. Mixed row types and group rows (SCENE_GROUP/VL_GROUP) also refuse — all via _refuse_report (Fixed 28), so the status bar explains it. Ordering lives in operators/_tree_ops_core.shift_selection(order, selected, direction) — pure list arithmetic, no bpy: each selected entry moves one step but only swaps with a NON-selected neighbour, so a contiguous run travels as a unit and an edge-blocked entry stops the rest of its run; relative order is invariant. This answers the old non-contiguous open question with no special case (rows 2/5/7 each advance one). apply_order() writes back via collection.move() so element identity survives. Containers: sg.members / vlg.members / take_set.versions, resolved by _selection_container(). Tooltip rewritten to describe both clicks, de_DE in lockstep (INFO-09). 15 tests (11 pure ordering + 4 bpy end-to-end incl. cross-group refusal and single-tick fallback). NOTE: two self-inflicted stumbles caught by those tests — a dirty fixture (a leftover scene tick made the selection 'mixed', which the code correctly refused) and a relative import one level too deep (..._tree_ops_core from operators/context/, where groups/ needs three dots and context/ two). Suite 1734. Commit b1dc139.

    20. 🟢 Highlight/selection coherence for the block move (follows Added 19). Three coupled parts, all user-ruled: (a) Leading-edge highlight — after _move_selection, the tree index lands on the topmost ticked row for UP and the bottommost for DOWN, i.e. the row in front and the one a following plain click would move. (b) Highlight follows the tick — _on_row_ticked (panels/context/properties.py) wired as update= on Scene.tks_selected and ViewLayer.tks_selected, reacting ONLY on the True edge so a batch clear (consume_multiselect, Select None) does not drag the blue bar around. Resolves the row via the shared selection_owner(). (c) Arrow gate ORs both clicks — the arrows serve plain (highlighted row) and Shift (selection), so draw_tree enables each direction when EITHER can use it; a highlight parked outside the selection (classically on the bottom row) previously greyed out a direction the block could still travel. Impossible clicks report via _refuse_report, so a half-live arrow is honest rather than dead. Availability is computed by block_can_move(items, selected_idx, depth_of, boundary) — a direction survives while ANY selected row has a non-selected sibling that way, exactly mirroring shift_selection. Asking only the leading row dims too early: in a GAPPED selection the topmost can be pinned at the edge while the ones behind still close up, needing further clicks (user's requirement: 'must click again … then it greys out'). Also fixed in passing: the selection path returned early from execute() and skipped notify_move_completed(), so the 4 Hz timer's index-snap guard was never armed and the new highlight was undone ~250 ms later; it now shares the single-move tail. _selection_owner promoted to _tree_ops_core.selection_owner + selected_indices() so the panel can reuse them (panels↔operators is a lateral, same-tier import). 11 new tests (5 pure block_can_move, 6 bpy). Test hygiene: the module-level pytest.mark.pure was sweeping the bpy tests into Blender-free runs — markers are per-test now. Suite 1745. Commit a3d9254.

    21. Take-data safety copy with automatic restore. The take/group store, Variant Switch products, Tag Library and Inspector watchlist all live on a carrier World (utils/store_world.py), so deleting or purging every World erased them. utils/store_snapshot.py mirrors all four to <presets>/snapshots/<uid>/<utc>.json; core/store_guardian.py decides when. Triggers: health-gated generation on load, one synchronous flush in save_pre, and a 2s heartbeat that is the ONLY routine writer (actions set a dirty flag, never write), so a cascade touching fifty takes costs one atomic tmp+os.replace write and an idle session none. File identity is a uuid4 stamped HIDDEN on every Scene - never only the carrier, whose death is the event being defended against - and candidates() falls back to matching the .blend path when a uid was re-minted. Carrier gets use_fake_user. Retention: 5 generations, dropped when a file closes matching its copy (load_pre), plus a 30-day sweep for sessions that never closed cleanly.

    23. NEEDS_RESTORE gate on the AI facade. A scripted caller can clear bpy.data.worlds in one line and never see a panel, and the tree then rebuilds itself flat so the file still looks usable. ai/errors.guard() refuses every acting verb with the new NEEDS_RESTORE code while an offer stands; status/describe/help stay open (an agent that cannot look cannot report), and restore_takes() / keep_current_takes() are the two ways out. The message names the constraint a human needs: Takes keeps its store on a World, so at least one must remain in the .blend.

Availability is a guard, not decoration, and reproduces all seven header rules: tks.rest_mode_toggle.poll() (no rest action), bool(bpy.data.scenes) for Still, core.vl_preload.is_preloading() holding the Value Lock, not vlock and not rest_on for Autokey, resolve_still(scene, view_layer) for Timeline Sync, tks.vsw_live_apply.poll() (a vsw World with ≥1 product) for Variant Live, and core.store_guardian.recovery_pending() closing all of them. An unavailable mode renders pie.separator() — hide-don't-grey, per keyframe_pies.py:113-119: Blender can only disable a pie slot by wrapping it in pie.row(), which strips the native pie styling, and the eight directions must stay positionally stable. Two slices needed their own answer: Still is tri-state and its header button opens TKS_MT_StillGlobal from invoke() (value='MENU'), so it contributes THREE slot ids (STILL/STILL_ANIM/STILL_OFF) each passing an explicit value, with the active state's slice sending OFF so Off is one click from anywhere; Timeline Sync is a WM property, so it rides wm.context_toggle with data_path="window_manager.tks_timeline_sync" and stays a real pie button. Keymap: 3D View/VIEW_3D, addon kc only — never Window (Blender 5.x dispatches Window from user kc alone, so an addon-kc entry there reads active=True and never fires, keyframe_keymap.py:273-277), never keymap_items.new() on wm.keyconfigs.user (Blender's rebuild pass wipes is_user_defined items wholesale), matched by idname + properties.name and never by key combo. Shift+Alt+Q avoids Ctrl+Alt (German AltGr sends it); Q alone is Quick Favourites. Master-off deactivates the kmi instead of removing it, preserving a rebind. panels/navigation/panel.py deliberately untouched — feat/vsw-live-apply was rewriting that row — so pointing the header at the shared reader is the follow-up. 27 tests in dev/tests/test_mode_pie.py, four of which run the real draw() body against a recording layout (headless Blender cannot open a pie): eight children always emitted, the West slot drawing the West mode, a held-off mode leaving its slot empty. Commits 39b4638f, 91655024, 85d4b9c8.

    27. 🟢 Mode Pie preferences section. MODE_PIE_SLOT_ITEMS (addon_prefs_constants.py, 8 entries + NONE) + TKS_ModePiePropsMixin (preferences/props/props_mode_pie.py, 8 direction enums with _resolve_mode_pie_duplicates de-dup and the is_prefs_loading() guard), mode_pie_enabled in props_misc.py (default False; update= autosaves then queries the keymaps.sync_mode_pie provider — must return None, see _update_navigation_pie), expand_pie_modes in props_logging.py + ACCORDION_GROUPS. EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 537→547 with a reason line; indexed in prefs_search.py under WORKFLOW/PIE. Slot enums rather than overlay_mode_*-style booleans: that shape answers presence AND order in one control, where booleans on top would give two competing ways to hide a mode. The configurator reuses the generic _draw_pie_grid (ui_draw_hotkeys.py:254), so the rebindable hotkey centre and the Reset button come from the existing tks.reset_pie_hotkey / tks.reset_pie_grid — no new operator, hence no manual_map.py operator entry (only the two pref entries). _PIE_HOTKEY_DEFAULTS gains TKS_MT_PIE_Modes: ('Q', False, True, True), asserted against the kmi we actually create. i18n gotcha recorded in doc/roadmap/_dev/mode-pie.md: i18n_extract harvests text= kwargs and texts/ constants but NOT module-level item lists, so MODE_PIE_SLOT_ITEMS labels are invisible to the drift guard — the Still slices therefore reuse features/still_mode/menus.py wording verbatim ("Still Mode"/"Animation"/"Off (per-take)"), which already carries German. 14 new strings translated in de_DE.py; extractor reports 0 untracked / 0 orphans.

    28. 🟢 Bulk switches for the logging topics. TKS_OT_ToggleAllLogTopics (preferences/ops_misc.py), drawn as a pair above the topic stack in draw_debug.py. scope is TOPICS or SUBTOPICS; state is TOGGLE (the button) / ON / OFF (a scripted caller). Deliberately NOT click-only (Constitution rule 7): it writes preference booleans and opens nothing, so a script gets exactly what a click gets — unlike TKS_OT_ToggleLogTopic beside it, whose behaviour depends on modifier keys and which correctly refuses. The switch list is read from RNA, not hardcoded. It already exists in three places (properties, drawer, accordion-flag tuple) and drifting them apart is the class of bug CORR-16 and MAINT-08 exist to catch; a fourth copy would be a fourth thing to forget. The log_topic_ / log_sub_ prefix test excludes expand_log_topic_*, which is accordion state. One disk write, not 63. Every logging property carries update=_autosave_preferences, which saves the WHOLE config, so a bulk flip of 63 switches would have been 63 JSON writes — the same shape as the keymap tick fixed in entry 99. New persistence_io.suspended_autosave() context manager (re-entrant; the outermost exit saves once) guards it. Icons read the live state, so the button says what the click will do rather than always claiming "all on". Manual-map entry added (INFO-04), de_DE +2.

    32. 🟢 world_needed_warning preference (opt-in "no World" warning). (In-app confirmed 2026-08-19.) BoolProperty on AutomationsPropsMixin, default False, drawn in Workflow > Automations > World under world_adopt_tier (Adopt mode only) and registered in prefs_search. EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 561 -> 562. The reminder used to fire unconditionally in ADOPT mode; a scene with no World is an ordinary deliberate setup, so it is now a reminder for people who asked for it rather than a fault report for everyone. The gate lives in the SCAN (core/cascade_drift.py::_world_needed_warning_enabled), not the draw, so with it off the drift is never raised at all - no panel, no toggle lighting up, no cost. _on_world_needed_warning_changed emits NAV_WARNINGS_INVALIDATE + signal_redraw() so ticking the box shows the result of ticking the box (the nav panel caches its warning scan), and the scan gained an elif scene.world is None fallback for scenes the cascade has not visited this session - the tracker-keyed branch can only speak for scenes it has already witnessed, which is exactly not the scene the user just ticked the box in.     33. 🟢 Pick Tag render scope — tags become a render-selection axis (roadmap: pick-tag-render). build_task_list() (features/batch_render/batch_render_task_builder.py) gains tag_filter=None, applied inside _keep_vl as a single string compare against the VL's OWN tks_assigned_tag. VL-only by user ruling 2026-08-18 — scene, VL-group and scene-group tags are deliberately INERT here, unlike the tree's Filter-by-Tag popover which matches upward (a scene shows because a child VL matches). The two axes read the same property and must not be assumed to share semantics: the tree filter answers "what should I look at", the render filter answers "what should I render", and inheritance would silently queue every layer of a tagged scene. Menu: TKS_MT_RenderTagPick / TKS_MT_RenderTagPickForce (panels/pie_menus/render_scope.py) mirror the Pick Scene pair one-to-one — FG/BG read live from wm.tks_render_mode, rows grey out on a 0 count, counts come from _scope_task_count(wm, action, tag_name=...) routing through the REAL builder so a shown number cannot drift from what execute() renders. _assigned_vl_tags() sweeps view layers only and orders by tag-library category order, appending library-orphaned tag strings so a stale assignment stays reachable rather than becoming unrenderable. Both "Pick Tag" rows sit under their Pick Scene sibling and disable (not hide) when no VL carries a tag — a hidden row reads as a missing feature, a greyed one as an empty state; the sweep runs once per menu draw, never on the panel redraw path. Dispatch: actions TAG_PICK / TAG_PICK_FORCE + a tag_name StringProperty on TKS_OT_RenderScopeDispatch (render_scope_ops.py, HIDDEN+SKIP_SAVE like scene_name), with a matching description() branch so the row tooltip names the tag. Both batch operators (TKS_OT_BatchRender, TKS_OT_BatchRenderBG[Fast]) expose tag_filter and thread it to the builder, so the capability is scripted-reachable without the menu (AI-01 clean — no click-only path was created). Deliberately deferred: multi-tag OR selection, a tag search popup, and an F12 pie slot (pie slots are fixed actions; a picker needs a submenu, and a dynamic enum there would require utils/enum_cache.retained_enum). No PointerProperty anywhere — tag identity is the name string, and properties/tag_library.py already migrates every assignment on rename. TDD: dev/tests/test_batch_tag_filter.py (4 — own-tag match with scene tag proven inert, force/no-filter composition, count routing for both actions, operator RNA exposure) written first and watched fail on all four before the implementation. Full suite 2137 passed (Blender 5.2, worktree build via BLENDER_USER_EXTENSIONS). de_DE re-keyed in lockstep (INFO-09): 6 new strings. Commit 7f870c04, branch feature/pick-tag-render.

    34. 🟢 Sequencer Take Follow — the playhead drives the cascade. features/sequencer/: follow_core.py (pure pick_strip/binding_of/should_apply), engine.py (apply_binding = apply_overrides(skip_action=True) + apply_vl_switch_unified + the variant provider, addressed at a scene the window is NOT showing), handlers.py (a 0.1s timer for scrubbing, because frame_change_post does not fire while a sequencer timeline is dragged, plus a frame_change_pre handler for playback, where 41ms/frame at 24fps outruns any timer). Blender 5.2 API notes: SceneStrip.view_layer is new in 5.2, and sed.strips replaced sequences — an EMPTY strip collection is FALSY, so getattr(sed,'strips',None) or sed.sequences crashes; matched with hasattr. The frame cache is held off while the follow drives (use_prefetch/use_cache_raw/use_cache_final): a cached frame keeps the take it was rendered with and is the one thing that makes a correct follow look broken.

    35. 🟢 Sequencer Scene Auto-Switch (sequencer_scene_autoswitch, default True). A Window shows exactly one Scene, and SpaceSequenceEditor has NO scene property of its own — verified against RNA on 5.2. So a sequencer always shows the ACTIVE scene, and while that scene holds no strips the follow has nothing to follow. tks.sequencer_focus_switch moves the window to the scene that owns the strips. ON by default unlike the follow itself: shipping it off ships the follow broken. timeline_target / switch_to_timeline are PLAIN functions the timer calls directly — an operator invoked from a timer can refuse on context, and reaching it through bpy.ops is what made the frame-detected triggers look dead while the detector was correctly reporting movement.

    36. 🟢 Five triggers, separately switchable (sequencer_autoswitch_on, ENUM_FLAG). HOVER/CLICK/PLAY arrive via keymap items carrying their rung in an operator StringProperty — an EnumProperty always carries a value, which would make "no trigger" inexpressible and filter the sidebar button as a hover. SCRUB and ARROWS come from the timer, told apart by screen.is_scrubbing: a drag is the playhead, a bare frame change is a key. Keymap placement is the whole lesson — SequencerCommon sits behind the region maps; the scrub bar's press is consumed by anim.change_frame modally; arrows live in the GLOBAL Frames map where Blender binds screen.frame_offset. Five routes were measured with the operator's own arrival log. A key press has no location, so the operator's context.area check is the right filter and a global binding is safe; a CLICK carries one the guard cannot see, which is why a Frames LEFTMOUSE entry made every click a playhead gesture and had to be removed.

    37. 🟢 The way back (tks.sequencer_go_back). Restores the (scene, view layer) the switch took you from, remembered by NAME — a remembered scene can be deleted while you are away, and a stale pointer would crash where a name declines. It APPLIES the destination via engine.apply_binding rather than only repointing the window: the scope that protects the move is the same thing that suppresses the depsgraph handler which would otherwise run the cascade, so the change is delivered while suppressed and nothing is left to trigger it. Field report with pictures — the shared cube kept the strip's Mat_C_Purple until it was clicked in the viewport.

    38. 🟢 Optional automatic return (sequencer_autoswitch_back, default False; sequencer_autoswitch_back_on = HOVER/CLICK). OFF by default: with both halves on, the window follows the mouse between the two editors and every crossing runs a full cascade. Known interaction, documented rather than fixed — with ONE shared datablock across scenes the viewport and the VSE preview cannot show different takes at once, so returning re-applies the origin's take and the preview then renders the strip with it.

    39. 🟢 Sequencer sidebar (TKS_PT_SequencerTakes). Names the binding under the playhead and the one actually applied when they differ, warns when the frame cache is on with a one-click fix, and tells the two silences apart: "no strip under the playhead" (on the timeline, between cuts) versus "this scene has no strips" (not on it at all), the latter with a Go To Timeline button running the SAME operator as the keymap and a scripted caller.

    3. 🟢 Internal: draw_wrapped_paragraph honors manual line breaks — no visible change until a text uses one. New pure seam ui/styles.py::split_paragraphs: \n in an INFOBOX_* constant starts a new wrapped line, a blank line becomes a paragraph gap (separator(factor=1.2)), blank runs collapse, and whitespace-only text still draws nothing — the empty-body wrapped_info_box call in the autokey-blocked warning depends on that.     4. 🟢 Internal: phase 1 of the texts/ centralization campaign — 18 sites migrated, plus the tool that does it. New dev/scripts/apply_text_centralization.py: reads the auditor's INFO-09 rows (kind / file / line / target module), lifts the literal at each site via AST anchors, appends NAME = <text verbatim> to the destination texts/ module and rewrites the site to reference it, adding or extending the relative import. Dry-run by default; --kind / --area scope a batch; already-migrated sites are skipped so re-runs are no-ops. Phase 1 cleared bl_description (9 → 0) and the static infobox_literal sites (11 → 2; the 2 survivors are f-strings needing a template constant): 18 constants across infoboxes.py, tooltips_preferences.py, tooltips_misc.py, tooltips_batch_render.py, tooltips_render_presets.py. Two tool bugs caught by tests before they shipped: (a) Blender's property syntax is an ANNOTATION (prop: BoolProperty(...)), so the Call hangs off .annotation not .value — every prop_desc constant would otherwise be named PROP_<CLASS> with no property segment; (b) the texts import must be placed after the last top-level import located via AST — a line-scan inserted INSIDE a parenthesised multi-line import and split it (features/smart_syntax/registry.py). Multi-line implicit-concat literals are now refused outright (splicing head+name+tail across the span drops the separating comma — it produced invalid Python at registry.py:662 on the first run) and reported for hand migration. 15 tool tests in dev/tests/test_text_centralization_tool.py; full suite 1341 passed on Blender 5.2; auditor re-scan 619 → 601 findings with orphans unchanged at 31 (a rewrite that stranded a constant would show up there). Remaining: 196 prop_desc, 403 op_docstring (phase 4 — ADD bl_description, keep __doc__), 2 f-strings, 31 orphans. Plan: dev/plan_text_centralization.md. Commit bd698c9.

Same REPLACE mode as phase 1: the description= literal at each property definition becomes a PROP_* constant in the matching texts module and the site references it. Blender promotes cls.__doc__ to the tooltip only while bl_description is absent, so 403 operators were shipping their developer docstring as user-facing UI. New ADD mode in dev/scripts/apply_text_centralization.py: instead of replacing a literal it inserts bl_description = OP_<NAME> directly after bl_idname at matching indentation and copies the RAW docstring value (ast.get_docstring(clean=True) re-indents, which would silently change the tooltip); the docstring stays for developers. Idempotent — skips classes already declaring bl_description, and those with no docstring (nothing to move). 403 constants across 9 texts modules (195 → tooltips_misc; splitting that module by area stays open), 109 files.     14. 🟢 Native world assignment reconciles immediately and lands on the most specific governing tier. New core/world_native_sync.py: msgbus subscription on (Scene, "world") → one-shot timer → WORLD-filtered apply_overrides (echo-filtered against _last_cascade_world; re-armed via persistent load_post since msgbus subs are wiped on file load; registered through the vl_handlers delegation chain). Inside the cascade, the WITNESS rule gates everything: scene.world counts as user intent only when it differs from the last cascade-applied value — un-witnessed states follow the tree (Alt-click tier clear removes the world; a take-switch winner change applies the new winner instead of adopting the stale one). A witnessed pick lands on the MOST SPECIFIC of (winning tier, adopt tier): a Take/VL/VLG override is updated in place (the drift-Accept write shape), otherwise the configured tier — so a Properties pick never silently reverts, and world drift rows with a non-None native world are suppressed in ADOPT (they all self-resolve). Numeric-suffix copies of the winner (SOLO.003 vs SOLO, the template_ID count-badge "make single user" trap) are recognized via _strip_dup_suffix as the SAME world and never adopted. KEY GOTCHA cemented in tests: registered bpy.props live in system idprop storage — scene['tks_world']=x is invisible to RNA; tier writes MUST be RNA setattr. Troubleshooting: doc/troubleshooting/world_adoption_witness_rule.md; repro scripts dev/experiments/repro_world_duplicate*.py. Commits 07d39ce, d2e6c95, 99fc483, b4fde91, e9dfa28.

Clearable winners (rank ≤ Scene AND ≤ adopt tier) get their record cleared; Scene-Group/Global records are SHARED defaults and are never cleared by a scene-local gesture regardless of Adopt To. All cascade tier writes go through _write_world_record, which flags TKS_VL_STATE.is_world_reconciling so the three world update callbacks (panels/context/properties.py) cannot re-enter apply_overrides on stale trackers — the log fingerprint was one ✕ firing three chained WORLD passes that wiped the VL override AND the inherited record (Fixed entry 12). The respected removal keeps the tracker on the inherited world, which powers the standing warning of Added 13. Commits c2b45d4, bee8733, 901de0b, d53c36b.

Meanwhile TKS_OT_DeleteSelectedContextItems.execute ALREADY trimmed those cases (sel = sel[:-1], same for scenes) and would have deleted the remainder — i.e. the panel vetoed work the operator was happy to do, contradicting Constitution rule 6 (auto-filter, process the valid, report the skips). Fix: _build_plan(context) returns the exact lists (takes/vls/scenes/vlgs/sgs) plus human-readable skipped reasons; invoke builds it, reports and CANCELs when nothing is deletable, and otherwise opens an invoke_props_dialog whose draw lists both halves; execute consumes the SAME plan (a scripted call builds its own), so the summary agreed to is the work done. The dialog is forced whenever skipped is non-empty even if confirm_delete_take is off, because then the outcome differs from the request. Panel gate relaxed to remove_col.enabled = multiselect_any_selected. Test fixture also had to clear stale ticks (third time this session a dirty selection fixture skewed a result). Suite 1754. Commit c8f52f7.

Probe (bpy.context.scene.view_layers.remove(...), Blender 5.2) confirms the engine refuses: RuntimeError: View layer 'ViewLayer' could not be removed from scene 'PROBE'. So 26's "keep one back" was working around a hard constraint rather than a policy. _build_plan() in operators/context/ops_versions.py now collects such scenes into escalate and folds them into plan['scenes'], with plan['escalated'] driving a separate ERROR-icon box in draw() so the blast radius is stated before the OK. Backstop kept where Blender's own is: if nothing would survive, the last doomed scene is popped back and its view layers fall back to a plain VL delete minus one, both reasons pushed to plan['skipped']. Ordering matters — escalation runs before the last-scene check, and the scene section now runs even under a VL type filter, since escalation can produce scene deletions from a VL-only selection.

    37. 🟢 Retarget offered destinations that moved nothing, and hid the one that mattered. Two defects in one dropdown. It listed the group the tag was ALREADY in, so the obvious pick was a no-op; and "Ungrouped" was not a destination at all — a single id, "__UNGROUPED__", served as both the "Select a Group" placeholder AND the value execute() reads as "move it out of its group", which execute() then rejected as "No group selected". Moving a tag OUT of a group was unreachable from the dialog. The ids are now distinct (RETARGET_PLACEHOLDER / RETARGET_UNGROUPED), and _tag_group_helpers.retarget_destinations() computes what is reachable from the tags that would actually move (tags_to_retarget(): the multi-selection, else the active row). It drops any destination that would move nothing — the group they are all in, and "Ungrouped" when none of them is grouped. With a single group that yields exactly the user's rule: a grouped tag is offered Ungrouped, an ungrouped tag is offered the group. poll() reads the same function (and poll_message_sets when there is nowhere to go), so what is offered and what is accepted cannot diverge.
