In _output_panel_draw_override, the reproduced native rd.filepath row was previously always drawn with filepath_row.enabled = not smart_on (grayed when Smart Output on); it's now gated if not smart_on: so it isn't drawn at all while Smart Output owns the output — the resolved Directory/File Name previews above already convey the final path, and a disabled duplicate was pure clutter. The use_property_split = False/use_property_decorate = False setup moved inside that guard. Added a layout.separator() at the end of draw_output_panel_prepend for spacing between the file-name preview box and the native Saving/image-settings section. No tests (pure draw-layout change in the panel override).

    32. 🟢 Shift+Click a group chevron to expand or collapse a whole list at once. Converted 5 execute-only collapse-toggle operators to the invoke→shift_all = event.shift→execute pattern (mirrors pm_toggle_group_expand), each gaining shift_all: BoolProperty(default=False, options={'HIDDEN'}): tks.profiler_toggle_group (every GROUP_HEADER in tks_profiler_items), tks.preload_toggle_section (new vl_preload.set_all_sections_collapsed, computing section keys from wm.tks_all_viewlayers), tks.vsw_tree_toggle (every tks_vsw_tree item), tks.tagtree_toggle_expand (every tks_tree_expand_<cat> WM bool, enumerated from lib.categories), tks.tag_group_toggle_expand (every group.is_expanded across all categories). Shift state = inverse of the clicked item applied to all; plain click unchanged. Audit of all collapsible lists found these 5 missing it (Takes tree toggle_scene_expand and Process Monitor pm_toggle_group_expand already had it).

    Fixed¶

    1. 🟢 find_vl_version_set() re-resolves the set by collection index to stop a stale-RNA EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION (@0x18). The helper cached live TKS_VLVersionSet element references in a module global, invalidated only by a length-token + rename event. Heavy custom-property churn on the World reallocates the IDProperty array backing tks_vl_version_sets without changing the element count, so the token never fired and a dangling element was returned — the next draw's len(vs.versions) dereferenced a freed IDProperty group and hard-crashed. The id_data guard can't catch it (the World ID stays alive, only the element slot moved). Fix: cache the collection INDEX and re-resolve sets[idx] from the freshly-fetched collection every call, with an identity re-check that rebuilds on a silent reorder; prefer the scene_name StringProperty over the .scene PointerProperty (Constitution Rule 1). draw_vl() wraps len(vs.versions) in try/except as defense in depth.

    2. 🟢 Pie-menu toggle update= callbacks return None. navigation_pie_enabled and f12_pie_menu_enabled used update= lambdas that returned a TUPLE of two calls (autosave + keymap sync). Blender requires update callbacks to return None, so registration raised ValueError: the return value must be None and the headless test runner crashed (exit 2, 0 tests). Replaced with named functions that call both and return None implicitly.

    3. 🟢 Autokey-mirror suppression was writing _suppress_until to the wrong module in two VL-switch call sites. core/vl_switch_fast.py:56-57 (in apply_vl_switch_unified, "Suppress autokey mirror handler" block) and operators/context/ops_crud_switch.py:162-164 (in TKS_OT_SwitchViewLayer._deferred_cascade) both imported features.rest_state.operators as _ref_ops and wrote _ref_ops._suppress_until = time.time() + N. The flag is defined and read from features.rest_state.mirror_logic (mirror_logic.py:29, checked at :48); writing it to operators silently creates a transient attribute on the wrong module that _handle_autokey_mirror never reads. Effect: both suppression windows were dead — the handler could fire during Action reassignment and produce double rest-state captures or unexpected snaps on VL switch. Pre-existing in both sites; not introduced by the module split. Correct write sites (cascade_actions.py:137, cache.py:321, logic.py:312,511) all use mirror_logic as _ml; _ml._suppress_until = ... correctly. Fix: changed both imports to mirror_logic as _ml; companion stale comment at vl_lifecycle.py:495 corrected ("Suppress was removed — _suppress_until is dead code" was false; only vl_lifecycle's own write was removed, the mechanism is live).

    4. 🟢 Sync Brackets now normalizes mismatched delimiter pairs (e.g. [scene)), not just whole-style differences. New SmartSyntaxEngine.convert_to_current_style(path) replaces the per-style conversion loop: a single module-level regex _ANY_BRACKET_TOKEN = re.compile(r'[\[{<(%$#]([^\[\]{}<>()%$#]+)[\]}>)%$#]') matches any-open + any-close (matched or not), and a _repl that rewrites to the current get_brackets() pair only when the inner is a known token (KNOWN_TOKENS or a _PARAMETERIZED_TOKENS base after :-split) — so arbitrary bracketed text, native #### padding (no inner content), and unknown tokens are untouched (Rule 71.437). needs_bracket_sync(path) = convert_to_current_style(path) != path, draw-safe (never raises), drives the conditional red button (Changed #9). ops_utils.TKS_OT_SyncBrackets.execute refactored to call convert_to_current_style (dropping its inline per-style loop + BRACKET_STYLES import), so detection and repair share one implementation. [scene)/(scene]/{scene> → [scene] (current style); verified by hand-traced cases + headless compile.

    5. 🟢 to_absolute normalizes ../ segments (was leaving literal .. in the field). features/batch_render/path_mode.py::to_absolute now wraps os.path.join(blend_dir, tail) in os.path.normpath(...) (then .replace('\\','/')), so .. collapses against the .blend folder — //../../[scene] from C:/proj/shots → C:/[scene]. Anchored at the file root (blend_dir = dirname(bpy.data.filepath)); tokens are ordinary path components and survive. to_relative already normalized via relpath, so the abs↔rel round-trip is stable. +2 tests (test_to_absolute_collapses_parent_segments, test_parent_segments_round_trip); 18 path_mode tests pass. Documented in doc/troubleshooting/path_mode_toggle_double_slash.md (3rd follow-up).

    6. 🟢 A Rest Action whose backing action was deleted now loads showing the name in red, not blank. The file-load handler only copied the saved Rest Action name into wm.tks_rest_action when the action datablock still existed, so a rest action deleted and then saved reloaded blank instead of red. Dropped the existence gate — the name is restored regardless, letting the popover render a missing action as red/stale, matching the runtime behaviour where deleting a live action shows the field red, not empty. (Files saved while already blank stay blank until the action is re-picked and saved — nothing was persisted to restore.) Added TestRestoreHandlerKeepsStaleName; full headless suite 518 passed. Commit 7daa5b4.

    7. 🟢 The Context tree view now repopulates on every file open, not just the first in a session. The tree stayed blank after the second-plus File ▸ Open: the sync timer's fast-path gate is driven by module-level globals that survive a file load, but the WindowManager-backed tree collection is reset by Load UI — so with nothing to re-arm the gate, sync_all_viewlayers was skipped on every load after the first. Added a persistent load_post handler (twin of the existing undo/redo handler) that re-arms the dirty flags, clears the fingerprint + structure key, and busts the UIList caches so the next timer tick rebuilds the tree. Verified in-app; 543 headless tests pass. Commit f712876.

    8. 🟢 The VL Switch Profiler's categories collapse, and stay collapsed. Two defects. (1) TKS_UL_Profiler (panels/navigation/monitors_profiler.py) had no filter_items, so tks.profiler_toggle_group flipped a GROUP_HEADER's is_expanded (and the chevron) but template_list still drew every child row — added filter_items delegating to a pure collapse_filter_flags(items, bitflag) that clears the filter bit on child rows of collapsed groups (tested in dev/tests/test_profiler_collapse.py). (2) ops_crud_switch._deferred_cascade rebuilds tks_profiler_items on every VL switch (items.clear() + re-add), and fresh GROUP_HEADERs defaulted is_expanded=True → every switch re-expanded all categories; now captures the collapsed group names before clear() and sets g.is_expanded = name not in _collapsed_groups on rebuild. Companion: new generic auditor rule CORR-10 (in the separate blender-addon-auditor repo) flags any UIList drawing a collapse chevron with no filter_items; # CORR-10-OK sentinel added to TKS_UL_ProcessMonitor, which legitimately rebuilds its collection each draw.

    9. 🟢 Editing a view layer that uses the Rest Action no longer snaps your changes back. The autokey-mirror handler's mirror phase already bows out when authoring the rest VL (mirror_logic.py, cascade_action == rest_action → continue, ~L387), but the two revert scheduling sites did not, so _revert_unkeyed_to_rest_deferred (revert_snap.py) reverted the just-edited, unkeyed property to the Rest Action's fc.evaluate(0) (the OLD baseline) ~0.1s later. Clearest with autokey OFF: a transform drag on the rest VL collected the object's action (= the rest action) into _revert_names → schedule_revert({rest_action}) → snap-back — and the rest action's own FCurves were never changed by an autokey-off drag, so the revert read the stale frame-0 value. Fix: new pure predicate revert_snap.revert_names_for_rest_vl(modified_names, rest_action_name, cascade_action_name) drops the rest action from the revert set only when cascade_action == rest_action, wired into both mirror_logic.py sites (the autokey-off branch and the post-mirror has_action_update branch) via _get_vl_cascade_action(context). Take actions modified in the same tick still revert; a normal VL is untouched (the autokey-off snap-to-rest behavior is preserved). Rejected the broader "skip every rest-action target inside the deferred timer" approach — pinned objects on a normal VL legitimately keep sub-targets in the Rest Action (mirror_logic.py ~L382), and the precise "are we on the rest VL?" signal is only reliable at the live-context schedule site. 7 new pure tests (dev/tests/test_rest_vl_revert.py) + 60 rest tests pass headless. doc/troubleshooting/rest_vl_revert_snapback.md.

    10. 🟢 Auditor CORR-07 (Missing poll()) cleared on the 8 flagged operators — quality 9.6 → 10.0. The 0.4 quality deduction was entirely missing_poll_real (8 × 0.05). Each got a poll() mirroring its existing draw-time .enabled gate (no new behavior beyond also guarding direct/keymap invocation): features/batch_render/token_builder.py — TKS_OT_BuilderMove/TKS_OT_BuilderRemove → wm.tks_token_sel_idx >= 0 (matches btns.enabled = has_sel), TKS_OT_BuilderCopy → non-empty wm.tks_token_builder, TKS_OT_BuilderApply → wm.tks_token_target_kind != 'none' (matches apply_row.enabled); all getattr-guarded against a missing WM. TKS_OT_BuilderAppend annotated # POLL_NOT_NEEDED (appending is unconditional; the auditor reads the marker in the two lines above the class def). features/rest_state/operators.py — TKS_OT_SnapAllToRest/TKS_OT_SnapPropertyToRest → get_rest_action() is not None (same cheap module-global lookup the sibling Unset*/Delete* ops already poll on). operators/context/ops_crud_switch.py — TKS_OT_PreloadViewLayersCancel → vl_preload.is_preloading() (lazy import, returns the _preloading module global). Confirmed no direct bpy.ops.tks.* call sites for these idnames (only utils/manual_map.py string entries), so the new polls can't surface as execute-time poll failures. Re-scan: missing_poll_real 8 → 0, harmless 294 → 295 (Append moved to the marker bucket), quality/footprint/health all 10.0.

    11. 🟢 Auditor STD-01 (Manifest validity) cleared — blender_manifest.toml license gains the SPDX: prefix. license = ["GPL-3.0-or-later"] → ["SPDX:GPL-3.0-or-later"]. Blender's local extension validator is lenient, but extensions.blender.org rejects the bare identifier; the SPDX-prefixed form is what the platform requires. No change to the license terms.

    [0.7.9] - 2026-06-05¶

    Added¶

    1. 🟢 Preset-JSON compatibility gate + Clean Up (migrate/quarantine). New features/render_presets/serialization/compat.py (bpy-free except a light from ....core.constants import ADDON_VERSION): validate_preset_data(preset_type, data) → (ok, reason) checking (a) structure — ≥1 non-_meta group with a properties dict; (b) _meta.schema_version int ≤ CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION (a DEDICATED format version, decoupled from the addon version — coupling them would falsely flag presets from any newer build; _meta.addon_version from ADDON_VERSION is stamped as provenance only and never gates); (c) _meta.preset_type match. migrate_preset_data upgrades the one known old format (bookmark export list {"type":"tks_bookmarks","bookmarks":[…]} → preset dict). serialization/crud.py: save_preset stamps schema_version+addon_version+preset_type; load_preset validates → skips incompatible (logs, falls through to next tier); list_presets returns compatible-only via mtime-cached _file_compatible (hot path — called per-type/per-redraw); added list_incompatible_presets and non-destructive quarantine_preset (→ _quarantine/ subdir, never deletes). ops_compat.py (NEW, registered in the feature __init__): TKS_OT_CleanupIncompatiblePresets (scan-all → migrate-or-quarantine behind a blast-radius invoke_props_dialog). Surfaced: nav badge only when incompatible presets exist (tks_show_incompatible_presets + _incompatible_cache in panels/navigation/panel.py, draw_incompatible_presets in warnings.py, registered in panels/navigation/__init__.py); ui/styles.py::preset_row distinguishes INCOMPATIBLE (file exists but fails validation → find_preset_tier not None while absent from compatible list_presets) from MISSING, routing to the cleanup op. Tests dev/tests/test_preset_compat.py (21). Doc doc/troubleshooting/preset_json_compatibility_and_capture_coverage.md.
    2. 🟢 "Check Coverage" preset-capture diagnostic. serialization/resolve.py gains a zero-overhead module _COVERAGE_SINK (None by default; when set to a list, _capture_properties_from_struct records every writable prop it can't store — path/RNA-type/reason). ops_compat.TKS_OT_PresetCaptureReport runs a capture of all types via preset_engine._capture_for_type with the sink and fills WindowManager.tks_capture_coverage (TKS_CaptureCoverageItem PG + TKS_UL_CaptureCoverage), drawn as a template_list in preferences/draw_data_storage.py (no console output, mirroring the Property Scanner). Surfaces the known drops: collection properties + ENUM_FLAG round-trips.

    3. 🟢 Driven and NLA-only values now surface in the Channels panel (CORR-09 Phase A). panels/channels/logic.py: new _collect_driver_nla_curves(target, selected_type, obj, scene) enumerates read-only sources the active-action-slot pass misses — drivers (animation_data.drivers, each an F-curve with a data_path and no keyframes) and NLA-only animation (animation_data.nla_tracks[].strips[].action, resolved slot-aware via get_slot_fcurves(act, slot)) — yielding (raw_data_path, 'DRIVER'|'NLA'), wrapped so a malformed strip can't break the panel draw. Both collectors consume it: _get_inspector_keyed_paths merges the normalized driver/NLA paths into the displayed set with a {path: source} tag map, and _get_key_count_for_target adds them to the current-frame total so the nav/type badge count matches the displayed list (the CORR-09.1 count-vs-list contract). An NLA-only object (active animation_data.action empty after an NLA push-down) now stays selectable in the type header instead of dropping to "No animated data". Closes the drivers + NLA-only strips entries from CORR-09's overseen-surface inventory; the CORR-09 Tier-2 probe (dev/scripts/channel_coverage_probe.py, dev/tests/test_channel_coverage_probe.py) proved the gap. Tests dev/tests/test_channels_driver_nla.py (3: source-tag surfacing, drivers don't inflate the keyed set, NLA-only object stays selectable).

    4. 🟢 Choose what happens to a duplicated object's animation — Strip / Independent Slot / Off. New auto_duplicate_action_mode pref on AutomationsPropsMixin (EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 493→494). When an object is duplicated it inherits the source's slot token, creating two live targets for one slot; detect_slot_renames now skips shared tokens (a shared_tokens set) so the rename pass doesn't flip name_display nondeterministically between the two objects. New core/slot_split.py + TKS_OT_SplitDuplicateSlot (operators/inspector/ops_split_duplicate_slot.py) give each copy its own canonical slot in the correct action; core/slot_tokens.py and the inspector viewport-sync updated in step. Commits ac457d9, 33e885a, 284b14d.

    Changed¶

    1. 🟢 Internal: four oversized modules split into focused submodules — no behavior change. Each split keeps a thin facade / re-export shim so existing import sites are untouched; all are behavior-neutral unless noted.
    2. (a) Pie-keyframe subsystem (panels/pie_menus/keyframe.py, −1608 → thin facade). Split into keyframe_pies.py (all TKS_MT_PIE_Keyframe* menus + the Still/Animation sub-pies, scope operators TKS_OT_InsertKeyframes/TKS_OT_ClearKeyframes/TKS_OT_DeleteAnimSlot/TKS_OT_Invoke|Native*, the reset ops, _SLOT_ACTION_MAP, _draw_pie_from_slots), keyframe_keymap.py (pie-kmi register/sync — public sync_kmi_to_prefs / sync_keymap_to_pref, _deferred_initial_sync, extracted _cancel_and_teardown, _is_master_enabled/_editor_enabled), and keyframe_keymap_natives.py (native I / Alt+I deactivation tables _NATIVE_*_DEACTIVATE / _EXTRA_NATIVE_*, _toggle_*, session-local _flipped_natives, _kmi_descr/_trace_kmi). keyframe.py is now a facade re-exporting register/unregister/sync_kmi_to_prefs/sync_keymap_to_pref, so the prefs-UI from ...pie_menus.keyframe import … is unchanged. Only non-mechanical change: class TKS_OT_DeleteSlot → TKS_OT_DeleteAnimSlot (bl_idname stays tks.delete_anim_slot — no scripter impact). Tests: test_anim_clear.py imports _SLOT_ACTION_MAP from keyframe_pies; test_slot_split.py registration suite (+33).
    3. (b) Navigation warning panels (panels/navigation/warnings.py, −1084, DELETED → warnings/ package). Realizes the naming_conventions.md §2.3 domain-split proposal. Nine domain modules — system_cache.py, system_preview_renames.py, presets_incompatible.py, presets_missing.py, presets_changes.py, cascade_rest_drift.py, cascade_slot_mismatch.py, cascade_drift.py, cascade_broken_assignments.py — plus shared _widgets.py (PRESET_TYPE_INFO, diff_pair, value_box, arrow_cell, collapsible_header) and a thin __init__.py re-export shim (all 9 draw_* fns), so panel.py's from .warnings import draw_* is untouched. Draw functions are behavior-identical but not byte-identical after the follow-up consolidation: the repeated diff-row layout (the [before] → [after] value chips and the collapsible type-header) was factored from the 7 diff-bearing modules into the shared _widgets builders (diff_pair / value_box / arrow_cell / collapsible_header) — layout-preserving, with split factors, keyframe / UNLINKED icons, alerts, and presets_changes's ASCII -> arrow all passed through as params. system_cache / presets_incompatible have no diff rows and are unchanged. (naming_conventions.md §2.3 flipped from "proposed" to built.)
    4. (c) Reference-state mirror logic (features/rest_state/mirror_logic.py, −570). The ~630-line _handle_autokey_mirror handler reduced to orchestration by extracting mirror_writes.py (_apply_mirror_writes — deferred undoable ref-keyframe write phase), revert_snap.py (_revert_unkeyed_to_rest_deferred / _flush_revert_timer / new schedule_revert + the debounced revert-timer globals — "split S1: timer-state lives in the module that owns it; no cross-module reassignment"), cascade_action_cache.py (_get_vl_cascade_action / invalidate_cascade_action_cache + per-tick name cache), and orphan_redirect.py (_redirect_orphan_action). Distinct from the Fixed #2 ref-cache/slot-divergence fix (that logic is unchanged, just relocated). Test import path updated (test_rest_state.py → from …rest_state.revert_snap import _revert_unkeyed_to_rest_deferred). Accompanying minor guard (not part of the split): TKS_OT_SnapSelectedToRest gained a poll() requiring a selection.

    5. (d) Inspector sync engine (panels/inspector/sync.py, −445). Split into sync_jit.py (Just-In-Time fresh-action→cascade merge: _is_jit_blocked / _is_fresh_action / _try_jit_object / _try_jit_sub_targets + per-object cooldown), sync_info.py (read-only empty-state messages get_objects_info / get_actions_info / get_slots_info, consumed by panel.py / inspector_sections.py), sync_actions.py (_process_fresh_actions / _process_rest_snaps / _on_vl_switch_pre_inspector + _obj_action_tracker / _pending_fresh_actions), and sync_viewport.py (_handle_viewport_selection_sync depsgraph handler). sync.py keeps the sync_*_collection orchestrators and re-imports the JIT helpers, so handlers.py / __init__.py imports are unchanged; panel.py / inspector_sections.py switched to from .sync_info import …. Cleanup pending: sync_jit.py still carries temporary [VERIFY] Phase-6 diagnostic logging to remove after in-app confirmation.

    6. 🟢 The Debug Monitor opens large log files faster. New _read_tail_lines() seeks from EOF and doubles the read window until it captures the requested line count, reaches the file start, or hits an 8 MB ceiling — so load time scales with lines displayed, not the whole (potentially multi-MB) log. Extracted _parse_lines() so the parse + level-filter step is reusable without loading duplicate data. Tests: dev/tests/test_log_reader_tail.py. Commit d3e2ad6.

    Fixed¶

    1. 🟢 Pie "Reset to default" buttons now work. All five slot-reset operators (TKS_OT_ResetPieOptions, TKS_OT_ResetF12PieOptions, TKS_OT_ResetKeyframePieOptions, TKS_OT_ResetKeyframeAltPieOptions, TKS_OT_ResetPieGrid) used prefs.property_unset(slot), which reverts the value in data but emits no RNA update notification → stale Preferences dropdowns and no update=/autosave (the reset was lost on reload). Replaced with two shared helpers in preferences/persistence_io.py (re-exported from persistence.py): reset_pref_slots_to_default(p, slot_names) — setattr(p, key, prop_rna.default) (same path as TKS_OT_ResetPreferences) inside prefs_loading_guard(), then one _autosave_preferences(), then redraw_preferences_areas(); and redraw_preferences_areas() — tags open PREFERENCES areas (the no-direct-tag_redraw rule covers the 3D viewport, not the Preferences window, which signal_redraw() can't reach). Call sites: preferences/ops_misc.py, panels/pie_menus/keyframe.py, panels/pie_menus/render_scope.py. See doc/troubleshooting/pie_reset_to_default_no_effect.md.

    2. 🟢 Switching between view layers with no action reliably snaps objects back to the rest pose — including right after you edit the reference. Two root causes from the v0.7.x single-sweep refactor. (a) Write/read slot divergence: insert_rest_keyframe deposited ref values via Blender's slot auto-match (ad.action_slot after assigning the action), which drifts to a stray duplicate object slot (Name_001_MESH) when one exists, while the snap reads the canonical name_display slot — so a set reference and the snap targeted different slots. Now insert_rest_keyframe prefers the caller-resolved canonical slot over auto-match. (b) Stale ref cache: the frame-0 ref-value cache (features/rest_state/cache.py::_rest_cache) was invalidated only by insert_rest_keyframe, so authoring the reference via native Auto-Key on the reference VL (which writes the FCurves directly) left the cache stale and action-less VLs snapped to the old pose. mirror_logic._revert_unkeyed_to_rest_deferred now calls invalidate_rest_cache() when the rest action is among the modified actions. Failed approaches (reverted): guarding resolve_cascade to return None for the rest action broke the watchlist ghost icon (draw_layers.py derives is_ref from resolve_cascade); and refusing to assign/merge the rest action (apply_vl_switch_unified demote-to-None, merge_action_into_cascade refusal) broke authoring on the reference VL — that VL is the intended authoring surface, so the reference must remain assignable/mergeable. The reference must resolve normally; only the write/read slot consistency and cache freshness needed fixing. See doc/troubleshooting/rest_state_duplicate_slot_write_read_divergence.md. Tests: dev/tests/test_rest_state.py::TestInsertRefKeyframeSlotTargeting, ::TestReferenceModificationInvalidatesCache.

    3. 🟢 The watchlist's VL-switch progress icons reflect actual work. apply_vl_switch_unified blanket-set all six wm.tks_cascade_step_* enums to SUCCESS at the end of every sweep — and because the interactive switch calls apply_overrides(skip_action=True), the accurate per-step tracking in cascade.py (reset→PENDING, then mark each phase) was skipped. The sweep now resets all six to PENDING at the start and, at the end, marks resolve/targets/done SUCCESS (always-run phases) but unassign/assign/snap SUCCESS only when _stat shows they did work — so the inspector icons (panels/inspector/inspector_sections.py: active = step=='SUCCESS', alert = step=='FAILED') read bright=fired / dimmed=not-fired. ("Red on crash" not yet wired.) Test: dev/tests/test_rest_state.py::TestCascadeStepIndicatorsReflectWork.

    4. 🟢 Bookmark presets show a change-warning + Save/Revert. preset_state.get_preset_state routes 'bookmark' to a membership-aware _bookmarks_state (dynamic key set — symmetric add/remove/relabel diff) BEFORE the fixed-schema if not preset_props/_auto_upgrade_preset path; bookmark mutations call _invalidate_bookmark_dirty_state (features/bookmarks/operators.py → invalidate_preset_cache('bookmark') + invalidate_nav_warnings() + signal_redraw()). 'bookmark' added to the Save-All loop / _TYPES / Revert-All lists (+ capture/apply branches) and to both TKS_OT_SelectPreset attr_maps (X-clear + Alt+X-delete were silent no-ops). See doc/troubleshooting/bookmark_preset_no_change_warning.md. (Note: an empty assigned bookmark preset short-circuiting to CLEAN is a known remaining edge — separate.)

    5. 🟢 Bookmarked channels visible without keyframes — rows AND category buttons. (a) panels/channels/logic.py::_get_inspector_keyed_paths merged bookmarked paths RAW (double-quoted, with the node_tree./data. accessor prefix) into active_paths, while active_paths/keyed_paths/section props use the normalized form (normalize_rna_path → single quotes, prefix stripped) — so an unkeyed bookmarked node/material property never matched a section prop. Added _normalize_path_for_type(path, selected_type) (same per-type strip + normalize_rna_path as the keyed loop) applied to each bookmarked path, building a NEW set so it doesn't alias keyed_paths. (b) panels/channels/draw.py::draw_channels filtered the per-target category buttons to keyframe count > 0, so a bookmarked-but-unkeyed target was dropped → "No animated data" + no buttons; now a target is kept when it has keys OR (tks_show_bookmarks and get_bookmarked_paths(scene, target_type) non-empty). Test dev/tests/test_bookmark_channel_visibility.py (RED proved the raw-vs-normalized mismatch); doc bookmark_channels_visible_without_keyframes.md.

    6. 🟢 Material / World / File-Output no longer silently dropped by preset dispatch. ops_manage_sync.py: material branch added to _type_to_attr + _capture_for_save + _apply_to_scene (per-type Accept&Sync of a material preset returned None → "Could not capture settings" CANCEL / getattr(config, None) failure). ops_manage_crud.py::TKS_OT_EditRenderPreset: the rename scene-config if/elif chain (dropped fileoutput/material/bookmark) replaced with a generic _ATTR_MAP lookup, and material added to the tag-ref attr_name map (bookmark stays out — TKS_Tag has no bookmark_preset field — marked # CORR-08-OK). preset_health.py: bookmark added to preset_types + _TYPE_LABELS (a stale config.bookmark_preset is now flagged). panels/navigation/panel.py:170: world added to the nav dirty-scan tuple. All surfaced by CORR-08 (below). Tests dev/tests/test_preset_dispatch_bugfixes.py; doc preset_type_dispatch_material_bookmark_gaps.md.

    7. 🟢 The Inspector channel search filters live as you type. WindowManager.tks_channel_search (panels/inspector/__init__.py) is consumed at DRAW time by panels/channels/{draw,sections}.py (search_term = getattr(wm, "tks_channel_search", "").lower()), but the prop had no update= callback and no options, so Blender only committed the typed value — and redrew — on Enter/focus-loss (text buttons don't write the RNA value mid-edit). Added options={'TEXTEDIT_UPDATE'} (the one StringProperty flag that fires update= on every keystroke during text editing) plus a redraw-only callback _on_channel_search_changed that calls signal_redraw() (Constitution Rule 3 — not tag_redraw()) and is guarded by the addon_is_mutating/is_undoing early-out. Deliberately does NOT call mark_inspector_dirty() (unlike _on_filter_changed): the channels view filters at draw time, so the heavier full-collection resync on the 0.2s sync timer is unnecessary per keystroke. Doc doc/troubleshooting/channel_search_live_filter.md. (The objects-list filter tks_inspector_filter retains its Enter-only commit — same TEXTEDIT_UPDATE fix applies if wanted, but it routes through mark_inspector_dirty().)

    8. 🟢 Orphaned transient .NNN reference baseline slots from action-duplication splitting now reliably swept. core/slot_split.py: the post-split cleanup of baseline slots the ref-state had baselined under a copy's transient .NNN name replaced a single mutation_queue.enqueue_mutation(_clean_transient_ref_baselines, scene.name) pass with _enqueue_ref_clean(scene.name) — a bounded, deduped retry chain. A baseline only becomes orphaned once its object is renamed away from .NNN, so the one-shot sweep raced the copies' auto-rename and left some behind; the retry chain re-enqueues until they've all settled.

    9. 🟢 Project presets resolve to the same folder at startup and after a reload. _get_project_presets_dir now owns the blend-dir/presets fallback as its single source of truth (read via getattr to avoid _RestrictData during addon registration), so register and the deferred reload resolve the same path. Commit 108cf6d.

    Tooling¶

    Maintainer-only — the doc/reports/ /stats code-quality dashboard. Not shipped in the add-on zip; no takes_for_blender/ runtime change.

    1. Overview layout gains a committed factory baseline plus Export / Import of the custom state. The hardcoded DEFAULT_OVERVIEW_LAYOUT in js/app.js is now only a fallback (_FACTORY_FALLBACK_LAYOUT); the real factory baseline lives in the new committed data/dashboard_layout.factory.js (window.DASHBOARD_LAYOUT_FACTORY), loaded via a <script> sidecar before app.js (same cache-buster pattern as codebase_stats.js) and resolved in app.js with a missing-file fallback. Three new sidebar controls: Reset to factory (_resetToFactory — removes only the live tks-overview-layout.v2 key and re-renders from the sidecar; leaves the tks-overview-layout-saved.v2 Save snapshot intact), Export layout (_exportLayout — Blob download dashboard_layout.json wrapped {schema_version, exported_at, layout}), and Import layout (_importLayout — hidden <input type=file> → JSON.parse → accepts the wrapped or a bare layout → existing _migrateLayout reconciliation → save + re-render, with console.warn + label-flash on bad input). download / upload icons added to the ICONS dict; inline feedback via a small _flashLabel helper (mirrors the Save button — the viewer has no toast). The page is static file://, so a download/upload is the only file channel.

    2. Settings popover reorganized into nested fly-out submenus. The flat ~10-button popover is grouped into Data / View / Layout / Tiles categories (.settings-group → .settings-cat row + .settings-submenu). Submenus are position: fixed, positioned to the right of the category from its bounding rect with a viewport-bottom clamp; open on hover and toggle on click, with a 200 ms close-timer bridging the category→fly-out gap, and close together with the popover (Esc / outside-click / resize). All existing button ids/classes are preserved, so every handler and the shared popover-button CSS still apply (.settings-cat added to those selector lists; collapse rule broadened to .settings-popover button > span).

    3. Per-tile show/hide with empty-section collapse. Hidden tile ids live in the layout object (layout.hidden), so visibility travels with Export / Import, resets with Reset-to-factory, and is captured by Save / Restore; _migrateLayout carries the list forward filtered to live data-tile-ids. New Tiles fly-out (_buildTilesMenu, rebuilt on open) lists every tile by data-tile-label with an eye toggle (_setTileHidden / _getHiddenTiles) plus Show all / Hide all; eye_off icon added. _renderOverviewLayout skips hidden tiles — they stay in the already-hidden #overview-tile-pool, keeping their grid slot — and tags columns/sections with zero visible tiles .is-empty. CSS hides .is-empty only via body:not(.layout-mode), so empties collapse in normal view but stay visible as drop targets in layout-edit mode (no re-render needed on mode toggle, since _setLayoutMode toggles the body class).

    4. New audit rule CORR-09 — Channel Coverage / Animatable-Value Routing (Tier 1, static). Catches the "this animated value never shows up in the Channels panel" class. The panel (panels/channels/) buckets each animated data_path into a UI type via substring path_filter lambdas; values are silently dropped three ways, each now checked statically by engine/parts/corr_09_channel_coverage.py::classify_part_channel_coverage (AST-only — the channel modules import bpy, so the part reads logic.py/draw.py from disk via ast.parse, exactly like CORR-08 reads _ATTR_MAP; degrades to channel_present=False when absent). 09.1 routing drift: the two collectors in panels/channels/logic.py — _get_inspector_keyed_paths (drives the displayed list) and _get_key_count_for_target (drives the badge count) — must encode the SAME per-type container set, else the badge and the list diverge. Container tokens are harvested ONLY from path_filter bindings (lambda body, or a local def assigned to path_filter like the ps_filter pattern), so the per-bone selection filter (bone_filter, applied directly to all_fcurves, never bound to path_filter) and the path-normalization block — both legitimately display-only — don't register as drift. Normalization via _norm_container (pathy [/trailing-. tokens + a bare-word vocab: shape_keys/key_blocks/nodes/…); BoolOp(And) branch tests (selected_type == "DATA" and obj:) and in (...) sets both narrow the type. 09.2 type symmetry: the UI type universe is the *type_info list literals in panels/channels/draw.py (tks.select_inspector_target rows); every UI type must be branched by the display resolver (unhandled → empty panel) and every branched type must be a real UI type (orphan → dead branch). 09.3 canonical surface diff: a maintainer-curated _ANIMATABLE_SURFACES inventory (mirrors CORR-03's seed symbol table) tags each animatable ID surface with the covering UI type or None; a None (or a covered_by the UI doesn't expose) is an "overseen" surface — currently 6: scene compositor node tree, grease-pencil layers, NLA-only strips, drivers, non-active materials, Freestyle line style. Sentinel # CORR-09-OK: <reason> on/above a type's branch in either collector exempts that type's drift (reuses crash_06's _s_line_has_sentinel). Scoring (report.py): 09.1 drift + 09.2 unhandled/orphan deduct 0.3 each from quality (functional band, == CORR-08 functional + Part CA); 09.3 surfaces deduct at CHANNEL_SURFACE_DEDUCT = 0.0 (informational-until-reviewed, mirroring COMPAT_DEDUCT_PER_FINDING) so landing the rule surfaces the gap list without re-baselining the health score. Wired into rules.py (CORR-09, CORR/HIGH/quality), state.py (channel_* metrics), report.py (import + dispatch after CORR-08, penalty pen_channel, quality-deduction summary row, full markdown ## Part CORR-09 section, dashboard summary + detailed CORR-09 part JSON). Current real-codebase result: 0 drift, 0 symmetry gaps, 6 overseen surfaces (score unchanged at 7.6). Tests: dev/tests/test_channel_coverage.py (29, incl. the keystone test_real_channel_files_present_and_collectors_agree guarding the shipped collectors against future desync).

    5. CORR-09 Tier 2 — headless ground-truth channel-coverage probe. The static Tier-1 check can only diff against a maintainer-curated surface list; Tier 2 proves the gaps against REAL Blender data. dev/scripts/channel_coverage_probe.py (run headless via tests_perf.py::run_channel_coverage, scraped between ===CHAN_JSON_BEGIN/END=== sentinels exactly like perf_capture.py; behind a --no-channel CLI flag, stored in m.channel_probe) builds a controlled scene that animates representative values across surfaces AND animation sources — action_slot (the only source routing reads), driver (obj.driver_add), nla_strip (rotation authored then pushed to an NLA track with the active action cleared), non_active_material (2nd material slot, distinct metallic path so no collision masks it), and compositor (scene.compositing_node_group, the Blender 5.x global compositor — legacy scene.node_tree is gone) — then drives the LIVE _get_inspector_keyed_paths for every selectable type, unions the surfaced (normalized) paths, and classifies each animated value as surfaced or fall-through. Pure aggregation in dev/scripts/channel_coverage_core.py (classify_coverage / normalize_path — no bpy, unit-tested directly). Each builder is defensive: an API mismatch is recorded in builders_failed (no silent caps), never sinks the run. Current probe result: 9 animated values, 5 surfaced, 4 fall-through (driver scale, NLA-only rotation_euler, non-active-material metallic, compositor nodes["Viewer"].location), 0 regressions, 0 unexpected-surfaced — empirically confirming the four structural gaps the static list claims. Scoring: only probe regressions (a curated-covered surface the live routing FAILED to surface) deduct (0.3 each, folded into pen_channel); the expected-overseen fall-throughs are informational (they confirm known gaps). Report: a ### Tier 2 block in the ## Part CORR-09 markdown + probe payload on the dashboard CORR-09 part. Tests: dev/tests/test_channel_coverage_probe.py — the pure core (9 cases incl. quote-normalization collision matching + regression/unexpected detection) plus test_probe_runs_and_confirms_structural_gaps, an in-Blender integration test asserting driver/NLA/non-active-material fall through and zero regressions.

    6. New audit rule CORR-08 — Preset-Type Dispatch Exhaustiveness (Tier 1, static). engine/parts/corr_08_preset_dispatch.py AST-extracts _ATTR_MAP from preset_state.py (the canonical 9 preset types, read from disk like CORR-09 — the module imports bpy) and AUTO-DETECTS any literal (dict keys / flat token seq / enum (id,…) tuples) already containing ≥75% of the canonical types as bare tokens, flagging the missing ones — no in-code opt-in marker (that first design was rejected by the maintainer); intentional subsets opt out with # CORR-08-OK (and attribute-name lists like _PRESET_FIELDS, which store *_preset names not bare tokens, are never candidates). Findings carry an impact tier (functional 0.3 / cosmetic 0.05) and an informational same-name "sibling-drift" signal (e.g. two type_info maps that disagree). Wired into rules.py (CORR-08, CORR/HIGH/quality, sentinel CORR-08-OK), state.py (preset_* metrics), report.py (penalty pen_part_preset, quality-row, ## Part CORR-08 markdown, dashboard summary + detailed JSON). Also: the dashboard side-menu now spells out category names (rules.py::CATEGORY_NAMES → taxonomy name → js/app.js, with CATEGORY_FULL_NAMES fallback). Tests dev/tests/test_preset_dispatch_exhaustiveness.py — the check surfaced 19 real gaps; the functional ones (material/world) are fixed in Fixed #6, the architectural subsets exempted with CORR-08-OK.

    7. New audit rule INFO-05 — Naming Conformance (informational, no deduction). engine/parts/info_05_naming.py::classify_part_naming replays doc/standards/naming_conventions.md over the AST — 7 sub-checks (NAME-01..07): file names (§2 folder patterns + forbidden / stdlib-shadow), registered class names (§3 TKS_<infix>_<Pascal>, base-branched + acronym / feature-infix aware), operator idnames (§4.1 tks.<snake>), custom-property infixes (§4.2 _PROP_INFIX_ALLOW ~70 tokens — static from bpy_props_registered / prefs_props_registered, plus a dynamic setattr(owner, f'tks_…', …Property()) JoinedStr/Constant re-walk where mid-token interpolation right after tks_ → naming_unverifiable, never flagged), feature↔directory agreement (§6 _FEATURE_REGISTRY ∃-containment; cascade scope-tier prefixes exempt; verb-first idnames never mistaken for codes), uppercase class sub-namespace infix (§3 — only VSW/PIE registered), and ASCII / byte limits (§5: idname ≤60, class ≤60, prop ≤63). Prefs props are class-namespaced, so only tks_-prefixed prefs props are infix-checked (bare auto_* / confirm_* out of scope — avoids ~400 false positives). Sentinel # NAME-OK: <reason> (reuses crash_06's _s_line_has_sentinel). Allow-list seeded from §4.2 + log / warn / assign (real logging prefs + the tks_warn_expand_* / tks_assign_expand_* dynamic families the §4.2 prose named but its grouped lists omitted — §4.2 updated in lockstep per §10). PG/mixin descriptor check strips an optional feature infix (fixed TKS_VSW_* PropertyGroups false-flagging non-PascalCase). Wired into rules.py (INFO-05, INFO/INFO/none, sentinel NAME-OK), state.py (naming_* metrics), report.py (dispatch after INFO-04, ## INFO-05 markdown section, DATA.parts['INFO-05'] JSON block with by_rule breakdown), js/app.js (HUMAN_CONTENT['INFO-05'], icon type). Informational only — surfaces the §11 migration backlog without re-baselining any score. Real result: 43 findings = exactly the §11 backlog (9 TKS_MT_create_*_preset + 8 TKS_PT_*_presets_popover snake descriptors, 2 TKS_OT_smart_undo/redo, 13 un-prefixed *PropsMixin, 5 ops_-prefix gaps, 4 NAME-05 word-collision idnames, 2 TKS_PG_* fake-infix). Tests dev/tests/test_naming_conformance.py (43; via Blender headless or dev/scripts/run_naming_tests.py in plain CPython — conftest's autouse bpy fixture blocks bare pytest). OPEN: maintainer triage of the 43 (fix vs # NAME-OK).
    8. Legacy Part A..Z audit-letter scheme eliminated — every check is its category ID end-to-end. rules.py drops the legacy field + BY_LEGACY + rule_for_legacy (the rule ID is the sole identity). report.py's parts dict is re-keyed to rule IDs ('S'→'CRASH-06', 'M'→'REG-07', 'SPEED'→'PERF-02', 'COMPAT'→'CORR-03', …); the taxonomy overlay simplified to BY_ID.get(id) (dropped legacy_part + legacy_map); the markdown Audit-Taxonomy table lost its "Was" column; 190 prose Part <token> comments across state.py / visitor.py / cli.py / tests_perf.py / parts/*.py rewritten to IDs. js/app.js: HUMAN_CONTENT re-keyed to IDs (the two non-rule overview cards → 'COMPOSITION' / 'QUALITY'), partCode() fallback no longer prepends "Part ", CATEGORIES maps via r.id; letter-flavoured part-key identifiers renamed (letters→partKeys, orderedLetters→orderedPartKeys, .letters group prop →.keys, letter / partLetter(s) params →partKey; terse loop var L left as a conventional counter). Migrator dev/scripts/migrate_legacy_part_scheme.py; docs (ROADMAP.md, reports/README.md, reports/other/*, 4 troubleshooting docs) + the maintainer memory swept too. Follow-up fix (same unreleased change, never shipped broken): the SPEED→PERF-02 re-key left three bespoke speed renderers reading DATA.parts.SPEED via dot-access (overview speed tile, recommendations, renderSpeedTable) — missed by the migrator's scoped patterns and by quoted/bracket greps — so the Speed card + breakdown rendered "Not measured" until all three were pointed at DATA.parts['PERF-02']; regression guard dev/scripts/verify_part_key_refs.py asserts every hardcoded DATA.parts.<key> resolves to a real data key; doc doc/troubleshooting/stats_speed_card_not_measured_after_rekey.md. Verified: all 26 part keys are IDs, zero legacy in the taxonomy, INFO-05/CRASH-06/PERF-02 stamped, node --check clean, 132 engine tests pass in Blender (naming + preset-dispatch + manual-map + channel-coverage).

    [0.7.8] - 2026-05-31¶

    Added¶

    1. 🟢 Keyframe pies gain Still and Animation sub-modes with scope. Six configurable pies — {kf_pie, kf_alt_pie} × {main, still, anim} — on the existing slot-enum system. New item lists KF_I_STILL_ITEMS / KF_I_ANIM_ITEMS / KF_A_STILL_ITEMS / KF_A_ANIM_ITEMS (preferences/addon_prefs_constants.py, with ('', "HEADER", "") separator rows); 32 slot EnumPropertys (kf_i_still_slot_*, kf_i_anim_slot_*, kf_a_still_slot_*, kf_a_anim_slot_*) + 4 enable toggles (kf_{i,a}_{still,anim}_enabled) + 4 collapse flags (expand_kf_*) across props_keyframe_pie.py / props_logging.py; per-slot dedupe via a _make_kf_updaters closure factory. Sub-pie menus TKS_MT_PIE_Keyframe{Still,Anim,ClearStill,ClearAnim} render through _draw_pie_from_slots. _SLOT_ACTION_MAP (panels/pie_menus/keyframe.py) reworked from 3- to 4-tuples (op_idname, props_dict, label, icon) so a slot can carry scope / whole_timeline / menu name; OPEN_STILL / OPEN_ANIMATION (+_CLEAR) map to wm.call_menu_pie and are gated in _draw_pie_from_slots by their kf_*_enabled toggle. New scope operators: tks.snap_selected_to_rest (TKS_OT_SnapSelectedToRest); tks.set_rest_default + scope Enum (_execute_scoped / _set_rest_field_obj, create-as-needed); tks.delete_rest_slot (scope-unified; legacy tks.unset_rest_slot / tks.clear_all_rest_keys_for_vl retained); tks.clear_keyframes (scope + whole_timeline — keyframe_points removed by reverse index to dodge reference invalidation); tks.delete_anim_slot (idname chosen to avoid the inspector's existing tks.delete_slot); tks.insert_keyframes (scope). Pure cores filter_drifts_by_scope / object_names_in_scope (features/rest_state/logic.py). Delete operators gate an invoke blast-radius invoke_confirm on the existing confirm_delete_slot pref (off = auto-accept). Tests: dev/tests/test_ref_scope.py, test_anim_clear.py, test_f12_pie_items.py. EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 449 → 493.
    2. 🟢 Ctrl+N "Add Context" default. Pure _ctrl_n_instant_plan(item_type, group_name, vl_default, scene_default) in operators/context/ops_add_item.py; TKS_OT_AddNewContextItem gains force_menu: BoolProperty and reads ctrl_n_viewlayer_default / ctrl_n_scene_default (AutomationsPropsMixin) to fire tks.add_viewlayer / tks.add_scene_to_group (INVOKE_DEFAULT, with group_name) instead of wm.call_menu. New zero-prop TKS_OT_GlobalNewMenu (tks.global_new_menu) bound to Ctrl+Shift+N in ops_global_shortcuts.register() forces the menu via add_new_context_item(force_menu=True) — the flag lives on the Python call, never on kmi.properties (stale-SRNA rule). Patterns are all-lowercase (Blender lowercases the rna_id before a case-sensitive fnmatch). Tests in dev/tests/test_manual_map.py.
    4. 🟢 Solo mode for the preferences accordions. accordion_solo_mode: BoolProperty (NavigationPropsMixin). TKS_OT_ToggleAccordion.invoke now delegates to a pure _accordion_new_states(target, group, current_open, solo, shift) (preferences/ops_misc.py): Shift → whole-group toggle (overrules); solo + opening → exclusive (siblings closed); otherwise → single toggle.     Fixed¶

    1. 🟢 Undo/redo now re-applies the right action when you switch View Layer between scenes. Regression from the v0.7.7 single-sweep rework. Post-undo, _deferred_cascade_apply (core/vl_lifecycle.py) runs apply_overrides(skip_action=True), so re-resolving the action tier is delegated entirely to _maybe_refire_cascade_snap → apply_vl_switch_unified (the forward switch writes ad.action inside the handle_viewlayer_switch depsgraph handler, which is not an undo-step boundary — Rule #2 — so memfile undo doesn't restore those writes). _maybe_refire_cascade_snap gated the re-fire purely on scene['tks_cascade_token'] == TKS_VL_STATE.last_cascade_token: a per-scene custom prop (rolled back by undo) compared against a single global int (survives undo, shared across every scene/VL). The values collide constantly — each scene has its own counter and all VLs of one scene share one — so the gate false-skipped, no Fast Sweep ran, and objects kept the previous VL's action. Confirmed in the user's takes_for_blender_2026-05-28.log: skipped deferred-cascades show apply_overrides … action=0.0ms with no following Fast Sweep … ASSIGN=N line (e.g. L259710, L259762); the tokens only ever held 0/1. Fix: added _vl_context_changed = bool(_vl_pre_undo) and _vl_pre_undo != (scene.name, view_layer.name) to the gate — _vl_pre_undo (captured in _handle_undo_pre/_handle_redo_pre as the pre-restore active context) is the authoritative per-VL "a switch was crossed" signal, immune to token aliasing; the token compare stays as a fallback. Non-switch undos still skip (the gate's _vl_pre_undo == landed case), so the inline ref-snap can't clobber undo-restored state. Rejected alternatives — per-scene-keyed last_cascade_token dict (misses within-scene VLs that share one counter), per-VL token (bumped on the destination, can't detect that the returned-to source VL needs re-establishing), and always-refire (over-snaps non-switch undos) — documented in doc/troubleshooting/undo_vl_switch_action_not_resolved.md. New regression tests dev/tests/test_undo_vl_refire.py (3): context-change-despite-token-collision re-fires, nothing-crossed stays quiet, raw token crossing still re-fires. Full suite 383 passed (Blender 5.1 headless).

    2. 🟢 Undo no longer snaps objects to the rest pose (follow-up to #1, same session). With #1 making the re-fire fire on every cross-/within-scene undo, the user reported "undo not working" — objects jumped to ref pose on Ctrl+Z. Cause: apply_vl_switch_unified STEP 3 snaps unkeyed props to ref state but bypassed is_snap_suppressed() (the suppress_snap_for_undo(1.0) window the undo handler opens and _revert_unkeyed_to_rest_deferred already honors — its docstring: "ref-state snap can overwrite Blender's undo-restored unkeyed transforms"). Post-restart log showed every re-fire logging Fast Sweep … ASSIGN=0 SNAP=3 (e.g. L267281/L267507/L268695) — 3 undo-restored transforms overwritten per undo (SNAP counts only changed values). Fix in core/vl_switch_fast.py: compute _snap_allowed = _has_ref and not is_snap_suppressed() once (after _has_ref), and gate STEP 3 on if _snap_allowed: instead of if _has_ref:. STEP 2 (action assign) still always runs, so the re-fire restores the action without snapping; forward switches are never inside the suppression window so they snap as before. The earlier "always-refire" failed-approach note in the troubleshooting doc predicted this exact regression. Regression tests added to dev/tests/test_undo_vl_refire.py::TestSnapSuppressedDuringUndo (2): apply_vl_switch_unified snaps a drifted object to ref when not suppressed (baseline), and skips the snap (drift preserved) inside the suppression window. Full suite 385 passed (Blender 5.1 headless).

    3. 🟢 Fixed a hard crash when adding View Layers and copying scenes — dangling dynamic-EnumProperty strings. User crash report (Blender 5.0.1): EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION (0xc0000005), fault addr 0x2, stack uiBut::~uiBut → UI_block_update_from_old → UI_block_end_ex → ED_region_header_layout → ED_region_header → ED_region_do_draw, after tks.add_viewlayer ×2 + scene.new(NEW) + scene.new(FULL_COPY). Root cause is the documented bpy.props gotcha: a dynamic EnumProperty(items=cb) whose callback builds identifier/name/desc strings at runtime (obj.name, f-strings, os.listdir, str(handle)) and returns a list nothing retains — Blender keeps raw char* into the PyUnicode buffers, the GC frees them when the list is replaced, and the next UI_block_update_from_old / uiBut::~uiBut dereferences freed memory. Direct trigger: TKS_OT_AddViewLayer.target_scene (operators/misc/ops_menus.py) was items=lambda self, ctx: [(s.name, s.name, "") for s in bpy.data.scenes]; add_viewlayer is REGISTER+UNDO with invoke()→execute(), so the redo panel draws that enum, then FULL_COPY mutated bpy.data.scenes, freeing the strings — the persistent editor header was simply the next block to redraw (heap-wide corruption, hence the varied/innocent-looking backtrace). 13 callbacks shared the pattern; preferences/props/props_preset_storage.py:_get_prefs_file_items and preferences/utils_sound.py:get_sound_file_items had already worked around it locally with global _xxx_cache (prior evidence of the same crash). Fix (3-Strikes centralization): new takes_for_blender/utils/enum_cache.py — retain(items) appends to a bounded deque(maxlen=256) and returns items unchanged (strong ref survives until Blender stops drawing the button; deque bounds memory); @retained_enum decorator wraps (self, context) callbacks and routes their return through retain(). Exported from utils/__init__.py; added to the __init__.py reload list. @retained_enum applied to ops_menus._addvl_target_scene_items (was the trigger lambda, hoisted to a named fn), panels/context/properties.py:get_scene_items, properties/slot_ui.py:get_slot_items, variant_switch/properties.py:_get_product_items + _get_variant_items_for_context, operators/inspector/ops_action_assign.py:_get_action_items, panels/navigation/monitors_debug.py:_get_log_file_items, operators/tags/_tag_group_helpers.py:get_tag_group_items, render_presets/operators.py:get_storage_mode_items, render_presets/properties.py:get_tier_filter_items. Indirect helpers retained at the lambda call site with retain(...): operators/context/groups/ops_hierarchy.py (4 lambdas → _enum_scene_groups / _enum_scene_groups_exclude / _enum_vl_groups), operators/inspector/ops_slot_mgmt.py:target_action, render_presets/operators.py:preset_name. Failed approach (recorded so we don't repeat it): a first retained_enum using a *args wrapper to also cover the 4-arg _enum_vl_groups made the addon fail registration — ValueError: EnumProperty(...): expected 'items' function to take 2 arguments, not 0 (a *args fn reports co_argcount==0); the decorator must keep the literal (self, context) signature, and extra-arg helpers retain at the lambda instead. The two pre-existing global _xxx_cache callbacks were left as-is (already correct). Regression tests dev/tests/test_enum_retention.py (7): retain identity, GC-survival, bounded store, decorator return-value + runtime-string retention + extra-arg call-site pattern, and an integration check that _addvl_target_scene_items self-retains. Full suite 392 passed (Blender 5.1 headless), addon registers clean. See doc/troubleshooting/enum_items_dangling_string_crash.md.

    4. 🟢 Cross-scene undo reliably keeps each View Layer's take assignment. Follow-up to Fixed #1/#2 above — and a regression introduced by #1's _vl_context_changed gate. Post-undo, apply_overrides runs skip_action=True, so the action tier is re-applied only by _maybe_refire_cascade_snap → apply_vl_switch_unified, with _post_undo_ping → _process_fresh_actions as the rebuild path (it renames an object's restored autokey-default action — e.g. CubeAction — to the cascade name and rewrites vl.tks_action). On a cross-scene undo landing on an intermediate snapshot, resolve_cascade(ACTION) returns None, but _maybe_refire_cascade_snap still called apply_vl_switch_unified(target_action=None) — whose STEP-1 unassign cleared the object's autokey-default action (Fast Sweep … UN=1 ASSIGN=0; Pass1b … Cube_MESH 'CubeAction' -> 'None') before the ping fired, so the ping found nothing and the tier stayed empty. It ran at all despite cur_token == prev_token because of the _vl_context_changed re-fire gate from #1. Fix in core/vl_lifecycle.py:_maybe_refire_cascade_snap: if _target_action is None: return — skip the destructive re-fire when nothing resolves, so the ping can rebuild the tier (the pre-0.7.7 behavior). Rest-snap is suppressed during the undo grace window anyway (#2), and the re-fire still runs when an action does resolve (cross-scene undo to a VL whose tier survived). Diagnosed by a controlled comparison: the same .blend run through TMP/takes_for_blender_v0.7.6 (works — zero Cascade-token boundary crossed … re-fired lines on undo, so CubeAction survives for the ping) vs HEAD (the re-fired line clears the action); both traces in the troubleshooting doc. NOTE: the v0.7.7 cascade performance work was ruled out — it doesn't touch the post-undo action path (which uses skip_action=True + apply_vl_switch_unified, perf-untouched); all four perf optimizations remain intact (benchmark p50 2.96 ms on the default scene, action-tier-dominant as documented). Open edge (accepted): if the snapshot action is already cascade-named rather than autokey-default, the ping's _is_autokey_default_action_name gate still rejects it — separate, pre-existing limitation. Regression guard dev/tests/test_undo_vl_refire.py::TestRefireBoundaryDetection::test_no_refire_when_cascade_resolves_none (the two sibling boundary tests updated to assert the re-fire does run when an action resolves). Full suite 408 passed (Blender 5.1 headless); user-confirmed in-app on the same file that failed. See doc/troubleshooting/undo_vl_switch_action_not_resolved.md.

    5. 🟢 CURRENT_VL / "Active Layer Only" dispatch guarded on unsaved files. _dispatch in render_scope.py checks bpy.ops.tks.render_active_vl.poll() and wraps the invoke in try/except, reporting a clean message instead of raising RuntimeError: Operator bpy.ops.tks.render_active_vl.poll() failed, context is incorrect when the file is unsaved or there's no active view layer.

    6. 🟢 Clear Pycache / Reload Addon reachable on an unsaved file. TKS_OT_ClearPycache and TKS_OT_ReloadAddon polled on bpy.data.filepath, disabling both whenever no .blend was saved. Neither touches on-disk .blend data (clear deletes __pycache__ under the addon's own install dir resolved from __file__; reload defers an addon disable+enable rebuilding only runtime/PG state), and the gate was inconsistent with TKS_OT_RebuildCache. Dropped both poll methods (commit d8186cf).

    Tooling¶

    Maintainer-only — the doc/reports/ /stats code-quality dashboard + engine. Not shipped in the add-on zip; no takes_for_blender/ runtime change.

    1. /stats Manual-Map Coverage audit (INFO-04). New doc/reports/engine/parts/info_04_manual_map.py (classify_info_04): AST-extracts WIKI_BASE + MANUAL_MAP from takes_for_blender/utils/manual_map.py (never imported — it imports bpy) and replays Blender's right-click → Online Manual matcher (lowercase rna_id + case-sensitive fnmatchcase, first-match-wins) against every right-clickable element: tks.* operators, TKS_AddonPreferences.* props, tks_* data props on Scene/WindowManager/ViewLayer, and operator redo-panel fields (counted only for REGISTER + non-INTERNAL + non-HIDDEN operators — fixed a 591→183 op-field over-count). Status taxonomy explicit/page/wildcard_home/uncovered. New INFO-04 rule in engine/rules.py; state.py gains MANUAL_MAP_PATH/WIKI_DOCS_PATH + ~20 wire_* metrics; visitor.py collects prefs-prop sites, operator bl_options/hidden props, and panel/menu ui_class_meta; report.py::_wireable_block buckets rows by status with an "Appears in (UI)" breadcrumb, the auto-wired suggestion, and a wiki page/anchor scan (_scan_wiki_pages/_scan_md_anchors, :icon: shortcodes stripped, heading level captured). Dashboard renderManualMapWiring (js/app.js) draws status filter tiles, the breadcrumb column, and a two-level page→section override picker (document-order, level-dashed anchors, per-row clear ✕), exporting picks to data/wire_assignments.json. dev/scripts/apply_wire_assignments.py folds those (override ?? auto-wire) into the AUTO-WIRED marker block of manual_map.py (434 lowercased exact entries). Note: the shipped wiring is already all-lowercase (see 0.7.8 Added #3) — the audit exists to keep it that way (uppercase patterns never match Blender's lowercased rna_id, the original 452-prefs dead-end). Tests: dev/tests/test_manual_map_coverage.py (14) + test_manual_map.py all-lowercase guard.
    2. Paste-to-find smart filter + live "Opens ↗" column. New pure, DOM-free doc/reports/js/wire_query.js. wireNormalizeQuery(raw) extracts the identifier from any Blender copy format: operator match is anchored at ^bpy\.ops\. and stops before (, so a kwarg-embedded bpy.ops.… string value can't hijack it; a path ending in ] → last ["…"] key (raw IDProperty); a path ending in .attr → trailing attribute (registered RNA — prefs/data full paths, datablock subscripts ignored); bare tokens pass through; 512-char cap + linear regexes (no O(n²)/ReDoS). wireFilterByQuery matches exact row-tail first (rna.split('.').pop() === token) so a full command lands on exactly that row — batch_render no longer drags in batch_render_bg, and type no longer substring-matches all 1150 rows — falling back to substring only when no tail matches (partial typing/prefix search preserved). Design was hardened against an adversarial review (workflow) that found fatal v1 bugs: lastIndexOf('bpy.ops.') kwarg hijack, prefs paths normalising to the package name takes_for_blender (→0 hits), and substring over-match (type→736, f→580). dev/tests/test_wire_query.js (50 assertions, all adversarial cases) + real-data check: 416/416 operators and 470/470 prefs each resolve to exactly one row. A non-empty search now bypasses the status chip + cause in draw() (all data/prefs props are status page, hidden by the default wildcard_home tile, which made paste-to-find silently return nothing) — Kind dropdown still applies — with a "searching all statuses (tile filter paused)" note; the search box gained an overlaid clear ✕ and Esc-to-clear (stops propagation only when it clears). New "Opens ↗" column: a live <a target="_blank" rel="noopener"> to p.wiki_base + effective-suffix (the dropdown selection, or the auto-wired page on KEEP), updated on every page/section change and clear.
    3. Refresh-command target fix + Settings consolidation + part-file renames. report.py built the website's Refresh command from os.path.abspath(__file__), so it copied python …/engine/report.py — a module that only defines functions and aborts with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'engine' when run directly (added a __main__ guard pointing at the entry point). Retargeted the command to os.path.join(REPORTS_DIR, "ast_stats_engine.py"); js/app.js::wireCommands() re-derives it from the repo root (cut at /doc/reports/) so it's correct even when the loaded data holds the old path. A first pass appended --no-tests --no-perf for speed, which blanked the TESTS ("Not run") and SPEED ("Not measured") cards — both passes run headless blender --background, so the flags suppressed them — reverted so the main Refresh runs the full pass; regenerated data/codebase_stats.json/.js (Tests 490 passed/1 failed, Speed totals.overall_score 9.9). Refresh + a new clipboard-command Rewire button (copies the apply_wire_assignments.py command) moved into the #settings-popover; .layout-save/.layout-restore added to the shared popover-button selectors (they were falling back to the boxed UA default). Internal refactor: legacy doc/reports/engine/parts/part_*.py renamed to ID-prefixed filenames (part_s→crash_06_restricted_context, part_t→reg_01_class_registration, part_x→corr_04_unreachable, … info_04_manual_map); symbol names (classify_part_*) kept; imports rewired in report.py/cli.py/ast_stats_engine.py. New js/wire_query.js loaded before app.js in index.html.

    [0.7.7] - 2026-05-27¶

    Added¶

    1. Link-and-Assign confirmation when picking a camera that's missing from some scenes. New TKS_OT_LinkCameraAndAssign operator in takes_for_blender/operators/cascade/ops_link_camera.py, registered via the canonical panels/context/_class_registry.py:classes chain (added in the same release after the dead-list trap below — see #5 under Fixed). The picker_menu (TKS_MT_CascadePicker.draw in operators/cascade/_picker.py) now checks each camera item against the tier's covered scenes (bpy.data.scenes for GLOBAL, [bpy.data.scenes.get(m.scene_name) for m in sg.members] for SG); incompatible items get icon='ERROR' + a (missing in N scene(s)) text suffix and route through tks.link_camera_and_assign instead of tks.set_cascade_prop. The operator's invoke() opens wm.invoke_popup(width=380) rendering a 3-button row driven by a mode: EnumProperty(items=[('PROMPT', …), ('LINK', …), ('ASSIGN', …), ('CANCEL', …)]) — the buttons chain back into the same op with a non-PROMPT mode so execute() can branch without a separate operator per action. LINK calls _link_camera_into_scenes(cam, target_scenes) in operators/cascade/_helpers.py which finds cam.users_collection[0] (the camera's "home" collection) and scene.collection.children.link(home_coll) for each target scene — preserving the user's existing collection structure rather than dropping the camera into the master root (per explicit user constraint). Falls back to scene.collection.objects.link(cam) if home_coll is itself a scene's master collection (RuntimeError on the children.link). Both LINK and ASSIGN then chain into bpy.ops.tks.set_cascade_prop() to apply the assignment.

    Changed¶

    1. Camera picker dropdowns now match each tier's reach. Two coordinated changes in takes_for_blender/operators/cascade/:
    2. Scene-bound tiers (Scene / VL / VLG / VLV) — camera_prop_search in _helpers.py:8 gained an optional scene=None kwarg; when provided, cam_col is populated from scene.objects instead of bpy.data.objects. Callers updated: ops_camera_levels.py:467 (Scene), ops_viewlayer_camera.py:118 (VL), ops_camera_levels.py:222-224 (SG popover — now passes g.member_scenes for the multi-scene warning). The generic popover_draw helper (_helpers.py:307) resolves cam_scene = bpy.data.scenes.get(scene_name) if tier in ('SCENE', 'VL', 'VLG', 'VLV') else None and forwards. Global popover at ops_camera_levels.py:83 intentionally passes no scene= so it lists every camera.

    3. Cross-scene tiers (Global / SG) — _camera_collection_fn in _picker.py:27 returns the full list, but TKS_MT_CascadePicker.draw (_picker.py:120) now computes covered_scenes (all scenes for GLOBAL, sg.members scenes for SG) and, per item, calls a new _scenes_missing_camera(cam_name, scenes) helper from _helpers.py. Items with non-empty missing lists get the route-to-link-prompt treatment (see Added #1) plus a visual mark. New _warn_camera_not_in_all_scenes(layout, cam_name, scenes) renders an icon='ERROR' label under the dropdown listing up to 3 missing scenes (then +N more).

    4. Global and Scene Group camera assignments survive scene switches. The auto-clear branch in core/cascade.py:507-557 previously walked back to whichever tier set the cascade and setattr(_owner, _prop, "") when the active scene couldn't resolve to the camera (camera.name not in scene.objects). For Global / SG sources this wiped the assignment for every scene the tier covers, the moment the active scene happened to be one without the camera linked. Pre-fix repro: set master_scene.tks_global_camera = "cam_master" (cam_master linked in Scene A only), switch to Scene B → global wiped, switch back to Scene A → cascade resolves to nothing. Fixed by branching on source: Global / Scene Group → logger.debug(...) + skip applying scene.camera, preserve the tier assignment; Scene / VL / VLG / VLV → auto-clear as before (those tiers are scene-bound, so stale picks are genuinely self-heal-able). The picker UI now warns up-front and offers LINK & ASSIGN (see Added #1), so this branch only fires for stale data from older .blend files or external script writes. See doc/troubleshooting/camera_picker_unfiltered_dropdown.md.

    Fixed¶

    1. Output, View Layer, and File Output standalone preset panels now appear in the Properties tab. TKS_PT_OutputPresetsStandalone, TKS_PT_ViewLayerPresetsStandalone, TKS_PT_FileOutputPresetsStandalone were declared in features/render_presets/panels_ui.py:304-340 and imported at features/render_presets/panels.py:50 but the classes = (...) tuple at L58-80 only contained TKS_PT_RenderPresetsStandalone, TKS_PT_WorldPresetsStandalone, TKS_PT_MaterialPresetsStandalone. The v0.7.5 fix for the same bug class (changelog #3 — "Render preset row visible in Render properties tab on every render engine") patched only the Render standalone; this commit adds the three siblings. Surfaced by the new Part T (Class Registration Coverage) audit which set-diffs declared Blender-base classes against the union of all *classes list members + direct register_class() calls anywhere in the codebase.

    2. Blender no longer prints a flood of _RestrictContext errors at startup. Same root cause across three files:

    3. features/sync/handlers_viewport.py:105 (_propagate_tool_settings) and :130 (_propagate_orientation) read scene = bpy.context.scene directly. The subsequent if scene is None: return guard couldn't help because the attribute access itself raised before the None check could execute. Switched both to scene = getattr(bpy.context, 'scene', None).
    4. utils/pinned.py:39 (_scene_name) previously did return bpy.context.scene.name if bpy.context and bpy.context.scene else "" — the truthy-gate dereferenced .scene before the truthiness check could short-circuit. Rewritten to scene = getattr(bpy.context, 'scene', None); return scene.name if scene else "".

    5. preferences/props/props_sync_viewport.py:23 had a misleading comment claiming _on_sync_toggle "only runs when the user actually toggles" — false, Blender invokes the callback during userpref restore for every prop whose stored value differs from default. Corrected to explicitly document the pref-load invocation path and the downstream getattr guards. Trigger: 10 BoolProperty(update=_on_sync_toggle) bindings on ViewportSyncPropsMixin fire during userpref restore at addon-enable time; the callback chain reaches the two _propagate_* functions which then raised AttributeError: '_RestrictContext' object has no attribute 'scene' — once per non-default toggle on every fresh Blender launch. See doc/troubleshooting/restricted_context_callback_chain.md.

    6. Pytest test runner no longer emits 244 caught fatal exceptions per run. Pytest's _pytest.runner._update_current_test_var writes / pops PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST in os.environ around every test. The teardown pop goes through os.environ.__delitem__ → os.unsetenv() → the Win32 environment API. In Blender's embedded CPython on Windows that path SEGV's — fires once per test teardown (244 access violations in a 375-test run on this machine). Blender's faulthandler catches each SEGV at the C level; pytest is unaware and the test "passes" cleanly. Pre-fix the /stats Tests KPI tile flagged this as Crashed · 2 runner errors (under-counted — engine stopped at the first marker). Patched dev/tests/run_tests.py to monkey-patch _pyt_runner._update_current_test_var = lambda *a, **k: None before pytest.main(). No addon code reads PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST (the tests use pytest fixtures for that), so suppressing the env update has zero cost. Verified: 244 SEGVs → 0. See doc/troubleshooting/pytest_current_test_env_segfault.md, which supersedes the earlier (wrong) order-dependent-state-corruption hypothesis in doc/troubleshooting/test_runner_soft_crash_order_dependent.md.

    7. _clear_actions_on_watched no longer label-walks every sub-target. SPEED audit (dev/scripts/perf_capture.py) flagged cascade_per_prop_ms[action] = 17.6 ms on the default-cube scene — 96 % of total cascade time. cProfile breakdown: 1.9k calls to naming_utils.generate_slot_name per cascade, each doing a bpy.context.preferences.addons.get(...) lookup + RNA attr read + template substitution (~1.5-2 ms each). The labels weren't being consumed — _clear_actions_on_watched in core/cascade_actions.py was iterating iter_anim_targets(obj) (yields (target, slot_label) tuples) purely to null .animation_data.action. Fix in core/vl_targets.py: new iter_anim_targets_only(id_data) mirrors iter_anim_targets's target-enumeration shape (same Object / Scene / World / Material / fallback branches, same dedupe rules for material id() and geometry-nodes node_group id()) but yields just the target ID with no label generation; helper _iter_node_groups_only mirrors _iter_node_groups the same way. Re-exported via core/vl_persistence.py:60 so the existing import path still works. _clear_actions_on_watched switched to the new iterator; the dead if not bpy.data.worlds: return; world = bpy.data.worlds[0] (world variable never referenced) was deleted; the per-iteration from ..utils.pinned import is_pinned was hoisted out of the inner loop; the four duplicated try: apply_rest_values(...) except (RuntimeError, ReferenceError): pass blocks were consolidated into a nested _apply_ref_safely(t) helper that short-circuits when rest_action is None. Measured: factory-startup scene (3 objs, no Rest Action) 14-18 ms → 0.047 ms p50 (~ 380× faster on the no-reference path). Caveat: user scene with 84 objs + Rest Action set stays at 14.9 ms — the residual hot path is apply_rest_values being called twice per sub-target with rest_slot_map rebuilt from scratch on every call (1.8k calls · 22 ms / 10 iter = 92 % of total). That's tracked separately as Fix 6 in doc/troubleshooting/cascade_action_clear_slow.md and deferred to a future commit so the semantics of rest-state snap-back stay untouched in this release.

    8. Undo/redo safety verified with dev/scripts/verify_undo_clear_path.py (assign → undo → null, redo → restored, action.use_fake_user preserved across 5 cycles, _clear_actions_on_watched(scene, vl) no-crash under forced TKS_VL_STATE.is_undoing = True — _apply_ref_safely correctly relies on apply_rest_values's pre-existing is_undoing/is_redoing/is_snap_suppressed() guard at features/rest_state/logic.py:38-52 to skip the ref-snap during undo grace) plus the full dev/tests/test_undo_safety.py suite (8 tests covering basic undo/redo, undo-after-action-creation, multiple-cycle stability, pointer stability, history jump, fake-user-survives-undo).

    9. Companion fix in core/vl_handlers.py:unregister() — the dead-register cleanup (entry #5 below) removed the empty classes = [] scaffold from vl_handlers.py, but the matching for cls in reversed(classes): unregister_class(cls) loop in unregister() was left behind referencing the deleted variable. Surfaced via [TKS INFO] [CORE:INIT] Failed to unregister takes_for_blender.core.vl_persistence: name 'classes' is not defined log line on every addon disable. Loop removed; no classes were ever registered from this file so no actual unregister logic was lost. Audit-engine test runs that disable/enable repeatedly went from 202 / 375 passed (345 ERROR rows from the dangling unregister) back to clean 375 / 375.
    10. Companion micro-fix in core/naming_utils.py — get_addon_prefs() now caches the prefs lookup result in a module-level _cached_prefs. The cache is invalidated explicitly via reset_addon_prefs_cache() wired into takes_for_blender/__init__.py:unregister() so addon-disable/enable cycles still resolve the new prefs instance. Pre-fix _build_token_values (called from generate_slot_name 1.9k times per cascade) re-resolved bpy.context.preferences.addons.get(ADDON_MODULE) each call. After Fix 1 the call frequency dropped enough that this cache contributes less than half a millisecond on its own, but it's the right shape going forward.
    11. Fix 6 (the deferred rest-state residual): apply_rest_values gained optional rest_slot_map= / rest_slot_map_short= kwargs (built once via new build_rest_slot_map(rest_action) helper) so the per-call rebuild is skipped; _clear_actions_on_watched pre-builds the maps once and drops the redundant per-sub-target _apply_ref_safely call (apply_rest_values(obj) already walks iter_anim_targets(obj) and snaps every sub-target). Also gated the per-call tks_log behind tks_log_active('CORE','REST'). User scene 14.9 → 9.7 ms p50 (SPEED 5.7 → 8.0). A lazy-label variant was prototyped and reverted (10.07 → 10.45 ms — most slots are template-named, so the lazy path always fell through to generate the label anyway).
    12. Fix v3 (core/naming_utils.py): session-scoped generate_name cache keyed by (template_key, separator, effective_kwargs), where _resolve_context_tokens pre-bakes every implicit context-derived token (scene / viewlayer / world / object / type / action / material / collection / parent) into the key so a context shift can't return a stale hit. _generate_name_uncached kept as a bypass escape hatch. Invalidation via reset_label_cache() from _autosave_preferences (covers template + separator edits) and reset_addon_prefs_cache. Rename safety is automatic (the new name flows into the key). 100 % hit rate post-warmup (dev/scripts/probe_label_cache.py); cache safety proven across all 6 context tokens (dev/scripts/verify_label_cache_safety.py). Plus a cached _log_ref flag in apply_rest_values replacing 4 per-FCurve tks_log_active checks. User scene 9.7 → 8.6 ms p50 (SPEED 8.0 → 8.4).

    13. Fix v4 (the big one — features/rest_state/logic.py + core/cascade_actions.py): extracted _resolve_rest_slot() (exact-key → template-label → raw-name → id-prefix substring fallback) and _snap_one_target() (per-target FCurve snap) from apply_rest_values so the per-object path and the cascade-clear path share one implementation. Rewrote _clear_actions_on_watched as a single labeled walk (was two walks: label-less clear + labeled snap) that resolves the slot inline and snaps only on a hit, with the undo-guard / mirror-suppress / slot-map build / log-active read hoisted to once-per-cascade-pass. A dev/scripts/probe_rest_snap_breakdown.py measurement showed only 1 of 84 objects (1.2 %) actually has a matching ref slot, so the second walk + per-call setup was ~99 % wasted. User scene 8.6 → 2.7 ms p50 (SPEED 8.4 → 9.9 🟢, cumulative 18.65 → 2.73 ms, −85 %). False-negative trap (an object matching only via the substring fallback being wrongly skipped) is avoided by resolving the slot for every target with the shared helper — no separate coverage heuristic. Locked down by new dev/tests/test_rest_state.py::TestClearActionsSnap (4 characterization cases: exact-name, no-match-untouched, substring-fallback, no-ref-action) that pass identically before and after the refactor. Full progression + the deferred Fix v4-followup levers documented in doc/troubleshooting/cascade_action_clear_slow.md.

    14. Internal: 8 dead register() functions removed across the addon; 2 orphaned operators routed to canonical registration. panels/popovers/__init__.py declared a 91-class classes = list(_cascade_classes) + list(_misc_classes) list + register() / unregister() pair that nobody called — panels/__init__.py:modules doesn't include popovers and no other module imports popovers.register. All 91 classes ARE registered, but via panels/context/_class_registry.py:classes (the canonical chain consumed by panels.context.register()). The dead infrastructure was a footgun: adding a class there appeared to work (no errors at import time) but the operator silently never registered. This trap caught TKS_OT_LinkCameraAndAssign when it was first added during the v0.7.7 work; layout.operator("tks.link_camera_and_assign", ...) returned None on every picker click and the next attribute assignment raised AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'camera_name'. Cleanups:

    15. panels/popovers/__init__.py — deleted _cascade_classes, _misc_classes, classes, register(), unregister(), plus the orphan TKS_CamFilterItem class (the matching WindowManager.tks_cam_filtered CollectionProperty went away too; camera_prop_search falls back to tks_scene_cameras which is registered via the canonical chain).

The engine's classify_part_t was extended to scan the 6 lines above each def register(): for # REGISTER_OK: and route matches into t_exempt instead of t_dead_register.
